jobs.title: Managing Director - Data & AI (Montreal, Canada)
jobs.description:
Founded in 2017, Unit8 is a fast-growing Swiss AI and data analytics consulting and services company dedicated to solving complex problems of traditional industries like automotive, chemical, financial services, manufacturing and pharma. We work with some of the biggest organisations in Europe to solve the challenges that directly affect their business - be it operations, finance, manufacturing or R&D. Since our foundation, we have successfully delivered more than 400 projects and have grown to 175+ talented individuals across 7 office locations.

 Unit8’s mission is to drive the adoption of AI and Data Science in the non-digital industries and to help accelerate their digital transformation. Among its activities, Unit8 dedicates a part of its resources and time on projects that deeply matter to us - that includes collaboration on pro-bono and “engineering for good” causes. You can learn more about what we are passionate about at and on our you can find more useful information about our business and recruiting process.

 Are You the Leader We're Looking For?
 As a Managing Director at Unit8, success isn't just about closing deals — it's about becoming a cornerstone of how we grow and deliver in the Canadian market. You will own both sides of the equation: originating high-value client relationships and ensuring the work we deliver actually moves the needle for our clients. If you've built your career at the intersection of commercial impact and technical credibility, and you're ready to operate with real autonomy in an expert-led environment, this is the role.

 What Success Looks Like in This Role
 This is a senior leadership position for someone as comfortable originating a complex engagement as overseeing its delivery. You shape and close the deal, build relationships and trust, and you stay close enough to ensure the technical execution actually delivers value. You will succeed by:

 Building and converting a pipeline of high-value opportunities in the Canadian market — primarily in financial services — through a network earned over years of credible work in data & AI
 Selling from expertise: clients engage with you because you understand their problem because of your deep problem solving skills and experience not because you have a polished pitch
 Staying embedded in delivery long enough to set the right pace, challenge client assumptions, and keep teams focused on the actual business problem
 Bridging the gap between a senior data scientist and a C-suite conversation — translating technical constraints into strategic decisions and vice versa
 Raising the delivery bar by knowing what good looks like and holding teams to that standard

 What You'll Do
 Leverage your existing network to source, shape, and close high-value engagements in Canada (new logos, not just expansions)
 Translate complex business problems into concrete Data & AI solutions: identify where value can be created, make sure the team is building toward it, and hold the client accountable to realising it
 Lead and shape complex, tech-enabled transformations — from early problem definition through to scaled delivery — ensuring the right technology choices serve the business outcome, not the other way around
 Act as the senior point of contact for key clients throughout delivery, ensuring technical execution stays anchored to business value
 Challenge clients when necessary — on scope, pace, and ambition
 Work closely with our engineering and data science teams, providing business context, removing blockers and coaching them.

jobs.title: Head of Data & AI
jobs.description:
About Burq 
 Burq started with an ambitious mission: to turn the complex process of offering delivery into a simple, turnkey solution. It’s a big mission, and now we want you to join us in making it even bigger. 🚀
 We’re proud to be recognized as one of Fast Company’s Best Workplaces for Innovators and a 2025 Inc. Magazine Power Partner, awards that highlight how we’re redefining the future of logistics while empowering our partners to grow.
 Backed by leading Silicon Valley investors like Village Global, the fund whose investors include Bill Gates, Jeff Bezos, Mark Zuckerberg, Reid Hoffman, and Sara Blakely, we’ve built a world-class team across the globe.
 We operate at scale but remain small enough for every person to have a massive impact. There’s a lot of important work ahead, and joining Burq means the opportunity to grow faster than ever while doing the most meaningful work of your career.

 Here’s a quick overview of what you will be doing:

 The Role
 We're looking for a Head of Data & AI to build the intelligence that powers Burq. 
 You'll build a world-class data-and-ML platform: the systems that turn data into models which make every delivery decision smarter and agents that automate the work the industry still does by hand. You'll set the strategy, make the hard architecture and modeling calls, ship models into production that move the business, and build the team to do it at scale.
 This is a player-coach role. You'll lead and grow the data and ML team while staying deeply hands-on — making architecture calls, reviewing engineering and modeling work, and ensuring the platform serves both product and business goals. You'll partner closely with the Head of Engineering, and with product and AI leadership on how intelligence shows up in the product.

 What You'll Do
 Data Platform

 Own the full data platform — the warehouse, streaming and batch ingestion, the semantic layer, and BI infrastructure.
 Define and enforce data governance — access management, quality standards, and a well-modeled, trustworthy "gold" layer.
 Make the warehouse the source of truth for operational, product, and financial analytics.

 Intelligence & Machine Learning 

 Build the models that power delivery intelligence — forecasting, prediction, optimization, matching/allocation, and reliability scoring that turn our data into better real-time decisions.
 Stand up the ML systems that make this real and reliable: feature pipelines, training, serving, evaluation, and drift monitoring.
 Design the learning loop — instrument decisions and outcomes so models continuously improve.
 Drive the AI agent initiative to production, partnering with product and engineering on the surrounding workflows.

 Team & Stakeholders

 Manage and grow the data and ML team (starting from a small core) — hire data engineers, analytics engineers, and data scientists/ML engineers as the platform matures.
 Establish a clear intake process for ad hoc data requests so the team works from a roadmap, not in reactive mode.
 Partner with Sales, Customer Success, and Finance on data-driven analyses and decisions.

Permanent Full Time

Reporting to the AVP, Accounting & Controls, the Director, Internal Controls over Financial Reporting (ICOFR) is responsible for leading the Canadian ICOFR program and ensuring the organization maintains a sustainable, risk-based, and effective control environment.

The Director serves as the central point of coordination across Canada Finance, Business, Technology, Risk & Controls, Internal Audit, and External Audit, providing governance and oversight over the design, evaluation, remediation, and continuous improvement of internal controls that support reliable financial reporting and CEO/CFO certification requirements.

This role is a key leadership position within the Canada Controller Group, responsible for driving control effectiveness, remediation governance, continuous improvement, and the overall maturity of the Canadian control environment.

What You Will Be Doing

Governance & Program Oversight: Lead the Canadian ICOFR program by providing governance and oversight that supports CEO/CFO certification requirements, coordinating across Canada Finance, Business, Technology, Risk & Controls, Internal Audit, and External Audit, and delivering timely reporting, insights, and recommendations to senior management
Control Design & Operating Effectiveness Oversight: Provide oversight of the design, documentation, assessment, and continuous improvement of the Canadian control environment through risk assessment and scoping activities, quality reviews, consistent application of ICOFR methodologies, and control optimization initiatives
Deficiency Evaluation & Remediation Oversight: Provide Canada-wide governance over control deficiency assessments and remediation activities, including severity evaluation, remediation oversight, progress monitoring, and validation of remediation outcomes. Communicate ICOFR assessments, remediation status, emerging risks, and key conclusions to senior management
Enhancing the Overall Control Environment: Lead the evolution of the Canadian control environment by identifying opportunities to strengthen processes and controls, enhancing the quality and consistency of control documentation, promoting stronger control ownership and accountability across the organization, and providing education and guidance to support control awareness
Leadership: Build and lead a high-performing team by providing coaching, mentorship, and development opportunities, while fostering a culture of collaboration, accountability, continuous improvement, and business partnership

8+ years of progressive experience in internal controls, external audit, internal audit, or financial reporting, including experience leading teams, complex initiatives, and cross-functional stakeholder groups
Strong knowledge of internal control frameworks, including COSO and Internal Controls over Financial Reporting (ICOFR/SOX), with experience evaluating control deficiencies, remediation activities, and financial reporting impacts

Strong project management and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines in a dynamic environment
Exceptional communication, presentation, stakeholder management, and relationship-building skills, with the ability to influence senior leaders and business partners

jobs.title: Director of Engineering, Data
jobs.description:
At BuildOps, we build software for modern commercial contractors, from service management through project delivery. We care deeply about the mission and look for people who are driven, self motivated, and excited by fast moving, high ownership environments.



Data sits at the center of BuildOps' AI first strategy. The operational data our customers generate on BuildOps is a long term advantage, but only if it is clean, reliable, and well governed. As Director of Engineering, Data, you will build and lead our unified Data \& AI engineering function. You will own the platforms, pipelines, quality standards, and operating discipline that power AI and ML products and help customers trust BuildOps as their system of record.



Reporting to the VP of Engineering, you will help define BuildOps' data strategy over the next three to five years and shape how we build data powered products. This is a foundational leadership role for someone who can think long term about architecture while staying close to the work. You have built and scaled data organizations before and know how to take a team from early stage scrappiness to operational excellence.


**What You'll Do**


* Own BuildOps' data platform and architecture end to end, including ingestion, transformation, orchestration, and an ML and streaming strategy that evolves with the business and scales efficiently
* Build scalable, repeatable customer and partner data onboarding capabilities that bring data into BuildOps quickly and reliably, reducing time to first value
* Run data systems with production grade discipline, including monitoring, alerting, SLAs, incident response, lineage, freshness, and clear ownership for critical datasets
* Create the data foundation required for AI and ML products, with accurate, well documented inputs today and the right training, inference, and feature infrastructure as those products mature
* Establish governance that supports speed, including access controls, data classification, audit trails, PII handling, and practical data contracts that teams can depend on
* Hire, develop, and lead a strong data engineering team, and establish the right operating rhythms across planning, on call, and stakeholder intake


**What We Look For**


* 10\+ years in data or software engineering, including experience building and scaling teams of 10\+ engineers, with a track record of hiring well, growing leaders, and leading through managers as well as individual contributors
* Deep hands on experience with modern data platforms, including a cloud warehouse or lakehouse such as Snowflake or Databricks, dbt and ELT patterns, orchestration tools like Airflow, and streaming technologies such as Kafka or Kinesis, with AWS experience strongly preferred
* Direct experience building data systems that support production ML use cases, not just analytics, with an understanding of feature stores, training data, real time inference, and the tradeoffs involved in building versus buying ML platform capabilities
* A track record of operational excellence in data, including monitoring, SLAs, incident response, and data quality practices applied with the same rigor as customer facing systems
* Experience delivering customer facing data products such as reporting, analytics, or APIs in B2B SaaS environments where performance, reliability, and trust matter
* Strong architectural judgment, including when to build, when to buy, how to design for change, and how to sequence investments behind validated needs instead of overbuilding
* A pragmatic approach to governance, with security and compliance built in, documentation and contracts that stay current, and access models that balance control with self service
* Early stage or scale up experience in Series B through D companies is a plus, and experience in vertical SaaS or construction tech is helpful but not required


**Who You Are**


* A builder who is comfortable with ambiguity and greenfield work, and can move quickly, ship an MVP, and still make sound decisions for long term scale
* Both hands on and strategic, willing to write code, debug issues, and carry operational responsibility when needed while maintaining a clear multi year vision
* You know how to influence across Product, Engineering, GTM, Finance, and the executive team, build trust, communicate clearly, and push back when priorities are misaligned
* Able to translate technical decisions into business impact and business goals into technical direction
* You have seen this stage of growth before and know what good looks like in a high growth data organization


**Compensation**


* $176,000 \- $235,000 base salary range \+ annual bonus \+ meaningful equity

**What we offer:**
* Generous equity grant, become an owner in our company!
* A comprehensive benefits package
* Flexible PTO and hybrid work schedules
* One\-time work\-from\-home allowance
* Hubs in Los Angeles, San Francisco, Toronto, and Raleigh with hybrid work schedules and lunch provided for in\-office days
* Company events and team\-building activities, both in\-person and virtual
* Fast\-paced, collaborative, and dynamic work environment
* Opportunities for growth and career advancement
* Chance to work with cutting\-edge technology and innovative solutions
* The chance to get in on the ground floor and build something truly groundbreaking for ourselves and our amazing customers


*We welcome applicants from across the U.S. where we are registered to do business and able to support employment. Currently, this excludes the following states: Alaska, Hawaii, Kentucky, Mississippi, Nebraska, New Mexico, North Dakota, Rhode Island, South Dakota, West Virginia, and Wyoming. This list is based solely on operational and compliance considerations and is reviewed from time to time as our footprint grows.*


#### **About BuildOps**



Join BuildOps, the largest commercial trade platform in the country, as we transform the multi\-billion dollar commercial contracting industry!

jobs.description:
Our Story & Purpose:

We’re Vancity, a member-owned credit union built on the principles of inclusion and social justice. Since 1946, our relentless commitment to these values has helped us challenge the status quo and break down barriers. We’ve made bold commitments to become net-zero by 2040 across all mortgages and loans, and we’re actively pursuing strategies in Indigenous banking and financial resilience for our members.  
As the largest private sector Living Wage Employer in Canada, we’re proud to be consistently recognized as one of the country’s Top Employers. If you’re ready to join our team of 2,300 diverse individuals, access competitive rewards and benefits, and be part of a greater movement - apply today!   
Your Role in Supporting Our Members:

As a Senior Director, Contact Centre Operations & Transformation
, you will provide enterprise-level leadership for the modernization of Vancity’s contact centre into a scalable, resilient, and advice-led channel. You will own the multi-year transformation agenda, shaping the future-state operating model, workforce strategy, quality framework, service model, governance routines, and technology-enabled capabilities.   
We’re looking for an accomplished strategic and operational leader who can navigate complex transformation and turn enterprise priorities into measurable results.   
This is a Full-time, Permanent
role based at our Surrey Central City Office
and will report directly to the VP, Inclusive Banking, Alternate Channels
. While this position provides a hybrid work arrangement, you will be expected to be on-site for events and business demands.  
How You'll Make an Impact:

Set the multi-year contact centre strategy, transformation roadmap, future-state operating model, and measures of success.  
Lead through leaders to build an inclusive, accountable, and high-performing culture.  
Modernize workforce management, quality, reporting, IVR, routing, automation, and enabling technology.  
Use operational, financial, risk and member insights to guide investment, capacity, and continuous improvement.  
Ensure strong oversight of risk, compliance, privacy, fraud, business continuity, and service quality.  
Partner across technology, digital, product, operations, and member-facing teams to deliver measurable transformation outcomes.  

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

Post-secondary education in business, technology, finance or a related field, or equivalent experience.  
10+ years of progressive leadership experience in contact centre operations, financial services, or large-scale transformation.  
Experience leading leaders and complex operational portfolios across people, financial, risk and member outcomes.  
A strong record of delivering transformation roadmaps, business cases, operating models, and service-model change.  
Experience modernizing contact centre capabilities, including workforce planning, quality, reporting, routing, automation, or digital platforms.  
Sound knowledge of risk, compliance, privacy, fraud, business continuity, and operational controls in a regulated environment.  
Strong analytical judgment and the ability to influence executives, partners, vendors, and frontline teams.  

Extra Skills That Set You Apart: 

A recognized change management, continuous improvement, or contact centre designation, such as Prosci, Lean Six Sigma or CCXP.  
Experience with Genesys or comparable enterprise contact centre technology.  
Success shifting a large contact centre from transactional service to advice-led member engagement.  

You’ll Thrive Here If You Are: 

Strategic and future-focused
- You turn enterprise priorities into practical roadmaps and measurable outcomes.  
Member-centred
- You put member relationships, financial well-being, and service quality first.  
Collaborative and influential
- You build alignment across leaders, partners, vendors, and frontline teams.  
Decisive and people-focused
- You create clarity, accountability, and inclusion through complex change.  

We value lived experience, so if you are interested in this role, we encourage you to apply even if you feel your skills don't perfectly align with those listed.  

What You’ll Earn:

This role offers a salary range of  $165,500 to $204,435 per annum
. The base pay offered may vary depending on factors such as relevant qualifications, skills, previous experience, and internal equity. As part of our total rewards package, employees may also be eligible for our annual incentive program, subject to program eligibility requirements.  

**Posting Deadline: Please apply by Wednesday, November 4th, at 3:00pm. **

Why You’ll Love Working Here:

A career at Vancity is more than just a job, you’re joining a tradition of change-makers who are creating lasting change for our communities. Beyond base pay, we offer a comprehensive total rewards package to ensure our employees are empowered to thrive:  
Purpose-driven workplace
: Join Canada’s largest private-sector Living Wage Employer and one of the country’s Top Employers.  
Flexible benefits
: Customize your health and dental coverage from your first day.  
Time to recharge
: Start with 3-4 weeks of vacation, plus additional holidays, and care days.  
Defined benefit pension
: Build toward a reliable, guaranteed retirement income.  

Vancity Talent Programs:

With special permission from the BC Human Rights Commissioner, this initiative provides access to career development opportunities, prioritized job screening, and feedback. Any information you choose to share will be stored securely and used only for recruitment and career development connected to this initiative, in line with the BC Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA). For details, please see our dedicated Talent Programs job posting.  
At Vancity we’re committed to creating a welcoming and inclusive workplace to help our people and communities thrive and prosper. Diversity in our workforce is integral so that we can truly represent, understand and respond to our community needs and deliver on our member experience.  
We are also committed to an inclusive, barrier-free, and accessible recruitment experience for all candidates. jobs.title: Chef(fe) de projet, déploiement de l'automatisation - Automation Deployment leader
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary

Le/la chef(fe) de projet, déploiement de l'automatisation, est un(e) expert(e) reconnu(e) en robotique et en automatisation, responsable de la coordination de la construction, de l'intégration et de la mise en service de bout en bout des solutions d'automatisation à l'échelle de l'entreprise GE Vernova. Ce(tte) professionnel(le) de haut niveau travaille de façon transversale avec des intégrateurs de systèmes, des équipes de préparation de site et des architectes technologiques pour assurer une exécution de projet et une transition opérationnelle harmonieuses. Le/la responsable du déploiement de l'automatisation gère les échéanciers, les budgets et l'alignement des intervenants afin de livrer des projets d'automatisation conformes aux exigences rigoureuses en matière de performance, de sécurité et de cybersécurité. Fort(e) d'une expertise approfondie en automatisation industrielle et en gestion de programmes/projets, ce rôle favorise des déploiements réussis dans des environnements complexes et à grande échelle. Le/la responsable du déploiement de l'automatisation joue un rôle crucial dans l'orientation de la stratégie mondiale d'automatisation de GE Vernova grâce à une implication soutenue sur le terrain et au sein de l'écosystème de l'automatisation.

The Automation Deployment Lead is a recognized expert in robotics and automation responsible for coordinating the end-to-end build, integration, and commissioning of automation solutions across GE Vernova’s enterprise. This senior professional works cross-functionally with system integrators, site readiness teams, and technology architects to ensure seamless project execution and handover into operations. The Automation Deployment Leader manages timelines, budgets, and stakeholder alignment to deliver automation projects that meet rigorous performance, safety, and cybersecurity requirements. With deep expertise in industrial automation and formal program/project management, this role drives successful deployments in complex, large-scale environments. The Automation and Deployment leader is critical in shaping and directing GE Vernova’s global automation strategy through deep engagement in the shops and throughout the automation ecosystem.

Job Description

Responsabilités essentielles :

Coordonner les activités de construction, d'intégration et de mise en service des projets d'automatisation, en assurant le respect des échéanciers et des budgets.
Diriger et exécuter le développement de la portée, des échéanciers, des livrables et des exigences d'intégration du projet, en partenariat avec les intégrateurs de systèmes, les équipes techniques internes et les responsables de la préparation des sites.
Piloter tous les aspects du déploiement de l'automatisation, incluant l'installation, les tests, la validation et la transition vers la production, en assurant la conformité aux normes de sécurité et de cybersécurité.
Gérer les risques, les problèmes et les changements tout au long du cycle de vie du projet, en assurant une communication proactive et une résolution rapide.
Suivre la performance du projet par rapport aux indicateurs clés de performance (ICP), aux jalons et au budget établis, en faisant rapport régulièrement au directeur, Intégration et Mise en service.
Établir et tenir à jour la documentation relative aux plans de projet, aux spécifications techniques, aux listes de contrôle de mise en service et aux leçons apprises.
Collaborer avec les architectes technologiques pour garantir des solutions robustes, évolutives et adaptées aux besoins.
Soutenir la gestion des fournisseurs et la supervision de la performance durant les phases de construction et de mise en service.
Favoriser l'amélioration continue en assurant des revues après-projet et en partageant les meilleures pratiques de déploiement de l'automatisation.
Favoriser l'établissement de solides relations de travail avec les intervenants de l'ingénierie, des opérations, de la sécurité, de la cybersécurité et des fonctions TI/OT.

Qualifications/Exigences

Baccalauréat en génie, en automatisation, en informatique ou dans un domaine technique connexe, assorti de plus de 5 ans d'expérience dans la construction et le déploiement de solutions d'automatisation industrielle au sein de grandes organisations OU Diplôme d'études collégiales (ou équivalent) en génie, en automatisation, en informatique ou dans un domaine technique connexe, assorti de plus de 10 ans d'expérience pertinente.
Bilingue français/anglais fluide requis. L'employé(e) sera amené(e) à interagir de manière fluide avec des collègues de nos autres installations à travers et/ou à l'extérieur du Canada, et qui sont généralement incapables de communiquer en français et dont la langue de travail est principalement l'anglais.
Expertise dans la gestion réussie de projets d'automatisation vastes et complexes, de la conception jusqu'à la mise en service.
Connaissance experte des architectures d'automatisation, des normes de sécurité et des exigences de cybersécurité en milieu industriel.
Solides compétences analytiques, organisationnelles et de résolution de problèmes.
Excellentes capacités de collaboration, de gestion des fournisseurs et de mobilisation des intervenants.
Compétences supérieures en communication, tant à l'écrit qu'à l'oral.
Autorisation légale de travailler au Canada requise. Nous ne parrainerons aucun visa de travail pour ce poste.
Doit être âgé de 18 ans ou plus.
Vous devez soumettre votre candidature sur la page carrières au www.careers.gevernova.com pour être considéré.

Caractéristiques Souhaitées

Maîtrise en génie, en automatisation, en informatique ou dans un domaine technique connexe.
Plus de 10 ans d'expérience dans la construction et le déploiement de solutions d'automatisation industrielle dans de grandes organisations.
Expertise en gestion de programmes/projets avec certification officielle (PMP, PRINCE2 ou équivalent) fortement préférée.
Expérience avec l'intégration de systèmes, la sélection de fournisseurs et les équipes de projet interfonctionnelles.
Expérience pratique en mise en service dans les secteurs de l'énergie, de la fabrication ou de l'industrie lourde.
Expérience éprouvée dans l'obtention de résultats au sein d'organisations matricielles et multisites.
Capacité à gérer l'ambiguïté, à mener des projets complexes à terme et à promouvoir les meilleures pratiques.
Apprenant continu avec une passion pour l'excellence opérationnelle et l'innovation.

Essential Responsibilities

Coordinate the build, integration, and commissioning activities for automation projects, ensuring delivery on time and within budget.
Lead and execute the development of project scope, schedules, deliverables, and integration requirements partnering with system integrators, internal technical teams, and site readiness leads to define
Drives all aspects of automation deployment—including installation, testing, validation, and transition to production—ensuring compliance with safety and cyber standards.
Manage risks, issues, and changes throughout the project lifecycle, providing proactive communication and quick resolution.
Track project performance against agreed KPIs, milestones, and budget, reporting regularly to the Director, Integration & Commissioning.
Establish and maintain documentation for project plans, technical specifications, commissioning checklists, and lessons learned.
Collaborate with technology architects to ensure solutions are robust, scalable, and fit for purpose.
Support vendor management and performance oversight during the build and commissioning phases.
Drive continuous improvement by ensuring post-project reviews and sharing best practices for automation deployment.
Foster strong working relationships with stakeholders across engineering, operations, safety, cybersecurity, and IT/OT functions.

Qualifications/Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Automation, Computer Science, or related technical field plus 5+ years of experience building and deploying industrial automation solutions in large organizations. Associate's Degree in Engineering, Automation, Computer Science, or related technical field plus 10+ years of experience building and deploying industrial automation solutions in large organizations.
Bilingual in French and English is mandatory. The employee will be required to interact fluidly with colleagues in our other facilities across and/or outside of Canada, and who are generally unable to communicate in French and whose language at work is predominantly English.
Expert in successfully managing large, complex automation projects from design through commissioning.
Expert knowledge in automation architectures, safety standards, and cybersecurity requirements in industrial settings.
Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
Excellent collaboration, vendor management, and stakeholder engagement abilities.
Superior communication skills, both written and verbal.

jobs.title: Director, Treasury Finance
jobs.description:
The primary responsibility of the Director is to lead Treasury Finance activities relating to corporate finance strategy, funding strategy, capital structure management, liability management, banking relationships, and capital markets execution. The Director serves as a key advisor to Treasury leadership and business partners on matters relating to funding, leverage, capital deployment, liquidity resources, and balance sheet optimization.

The role is accountable for developing and executing funding strategies that support Manulife's financial objectives while maintaining appropriate financial flexibility, regulatory capital levels, liquidity resources, and access to global capital markets. You will also be responsible for maintaining strong relationships with banking partners, investors, rating agencies, and advisors, while ensuring treasury financing activities are executed efficiently, effectively, and in accordance with approved governance frameworks.

Position Responsibilities

Act as Treasury Finance advisor with an overall mandate to support Treasury leadership, Capital Management, Investor Relations, Treasury Operations, Manulife Bank and other stakeholders through strategic analysis, funding recommendations, and corporate finance expertise.
Develop recommendations regarding capital structure, leverage, funding strategy, refinancing, capital deployment, and balance sheet optimization to support the Company's financial objectives.
Lead the development and ongoing assessment of funding strategies, incorporating market conditions, regulatory and rating agency considerations, funding requirements, investor demand, and competitive developments.
Serve as the primary Treasury Finance lead for debt issuances, liability management transactions, wholesale funding programs, share repurchase initiatives, and other treasury-related financing activities, including strategy, analysis, execution and post-transaction review.
Lead and manage Treasury-owned banking relationships, including revolving credit facilities, letters of credit and other financing arrangements, and negotiate pricing, terms, capacity, documentation and service levels.
Lead complex commercial negotiations with banking partners, dealers, investors, legal counsel and other external stakeholders. Review, analyze and negotiate credit agreements, underwriting agreements, term sheets, offering documents, trust indentures and other financing-related documentation.
Support and influence strategic decision-making through the preparation of financial analysis, funding plans, capital structure assessments, Board materials, executive presentations and other management reporting.
Lead strategic initiatives impacting Treasury Finance, including evaluating alternatives, assessing risks and opportunities, coordinating stakeholders and supporting implementation.
Maintain relationships with banking partners, fixed income investors, rating agencies and other market participants to monitor trends, identify opportunities and support continued access to capital.
Ensure funding instruments remain compliant with contractual, regulatory, reporting and governance requirements, including ongoing monitoring of covenants, obligations and maturity profiles.
Identify and implement process improvements related to treasury strategy, funding activities, governance, reporting, controls and transaction execution.
Responsible for coaching, mentoring and development of staff supporting Treasury Finance activities.

Required Qualifications

Post-secondary education in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration or a related discipline and/or a minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in treasury, corporate finance, capital markets, commercial banking, investment banking, insurance finance or a related field.
Strong knowledge of corporate finance, capital structure management, leverage analysis, capital allocation, liquidity management and balance sheet optimization.
Strong understanding of debt and equity capital markets, funding strategies, banking products, credit facilities and liability management activities.
Experience executing complex financing transactions and negotiating commercial arrangements with financial institutions and other counterparties.
Ability to review, understand and negotiate financing documentation, including credit agreements, underwriting agreements, term sheets, offering documents and related contracts.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to evaluate strategic alternatives and develop actionable recommendations.
Demonstrated ability to build and maintain strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
Thorough understanding of risk management, governance and controls as they relate to treasury and financing activities.
Excellent communication, presentation and influencing skills, including the ability to work effectively with senior management and executive stakeholders.
Strong project management, organizational and stakeholder coordination skills.
Demonstrated leadership capabilities with experience managing change, developing talent and fostering high-performing teams.
Ability to manage multiple priorities, work under pressure and adapt to changing business requirements.
Capital markets, commercial banking, investment banking, treasury or corporate finance experience within a financial institution is considered a strong asset.

jobs.description:

Description

Why This Role Exists

Creative is one of the biggest levers in scaling our clients’ paid media performance.

We’re looking for a Head of Creative Strategy to build the people, systems, and operating model that turn creative into a repeatable performance advantage across our portfolio, both in social and display networks.

You’ll lead Creative Strategy and oversee Creative Execution through the Performance Creative Manager, ensuring strategy, production, performance, and learning operate as one connected system.

Key Responsibilities

Who We Are

Clever Digital Marketing is a performance marketing agency helping large home improvement companies across the US and Canada grow through Paid Social, Paid Search, CRO, and strategic advising.

We manage a large portfolio of accounts, an in-house creative team, and significant monthly ad spend. As we scale, we're building a stronger creative-strategy function to help clients find new creative winners — and to turn one-off learnings into repeatable systems that compound across every account.

Skills, Knowledge And Expertise

What You'll Do

Build and lead CDM’s Creative Strategy function, defining the methodologies, standards, and operating system behind how we research, ideate, test, learn, and scale creative.
Manage Senior Creative Strategists and the Performance Creative Manager.
Build systems that turn customer, market, and performance data into actionable creative direction.
Create a cross-account learning system so wins, losses, hypotheses, and insights compound across the portfolio.
Set and maintain the strategic and creative quality bar across the department, regularly reviewing work and challenging thinking.
Ensure Creative Strategy and Creative Execution scale together with the right quality, capacity, velocity, prioritization, and feedback loops.
Build testing frameworks, briefing standards, and learning loops that improve creative performance and decision-making.
Build training, playbooks, and frameworks that improve creative thinking across Media Buyers and Creative.
Build AI-enabled workflows that improve research, analysis, creative intelligence, and decision-making.
Partner closely with Paid Social, CRO, Paid Search, Client Success, and leadership.
Ensure creative decisions are connected to business outcomes such as Creative Win Rate, CPL, CPS/CPD, lead quality, COM, and account growth.
Hire and develop future Creative Strategy talent.

What We’re Looking For

Proven experience leading creative strategy or performance creative.
Experience building or scaling a team, department, or operating system.
Strong performance-marketing and commercial understanding.
Strong direct-response and consumer-psychology background.
Experience building creative testing frameworks, learning systems, and standards.
Experience managing strategists and/or creative-production teams.
Strong cross-functional leadership and ability to drive adoption.
Strong understanding of AI and how to apply it across a team, not just individually.
Able to operate at portfolio level while still maintaining a strong account-level creative quality bar.
Clear, decisive communicator who can simplify complexity and turn strategy into action.

Nice to Have

Lead generation or high-ticket services experience.
Home improvement experience.
CRO and landing-page testing familiarity.
UGC, founder-led, or spokesperson-led creative experience.
Hands-on familiarity with editing or design tools.

What Success Looks Like

CDM consistently introduces genuinely new creative ideas instead of recycling the same concepts and formats.
Creative iterations are more deliberate, strategic, and evidence-based.
Media Buyers and editors produce stronger briefs and creative recommendations on their own.
Learnings are captured, shared, and applied across accounts.
AI-supported research and creative workflows are adopted department-wide.
CDM has a repeatable creative-strategy engine that gets stronger with every test.

Benefits

Benefits of Working at CDM

Competitive base salary + performance-based bonuses
Flexible remote work environment with option for in-person collaboration (Vaughan, ON)
Group Benefits - Medical, Dental, Vision, RRSP/401k Plan w/matching, more.
Company-provided MacBook computer
Home office budget and Clever merch delivery to get you started
Work Abroad Policy: Need a new working environment? Our work abroad policy supports this!
The chance to shape and grow a high-performing Client Success team
A culture of performance and respect where the best work happens with extreme ownership and accountability meets collaboration.

McCann is seeking a Strategy Director, Performance & Creative Integration to lead strategies that connect brand building, creative ideas and measurable business outcomes. Rooted in our Truth Well Told ethos, you will turn business, audience and cultural insight into clear strategic direction, then work with creative, media, analytics, CRM and commerce partners to bring that direction to life. You will lead client relationships, guide strategists and help grow our clients and the agency.

What you will do:

Lead strategy and creative development

Understand client business and marketing problems. Draw on consumer, cultural, category, media and performance data to find meaningful truths and opportunities.
Develop integrated strategies that connect brand objectives, customer needs, acquisition and measurable business results.
Write clear briefs and strategic narratives that inspire original creative work across channels and customer journeys.
Partner with Creative and Business Leadership to develop ideas, give constructive feedback and carry the strategic story from opportunity through execution and impact.
Stay close to digital behaviour and social conversation. Explain what people do and why it matters for the work.

Connect performance and creative

Bring creative, media, analytics, CRM and commerce teams together around shared audience insight, campaign objectives and measurement.
Shape demand generation, lead generation, customer acquisition and digital commerce strategies where they serve the client’s business.
Use campaign results to identify creative opportunities, guide versioning and personalization, and recommend what to test next.
Develop practical approaches to testing and iteration, including dynamic creative optimization where appropriate.

Lead clients and the team

Present persuasive strategic recommendations and lead confident, productive conversations with clients and internal teams.
Bring proactive thinking to client relationships, new business opportunities and agency growth.
Mentor strategists, adapt your coaching to their needs and give clear feedback that helps people and the work grow.

What you bring

At least eight years of relevant strategy experience, including agency experience and leadership of client work.
A record of turning insight into strong creative work and clear business outcomes.
Working knowledge of media, audience strategy, analytics and measurement, with experience in performance marketing, lead generation, CRM, customer acquisition or digital commerce.
The ability to decide which data matters, explain what it means and translate it into creative direction.
Strong writing, storytelling, presentation and client leadership skills.
Curiosity about culture and digital behaviour, sound judgment, and an open approach to collaboration and feedback.
Experience guiding or managing strategists and helping multidisciplinary teams work together.

Your strategies will help clients build their brands and achieve measurable business results. Teams will use your direction to create connected work, learn from its performance and improve what comes next. Job Information

J ob Title: Director, Cloud Platform Services

Job Requisition ID: 87808

Ministry: Technology & Innovation

Location: Edmonton or Calgary

Full or Part-Time: Full Time

Hours of Work: 36.25 hours per week

Permanent/Temporary/Wage: Permanent

Scope: Open Competition

Closing Date: November 3, 2026

Classification: Management, Senior Manager Zone 2

Salary: $5,139.30 to $6,526.16 /bi-weekly ($134,135 - $170,332/year)

The Alberta Public Service works to build a stronger province for current and future generations. We make a difference in the lives of Albertans through rewarding and diverse career opportunities.

Technology and Innovation is responsible for making innovation and technology the driving force behind Alberta’s economic growth and diversification. To learn more about us, please visit: https://www.alberta.ca/technology-and-innovation.aspx .

The passionate and solutions focused people that we hire help us to drive vital programs and services that affect Albertans. Whatever your position is here, you will be a part of something great. Join us!

Role Responsibilities

Lead The Cloud. Enable What’s Next.

As Director, Cloud Platform, you will provide strategic leadership for the Government of Alberta’s cloud and digital platform services, enabling secure, scalable, reliable, and modern technology solutions across government. You will set the vision, priorities, and outcomes for a portfolio spanning cloud platforms, identity and authentication, messaging, web hosting, and related foundational services.

Reporting to the Executive Director, Business Technology Operations, you will lead a diverse team and work closely with senior leaders across IMT, business partners, and technology vendors to align services with government priorities, client needs, security and risk requirements, and fiscal and contractual obligations. You will foster a collaborative, agile, and innovative culture while ensuring service availability, continuity, and operational excellence.

Responsibilities

Some of the responsibilities of this position include, but are not limited to:

Service/Platform Ownership

Lead the strategy, delivery, and lifecycle management of key technology services and platforms. Manage resources, budgets, contracts, vendors, and service agreements. Engage senior business leaders to align services with ministry priorities and client needs. Ensure services meet applicable security, privacy, legal, information management, and architectural standards. Oversee service performance, escalations, change management, and continuous improvement.

Leadership, Planning and Implementation

Lead workforce, financial, and operational planning to deliver effective technology services. Align priorities and resources across teams and stakeholders. Direct implementation of new solutions, projects, and services. Monitor performance, address issues, and report on progress and outcomes.

Service Level Management

Ensure services meet client and stakeholder needs and agreed service levels. Monitor service performance and drive improvements in service delivery. Contribute to GoA-wide service standards and practices.

Architecture and Standards

Provide direction on technology, architecture, standards, and processes across the portfolio. Ensure solutions align with GoA standards, approved environments, and business requirements. Advance modernization, innovation, and integration of technology services.

Risk Management

Identify, assess, and mitigate risks affecting services and initiatives. Provide leadership on risks related to cost, schedule, quality, security, and technical performance. Collaborate with Cybersecurity and other partners to address technology and security risks.

Unit Leadership and Operations

Develop and execute operational plans aligned with ministry and GoA priorities. Lead staffing, performance, workforce planning, and employee development. Oversee financial management, procurement, contracts, vendors, and service agreements. Foster a collaborative, inclusive, agile, and innovative workplace culture. Oversee executive briefings, correspondence, and other decision-support materials.

Branch and Division Leadership

Provide strategic advice and recommendations to executive leaders. Report on branch plans, performance, and outcomes to support division and ministry priorities. Collaborate across branches, divisions, and departments to advance shared priorities and service delivery. Drive collaboration, innovation, efficiency, and continuous improvement. Serve as Acting Executive Director, as required.

AI Stewardship

This role is designed with an AI-first mindset, requiring the successful candidate to leverage AI-powered tools and capabilities to strengthen stakeholder engagement through automated insights, personalized communications, and enhanced collaboration; create tailored, high-impact materials that align with stakeholder needs using AI-assisted content generation and feedback analysis; and develop, monitor, and refine key performance indicators.

To Be Successful In This Position You Will Demonstrate

Exceptional communication, consultation, and engagement skills, with the ability to adapt approaches for diverse audiences.
Strong political acumen and sensitivity, with the ability to navigate complex and sensitive situations effectively.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to assess complex and competing issues and develop practical recommendations.
Expertise in building productive relationships across the ministry, Government of Alberta, partner organizations, and key stakeholders.
Experience in leading and managing a variety of projects and processes and delivering high quality results within established timelines.
Embraces technology and data by using AI-powered tools and performance metrics to inform strategy, measure success, and optimize delivery.

The Job Description is provided for further details on this position.

APS Competencies

Competencies are behaviors that are essential to reach our goals in serving Albertans. We encourage you to have an in depth understanding of the competencies that are required for this opportunity and to be prepared to demonstrate them during the recruitment process.

Some Of The Competencies Critical For This Position Are

Systems Thinking: You will consider how work completed can impact various other groups/projects inside and outside the Alberta Public Service.
Agility: Proactively incorporates change into processes. Creates opportunities for improvement. Is aware of and adapts to changing priorities. Remains objective under pressure and supports others to manage their emotions. Proactively explains impact of change on roles and integrates change in existing work. Readily adapts plans and practices.
Develop self and others: A commitment to lifelong learning and the desire to invest in the development of the long-term capability of yourself and others.
Build Collaborative Environments: Collaborates across functional areas and proactively addresses conflict. Encourages broad thinking on projects and works to eliminate barriers to progress. Facilitates communication and collaboration. Anticipates and reduces conflict at the outset. Credits others and gets talent recognized. Promotes collaboration and commitment.
Develop Networks: Leverages relationships to build input and perspective. Looks broadly to engage stakeholders. Open to perspectives towards long-term goals. Actively seeks input into change initiatives. Maintains stakeholder relationships.
Creative Problem Solving: Engages the community and resources at hand to address issues. Engages perspective to seek root causes. Finds ways to improve complex systems. Employs resources from other areas to solve problems. Engages others and encourages debate and idea generation to solve problems while addressing risks.
Drive for Results: You will work with your team to set goals and priorities and deliver outcomes that are consistent with the department's direction.

Qualifications

Requirements:

University graduation in a related field such as Computer Sciences, Information Technology or other Technology related disciplines.
Minimum of 7 years of experience in developing and implementing new IT services and solutions in a cloud-based service environment
Experience in a management/leadership position leading high performing technical teams.
Experience in project management processes and methodologies like waterfall and agile.
Strong IT technical expertise and the ability to guide operations and develop strategic roadmaps for enterprise technology services.

Equivalencies

1 year of education for 1 year of experience; or
1 year of experience for 1 year of education

Experience with IT security, hardware and software, business change, and project management methodologies, including ITIL, COBIT, and PMBOK.
Expertise in Agile methodologies, Lean practices, and Service Design.
Leadership experience in leading teams through innovation, transformation, and organizational change.
Knowledge of government and ministry priorities and the ability to translate them into operational plans and strategic decisions.
Experience in assessing new opportunities and performing necessary due diligence around technical, operational and financial impacts.
Experience working with Identity Access Management, M365 implementations, and Cloud Landing Zone environments.

jobs.title: Chief Technology Officer
jobs.description:
BE AT THE FOREFRONT OF CANADA'S CLEAN ENERGY TRANSFORMATION.

Salient Energy Inc. is advancing the next generation of safe, sustainable energy storage technology. Our zinc-ion batteries are designed to accelerate the global shift toward renewable power, providing a safer, more cost-effective, and scalable alternative to lithium-ion.

We're looking for a results-driven, technically savvy Chief Technology Officer who understands the pace, complexity, and challenges of a startup environment and brings a genuine passion for clean tech energy. As we move into the heart of commercialization, this leader will drive the continued advancement of our zinc-ion battery platform, aligning technology, execution, and team leadership to support scale, market readiness, and commercial success.

THE ROLE

Reporting to the CEO, the Chief Technology Officer will provide strategic and hands-on leadership across Salient Energy's technology function at a critical stage in the company's growth, balancing deep technical expertise with the operational and commercial oversight needed to advance through commercialization.

Leading the RCD, Cell Development, and Quality teams, the CTO will align technical direction, cross-functional execution, and team capability to support scale, certification, market readiness, and accelerated commercial success. As a member of the executive team, this leader will foster a strong, accountable, and collaborative culture while also serving as a trusted technical voice with the Board, investors, and external partners.

What You Will Do

Lead Salient's technology function by providing strategic and technical leadership across RCD, Cell Development, and Quality.
Define and deliver product specifications, technical priorities, and performance metrics aligned with Salient's technology roadmap and TRL targets.
Support the successful advancement of Salient's battery platform through commercialization, including readiness for scale, certification, and market adoption.
Ensure required product and process certifications, including UL and CSA standards, are achieved.
Represent Salient externally as a credible technical leader with the Board, investors, partners, and at relevant industry and technical forums.

Your Skills, Education & Experience

Education & Technical Depth

PhD in Chemistry, Chemical or Mechanical Engineering, or Materials Science/Engineering.
Deep expertise in battery chemistry, electrochemistry, and testing processes, supported by 10+ years in a chemistry lab environment.
Experience with advanced battery materials and ion transport mechanisms is considered an asset.

Product Development & Commercialization

8-10 years leading development projects, with demonstrated experience bringing new products to market.
Proven ability to align technical priorities with commercialization milestones, performance goals, and market needs.

Leadership Profile

Strategic & Commercial Acumen - able to connect technical direction to commercialization, scale, and business goals.
Technical & Operational Leadership - brings rigor, focus, and accountability across complex technical programs.
People & Stakeholder Influence - builds strong teams and communicates credibly with employees, executives, investors, and partners.

THE IDEAL CANDIDATE

The ideal candidate brings the technical depth and scientific credibility expected of a CTO, along with the leadership, operational oversight, and commercial mindset needed to advance Salient's technology through commercialization. While technical capability is essential, success in this role will depend on the ability to translate innovation into practical commercial application, aligning technical priorities with business objectives, supporting teams with clarity and accountability, and sustaining momentum toward scale, market readiness, and performance. This leader will understand how to balance thoughtful refinement and continuous innovation with the urgency required to meet business goals and move the product forward.

Excellent communication skills, with the ability to mentor teams and translate complex technical concepts into clear business value.

WHY SALIENT?

At Salient, you'll work alongside a team of scientists, engineers, and innovators who are deeply committed to building a safer, cleaner energy future. We believe the best ideas come from curiosity, collaboration, and continuous learning. As CTO, you will play a defining leadership role in shaping our technology strategy, strengthening our technical organization, and advancing our products toward market adoption. Your work will directly influence how Salient scales its zinc-ion platform and delivers meaningful impact in one of the world's most important sectors: clean energy storage.

We offer a competitive salary and a collegiate, supportive, and diverse team environment. Here, you'll have the opportunity to lead meaningful innovation, develop exceptional teams, and help build a technology company positioned to make a real difference.

jobs.title: Director of Finance
jobs.description:
The Nova Scotia Nursing and Midwifery Regulator
(NSNMR) protects the public by regulating licensed practical nurses, registered nurses, registered psychiatric nurses, nurse practitioners, and registered midwives across Nova Scotia.

As the largest health profession regulator in Atlantic Canada, NSNMR is entering a pivotal stage in its evolution. Building on the transition to the Regulated Health Professions Act and the integration of nursing and midwifery regulation, the organization is focused on strengthening its operational foundations, modernizing systems and processes, advancing data-informed decision making, and positioning itself as a leading regulator within the region.

To support this important work, NSNMR is seeking a Director of Finance
.

This is an exceptional opportunity for a strategic and collaborative finance leader to contribute to an organization dedicated to public protection and regulatory excellence. The Director of Finance will help guide the organization's long-term financial sustainability while providing the financial insight, stewardship, and leadership required to support informed decision-making, effective governance, and organizational success.

The Role

Reporting to the Senior Director, Corporate Services, the Director of Finance provides leadership and oversight for NSNMR's financial operations, planning, reporting, audit, risk management, and internal controls. As a member of the leadership team, the Director serves as a trusted advisor to senior leadership and the Board, providing strategic financial guidance that supports effective decision-making, strong governance, and long-term organizational sustainability. Working closely with leaders across the organization, the Director helps ensure financial resources are aligned with strategic priorities and supports a culture of accountability, stewardship, and continuous improvement.

Key Responsibilities

Leading NSNMR's financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, and reporting processes to support organizational priorities and long-term sustainability.
Providing strategic financial advice and analysis to support executive and Board decision-making, governance, and resource allocation.
Overseeing all financial operations, including accounting, payroll, investments, cash management, audit, and financial reporting.
Ensuring effective financial controls, compliance practices, and risk management frameworks are in place to safeguard organizational resources.
Supporting organizational planning and performance by translating financial information into meaningful insights for leaders across the organization.
Building and maintaining productive relationships with the Board, auditors, financial institutions, and other external partners.
Leading and developing the finance team while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

Ideal Candidate Profile

As the ideal candidate, you are a strategic and accomplished finance leader with a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation and progressive experience leading finance functions within complex organizations. You bring expertise in financial planning and analysis, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, audit, risk management, and internal controls, along with experience providing financial advice and insight to senior leaders and Boards.

You combine strong financial stewardship with sound business judgment and a collaborative leadership style. Comfortable navigating complexity and change, you use financial insight to support decision-making, long-term planning, and organizational sustainability.

An effective communicator and relationship builder, you excel at translating complex financial information into practical insights and building trusted partnerships with colleagues, executives, Board members, and external stakeholders. Experience in a regulated, healthcare, public sector, or not-for-profit environment would be considered an asset.

How to Apply

If you are interested in pursuing this exciting opportunity, please apply by visiting our website https://www.kbrs.ca/Career/17866390385010000008wjg. For more information or to ask any questions, please contact Daniella Sam at dsam@kbrs.ca or Erin MacDonald at emacdonald@kbrs.ca .

jobs.description:
Serv, a global executive recruitment partner, is hiring on behalf of our client Martell Ventures for a Chief Technology Officer.

Join the Team:
The Martell Group exists to build people, brands, and ventures that create meaningful impact. Founded by serial entrepreneur and investor Dan Martell, we combine audience, operators, and execution to launch and scale products in Media, B2B SaaS, and AI.

Martell Ventures is a software and AI company that happens to have two services companies in it. Dan is also an investor in companies like Udemy, Intercom, and Unbounce. Our values: Build the people. Be the example. Simple scales.

For more information, visit: https://www.danmartell.com/
Why you shouldn't work here: Radical Transparency from our CEO

Position Responsibilities:
Martell Ventures is looking for a highly technical builder and strategic thinker to lead engineering excellence across its growing portfolio of businesses.

This is not a traditional CTO role focused solely on executive oversight. We need someone who can think strategically, challenge assumptions, and get directly involved in the technical work when it matters most.

You will be the technical authority across the Ventures portfolio, helping companies build better products, solve complex engineering challenges, strengthen technical teams, and move faster with modern AI and agentic development.

You'll work closely with Dan Martell, portfolio business leaders, and experienced technology advisors to turn ambitious ideas into practical, scalable solutions.

A significant part of your mandate will be establishing Martell Ventures' technical presence in Waterloo, building a strong local engineering community, and creating the standards that enable our portfolio companies to scale.

This is an opportunity to shape how multiple businesses build, operate, and grow while remaining close to the technology itself.

This role includes:
Technical Strategy & Architecture
Evaluate the technical infrastructure, architecture, codebases, and engineering practices across portfolio companies, identifying opportunities to improve quality, security, scalability, and performance.
Work directly with engineering teams to diagnose technical challenges, improve architecture, and implement practical solutions.
Establish consistent engineering standards, shared development practices, frameworks, and tooling across the portfolio.
Drive adoption of modern AI and agentic development practices to improve engineering speed, efficiency, and product delivery.
Ensure portfolio companies maintain appropriate technical infrastructure, security practices, backups, and operational resilience.
Help portfolio leaders understand technical risks, opportunities, and priorities so they can make informed business decisions.
Support technical readiness for future acquisitions, investment opportunities, and potential exits.

Building & Developing Technical Talent
Establish and grow Martell Ventures' technical presence in Kitchener-Waterloo.
Help recruit, assess, and develop exceptional engineering talent across the portfolio.
Partner with portfolio business leaders on technical hiring decisions, including engineering leads and senior technical positions.
Provide technical guidance and mentorship to portfolio engineering leaders while maintaining a dotted-line relationship with those leaders.
Establish consistent technical practices, knowledge-sharing, and training opportunities across portfolio teams.
Develop relationships with the University of Waterloo, Communitech, and the broader Waterloo technology ecosystem to build a sustainable talent pipeline.
Collaborate with Waterloo-based technology advisors Michael Litt and Marcelo Cortes to strengthen the group's engineering capabilities and local network.

Product Development & Execution
Translate ambitious business ideas into practical technical plans with clear priorities, realistic timelines, and measurable outcomes.
Provide hands-on technical support when portfolio companies face complex engineering challenges or execution bottlenecks.
Evaluate build-versus-buy decisions and help prioritize technical investments based on business value.
Support engineering teams in delivering reliable, scalable products that meet customer needs.
Identify opportunities to share technical capabilities, infrastructure, and resources across portfolio businesses.
Balance long-term technical architecture with the immediate needs of fast-moving businesses.

Strategic Partnership & Leadership
Serve as a trusted technical thought partner to Dan Martell and the Ventures leadership team.
Bring independent technical judgment, including the confidence to challenge ideas, push back on unrealistic commitments, and recommend alternative approaches.
Help establish a culture of technical excellence, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Work across multiple businesses and priorities while maintaining a clear focus on the highest-impact opportunities.
Communicate technical decisions, risks, and progress clearly to both technical and nontechnical stakeholders.
Lead by example through a combination of strategic thinking, practical execution, and strong technical credibility.

Qualifications
We are looking for someone with exceptional technical depth, strong product judgment, and the ability to build in fast-moving environments.
You may have held a CTO or VP of Engineering position, or you may be an exceptional Staff Engineer, Principal Engineer, or technical founder ready to take on broader responsibility.

What matters most is your ability to solve difficult technical problems, raise engineering standards, and build products that work.
Deep hands-on experience in software engineering, systems architecture, and building scalable production applications.
Recent, practical experience developing with modern AI technologies, LLMs, agents, and agentic development tools.
Demonstrated ability to evaluate existing software architecture, identify technical weaknesses, and implement effective solutions.
Strong technical credibility and the ability to work directly with experienced engineers on complex technical challenges.
Experience building and shipping software products in startup, scale-up, or similarly fast-moving environments.
Strong product and business judgment, with an understanding of how technical decisions affect customers, revenue, and growth.
Experience assessing engineering talent, making technical hiring decisions, and helping build high-performing teams.
Ability to balance technical quality with speed, pragmatism, and commercial priorities.
Confidence working with strong founder personalities and challenging ideas when necessary.
Strong communication skills, with the ability to translate complex technical concepts into clear business recommendations.
High ownership, adaptability, and comfort operating across multiple businesses with changing priorities.
Based in, or willing to relocate to, Kitchener-Waterloo and work in person full-time.

Nice-to-Haves
Previous experience as a CTO, technical co-founder, VP of Engineering, or senior technical leader.
Experience supporting multiple products, portfolio companies, or venture-backed businesses.
Experience building or scaling an engineering function from an early stage.
Involvement in a successful company exit or technical due diligence process.
Existing connections within the Waterloo technology ecosystem, including the University of Waterloo or Communitech.
Experience establishing engineering standards and shared infrastructure across multiple teams.

Our Dream Teammate Is Someone Who:
Is a builder at heart and genuinely enjoys getting into the technical details.
Is excited by the pace of change in AI and is actively experimenting with emerging tools and technologies.
Can move comfortably between high-level strategy and hands-on execution.
Knows when to challenge an idea, when to simplify a solution, and when to move quickly.
Has strong technical opinions but remains open to learning and feedback.
Thrives in entrepreneurial environments where priorities evolve and ownership matters.
Is proactive and accountable.
Thinks strategically and executes consistently.
Communicates with clarity and confidence.
Brings a positive, growth-oriented mindset.
Is highly organized and dependable.
Cares deeply about building great products and developing great people.

Hiring Process
We take our hiring process seriously and evaluate candidates based on both capability and culture fit. Our goal is to ensure you step into a role where you feel genuinely excited and fulfilled. That's important for you, and it's equally important for us.

Below is a snapshot of what you can expect throughout our hiring process.

Please note that steps may vary slightly depending on the position.

Leadership and culture-fit conversation with Martell Ventures.
Technical evaluation with members of the Martell Ventures technical leadership or advisory network.
Final-stage conversations with key stakeholders.

Location
Kitchener-Waterloo, Ontario, Canada

This is a full-time, in-person position. The CTO will play a central role in establishing and leading Martell Ventures' Waterloo technical hub.

Compensation
$150,000- $250,000 CAD base, based on experience.

The opportunity also includes a proposed portfolio-level phantom equity component designed to align long-term incentives with the performance and success of the Ventures portfolio. Final terms are subject to confirmation.

Position:
                   Director of Finance and Administration
Location:
                  Martin Luther University College, Waterloo, Ontario

1 - 2 roles
