jobs.description:
University Hospital Foundation

The University Hospital Foundation is dedicated to a powerful, singular purpose: to continuously seek, inspire and support bold solutions to seemingly insurmountable challenges and ignite new discoveries in health. Responsible for raising and managing funds to advance innovation in prevention, research and patient care, the Foundation strives to transform and redefine health in the Edmonton area, throughout Alberta and around the world so everyone can live a longer, healthier life.

In the past ten years, generous donations from individuals and our corporate and strategic partners have contributed nearly $220 million to advance world-leading patient care at the University of Alberta Hospital, Mazankowski Alberta Heart Institute, and Kaye Edmonton Clinic, as well as groundbreaking research at the University of Alberta.

As an outcome-focused organization, UHF offers a flexible hybrid working environment. To learn more about the University Hospital Foundation, visit www.GiveToUHF.ca and if you have a keen interest in being a part of the future of healthcare in Alberta, please consider applying today!

The Opportunity

As a key member of the Executive Leadership Team (ELT) and reporting to the President & CEO, the Chief Catalyst, Enabling Systems and Chief Financial Officer. plays a critical role in developing and implementing the business and financial strategy and enabling systems strategy of the University Hospital Foundation (the Foundation). This position is integral to organizational success in support of the mission, vision, values, and goals of the Foundation.

This role serves as a critical advisor to the President & CEO, the Executive Leadership team and support to the Board of Trustees including their supporting committees.

This role leads the Finance, People & Technology Portfolio and manages a diverse department of professionals who are passionate about contributing to the Foundation’s mission through providing the most efficient and effective operational support. This role is a pivotal member of the leadership team that embraces change as an opportunity to learn and is constantly looking for ways to improve the level of service to internal and external customers.

Key accountabilities include financial and operational activities in the areas of finance & investments, accountability of funded projects, donation services, fund management and distributions, information technology & management, people practices, legal & risk management, and facilities & property management.

Key Responsibilities

The responsibilities of this role include, but are not limited to:

Provide strategic management and oversight to the People, Finance and Technology teams to align with UHF’s long-term strategy to support multiple stakeholders including donors and funding recipients.
Lead financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, audit, compliance, investment oversight, and stewardship of donor funds.
Support the President & CEO, Executive Leadership Team, and Board committees with clear, timely, and strategic advice.
Champion innovation and continuous improvement by modernizing systems, strengthening operational capacity, and encouraging new ways of working.
Advance the Foundation’s technology strategy and roadmap, using technology to improve processes, productivity, decision-making, and organizational scalability.
Ensure strong governance, risk management, legal, privacy, procurement, and compliance practices.
Build and lead a collaborative, customer-centric team that provides excellent service to internal and external stakeholders.
Foster trusted relationships with donors, partners, board members, auditors, investment managers, government representatives, and health-system stakeholders.
Contribute to a culture that is accountable, courageous, innovative, collaborative, and focused on measurable impact.

Qualifications and Experience

The ideal candidate is an innovative, experienced executive financial and operational leader with the ability to translate strategy into effective systems, structures, and results.

They will bring a strong track record in financial stewardship, people leadership, technology-enabled transformation, risk management, and organizational capacity building. Experience in a complex not-for-profit, charitable, healthcare, post-secondary, public-sector, or similarly mission-driven environment would be considered an asset.

Education & Experience

Preferred qualifications include:

A professional accounting designation, such as CPA, or equivalent senior financial leadership experience.
A post-secondary degree in business, finance, human resources, or a related discipline; an MBA or relevant graduate degree would be an asset.
Significant senior financial leadership experience, including experience in a CFO or comparable executive role.
Proven experience leading teams through growth, change, transformation, or modernization.
Strong knowledge of financial planning, investment oversight, fund accounting, reporting, compliance, and risk management.
Experience working with a Board of Directors or Board of Trustees and supporting board-level committees.
Demonstrated expertise in leveraging data, systems, and technology to drive organizational performance, inform strategic decision-making, and advance enterprise priorities.

Behavioral Competencies and Personal Attributes

Strategic, financially astute, and future-focused.
Innovative and curious, with a willingness to challenge the status quo and explore better ways to deliver impact.
Collaborative, approachable, and able to build trust across teams, partners, and stakeholders.
A clear communicator who can make complex financial and operational matters understandable to non-financial audiences.
Customer-centric, service-oriented, and committed to supporting both internal teams and external partners.
Courageous, accountable, and comfortable leading through ambiguity and change.
A values-driven leader who operates with integrity, sound judgment, and humility.

Measurements of Success Within the First Year

Success In The First Year Will Include

Building trusted relationships with the Board of Trustees, President & CEO, Executive Leadership Team, direct reports, and key external stakeholders.
Establishing clear priorities, accountabilities, and decision-making practices across the enabling systems portfolio
Strengthening finance, people, technology, and operational systems to support improved service, efficiency, and scalability.

Supporting strategic partnerships across the health, life sciences, wellness, philanthropic, and public-sector ecosystems.
Contributing meaningfully to organizational priorities, including leadership development, inclusion, operational excellence, and long-term sustainability.

Clio is at an inflection point. The Director of Enterprise Revenue Operations will be the single operational owner responsible for scaling and maturing our Enterprise GTM motion end-to-end — from Sales Operations through to Customer Success operations — ensuring our Enterprise business runs with the speed, precision, and sophistication that our customers and growth targets demand.

jobs.title: Director, Sponsor Analytics
jobs.description:
The Director, Sponsor Analytics will lead the Sponsor Analytics function within Group Benefits, with primary accountability for delivering meaningful, actionable insights and reporting to plan sponsors, Distribution partners and internal business leaders.

The Director will shape the strategy and evolution of sponsor reporting and analytics, ensuring sponsors have access to trusted, relevant and increasingly sophisticated insights to better understand their benefits programs, member populations and key areas of opportunity. Through improved use of data and insights, the role will support informed decisions that contribute to healthier outcomes and the health and well-being of Canadians.

The Director will also lead and contribute to broader analytics initiatives across Group Benefits where the team’s capabilities, data and expertise can create value, including strategic business priorities, portfolio analytics, operational insights, customer and member analytics, and emerging analytical needs.

Working closely with Plan Sponsor Services, Distribution, Product, Operations, Data and Technology partners, the Director will lead the development and evolution of standardized and customized reporting, self-service analytics, data products and insights. The role will balance evolving sponsor and business needs with scalable solutions, strong data governance, appropriate data protection and a focus on business value and customer outcomes.

The Director will lead and develop a high-performing analytics team, establishing clear priorities, strengthening analytical capabilities and fostering a culture focused on meaningful outcomes for sponsors and the broader Group Benefits business.

Position Responsibilities

Lead the Sponsor Analytics function and team. Establish priorities and a roadmap aligned with the Group Benefits sponsor reporting and analytics strategy, while coaching and developing a collaborative, accountable and high-performing team.
Partner with plan sponsors, Distribution and business leaders. Translate sponsor and business needs into meaningful reporting, analytics and insights, balancing individual requests with strategic priorities and scalable solutions.
Advance the sponsor reporting strategy. Evolve traditional reporting toward proactive, insight-driven analytics that help sponsors understand their benefits programs, emerging trends and opportunities for action.
Lead sponsor-facing analytics products and reporting. Oversee standardized and customized reporting, dashboards and self-service capabilities, ensuring a consistent and effective sponsor experience.
Use analytics to improve outcomes for sponsors and members. Identify trends, opportunities and insights that support informed benefits decisions and contribute to improving the health and well-being of Canadians.
Support broader Group Benefits analytics priorities. Apply the team’s capabilities and expertise to strategic business questions across product, customer, member, portfolio and operational analytics.
Identify emerging analytical opportunities. Partner with business leaders to frame questions, assess available data, develop analytical approaches and translate findings into actionable recommendations.
Strengthen data storytelling. Translate complex information into clear, relevant and actionable insights for sponsors, Distribution partners and senior business leaders.
Drive consistency, efficiency and automation. Simplify reporting and analytical processes, reduce manual effort and create reusable capabilities that scale across Group Benefits.
Advance the analytics data ecosystem. Partner with Data and Technology teams to establish the data, platforms and capabilities required for reliable, timely and increasingly sophisticated analytics.
Champion data quality, governance and protection. Ensure reporting and analytical products use trusted data and adhere to enterprise governance, privacy and data protection standards.
Establish measures of success. Define and monitor adoption, stakeholder value, reporting effectiveness, operational efficiency and advancement of analytical capabilities.
Drive innovation and continuous improvement. Assess emerging technologies, analytical techniques and business opportunities that can improve sponsor insights and create value across Group Benefits.
Represent Sponsor Analytics in cross-functional forums. Ensure sponsor reporting and broader analytics requirements are considered in Group Benefits data, product and technology decisions.

Required Qualifications

University degree in business, finance, analytics, technology, mathematics, engineering or another quantitative field. An advanced degree is considered an asset.
Significant leadership experience in analytics, business intelligence, reporting or a related data function, including leading teams through change and transformation.
Strong experience developing client-, sponsor- or externally facing analytics and reporting solutions and translating complex data into meaningful business insights.
Demonstrated ability to apply analytics across business problems, including recurring reporting, exploratory analysis, strategic insights and scalable analytical solutions.
Strong understanding of the Group Benefits business and the needs of plan sponsors, Distribution partners and internal stakeholders.
Demonstrated experience developing and executing analytics and reporting strategies that balance immediate stakeholder needs with longer-term scalable capabilities.
Experience partnering with Distribution and client-facing teams and using data visualization and storytelling to communicate with technical and non-technical audiences.
Experience with modern analytics, business intelligence and data technologies, including dashboards, automated reporting and self-service analytics.
Ability to identify analytical opportunities, structure ambiguous business questions and translate data into recommendations and business outcomes.
Strong understanding of data quality, governance, privacy and protection, particularly for sponsor- or external-facing reporting.
Demonstrated ability to translate business requirements into analytical solutions, challenge requests appropriately and prioritize based on sponsor and business value, strategic alignment and organizational capacity.
Strong executive communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to establish credibility with senior leaders, Distribution partners and cross-functional teams.
Ability to work effectively in a complex, matrixed organization and align business, data and technology partners around shared objectives.
Curious, pragmatic and outcome-oriented, with a passion for using data and analytics to improve the sponsor experience, support healthier outcomes and drive better business decisions.

Preferred Qualifications

Bilingualism (English and French) is an asset. If the successful candidate is in Québec, proficiency in both languages will be required to support clients from various provinces outside of Quebec.

When You Join Our Team

We’ll empower you to learn and grow the career you want.
We’ll recognize and support you in a flexible environment where well-being and inclusion are more than just words.
As part of our global team, we’ll support you in shaping the future you want to see.

jobs.description:
Title:
Director, Corporate Development and Strategy
Department:
Corporate Development
Reports to:
Global CEO – Pulses Vertical
Location:
Mississauga, Ontario

Job Overview:

The Director, Corporate Development and Strategy leads the strategic planning and development, M&A, and special strategic projects agenda for ETG’s Pulses vertical. Reporting to the Global CEO and working closely with the CFO, the executive leadership team, consultants, and key operating personnel, the Director drives the implementation of the vertical’s long-term growth strategy and provides support to all areas of the business to achieve the company’s strategic objectives. The role combines investment-banking-level transaction rigor with a deep commercial understanding of the pulses value chain to turn strategy into executed, value-creating deals, projects, and initiatives.

Responsibilities:

Corporate Strategy & Planning:

Lead implementation and ongoing development of the Pulses vertical’s multi-year strategic plan, including supporting new project development, M&A, and business analysis.
Identify and evaluate growth avenues—new geographies, adjacent products, value-added processing, and vertical integration.
Support the annual strategic planning cycle with the CEO, CFO, and business leaders, translating strategy into measurable targets and KPIs.
Monitor industry, commodity, trade-policy, and competitive developments and advise leadership on their implications.
Translate complex financial data into actionable insights for Board and investor presentations.
Prepare strategy materials for the Board and executive committee.

M&A and Corporate Transactions:

Own the end-to-end M&A process: target screening, origination, valuation, deal structuring, negotiation, due diligence, and closing.
Build and maintain a prioritized pipeline of acquisition, divestiture, joint venture, and partnership opportunities.
Lead transaction workstreams for carve-outs, acquisitions, and redomiciliation, coordinating finance, tax, legal, and operations.
Develop investment cases and present recommendations to the CEO, executive committee, and Board.
Oversee post-acquisition integration planning and track realization of synergies against the investment case.

Investor/Stakeholder Relations:

Shape and own the vertical’s equity story, ensuring coherent messaging across strategy, structure, valuation, and growth.
Lead preparation of investor materials—CIMs, management presentations, Q&A briefs, and valuation summaries—and support the CEO and CFO in investor engagements.
Direct due diligence and data room readiness for capital raises and investor processes.
Evaluate capital structure, refinancing, and funding alternatives in support of strategic priorities.
Benchmark peer performance, transaction multiples, and sector valuations to inform positioning.
Support Finance in raising debt and equity funding to support business growth.

Special Strategic Projects:

Lead special strategic projects at the direction of the CEO, from scoping and analysis through recommendation and implementation.
Conduct business analysis of operations, product lines, facilities, and markets to inform decisions on whether to invest, grow, restructure, or exit.
Lead portfolio and asset rationalization reviews, including consolidation of facilities, product lines, and legal entities, and divestiture of non-core assets.
Design and support internal reorganizations, including changes to organizational structure, reporting lines, and operating models.
Build business cases that quantify financial, operational, and people impacts, and track realization of expected benefits after implementation.
Coordinate cross-functional project teams and external consultants to deliver projects on time and on budget.

Leadership & Stakeholder Management:

Build and lead a high-performing corporate development and strategy function within the company, earning credibility across the organization by consistently adding value.
Manage relationships with investment banks, advisors, valuation firms, legal firms, private equity investors, and prospective partners.
Partner with operations, finance, legal, and IT leaders to align strategic initiatives with execution.
Serve as a trusted advisor to the CEO and executive leadership on strategic and transaction matters.

Employment Qualifications & Requirements:

MBA, CFA, and/or Chartered Accountant (CA/CPA) designation preferred.
10+ years of experience in corporate development, M&A, investment banking, private equity, or strategy consulting, including at least 3 years in a leadership role.
Proven track record of originating, leading, and closing multiple M&A transactions end to end, and of leading complex cross-functional initiatives such as reorganizations and business rationalizations.
Experience in agribusiness, commodities, food, or manufacturing sectors in global environments strongly preferred.
Deep expertise in valuation, financial modeling, deal structuring, and negotiation.
Experience preparing Board-level strategy materials and engaging directly with investors, lenders, and advisors.
Strong grounding in IFRS, multi-entity structures, and cross-border transactions.
Comfortable with frequent international and domestic travel.

Personal Attributes:

Strategic thinker with strong commercial judgment and a bias for execution.
Credible, influential presence with Boards, executives, investors, and counterparties.
Skilled negotiator who manages ambiguity, confidentiality, and competing priorities with discretion.
Exceptional communicator—able to craft clear narratives for financial and non-financial audiences.
Hands-on change leader who builds buy-in across the organization and delivers under tight timelines.

Success in this Role Means:

Maintaining organizational focus on a Board-endorsed growth strategy for the Pulses vertical with a well-prioritized execution roadmap.
A robust deal pipeline, closed transactions, and special strategic projects that deliver on their investment cases and targeted benefits.
A company story that strengthens investor and lender confidence in the vertical’s performance and growth.
A high-caliber corporate development and strategy function trusted by leadership.

jobs.description:
A propos de l'équipe

L’équipe TI et Transformation des Affaires
est une fonction mondiale relevant directement du PDG de Graitec. Elle est composée de quatre équipes : Transformation des Affaires, Données et IA, Sécurité de l’Information, et Opérations TI et Plateformes
. Ensemble, nous assurons les capacités opérationnelles qui permettent à Graitec de fonctionner efficacement et nous accompagnons sa transformation continue.

Nous travaillons en équipes fusionnées
, où les expert(e)s des affaires et des technologies collaborent autour d’objectifs communs et de résultats concrets.
L’équipe Opérations TI et Plateformes
soutient quotidiennement l’ensemble de l’organisation : plateformes d’affaires, infrastructure infonuagique, environnement numérique de travail et soutien aux utilisateurs. Son périmètre couvre notamment Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations
, Dynamics 365 CRM
, les outils de services professionnels, les systèmes RH, les plateformes clients et web, le centre de services TI, Microsoft Azure
, les réseaux et la gestion des identités. L’équipe dessert l’EMEA et l’Amérique du Nord et s’organise autour des domaines d’affaires qu’elle soutient.

Raison d’être du poste et contribution à la valeur d’affaires

Ce poste de direction est responsable de tout ce sur quoi les employés et les clients de Graitec comptent pour accomplir leur travail : les applications d’entreprise, l’infrastructure infonuagique et numérique ainsi que l’expérience globale de service TI.

Vous serez responsable de la qualité des services, de la fiabilité des plateformes, de la maîtrise des coûts et de la capacité de livraison. Plus qu’une fonction de soutien, vous agirez comme un partenaire stratégique auprès des équipes d’affaires, en bâtissant un environnement technologique agile, optimisé par l’IA et capable d’évoluer avec la croissance de l’entreprise.

Votre succès sera mesuré selon des indicateurs d’affaires tels que :

La productivité et l’expérience des employés;
La disponibilité, la performance et la résilience des plateformes;
L’optimisation des coûts opérationnels;
Les gains d’efficacité et d’échelle.

Ce que le succès représente dans les 12 premiers mois
Déployer un centre de services TI mondial axé sur l’expérience client, avec des niveaux de service publiés, un catalogue de services complet et des options libre-service largement adoptées. Les indicateurs de satisfaction (CSAT) et de recommandation (NPS) sont mesurés et en amélioration.
Assurer le soutien opérationnel complet du programme Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations
, avec un modèle d’exploitation et de soutien défini avant chaque mise en production.
Consolider l’environnement infonuagique et automatiser de bout en bout le cycle de vie des employés (arrivées, mobilités internes et départs).
Fournir une vision consolidée et fiable des coûts de plateformes, du positionnement des licences et de la performance des fournisseurs, tout en générant des économies.
Structurer les équipes comme une seule fonction intégrée, avec une taille optimale et une réduction des dépendances critiques.
Mettre en production une première vague d’initiatives d’IA et d’automatisation permettant de réduire les interventions manuelles et le volume de billets.
Renforcer la résilience opérationnelle grâce à des mécanismes éprouvés de sauvegarde et de relève informatique.

Responsabilités principales

Plateformes d’entreprise
Assurer la gestion complète du cycle de vie des plateformes d’entreprise : Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations, CRM, solutions d’automatisation des services professionnels, systèmes RH et de paie ainsi que plateformes clients et web.
Collaborer avec l’équipe Transformation des Affaires pour assurer une transition harmonieuse des projets vers les opérations.
Travailler avec l’équipe Données et IA afin de garantir la qualité et la fiabilité des données.
Gérer les plateformes comme des produits : responsables identifiés, adoption mesurée et feuille de route alignée sur la valeur d’affaires.

Excellence des services TI
Développer une expérience de services TI mondiale alignée sur les meilleures pratiques ITIL et centrée sur l’utilisateur.
Définir et publier les niveaux de service et le catalogue de services.
Superviser la gestion des incidents, des problèmes et des changements à l’aide d’une plateforme ITSM moderne.
Assurer la gestion de l’environnement numérique de travail : Microsoft 365, Copilot, gestion des postes de travail et cycle de vie des employés.
Exploiter les données d’adoption et les commentaires des utilisateurs afin d’éliminer les causes récurrentes des demandes plutôt que de simplement les traiter.

IA et automatisation des opérations
Définir la stratégie d’intégration de l’IA au sein des opérations TI : résolution assistée ou automatisée, opérations auto-réparatrices et optimisation de l’environnement de travail numérique.
Collaborer avec les équipes Données et IA pour intégrer des solutions d’IA générant des bénéfices mesurables.
Mesurer et communiquer les gains obtenus : réduction des efforts manuels, diminution des délais de résolution et économies réalisées.

Infonuagique, infrastructure et résilience
Superviser les environnements Azure, les réseaux, la gestion des identités, les plateformes d’intégration et la modernisation des environnements existants.
Être responsable de la disponibilité, de la performance, de la sauvegarde, de la reprise après sinistre et de la résilience opérationnelle.
Promouvoir l’automatisation et l’infrastructure comme code afin de soutenir la croissance sans augmentation proportionnelle des effectifs.

Leadership et développement des équipes
Diriger et développer une équipe distribuée composée de gestionnaires d’infrastructure, de plateformes et de support.
Favoriser le développement des compétences, la relève et une culture d’imputabilité.
Accompagner les initiatives de gestion du changement pour assurer l’adoption des nouvelles façons de travailler.

Gestion des fournisseurs et des licences
Gérer les coûts des plateformes et de l’infrastructure, les licences et les relations avec les fournisseurs stratégiques.
Négocier les partenariats en fonction des résultats d’affaires recherchés.
Améliorer la transparence des coûts unitaires et démontrer les gains d’efficacité.
Construire les dossiers d’investissement pour les dépenses technologiques majeures et mesurer les bénéfices obtenus.

Sécurité de l’information et intégration d’acquisitions
Collaborer étroitement avec l’équipe Sécurité de l’Information afin d’intégrer les contrôles de sécurité, la gestion des accès, la conformité et les audits.
Soutenir les certifications telles que SOC 2 et ISO 27001.
Diriger l’intégration TI des acquisitions, de la préparation initiale à l’intégration complète dans l’architecture de l’entreprise.

Profil recherché

Expérience requise
Expérience significative à un poste de direction dans les opérations TI et la gestion d’applications d’entreprise dans un environnement international.
Expertise approfondie de l’écosystème Microsoft : Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations, Dynamics 365 CRM, Microsoft 365, Azure, Entra ID et gestion moderne des postes de travail.
Expérience démontrée dans la mise en place de services TI orientés client et hautement performants.
Participation à des programmes majeurs de modernisation ERP et transition vers les opérations courantes.
Solide expérience de gestion des coûts, des licences, des fournisseurs et de l’intégration TI lors d’acquisitions.
Réalisations concrètes en matière d’IA et d’automatisation à grande échelle.
Capacité à interagir avec les équipes de direction et à présenter clairement les coûts, les risques, les bénéfices et le retour sur investissement.
Leadership calme et efficace en situation de crise ou lors d’incidents majeurs.

Atouts
Certification ITIL v4, TOGAF ou équivalent.
Certification PMP, PgMP ou équivalent.
Expérience dans un environnement multisociété et multinational.
Expérience au sein d’une entreprise en forte croissance, active en acquisition ou soutenue par du capital-investissement.

Processus d'entretien

Diversité et inclusion

Chez Graitec
, nous sommes fiers de promouvoir un milieu de travail inclusif où chacun peut être authentique et contribuer pleinement à notre succès. Nous accueillons les candidatures de toutes origines et évaluons chaque personne uniquement en fonction de ses compétences, de son expérience et de sa capacité à réussir dans le rôle.
Graitec utilise l’intelligence artificielle pour soutenir certains processus internes. Toutefois, toutes les décisions liées au recrutement, à l’évaluation des candidatures et à l’embauche sont prises exclusivement par notre équipe Acquisition de talents et nos gestionnaires recruteurs.

Responsibilities of the position include, but may not be limited to:

Indigenous Partnership Development:

Accountable for developing, implementing, and managing the Indigenous Partnerships, Data and Analytics (IPDA) department at ICES. This includes facilitating the assertion of representative and diverse First Nations, Inuit, and Métis approaches, perspectives, protocols, and practices to leadership at ICES.
Effectively manage all aspects of performance management for direct reports, including coaching individuals and conducting continuous evaluations to enhance team effectiveness and alignment with departmental goals.
Utilize leadership and project management skills to ensure that departmental initiatives align with ICES' strategic objectives and community needs.

Strategy Management and Operational Planning:

Manage the design and development of an effective and ongoing strategy related to Indigenous data and partnerships. This involves advancing the harmonization of ongoing ICES scientific and corporate strategies with First Nations, Inuit, and Métis requirements and protocols.
Employ analytical and strategic planning skills to assess current practices and develop actionable plans. This includes utilizing data analysis tools and stakeholder feedback to inform strategy development and ensure alignment with community needs and organizational objectives.
Work with cross-functional teams to ensure that the strategy is responsive to evolving Indigenous data sovereignty principles, leveraging collaborative skills to engage stakeholders in the process.
Oversee departmental expenses and recovery of costs by reviewing financial reports and tracking operational expenditures and ensure budget compliance.
Analyze budget requirements and make recommendations for resource allocation, ensuring that financial resources are used efficiently to support research projects and departmental initiatives.

Policy Advisory:

Advise on adapting ICES policies and processes to align with the visions, principles, and requirements of First Nations, Inuit, and Métis Peoples across Ontario. This ensures that all organizational practices are culturally relevant and compliant with community expectations.
Utilize knowledge of Indigenous governance and policy frameworks to facilitate discussions with stakeholders, gathering insights and recommendations for policy adaptation. This involves conducting research and engaging with community leaders to ensure that ICES practices reflect Indigenous perspectives and values.
Prepare policy briefs and reports to communicate recommendations to ICES leadership, ensuring that information is clear and actionable.

Education and Capacity Building:

Educate and provide expertise to internal and external partners regarding First Nations, Inuit, and Métis Peoples' data and data use at ICES. This includes developing training materials and conducting workshops to enhance understanding of Indigenous data sovereignty principles.
Leverage communication and presentation skills to effectively convey complex information, utilizing multimedia tools and resources to engage diverse audiences.
Oversee the development of internal and external capacity-building initiatives, collaborating with educational institutions and community organizations to strengthen partnerships and enhance data literacy.

External Representation:

Represent ICES at external meetings and share ICES’ approach to integrating Indigenous data sovereignty principles. This involves engaging with Indigenous thought leaders to seek guidance on best practices and emerging trends in Indigenous data management.
Utilize networking and relationship-building skills to establish and maintain connections with key external stakeholders, ensuring that ICES remains responsive to community needs and perspectives.
Develop proposals and oversee reporting documents for funders and stakeholders

Team Management and Development:

Manage, coach, and evaluate the team by providing regular feedback and facilitating team-building activities to promote collaboration and alignment with goals, utilizing performance management tools and techniques.
Foster a culture of continuous improvement by identifying training needs, organizing professional development opportunities, and mentoring team members to enhance their skills and career growth, ensuring access to relevant resources and training programs.
Utilize leadership and mentoring skills to enhance departmental effectiveness and individual growth, ensuring alignment with ICES' mission and values by creating an inclusive and supportive team environment.

Other:

Other duties as may be assigned within the scope of this position.

Knowledge, skills, and abilities:

Minimum Required Education, Years of Experience:

Bachelor’s Degree in related field;
At least 8 years of Indigenous community and/or research experience;
Experience working with major health system and Indigenous stakeholders and leaders within Ontario;
A minimum of 5 years management experience;
Demonstrated knowledge of Indigenous cultures and histories in Canada.

Preferred Education, Years of Experience:

Master’s degree in related field.;
Demonstrated knowledge of Indigenous cultures and histories in Canada, through personal lived experiences.

Minimum Required Position-Specific Knowledge and Technical Skills:

Understanding and experience working with principles of Indigenous data sovereignty.
Familiarity and knowledge of the diversity of First Nation, Inuit, and Métis Peoples.
Recognized leadership in First Nations, Métis, and/or Inuit communities, demonstrating a commitment to cultural competence and community engagement.
Experience working with Provincial, Territorial and/or Federal government and government agencies;
Demonstrated understanding of Indigenous research methodologies and approaches, with an asset being knowledge of quantitative Indigenous health research methodologies.
Demonstrated understanding of strategic planning and program implementation, ensuring alignment with community needs and organizational goals.
Demonstrated project management expertise, including budget and timeline management, to ensure successful delivery of initiatives.
Demonstrated understanding of the health care system, policy development, and planning in Ontario, particularly as it relates to Indigenous health.
Collaborative leadership skills, demonstrating the ability to lead effective teams toward desired outcomes.

Preferred Position-Specific Knowledge and Technical Skills:

Excellent oral and written communication skills, with the ability to convey complex information clearly and effectively to diverse audiences.
Relationship building skills, with a proven ability to foster trust and collaboration among stakeholders.
Flexibility and adaptability to work on multiple projects simultaneously, managing competing priorities effectively.
Demonstrated strategic planning and management skills, with a focus on achieving measurable results and community impact.

jobs.description:
Version anglaise ci-dessous | English version below

IPEX est l’un des principaux fournisseurs nord-américains de systèmes de canalisations en plastique de pointe. Notre mission est de façonner un avenir meilleur en reliant les collectivités à l’eau et à l’énergie
.

Nous sommes actuellement à la recherche d’un Directeur du programme PRE
pour se joindre à notre équipe. Ce poste est basé à Oakville (Ontario) ou Montréal (Québec)
et relève du vice-président, TI.

Ne manquez pas l’occasion de vous joindre à une équipe diversifiée de professionnels centrés sur l’humain, de leaders d’opinion, d’esprits novateurs et d’entrepreneurs qui remettent en question le statu quo.

Sommaire du poste

À titre de Directeur du programme PRE, vous serez responsable de la gouvernance et de l’exécution de bout en bout de l’écosystème ERP d’IPEX, avec une responsabilité particulière à l’égard du programme de transformation SAP S/4HANA. En étroite collaboration avec les dirigeants des secteurs d’affaires et des technologies de l’information, vous assurerez la réalisation d’une initiative stratégique d’envergure visant à soutenir les objectifs opérationnels et la croissance à long terme de l’entreprise.

Cette fonction représente une occasion unique de jouer un rôle de premier plan au sein de l’un des plus importants programmes de transformation technologique et organisationnelle d’IPEX. À la croisée des technologies, des opérations et de la gouvernance d’entreprise, vous veillerez à l’alignement des priorités d’affaires avec l’exécution du programme à l’échelle de notre réseau manufacturier nord-américain. La personne retenue possède une expertise approfondie de SAP, une solide expérience en gouvernance de programmes et la capacité de piloter des initiatives complexes dans un environnement en constante évolution.

Responsabilités principales

Assurer le succès du programme grâce à un partenariat tripartite structuré entre les TI, les unités d’affaires et l’intégrateur de systèmes, en définissant clairement les rôles, les droits décisionnels et les responsabilités à tous les niveaux de gouvernance.
Être responsable de l’atteinte des résultats d’affaires ciblés, de la réalisation des bénéfices attendus ainsi que de la stabilisation opérationnelle suivant les principales phases de déploiement et les mises en production.
Établir et appliquer les cadres de gouvernance du programme, incluant les points de contrôle, les comités de pilotage, les registres de risques et les mécanismes d’escalade.
Gérer les calendriers intégrés du programme, les plans de ressources, les risques, les interdépendances et les budgets excédant 10 M$.
Diriger des équipes multidisciplinaires composées de plus de 50 employés internes et consultants externes.
Assurer la production des rapports destinés à la haute direction et au conseil d’administration, notamment les tableaux de bord de performance, les prévisions financières et le suivi des jalons stratégiques.
Établir et maintenir des relations de confiance avec les intégrateurs de systèmes et les fournisseurs stratégiques, tout en assurant le respect rigoureux des engagements contractuels, des échéanciers et des normes de performance.
Piloter les stratégies de préparation organisationnelle, de gestion du changement et de communication en partenariat avec les équipes responsables de la transformation et des affaires chez IPEX.
Promouvoir la standardisation des processus, la gouvernance des données et la gestion des données maîtres à l’échelle de l’entreprise.

Qualifications Et Expérience

Plus de 10 ans d’expérience progressive en leadership dans le domaine des technologies de l’information, dont un minimum de 5 ans dans des fonctions de direction associées à la livraison de programmes ERP.
Baccalauréat en technologies de l’information, en informatique, en génie ou en administration des affaires (obligatoire); MBA fortement souhaité.
Expérience éprouvée dans la conduite d’implantations complètes de SAP S/4HANA (greenfield ou brownfield) au sein d’environnements manufacturiers ou industriels.
Expérience de gestion de programmes ERP pluriannuels comportant des budgets supérieurs à 10 M$ et des équipes de plus de 50 personnes réparties sur plusieurs sites et plusieurs pays.
Excellente connaissance des modules SAP S/4HANA; familiarité avec SAP BTP ainsi qu’avec la gestion des versions et des environnements SAP.
Excellentes compétences en communication exécutive et capacité à vulgariser des concepts techniques complexes auprès de la haute direction et du conseil d’administration.
Solides aptitudes en négociation, en gestion de fournisseurs et en influence au sein d’environnements matriciels.
Capacité démontrée à évoluer dans l’ambiguïté, à prendre des décisions sous pression et à instaurer un climat de confiance auprès d’équipes multidisciplinaires.
Aptitude à diriger des transformations organisationnelles d’envergure en favorisant l’adhésion, l’alignement et l’engagement des parties prenantes.
Expérience démontrée dans l’atteinte des résultats convenus, la réalisation des bénéfices escomptés, l’amélioration de la performance opérationnelle et l’atteinte des objectifs du programme.
Capacité à identifier, évaluer et atténuer les risques de façon proactive tout en assurant l’efficacité des mécanismes de gouvernance et d’escalade.
Engagement envers l’innovation, l’optimisation des processus et l’excellence opérationnelle afin de maximiser la valeur d’affaires et les capacités de la plateforme ERP.

Mobilité

Une mobilité est requise selon les besoins de l'entreprise et les étapes clés du programme, incluant des visites dans les installations d'IPEX, sur les sites de projets et auprès de partenaires, au besoin.

IPEX s’engage à offrir des mesures d’adaptation aux personnes en situation de handicap tout au long du processus de recrutement. Sur demande, nous collaborerons avec les candidats qualifiés afin de fournir des accommodements adaptés à leurs besoins en matière d’accessibilité. Les demandes d’adaptation sont les bienvenues à toutes les étapes du processus de sélection. Pour obtenir une mesure d’adaptation, veuillez communiquer avec les Ressources humaines à l’adresse askhr@ipexna.com.

______________________________________________________________

IPEX is one of the North American leading providers of advanced plastic piping systems. Our mission is to shape a better tomorrow by connecting people with water and energy
.

We currently have an exciting opportunity as a Director, ERP Delivery
. This role is based in our Oakville, ON or Montreal, QC
location and reports to the VP, IT
.

Do not miss the opportunity to join a diverse group of people-centric professionals, thought leaders and rapid thinkers, entrepreneurs in spirit and status quo-fighters!

Job Summary

As Director, ERP Delivery,
you will be accountable for the end-to-end governance and delivery of IPEX's ERP landscape, with a primary focus on our SAP S/4HANA transformation program. Working in partnership with business and IT leaders, you will help drive the successful execution of a complex, multi-year transformation initiative that supports IPEX's strategic and operational objectives.

This is an opportunity to play a key leadership role in one of IPEX's most significant technology and business transformation programs. You will operate at the intersection of technology, operations, and executive leadership, helping to align business priorities with program delivery while supporting our North American manufacturing footprint. The ideal candidate brings deep SAP expertise, strong program governance capabilities, and the ability to lead large-scale initiatives in a complex and evolving environment.

Principal Responsibilities

Drive program success through a deliberate three-way partnership among IT, the Business, and the System Integrator, with clearly defined roles, decision rights, and accountability across all levels of governance.
Accountable for delivery of targeted business outcomes, value realization, and operational stabilization following key deployment milestones and go-live events.
Establish and enforce program governance frameworks including stage gates, steering cadences, risk registers, and escalation protocols.
Manage integrated program schedules, resource plans, risks, dependencies, and budgets exceeding $10M.
Lead cross-functional teams of 50+ internal staff and external consultants.
Drive executive and board-level reporting including program health dashboards, financial forecasts, and milestone tracking.
Build and sustain high-trust partnerships with system integrators and third-party vendors while maintaining rigorous accountability to contractual commitments, delivery milestones, and performance standards.
Lead organizational readiness, change management, and communications strategies in partnership with the IPEX Change Management and Business Leads.
Champion process standardization, data governance, and master data management across the enterprise.

Qualifications & Experience

10+ years of progressive IT leadership and a minimum of 5 years in senior ERP program delivery roles.
Bachelor's degree in IT, Computer Science, Engineering, or Business (required); MBA strongly preferred.
Proven track record leading full-lifecycle SAP S/4HANA implementations (greenfield or brownfield) in a manufacturing or industrial environment.
Experience managing multi-year ERP programs with budgets exceeding $10M and teams of 50+ across multi-plant, multi-country environments.
Deep knowledge of SAP S/4HANA modules; familiarity with SAP BTP and SAP release and environment management.
Exceptional executive communication skills, with the ability to translate technical complexity into clear business language for C-suite and board audiences.
Strong negotiation, vendor management, and influencing skills in a matrixed organization.
Demonstrated ability to lead through ambiguity, drive decisions under pressure, and build trust across cross-functional teams.
Ability to effectively lead large-scale organizational change, driving alignment, adoption, and commitment across diverse stakeholder groups.
Demonstrated accountability for delivering agreed outcomes, benefits realization, operational improvements, and program objectives.
Proactively identifies, assesses, and mitigates risks while ensuring effective governance and escalation processes.
Champions innovation, process optimization, and operational excellence to maximize business value and ERP platform capabilities.

Travel:
Travel required based on business needs and key program milestones, including visits to IPEX locations, project sites, and partner locations as necessary.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
THE OPPORTUNITY

We have an amazing opportunity for a motivated operational Chief Financial Officer (CFO) to lead the organization’s strategic financial management, maintain stakeholder confidence and ensure the integrity of publicly filed financial statements. Reporting to the CEO, the CFO will provide timely and accurate financial information to support decisions concerning the organization’s short-, medium- and long-term direction. The CFO will provide advice and quarterly updates to the Audit Committee and Board of Directors, with additional updates as required.

The CFO will oversee accounting, budgeting, cash flow forecasting, liquidity management and financial systems across Nanalysis and its subsidiaries, including KPrime and RS2D. Working closely with operational leaders, the CFO will maintain effective internal financial controls, oversee consolidated financial reporting and ensure compliance with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS).

THE ORGANIZATION

Nanalysis Scientific Corp. is a publicly traded company listed on the TSX Venture Exchange under the ticker symbol NSCI. The company develops and manufactures compact nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) instruments and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) technology for laboratory and industrial applications. Its products serve customers across pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, energy, chemicals, food science and materials, as well as government and university research laboratories worldwide.

Through RS2D, Nanalysis also offers magnetic resonance electronics and software for NMR and MRI applications. The group includes KPrime Technologies, which focuses on Canadian aviation and urban security markets, providing maintenance services for passenger screening and imaging equipment and offering security technology solutions.

Nanalysis operates across Scientific Equipment and Security Services. Its services business includes a long-term, $160 million contract with the Canadian Air Transport Security Authority (CATSA) to maintain security scanners at more than 80 Canadian airports.
For more information, please visit: www.nanalysis.com

PRIMARY DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES

Participate in strategic business, financial, and human resource planning, coordinating the preparation of budgets for the organization and commercial bank.
Lead an accounting/finance department of fifteen accounting and varied staff locally and internationally, and play a role in the overall administration and management of the organization.
Responsible for day-to-day financial operations including: operating cash-flow, management of the general ledger, banking, investments, payroll, accounts payable, accounts receivable, government reporting, and remitting.
Driving and overseeing the upgrading of accounting systems, the implementation of a new Microsoft-based ERP, that is suitable for the size and nature of Nanalysis and its subsidiaries.
Monitor revenue and expenditures as compared to budget and explain variances.
Provision of appropriate performance reports to the various departments within the organization, including subsidiaries.
Skills and experience in timely consolidation of quarterly financial statements required.
In addition to providing financial reports to CEO and the Board of Directors, the CFO will provide the management team with the financial and business process information they require to do their jobs optimally.
Preparation of quarterly F/S for external distribution along with meaningful MD&A.
Management of NCIB as directed by CEO and Board of Directors, and preparation of AIF and any regulatory documents required by the organization, as determined by the CEO and Board of Directors.
As authorized by the organization’s CEO and Board of Directors, endorse cheques, contracts, and other legal documents on behalf of the organization.
Liaise with external financial accountants and ensure production of annual audited financial statements.
Oversee the financial elements of strategic partnerships with outside entities.
Work with HR to maintain personnel files with employment information and salary verification; track vacation, leave, sick time, and overtime.
Review and challenge external invoices from accounting and legal firms as necessary.
Coordinate all payroll requirements, including new hires, terminations, and salary adjustments.
Administer employee benefits plan.
Maintain banking relations, including maintaining operating lines of credit that are required for business operations.
Liaise with legal advisors on financial matters.
Lead financial Due Diligence and ultimately integration for an aggressive multi-pronged acquisition strategy over the coming five years.
Other related work may be required.

QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum of 15 years of broad financial management experience, preferably with familiarity with public-company markets and M&A.
Experience managing finance (accounting, budgeting, control, reporting) for start-ups and/or small manufacturing organizations with international clients and multiple funding sources, including federal, provincial, and international governments, is preferred.
Professional accounting designation (CPA) with a related university degree.
Proficiency in accounting software (e.g. QuickBooks) and electronic payment systems.
Experience with ERP implementation and maintenance.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite as well as familiarity with Microsoft Dynamics.
Ability to undertake occasional business-related travel.

KEY COMPETENCIES

Excellent organizational, analytical, research, and time management skills.
Ability to work with an open and consultative communication style.
Capacity to work both independently and as a strong team player and leader, demonstrating flexibility, adaptability, timeliness, and responsiveness.
Ability to set priorities, to act decisively, and to exercise a high degree of initiative, diplomacy, and judgment on a wide range of issues, especially when dealing with confidential matters.
Superior skills in building and maintaining productive and supportive working relationships and dealing with others in a professional and respectful manner.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

Scopely
is seeking a Director, Cloud Governance
to lead efforts in establishing and enforcing standards, policies, and guardrails across Scopely’s multi-cloud environment. This is a remote opportunity for individuals in Canada or the United States.

As a Director, Cloud Governance
you will play a pivotal leadership role in defining and executing the Scopely’s Cloud Governance strategy. This team will define, implement, and enforce the policies and controls that govern how cloud infrastructure is used across a decentralized organization of game, platform, and product teams.

This role is critical to bringing structure, consistency, and guardrails to Scopely’s cloud footprint, and will be key in modernizing our overall governance posture. As a central leader, you will drive alignment across highly autonomous teams and translate governance into practical, adoptable solutions while balancing control and development velocity.

This is a foundational leadership role; you will establish governance from the ground up, introduce scalable and enforceable controls, and drive adoption and buy-in across various teams, stakeholders, and senior leaders.

What You Will Do

Build & Lead Cloud Governance

Build and lead a Cloud Governance team
Define the operating model for how governance partners with game teams, security, and FinOps
Establish clear ownership and enforcement mechanisms for cloud policies

Define & Enforce Cloud Guardrails

Design and implement enforceable controls across AWS and GCP, including:
AWS Organizations, Service Control Policies (SCPs)
GCP Organization Policies and IAM constraints

Establish guardrails around:
Resource provisioning and service usage
Region restrictions and data residency
Identity and access management
Network architecture and environment isolation

Own the mandate to enforce policies, including the ability to restrict or block non-compliant usage

Standardize Cloud Structure

Define and implement standards for:
AWS account structure and GCP project/folder hierarchy
Environment segmentation (prod, staging, dev)
Naming conventions and resource organization

Bring consistency across a fragmented, multi-team cloud footprint

Tagging & Governance

Define and enforce tagging standards in partnership with FinOps
Ensure all resources are attributable (ownership, environment, cost center)
Enable downstream cost allocation and operational visibility

Stakeholder Partnership

Collaborate with FinOps on cost allocation and optimization levers (budgets, quotas, usage controls)
Partner with Security to align governance with security and compliance requirements
Work directly with game teams to safely roll out and drive adoption of policies and standards

AI-Forward Governance & Automation

Define and execute an AI-native vision for cloud governance, transforming the function into an intelligent, policy-driven operating model powered by autonomous and agentic systems
Establish the organization’s strategy for governance autonomy, defining where fully autonomous operations, human-on-the-loop oversight, and human-in-the-loop approvals are appropriate based on risk, business impact, and compliance requirements
Architect and drive agentic governance capabilities that continuously monitor cloud environments, detect risk, and autonomously remediate anomalies at scale
Partner across engineering, data, and security, and platform teams to embed responsible AI governance into cloud platforms, establishing guardrails for AI adoption, autonomous decision-making, and auditability

What We're Looking For

10+ years in cloud infrastructure, platform engineering, or SRE
3–5+ years leading teams in complex, multi-team environments
Experience operating in decentralized or federated engineering organizations
Proven track record implementing cloud governance and enforcement at scale
Experience managing or influencing environments with $50M+ cloud spend
Deep hands-on experience with AWS and/or GCP
Strong experience with Infrastructure as Code (e.g., Terraform)
Experience with policy-as-code and governance tooling (e.g., OPA, Sentinel, AWS Config)
Strong understanding of cloud networking, identity, and multi-account design

For candidates in CA, CO, NJ, NY, and WA, the annual salary range is provided below. In addition to base pay, employees may be eligible for equity, bonuses, and a comprehensive benefits package, including healthcare benefits, retirement benefits, pet insurance, paid holidays, paid Scopely free days, and unlimited paid time off. Base pay offered may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

CA, CO, NJ, NY, and WA Annual Salary Range

$175,000—$210,000 USD

About Scopely

Scopely is a leading video game and global interactive entertainment company, home to many of the world’s most beloved and enduring experiences, including two of the most successful mobile games of all-time “MONOPOLY GO!” and “Pokémon GO,” along with “Stumble Guys,” “Star Trek™ Fleet Command,” “MARVEL Strike Force,” “WWE Champions,” the Scrabble® franchise, “Yahtzee® With Buddies,” and many others. Across mobile, web, PC, and console, Scopely creates, develops, publishes, and live-operates one of the most diversified and award-winning portfolios in the games industry — bringing hundreds of millions of players together through a shared love of play.

Founded in 2011, Scopely is powered by its exceptional team — including thousands of world-class gamemakers around the globe, a distinctive tenet-driven culture, and its proprietary technology platform, Playgami. Together, these strengths have fueled Scopely’s position as the #1 mobile games company in the U.S. and #2 globally, generating more than $10 billion in lifetime revenue. Whether building global sensations like “MONOPOLY GO!” from the ground up, or expanding through strategic acquisitions, including the FoxNext, GSN, and Scopely Explore games businesses — Scopely consistently delivers experiences players love today and return to for years to come.

Recognized multiple times as one of the "100 Most Influential Companies in the World" by TIME magazine and one of Fast Company's "World's Most Innovative Companies" and “Best Workplaces for Innovators,” Scopely believes that video games can be a force for good — creating meaningful connections, vibrant communities, and making life better through play.

The Museum acts as a global learning hub, playing a unique and pivotal role in building connections between people and communities locally, nationally, and internationally.

Purpose of Position

Reporting to the Director & Chief Executive Officer, the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) is a key member of the Senior Leadership Team (SLT) responsible for the financial sustainability, stewardship, risk management and financial governance of the organization, while serving as a strategic advisor to the Director & CEO, Board of Directors, and SLT. The CFO also provides financial and strategic oversight of the Museum’s commercial activities.

Leadership Profile

The ideal candidate is a strategic and financially sophisticated executive who combines disciplined stewardship with sound commercial judgment. They are collaborative, analytical and results-oriented, with exceptional integrity, sound judgement and the ability to communicate complex financial matters clearly. They build strong relationships with the internal senior leaders and external partners and are capable of leading through change and complexity while advancing the Museum’s mission.

Ultimately, the CFO is responsible for safeguarding the organization's financial health and long-term sustainability.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership

Serve as a strategic advisor to the Director & CEO, SLT, and Board of Directors.
Serve as the principal management liaison with the Board, Finance & Audit Committee, and the Investment Committee by preparing and presenting financial information and recommendations, supporting Committee mandates, agendas and decision-making, advising the Board on significant financial risks and ensuring appropriate follow-up on Board and Committee decisions.
Foster collaboration, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement.
Build, develop and lead high-performing finance, procurement, and commercial teams with appropriate capabilities, succession, accountability and service orientation.

Financial Stewardship

Develop and maintain a long-term financial sustainability framework, including scenarios focused on funding, operating costs, reserves, liquidity and capital requirements aligned with the organizational strategy of the Museum.
Lead the annual budgeting, multi-year financial planning, forecasting, management reporting and financial performance analysis processes, ensuring that financial resources are aligned with the Museum’s strategic priorities.
Lead the Museum’s preparation for and coordination of the annual external financial statement audit, serving as the senior management liaison with the external auditors and ensuring the timely resolution and communication of significant audit matters, findings and recommendations.
Partner with the Development team to support fundraising and grant objectives through sound financial planning, proposal development and reporting, and ensure appropriate accounting and stewardship of restricted funds, grants, funding agreements and donor-designated resources.
Identify opportunities to enhance revenue, control costs, and improve Museum performance.

Risk, Compliance & Governance

Accountable for the integrity and timeliness of the Museum’s financial statements, management and Board reporting, accounting practices, internal controls, external audit and statutory and regulatory reporting.
Oversee treasury, liquidity, banking and financing arrangements, reserve strategy, investment governance and performance, and the financial planning and oversight of major capital requirements and projects.

Lead the Museum’s enterprise risk management framework and consolidated risk reporting, ensuring that significant financial, operational, insurance, legal, contractual, technology and other organizational risks have appropriate ownership, assessment and mitigation plans.

Accurate and timely reporting
Faster and disciplined close
Strong controls and reconciliations
Improved collections and working capital
Reliable budgets and forecasts
Efficient accounting processes
A capable and accountable finance team

This is more than a CFO role. It's an opportunity to step into a key leadership position, partner directly with the CEO, and help shape the future of a growing healthcare organization. If you're ready to build, lead, influence, and make a lasting impact, we encourage you to apply.

Reporting to the Executive Director, Corporate Services, the Director, Finance (Director) is the senior financial advisor for the Department of Health. The position is responsible for the financial stewardship and accountability of public funds administered by Health. At the core of their duties is the oversight of the department’s capital and operations and maintenance budget, ensuring that financial resources are allocated efficiently and in accordance with government policies and regulations. The Director of Finance is also accountable for compliance with financial regulations and standards. They must ensure that all financial transactions and operations within the department adhere to the Financial Administrative Manual (FAM) as well as legal and ethical guidelines.

The main responsibilities of the Director are, but are not limited to:

Leading the process of developing the department's annual budget, working with program managers and finance staff to gather input, projections, and cost estimates;
Facilitating the budget approval process, working closely with government agencies, legislative bodies, and stakeholders to address questions, concerns, and revisions;
Overseeing the allocation and execution of budgeted funds, ensuring that expenditures are in line with approved allocations and regulatory guidelines;
Managing the process for budget amendments or revisions as necessary, providing clear justifications and seeking necessary approvals for changes;
Ensuring that all financial reports meet regulatory requirements and government accounting principles, providing transparency and accountability in financial disclosures;
Establishing and maintaining robust internal controls to safeguard financial assets, prevent fraud, and ensure the accuracy and integrity of financial data;
Overseeing and leading a team of financial professionals, providing guidance, mentorship, and support to promote their professional growth and ensure effective departmental operations;
Fostering a culture of collaboration and cross-functional teamwork, working closely with other department heads to ensure financial considerations are integrated into broader strategic planning.

The knowledge, skills, and abilities required for this job are usually obtained through a recognized:

Undergraduate degree in accounting, finance, business administration, economics, commerce, or related field;
Completion of a professional accounting designation CPA (CMA, CGA or CA);
Eight (8) years of related experience;
Five (5) years of progressive managerial experience in assigning priorities and managing performance of professional teams.

This is a Position of Trust and a satisfactory Criminal Record Check is required.

The Official Languages of Nunavut are Inuktut, English and French. Applicants may submit their resume in any of the official languages of Nunavut. Fluency in more than one of Nunavut’s official languages would be considered an asset. Knowledge of Inuit communities, culture, land, Inuit Qaujimajatuqangit, Inuktut and experience working in a northern cross-cultural environment are also considered assets.

Acceptable combinations of education and experience may be considered for this position. We encourage you to apply if you have equivalent years of education and/or experience equal to the education and experience requirements listed above.

The Government of Nunavut is committed to creating a representative workforce; therefore, priority will be given to Nunavut Inuit who self-identify as being enrolled under the Nunavut Agreement in accordance with the Priority Hiring Policy.
Government of Nunavut employees serving a probationary period must obtain and provide written authorization from the deputy head of their employing department. The authorization from the deputy head must accompany your application for your application to be considered.
Possession of a criminal record may not disqualify candidates from being considered. An assessment of the criminal record will be measured against the scope and duties of the position. This is only a requirement for positions that require a satisfactory criminal record or vulnerable sector check.
Applicants may submit their resume in any of the Official Languages of Nunavut.
Only those candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

Venor is proud to partner with Commissionaires Nova Scotia in the recruitment of a Chief Financial Officer.

Based in Bedford, Nova Scotia, Commissionaires Nova Scotia (CNS) is the province’s leading not-for-profit security provider, delivering guarding, monitoring, investigative, and specialized security services to more than 200 sites across the province. With roughly 1,300 employees, a large share of them veterans of the Canadian Armed Forces and RCMP, CNS is the largest private-sector employer of veterans in Nova Scotia. As part of the national Commissionaires federation of over 22,000 security professionals across Canada, CNS reinvests more than 90% of its annual revenue directly into employee wages, training, and benefits.

On their behalf, we are seeking a strategic and hands-on Chief Financial Officer to join the executive team. Reporting to the CEO, you will lead the organization’s financial strategy, reporting, planning and analysis, budgeting, forecasting, capital allocation, risk management, regulatory compliance, and governance. As a trusted advisor to the CEO, Executive Team, and Board of Governors, you’ll bring financial insight to strategic decision-making while leading a team of finance, IT, and procurement professionals and ensuring the organization’s long-term financial sustainability.

What You’ll Be Doing

In this role, you’ll lead the organization’s financial strategy and provide executive-level financial advice across all business lines. You’ll develop, implement, and maintain financial policies, internal controls, and governance frameworks, and oversee financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, controllership, treasury management, and audit activities. You’ll also manage the enterprise financial systems and reporting platforms that keep the organization’s financial information timely and accurate, preparing and presenting financial reports to the CEO, Executive Team, Finance and Audit Committee, and Board of Governors, and developing the annual operating and capital budgets, including required submissions to Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC).

You’ll provide strategic pricing guidance, including contract billing and labour rates, and ensure compliance with financial, regulatory, tax, and not-for-profit reporting requirements, including CRA obligations. Externally, you’ll manage relationships with financial institutions, auditors, insurers, the national Commissionaires federation, and government partners, and contribute to organizational strategy through financial analysis, business cases, and recommendations that support sustainable growth. Internally, you’ll provide executive oversight of payroll, compensation, benefits, and related financial administration, and lead, mentor, and develop a finance team spanning budgeting, payroll and accounts, IT/cyber, and procurement.

What You’ll Bring

You bring a Bachelor’s degree in Commerce, Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, or a related field (or an equivalent combination of education and executive experience), along with a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation in good standing. You have 10+ years of progressive senior financial leadership experience, including strategic planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, and governance within a complex organization, and a track record of advising executive teams, Boards of Directors or Governors, and senior stakeholders. Your knowledge of financial management, accounting standards, regulatory compliance, risk management, and corporate governance is strong, and you’ve demonstrated the ability to translate strategic priorities into measurable financial plans and business cases. You’ve led and developed high-performing finance teams, and you communicate complex financial information clearly to both financial and non-financial audiences.

The ideal candidate is a thoughtful, collaborative leader with strong business acumen and a genuine commitment to integrity, innovation, and service excellence. You’re as comfortable in the details of financial reporting as you are advising the boardroom, and you bring the judgment to manage competing priorities during budgeting, audit, and Board reporting cycles.

jobs.description:
Help us use technology to make a big green dent in the universe!

Kraken powers some of the most innovative global developments in energy.

We create the technology that redefines utilities and unlocks a new energy system of the future. By optimising renewable generation, building a more intelligent grid, and empowering utilities to deliver an exceptional customer experience, our operating system is transforming the industry worldwide.

It’s an incredibly exciting time to work in energy. Join us on our mission to improve the lives of ONE BILLION humans within the decade and shape a cleaner, better future for everyone.

Kraken Customer

What we do: build the most AI-driven, innovative, forward-thinking platform for energy management. From optimizing resources to delivering cost-effective, exceptional customer experiences through advanced Customer Information Systems (CIS), billing, meter data management, CRM, and AI-driven communications, Kraken is powering the next wave of innovation in the energy industry.

Why we do it: future energy will not look like energy as we know it today. We need to not just think about our future, but build for it. Now.

Why it matters: There are singular moments in every industry where a tectonic shift reshapes the entire sector and unlocks previously unheard of possibilities. There are few industries remaining that are ripe for disruption. Those moments need leaders and the energy sector is in that moment. The disruption is happening now.

Our Kraken software and operating model enable our energy clients to lead this shift while enhancing their operational effectiveness. The accelerated adoption of Kraken means we need someone to lead a major North America client implementation to deliver world-changing results. Are you that leader?

The Company

Kraken launched to market five years ago, offering energy utilities one simple end-to-end customer management and local flexibility optimization solution to help them and their customers transition to a decarbonized future. The Kraken platform is effectively the operating system for utilities, at the core of how they run their business.

Kraken is growing rapidly, disrupting the incumbent tech landscape, with over 64 million end-customer accounts contracted across 11 markets globally and managing the optimisation of over 65GW. Kraken has secured licensing deals with large international energy clients to replace their core technology stack and re-image their operations with an unblemished track record of transformation success.

We are tracking toward 100 million customer accounts on the platform by 2027.

At the end of 2025 Kraken was independently valued at $8.65 billion, and received $1 billion in investment.

🏠 Where You'll Fit In

The individual in this role will serve as both the face of, and the delivery leader for the next North American utility transformation. Develop deep trust with our C-suite client executives
Lead a team of Client Delivery Leads across functional delivery areas

Communicate effectively to stakeholders at all levels, both internally and externally
Continuously demonstrate Kraken’s business value to the client and build a governance model which can last once the implementation program is completed
Set the direction and pace for implementation program execution. Managing internal and external expectations, removing blockers and making prioritisation decisions to enable successful client transformations
Understand the implementation program details and report progress to the client and internal stakeholders
Embody the Kraken ways of working. Provide support and feedback to members of the Kraken team and reinforce an environment of psychological safety.

🧠 What You'll Bring To The Party

Extensive experience in Regulated Utilities (ideally in the North American market)
Strong experience leading large, enterprise-level technology implementations and the significant transformation of business operations , ideally in utilities or similar industries (e.g. telecom, public sector)
Proven experience with C-suite clients, leading strategic conversations, negotiating win-wins, and advising on business transformation
Hands-on leader of global implementation teams consisting of experts representing implementation, product, data, engineering, change management, and enablement
Problem solver with an ability to focus conversations on the things that truly matter
Ability to understand what success looks like for the client and laser-focused on how to enable them to achieve that without always saying yes
Team player who can work effectively with national and global teams across Kraken
Excellent communication and facilitation skills. You are well respected with a natural gravitas
Client and quality focus; highly effective at building and improving customer relationships as peers
Mobile - You will be expected to invest in face-to-face relationship building with our clients and internal teams. Frequent travel will be expected.

Soft Skills

Kraken is at the forefront of innovation in the energy industry and we succeed in large part thanks to our people. To fit well at Kraken, you’ll also be:
Passionate about helping clients (without them, we don’t exist)
Passionate about technology (we are a tech business disrupting energy)

Open-minded, flexible and adaptable (we are constantly growing, changing and evolving)
Confident in decision-making
Supportive
Approachable and fun to work with
Inclusive
Resilient, working well under pressure
Believe in big ambitions and small egos
Embrace the servant leadership philosophy

Why You'll Love It Here

Opt in medical, dental, and vision insurance options.
