jobs.title: Director, AI & Agentic Engineering
jobs.description:
About The Job

Do you think like a management consultant, thrive in a startup environment, and can’t stop thinking about the intersection of data, technology, and marketing?

With over 2000 employees, offices on five continents, and world-class clients like Samsung, L’Oreal, and Mattel, Artefact
is a consulting firm that transforms data into value and business impact. We’ve recently launched in the US with offices located in NYC and Los Angeles, and we want you to join us as an integral part of our founding team!

Who We Are

Founded and headquartered in Paris, Artefact is a next-generation consulting firm, specializing in data, analytics & AI consulting, dedicated to transforming data into business impact across the entire value chain of organizations. We are proud to say that we help our clients grow their data and digital capabilities, and that we’re also growing in parallel.

We have 2000 employees across 36 offices who are focused on accelerating digital transformation. Our state-of-the-art data technologies, lean AI agile methodologies, and cohesive teams of the finest business consultants, data analysts, data scientists, data engineers, and digital experts are all dedicated to bringing extra value to every client. We design data-based solutions to meet our clients' specific needs, always conceived with a business-centric approach and delivered with tangible results. Our data-driven services are built upon the deep AI expertise we've acquired with our 1000+ client base around the globe.

Find out more at artefact.com.

What You Will Be Doing

You will lead a team of AI & machine learning engineers and managers, driving the design and delivery of production-grade AI solutions — from classical machine learning models to LLM-powered applications — and the pipelines that power them. You’ll bring senior technical judgment to architecture and model decisions, partner closely with clients and business stakeholders — including hands-on pre-sales work shaping proposals and solution designs — and define how context engineering, agent harnesses, and fine-tuning practices get embedded into every solution, while reporting into senior AI/technology leadership on strategy and priorities.

AI & ML Solution Architecture: Leading the design, build, and optimization of production AI systems — classical machine learning models, LLM applications, and agentic systems — ensuring scalability, reliability, and cost-efficient inference.
Context Engineering: Defining and standardizing context engineering practices — prompt and system design, RAG architectures, vector stores, memory management, and tool/function calling — so models receive the right information at the right time.
Harness Engineering: Directing the build of robust agent harnesses — orchestration layers, evaluation frameworks, guardrails, and observability — that make LLM systems reliable, safe, and measurable in production.
Fine-Tuning Pipelines: Leading the design and operation of fine-tuning and model adaptation pipelines — training data curation, supervised fine-tuning, evaluation, and deployment — to specialize models for client use cases.
Platform Stack: Architecting and deploying solutions on Google Gemini Enterprise and Vertex AI as the primary stack, applying working knowledge of Microsoft AI Foundry and AWS Bedrock where client contexts require.
Team Leadership: Managing, mentoring, and developing a team of AI & ML engineers; setting technical standards and fostering best practices and knowledge sharing.
Pre-Sales & Business Development: Supporting pre-sales activities — scoping engagements, building demos and proofs of concept, and presenting solution architectures to prospective clients alongside account teams.
Machine Learning Modeling: Overseeing the development of classical and modern ML models — predictive modeling, forecasting, recommendation, and deep learning — choosing the right technique for each business problem, LLM or not.
Contributing to AI Strategy: Partnering with senior leadership to shape GenAI architecture direction, tooling decisions, and platform roadmap within your area.

What We Are Looking For

The ideal candidate has a substantial software engineering and AI background with 8+ years of experience, including at least 2–3 years working on LLM architecture, agentic design, and harness & context engineering.
Strong expertise in generative AI/LLM engineering — context engineering, agent harnesses, RAG, and agentic coding — and in cloud-native software architecture, with proven production deployments.
Master’s degree (or higher) in computer science, software engineering, or a related field.
Hands-on command of agentic SDKs (LangGraph/LangChain, Google ADK, Claude Agent SDK), agentic coding tools (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor), and modern full-stack frameworks (TypeScript/React front ends; Python/Node backends).
Experience designing cloud architectures: microservices, serverless, containers/Kubernetes, CI/CD, and infrastructure as code.
Solid grasp of AI system design: agents, tool use, evaluation harnesses, guardrails, observability, and LLMOps.
Experience with data & context modeling and ingestion/processing pipelines on data lakes and data warehouses, including vector and graph storage strategies (embeddings, knowledge graphs).
Deep experience with Google Gemini Enterprise / Vertex AI; basic working knowledge of Microsoft AI Foundry and AWS Bedrock.
Experience leading and growing engineering teams, and supporting pre-sales: proposals, demos, and solution scoping with clients.
Excellent communication skills and comfort collaborating across teams and with stakeholders.
Strong business acumen with an interest in business-facing work.
Adaptability and a start-up mentality to thrive in a dynamic environment.

Why Join Us

We are united by our values
and strengthened by our hybrid expertise
.

There is always a way: We're from the breed of does, of diggers, of makers. Because ideas are valuable only if executed.
Client trust is won on the field: Addressing client needs flows better hands on at their side.
If not used, it is useless: Our love for technology translates into a steep desire for adoption, true brilliance is about impact.
If not shared, our work is not done: Sharing knowledge is the best way to button up a mission, benefitting clients and colleagues.
We learn everyday: Tech is a land where everything moves at the speed of light, you better be ready to challenge yourself.

The estimated base compensation for this role starts at $200,000 (NYC location). Individual compensation is determined by skills, qualifications, and experience. In addition, this role is eligible for competitive benefits.

jobs.title: Managing Director, Data, AI, & Cloud
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Welcome to TELUS Digital, where innovation drives impact at a global scale. As an award-winning digital product consultancy and the digital division of TELUS, one of Canada’s largest telecommunications providers, we design and deliver transformative customer experiences through cutting-edge technology, agile thinking, and a people-first culture.

With a global team across North America, South America, Central America, Europe, and APAC, we offer end-to-end expertise across eight core service areas: Digital Product Consulting, Digital Marketing Services, Data & AI, Strategy Consulting, Enterprise Technology, Enterprise Applications, Cloud Engineering, and QA & Test Engineering.

From mobile apps and websites to voice UI, chatbots, AI, customer service, and in-store solutions, TELUS Digital enables seamless, trusted, and digitally powered experiences that meet customers wherever they are, all backed by the secure infrastructure and scale of our multi-billion-dollar parent company.

Location

This role will be based out of one of our major US or Canada
office locations: Charlottesville, VA, Durham, NC, Columbus, OH, Boston, MA, Toronto, ON, or Vancouver, BC.

The Opportunity

This business unit specializes in data-driven solutions and strategic AI implementation. We help our clients unlock the full potential of their data and transform their business through innovative, AI-powered strategies.

Our Managing Director, Data, AI & Cloud, will lead our Data & AI advisory, AI solutions, Data platforms, and cloud transformation capabilities. In this role, you will be responsible for driving the growth, profitability, and success of the practice. You will provide strategic guidance, lead cross-functional teams, and deliver outstanding client value across our global footprint. The Managing Director, Data, AI & Cloud will have P&L responsibility and will play a critical role in shaping our company's overall vision, strategy, and growth.

This is an exceptional opportunity for a talented and results-oriented leader to make a significant impact in shaping our company's future and driving data-driven solutions in the evolving digital landscape. If you are passionate about data, AI, and strategic consulting, we invite you to apply and join our high-performing team.

To learn more about our AI practice: https://www.telusdigital.com/solutions/enterprise-ai

To learn more about our Cloud practice: https://www.telusdigital.com/solutions/enterprise-technology-modernization/cloud-services

Responsibilities

Strategy and Leadership:

Collaborate with the executive leadership team to define the company's Data, AI & Cloud vision, strategy, and goals
Drive growth by identifying emerging trends, market opportunities, and industry best practices
Lead the planning, development, and execution of the Data, AI & Cloud strategic roadmap

P&L Responsibility

Assume overall accountability for the financial performance of the Data, AI & Cloud consulting practice
Partner with Practice Leaders and Business Development to continue to grow managed accounts
In partnership with Business Development, develop and implement effective revenue generation strategies to meet or exceed annual revenue targets
Monitor financial performance, identify areas for improvement, and implement corrective actions as necessary

Team Leadership And Management

Build and lead high-performing teams, including Data Engineers, Data Scientists, AI Strategists, and AI Engineers
Foster a culture of excellence, innovation, collaboration, and continuous learning within the Data, AI & Cloud teams globally and more broadly through the Practice Advisor team

Client Engagement And Delivery

Partner with clients to identify their business challenges and design tailored Data, AI & Cloud solutions
Oversee the delivery of high-quality data-driven insights, models, and strategic recommendations
Provide thought leadership and build trusted advisor relationships with key client stakeholders

Competencies

Experience

10+ years of relevant leadership and team management experience within a top-tier management consultancy (Partner-level) or global and publicly traded enterprise (VP, SVP, or C-level) with a focus on AI, Data Engineering, Data Science, or Related Fields
Leads a line of business for a mid-size to large consultancy (i.e., office, industry, etc.)
Leadership experience in technology consulting, project management, and executive partnerships
Clear and tested experience in leading cross-functional teams and managing P&L responsibilities

Industry Knowledge

In-depth knowledge of Data Engineering, Data Science, and AI technologies and tools
Familiarity with emerging trends, best practices, and advancements in Data, AI & Cloud applications
Track record of being a dynamic decision-maker and having adaptability in a quickly changing environment
Deep knowledge of customer experience strategies and digital transformation

Leadership Competencies

Exceptional leadership and people management skills, inspiring and motivating cross-functional teams
Excellent strategic thinking and problem-solving abilities, with strong business acumen
Proven ability to develop and maintain effective relationships with clients and key stakeholders

Communication And Collaboration

Outstanding communication skills, both written and verbal, with the ability to present complex ideas effectively to C-level and Executive audiences
Strong collaborator with the ability to work seamlessly across diverse teams and cultures
Proficiency in English is required; additional fluency in Spanish or Portuguese is a plus

Equal Opportunity Employer

All aspects of employment, including the decision to hire and promote, are based on applicants’ qualifications, merits, competence and performance without regard to any characteristic related to diversity.

We will only use the information you provide to process your application and to produce tracking statistics. Since we do not request personal data deemed sensitive, we ask you to abstain from sharing that information with us.

jobs.description:
Director of Clinical Informatics – Enterprise EHR/CIS Implementation

Program:
Symbio – Provincial Clinical Information Solution Program
Client:
Department of Health, Government of New Brunswick (GNB)
Location:
Remote, with travel to New Brunswick at least once per month
Contract Duration:
November 2, 2026 – November 1, 2028, with one optional one-year renewal
Work Schedule:
Full-time
Maximum Rate:
$120 per hour, based on a standard 7.5-hour workday

Position Overview

The Department of Health, Government of New Brunswick, is seeking an experienced Director of Clinical Informatics (BA3)
to support the Symbio Provincial Clinical Information Solution Program. Symbio is a province-wide healthcare transformation initiative focused on replacing fragmented hospital information systems, paper-based clinical records, and disconnected applications with a unified, standardized, and integrated Clinical Information Solution (CIS).
Reporting to the Chief Clinical Information Officer (CCIO) for the Symbio Program and working closely with the CCIO and Chief Nursing Information Officer (CNIO), the successful candidate will establish, mature, and sustain the clinical informatics capabilities, operating methodologies, governance structures, and delivery practices required for the program.
This senior leadership role will oversee the day-to-day delivery of clinical informatics activities across a multi-site acute care health system, ensuring that provincial clinical workflows are standardized while accommodating approved local variations across large, medium, and small hospitals. The Director will bridge clinical stakeholders, physicians, nursing professionals, clinical operations, informatics specialists, and technical EHR/CIS build teams to ensure that the solution reflects approved clinical requirements and supports patient safety, clinical quality, operational readiness, and effective clinician adoption.
The successful candidate will also mentor New Brunswick program personnel, transfer knowledge, and develop sustainable internal capabilities to support the long-term operation and continuous improvement of the provincial clinical information solution.
Key Responsibilities

1. Clinical Informatics Strategy and Program Delivery

Work with the CCIO and CNIO to establish and maintain a sustainable clinical informatics operating model, methodology, and integrated workplan aligned with the Symbio Prepare, Adopt, and Improve journey.

Lead the day-to-day execution of clinical informatics activities across steady-state operations and project-based initiatives.

Establish transparent oversight of milestones, deliverables, progress, risks, dependencies, priorities, and escalations.

Provide regular status and risk reporting to the Department of Health.

Coordinate clinical informatics resources, activities, and priorities to support the program's overall objectives.

2. Provincial Clinical Workflow Standardization and Localization

Develop and lead a methodology for standardizing clinical workflows across a large regional or provincial health system.

Establish consistent clinical workflow standards applicable to large, medium, and small hospital facilities.

Lead the implementation and localization of standardized workflows to accommodate facility-specific operational needs while preserving provincial standards.

Assess proposed local variations, document their rationale, evaluate their impact, and support formal review and approval through established governance processes.

Ensure workflow design promotes consistency, efficiency, patient safety, and effective care delivery across participating facilities.

3. Physician and Clinician Engagement

Develop and execute engagement and advocacy approaches for physician groups, nursing professionals, and other clinical stakeholders.

Engage physician leads and frontline clinicians in clinical workflow design, EHR/CIS configuration decisions, validation, and implementation planning.

Represent physician and clinician needs in clinical governance forums, design discussions, prioritization decisions, and issue resolution.

Facilitate collaboration between clinical stakeholders, program leadership, clinical operations, and technical delivery teams.

Ensure frontline clinical requirements are accurately reflected in approved workflows, system design, and implementation decisions.

4. Clinical Governance and Decision-Making

Establish, lead, or support clinical working groups, committees, and governance forums responsible for clinical workflows, EHR/CIS design, prioritization, and cross-site decisions.

Define decision-making processes, governance structures, escalation pathways, and accountability mechanisms.

Facilitate timely and transparent resolution of clinical design issues, competing priorities, and workflow conflicts.

Maintain documented decisions, approved requirements, priorities, risks, actions, and escalations.

Ensure governance decisions are communicated to relevant clinical, operational, informatics, and technical stakeholders.

5. Clinical Informatics and Technical Build Team Alignment

Manage the day-to-day relationship between clinical informatics and technical EHR/CIS build teams.

Translate clinical requirements, approved workflows, and clinical design decisions into clear functional requirements and build specifications.

Prioritize build requests and coordinate capacity, dependencies, competing requirements, and delivery timelines.

Resolve conflicts between clinical needs, technical constraints, and approved design standards.

Oversee delivery against approved requirements and ensure that system configuration reflects intended clinical workflows.

Establish effective processes for requirement traceability, design review, build validation, and issue resolution.

6. Technical Build Governance and Oversight

Provide leadership and oversight to technical EHR/CIS build teams.

Establish build governance, standardized build methodologies, configuration standards, and delivery processes.

Manage build priorities, resource capacity, work allocation, and competing demands.

Oversee system build, configuration, testing, release management, and deployment readiness.

Coordinate planning and impact assessments for major system changes, including code upgrades and other significant platform changes.

Ensure appropriate alignment between technical delivery, clinical requirements, system quality, and operational needs.

7. Clinical Workflow Validation, Testing, and Release Readiness

Define and lead clinical workflow validation, testing, release-readiness, and cutover approaches.

Coordinate clinical and technical testing cycles to verify that configured workflows meet approved requirements.

Assess system quality, clinical safety, operational readiness, and unresolved risks before deployment.

Establish and apply clear go/no-go criteria and provide release-readiness recommendations.

Develop and oversee clinical and technical cutover plans, including stakeholder coordination, issue escalation, and contingency considerations.

Ensure readiness decisions are supported by documented validation results, identified risks, and appropriate stakeholder approvals.

8. Patient Safety and Clinical Quality

Embed patient safety and clinical quality considerations into EHR/CIS design, configuration, validation, and implementation.

Apply comprehensive clinical informatics knowledge across clinical documentation, order management, order sets, clinical decision support, medication management, and workflow analysis.

Focus on medication systems and orders management to ensure the solution supports safe and reliable clinical practices.

Partner with Clinical Operations to translate intended safety and quality outcomes into practical operational improvements.

Identify clinical workflow risks, system-related safety concerns, and improvement opportunities and coordinate appropriate mitigation activities.

9. Go-Live, Incident Management, and Stabilization

Lead or support planning and execution for large-scale EHR/CIS activations from a clinical informatics perspective.

Coordinate clinical readiness activities, activation planning, command-centre operations, and incident-management processes.

Support clinical incident triage, prioritization, escalation, and resolution during implementation and stabilization.

Monitor clinical workflow performance and system issues following deployment.

Coordinate stabilization activities and transition the program toward sustained operations and continuous optimization.

Ensure clinical stakeholders receive the support required to maintain safe and effective care delivery during system transitions.

10. Clinician Education, Adoption, and Optimization

Develop and support clinician education strategies and learning materials for new and revised clinical workflows.

Apply adult learning principles to training design, delivery, and evaluation.

Coordinate clinician readiness, adoption support, and communication activities.

Evaluate education effectiveness and identify opportunities to strengthen user confidence and system utilization.

Lead post-go-live optimization activities based on clinician feedback, operational performance, workflow issues, and lessons learned.

Support continuous improvement of clinical workflows and system usability.

11. Clinical Informatics Team Leadership and Enterprise EHR/CIS Experience

Build, lead, mentor, and develop clinical informatics teams supporting enterprise-scale EHR/CIS implementation and optimization.

Provide direction, coaching, and oversight to clinical informatics personnel and multidisciplinary delivery teams.

Apply experience with a major enterprise EHR/CIS platform to the platform selected for the Symbio Program.

Establish sustainable team practices, operating procedures, and knowledge-sharing mechanisms.

Promote collaboration across clinical, operational, informatics, and technical teams.

12. Knowledge Transfer and Capability Development

Mentor and develop New Brunswick program personnel throughout the engagement.

Transfer practical knowledge, skills, methodologies, and expertise in clinical workflow standardization, facilitation, governance, validation, and documentation.

Develop and maintain reusable processes, guidance, and documentation that support continuity of clinical informatics operations.

Enable internal program personnel to independently apply established practices and sustain the program beyond the engagement.

Support the long-term maturity and self-sufficiency of the province's clinical informatics capabilities.

in clinical informatics, large-scale EHR/CIS implementation or optimization, and clinical workflow design within a health system.

jobs.title: Interim Chief Information Officer
jobs.description:
IMMEDIATE INTERIM OPPORTUNITY

Interim Chief Information Officer

Reports to: President

Location: Greater Toronto Area, Ontario

Duration: 6-12 Months

Hybrid working

Our client, a large and complex Ontario post-secondary institution, is seeking an accomplished Interim Chief Information Officer
to provide leadership through an important period of transition, modernization and organizational evolution.

This is an exciting opportunity for a seasoned technology executive who can combine strategic thinking with hands-on execution
.

The organization recognizes that technology has the potential to play a much greater role in how it operates, how decisions are made, how services are delivered and how students experience the institution. The Interim CIO will be asked not simply to manage the existing technology environment, but to challenge conventional thinking about how technology is deployed and where it can fundamentally improve the operating model.

Leading a team of more than 100 technology professionals, the successful executive will initially provide stability, clarity and leadership through transition. Beyond this, they will help establish the priorities, capabilities, operating model and roadmap required for the next stage of the organization's technology journey.

This is therefore a mandate for a builder, modernizer and objective disruptor
, someone able to respect what is working while constructively challenging what could be done differently.

The Mandate

The Interim CIO will provide overall leadership to the technology function while working closely with the organization's senior leadership team to determine how technology can better enable its academic, student and operational priorities.

A central component of the mandate will be assessing the technology operating model
and identifying opportunities to improve effectiveness, service, scalability and value.
The Interim CIO will be expected to create alignment between technology strategy and organizational strategy, while maintaining a bias toward execution and measurable outcomes.

Key priorities will include:

Technology Strategy & Operating Model

Assess the current technology environment, capabilities, organizational structure and priorities and establish a clear roadmap for the next phase of modernization.
Challenge existing assumptions around how technology services are organized, delivered and supported.
Identify opportunities to simplify processes, reduce complexity, improve scalability and improve the value generated from technology investment
.
Evaluate the appropriate balance between internal capabilities, external partnerships, managed services and selective outsourcing.
Introduce stronger prioritization and governance disciplines to ensure technology resources are focused on the areas of greatest institutional impact.
Translate technology strategy into a practical execution agenda with clear accountabilities and outcomes.

Leadership Through Change

The Interim CIO will inherit a substantial team of 100+ technology professionals
and will need to quickly establish credibility and provide visible, confident leadership.

The organization operates within a unionized environment. Accordingly, the executive must understand how to lead meaningful organizational and operational change while respecting collective agreements, established processes and employee relationships.

The successful individual will:

Provide stability and clarity during transition.
Assess organizational capability, structure and accountabilities.
Coach and develop technology leaders.
Build stronger accountability for results.
Engage employees in the modernization journey.
Create a strong service and performance culture.
Navigate change thoughtfully within a complex unionized environment
.
Maintain momentum while making difficult decisions where required.

ERP Optimization & Enterprise Platforms

An important priority will be continuing to optimize the organization's ERP and broader enterprise technology environment.

The Interim CIO will:

Assess the current ERP implementation and identify opportunities to increase adoption, functionality and organizational value.
Address process, integration, data and operating-model issues that may inhibit the organization from realizing the full value of its enterprise platforms.
Challenge the proliferation of unnecessary processes, applications and workarounds where these create complexity.
Ensure technology modernization is accompanied by process modernization rather than simply automating existing ways of working
.
Strengthen the connection between enterprise systems, organizational processes and user experience.

Cybersecurity, Risk & Resilience

Cybersecurity will be a significant part of the mandate.

The Interim CIO will assess and evolve the organization's cybersecurity posture, governance and protocols, ensuring they remain appropriate for a large, complex and highly distributed post-secondary environment.

The executive will work to strengthen areas including security governance, accountability, organizational awareness and operational resilience, while ensuring cybersecurity is understood as an enterprise risk rather than simply an IT responsibility
.

The successful candidate will balance increasingly sophisticated security requirements with the accessibility, flexibility and innovation expected within a modern educational institution.

Cloud & Technology Modernization

The organization has begun elements of its cloud journey, but further opportunity remains to modernize its technology architecture and operating environment.

The Interim CIO will assess where further migration and modernization create genuine operational, financial, resilience or user-experience benefits.

They will bring an objective perspective regarding cloud strategy, legacy environments, technical debt, architecture and application rationalization
, ensuring modernization is driven by institutional value rather than technology for technology's sake.

Data Governance, Analytics & Decision Support

Data represents a significant opportunity for the organization.

The Interim CIO will help establish stronger data governance, ownership, quality and analytics capabilities
, enabling leaders across the institution to make better and faster decisions based on reliable information.

The mandate will include helping the organization move beyond reporting toward a culture where trusted data and actionable insights routinely inform operational, financial, academic and student-focused decision-making.

This will require both technology leadership and the ability to address the governance, accountability and behavioural changes necessary to establish a more mature data culture.

Artificial Intelligence

The organization recognizes the potentially significant role AI could play in both its operating model and the broader evolution of post-secondary education.

The Interim CIO will help leadership distinguish between experimentation and sustainable enterprise adoption, identifying practical opportunities where AI, automation and emerging technologies can improve productivity, decision-making and service delivery
.

Equally important will be establishing appropriate governance around the adoption of these technologies, including cybersecurity, privacy, data, risk and responsible use.

The successful executive will bring curiosity and ambition around AI while maintaining the pragmatic judgment required to translate emerging technology into sustainable institutional value.

The Evolving Student Experience

Technology is increasingly integral to the complete student journey.

How students learn, interact with faculty, access services, consume information and engage with an institution continues to evolve.

The Interim CIO will work across the organization to consider how technology can help create a simpler, more integrated, personalized and contemporary student experience
.

The opportunity extends beyond classroom technology. It is about understanding how technology can differentiate the institution and reduce friction across the entire student journey.

Service Culture

A key leadership priority will be continuing to evolve the technology function toward a highly responsive, accountable and customer-focused service organization.

The Interim CIO will establish clear expectations around service delivery, ownership, responsiveness and partnership with internal stakeholders.

Technology should increasingly be viewed as an enabler and partner to the organization
, rather than simply a provider of systems and infrastructure.

The Ideal Interim Executive

The successful candidate will be an accomplished CIO or senior enterprise technology executive
who has led a sizeable, complex technology function through significant modernization and organizational change.

They will bring experience across a combination of:

Enterprise technology strategy and execution.
Leadership of large, multidisciplinary technology teams.
Technology operating-model transformation.
ERP and enterprise application optimization.
Cloud migration and modernization.
Cybersecurity, risk and technology governance.
Data governance, analytics and information management.
AI, automation and emerging technologies.
Process optimization and organizational simplification.
Managed services, strategic sourcing and outsourcing.
Vendor and commercial management.
Digital/customer experience transformation.
Leadership in a unionized environment.
Organizational change and talent development.

Experience within higher education or the broader public sector
would be highly relevant, although the organization will also be interested in executives from other large, complex and regulated environments who can bring fresh thinking and transferable experience.

Leadership Style

This mandate requires more than technical credibility.

The ideal executive will be pragmatic, curious, commercially minded and comfortable challenging the status quo
. They will know when to listen and preserve institutional knowledge, but equally when to push the organization toward a different approach.

They will be capable of moving comfortably between the boardroom and the technology organization, translating complex technology issues into clear discussions about risk, cost, service, productivity and organizational outcomes
.

Most importantly, this individual will be an objective disruptor with strong execution discipline
.
They will leave the organization not simply with better technology, but with a stronger technology function, clearer priorities, improved governance, better use of data, enhanced cybersecurity and a pragmatic roadmap for how technology can enable the institution's future operating model.

The attraction of the assignment

For an experienced CIO, this is a rare opportunity to have meaningful impact in a relatively short period.

The mandate combines people leadership, technology modernization, ERP optimization, cyber, cloud, data and analytics, AI, operating-model transformation and student experience
within one of the most rapidly changing sectors in Canada.

The successful interim will have the platform to challenge existing thinking, accelerate decisions and help redefine the role technology plays across the institution.

This is not a mandate to simply keep the lights on. It is an opportunity to shape what technology leadership, capability and service should look like for the organization's next chapter.

jobs.title: Head of Artificial Intelligence
jobs.description:
Enterprise AI | Manufacturing | Supply Chain | Private Label | Business Transformation

Scope:
Enterprise-wide, multi-site
Locations:
Toronto, Wixom, Chicago and Sardis; regular site travel required
Role model:
High-leverage individual contributor / transformation owner, supported by internal teams, vendors and consultants
Primary measure:
Measurable business value from AI-enabled process and decision improvement

About the Company

The company is a large contract manufacturer and packager of household cleaning products serving branded and private-label customers across North America.

Position Overview

This position will define and drive the company’s practical adoption of artificial intelligence across the business. This is not primarily an IT infrastructure, software development or research role. It is a business transformation role for someone who can understand how the company makes money, how its plants and customer programs operate, where decisions and processes break down, and where AI can create measurable advantage.
The person will own the AI opportunity portfolio from discovery through value realization: identifying and sizing high-value use cases, redesigning workflows and decision processes, determining data and technology requirements, coordinating internal and external technical resources, guiding pilots into scaled deployment, building organizational capability, and measuring financial and operational results.
The role will initially operate as a high-leverage individual contributor. Success depends less on personally building every model and more on asking the right questions, selecting the right problems, challenging vendors and specialists, and ensuring solutions are adopted in the business and sustained.

Core Mandate

Build a phased enterprise AI roadmap tied directly to company business priorities, plant economics and customer-program economics.
Create a repeatable method for finding, evaluating and prioritizing AI opportunities based on value, feasibility, data readiness, adoption requirements and risk.
Turn selected opportunities into implemented solutions that change how work is performed and how decisions are made, rather than producing disconnected pilots or demonstrations.
Develop the internal operating model, governance, external partner ecosystem and AI literacy required to scale successful solutions across facilities and functions.
Own value realization: each meaningful initiative should have a baseline, business case, accountable owner, adoption plan and measurable outcome.

Key Responsibilities

1. AI Strategy, Opportunity Portfolio & Roadmap
Develop and maintain the enterprise AI transformation roadmap across manufacturing, supply chain, procurement, quality, R&D/formulation, commercialization, commercial/customer processes, finance and supporting functions.
Build a decision and process inventory to identify repetitive, high-value, data-rich business situations where AI, automation or advanced analytics can materially improve outcomes.
Prioritize use cases by expected economic value, strategic importance, feasibility, data readiness, scalability, change impact and risk; stop low-value or poorly grounded initiatives early.
Continuously assess the AI landscape—including generative AI, agents, machine learning, computer vision, optimization, digital twins and industrial AI—and translate relevant advances into practical recommendations for the company.

2. Manufacturing & Intelligent Operations
Work directly with plant, engineering, maintenance, quality and operations leaders to identify AI-enabled improvements in process control, batch optimization, yield, quality, line performance, changeovers, reliability, downtime, energy, waste and safety.
Identify opportunities for predictive quality, predictive maintenance, machine vision, intelligent scheduling, digital twins and decision support where the operational data and economics justify them.
Design pilots with clear operating baselines and success measures, then create the playbook required to replicate proven solutions across relevant sites and assets.
Ensure AI is embedded into standard operating processes and decision routines with appropriate human oversight, rather than operating as a separate technology layer.

3. Contract Manufacturing, Customer Programs & Commercialization
Apply AI to the full customer-program lifecycle, including opportunity identification, RFQ/quoting, formulation and product development, packaging/specification management, commercialization, production readiness, fulfillment and ongoing program profitability.
Develop better decision support around bid/no-bid, pricing floors, capacity implications, changeover burden, working capital, forecast reliability, customer service requirements and true program economics.
Explore AI-enabled customer and category intelligence that can identify assortment gaps, private-label opportunities, cross-sell opportunities, packaging gaps and product concepts the company can proactively bring to customers.
Use connected data to improve launch execution, specification/artwork consistency, retailer/customer compliance, deductions/chargebacks and root-cause learning from complaints and service failures.

4. Supply Chain, Procurement & Planning
Identify AI opportunities in forecasting, S&OP/IBP, inventory, raw-material planning, procurement, sourcing, supplier intelligence, production scheduling, warehousing and transportation.
Improve the company’s ability to predict customer demand and forecast reliability, allocate capacity and materials, sequence production and manage working capital under uncertainty.
Use AI to surface exceptions and recommended actions so teams can spend less time assembling information and more time resolving the decisions that matter.

5. Data, Technology & Partner Orchestration
Define practical data-readiness requirements for AI use cases and work with IT, plant systems, Finance, Quality, R&D and other data owners to improve access, context and reliability.
Evaluate AI platforms, specialist vendors, consultants and implementation partners based on business fit, architecture, security, scalability, interoperability, total cost and expected value.
Make informed build-vs-buy-vs-partner recommendations and ensure the company retains appropriate knowledge, control and portability as capabilities scale.
Act as the business product owner for AI initiatives while technical specialists own the detailed engineering, infrastructure and model construction where appropriate.

6. Governance, Risk & Responsible AI
Establish proportionate AI governance covering privacy, cybersecurity, customer confidentiality and IP, data access, model risk, human oversight, transparency, validation and regulatory requirements.
Create clear decision rights defining where AI may inform, recommend or execute, and where human approval remains required.
Ensure use cases involving regulated products, quality systems or customer-sensitive information are developed and validated with the appropriate functional experts.

7. Change, Adoption & Capability Building
Build AI literacy among executives, plant leaders, managers and frontline users through practical education tied to the company’s work rather than generic technology training.
Create a network of functional and site champions who can identify opportunities, support adoption and help scale what works.
Address resistance, role changes, trust and skill gaps directly; redesign processes and responsibilities where AI changes how work should be performed.
Communicate wins, failures and lessons openly so the organization becomes progressively better at selecting and deploying AI.

8. Value Realization & Executive Reporting
Build business cases and establish measurable baselines before meaningful investment is made.
Track value across cost, margin, working capital, throughput, yield, quality, service, innovation speed, risk reduction and employee productivity as relevant to each use case.
Maintain a portfolio view of AI investments, adoption and realized value, and report progress, risks and priorities to senior leadership.
Treat adoption and sustained operating impact—not the number of pilots launched—as the primary definition of success.

Illustrative Initial Opportunity Areas

Manufacturing:
Batch/process optimization; predictive quality; machine vision; maintenance/reliability; line scheduling/changeovers; energy, yield and waste.
Product & R&D:
Formulation optimization; raw-material substitution; experiment prioritization; specification knowledge; faster customer/product development.
Supply Chain:
Demand forecasting; customer forecast quality; inventory; procurement; supplier intelligence; production planning; logistics and working capital.
Private Label / Commercial:
RFQ and quote intelligence; bid/no-bid; customer/program profitability; assortment whitespace; cross-sell; customer opportunity intelligence.
Commercialization & Quality:
Launch control tower; specification/artwork consistency; complaints-to-root-cause; regulatory/product-stewardship impact analysis; customer compliance.
Knowledge & Administration:
Plant/SOP/maintenance knowledge assistants; document processing; management reporting; finance and back-office workflow automation.

Candidate Profile

The strongest candidate is likely an experienced manufacturing, operations, supply-chain, analytics or business-transformation leader who has become sophisticated in AI—not necessarily a career AI researcher or software engineer. Because modern generative AI and agent technologies are new, depth of practical use and demonstrated outcomes matter more than an arbitrary number of years with “AI” in a title.
Typically 10+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing, operations, supply chain, digital/business transformation, advanced analytics or a closely related environment.
Demonstrated recent ownership of meaningful AI, advanced-analytics, automation or digital-transformation initiatives from problem definition through deployment and measurable business impact.
Strong understanding of manufacturing economics and operational processes; experience in process manufacturing, CPG, chemicals, private label, contract manufacturing or other complex multi-site industrial environments is strongly preferred.
Practical fluency in current AI capabilities, including generative AI, AI agents, machine learning, predictive analytics, optimization, computer vision and intelligent automation. The candidate does not need to personally code every solution, but must understand enough to challenge technical assumptions and vendors.
Strong financial and business acumen: can build a credible business case, quantify value, understand trade-offs and distinguish an interesting technology from an investable business opportunity.
Proven ability to lead through influence across plant operations, engineering, supply chain, quality, R&D, Finance, IT/data teams and senior leadership without necessarily owning those functions directly.
Experience working with external consultants, software/platform providers and specialist technical partners; capable of making build/buy/partner decisions.
Excellent facilitation and communication skills, from plant-floor working sessions to executive presentations.
Comfort with ambiguity and an entrepreneurial bias toward practical experimentation, learning and scale.
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Business, Computer/Data Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Advanced degree is beneficial but not required.
Ability and willingness to travel regularly among company facilities as projects require.

Create an enterprise AI opportunity map and prioritized initial roadmap with business cases, data requirements,

About Teneo

Teneo is the global CEO advisory firm. We partner with our clients globally to do great things for a better future.

Drawing upon our global team and expansive network of senior advisors, we provide advisory services across our five business segments on a stand-alone or fully integrated basis to help our clients solve complex business challenges. Our clients include a significant number of the Fortune 100 and FTSE 100, as well as other cor­po­ra­tions, financial insti­tu­tions and organizations.

Our full range of advisory services includes strategic com­mu­ni­ca­tions, investor relations, financial trans­ac­tions and restruc­tur­ing, management consulting, physical and cyber risk, orga­ni­za­tion­al design, board and executive search, geopolitics and government affairs, corporate governance, ESG and DE&I.

The firm has more than 1,800 employees located in 50+ offices around the world.

Description

Teneo Digital advises the world's leading CEOs and organizations on how to show up, compete and win in a digital-first world, where reputation is shaped across social media, search, paid campaigns, AI-generated answers and emerging platforms.

We work at the intersection of strategy, communications and digital, helping clients navigate how influence is evolving and translating those changes into practical communications, campaign and reputation strategies.

We're looking for a senior digital strategist to help build Teneo Canada's capability at the intersection of digital strategy, campaigns, AI and reputation. This is a client-facing advisory role, working with senior communications and corporate affairs leaders to develop digital strategies, lead campaign strategy and oversee execution with specialist partners and translate emerging trends into practical recommendations that drive business outcomes.

Day to day, you'll help clients understand where digital influence is moving, how technology is reshaping communications, and how to apply those insights to campaigns, reputation management and executive positioning.

This person does not need to be a media buyer or AI engineer but should understand those disciplines well enough to lead strategy, manage specialist partners and confidently advise clients.

Responsibilities

Advise clients on digital strategy across reputation, stakeholder engagement, social, search, paid media, AI-driven discovery and executive visibility, connecting digital considerations to broader business and communications objectives.
Develop digital and integrated communications strategies, helping define audiences, narratives, channels, objectives and measurement frameworks while coordinating with specialist internal and external partners.
Lead and contribute to client workstreams, workshops and strategic discussions, translating complex digital and emerging-technology trends into practical recommendations for senior communications and corporate affairs leaders.
Contribute to multidisciplinary teams working on complex or high-stakes client situations, including assignments where digital is only one part of the broader strategic challenge.
Develop client-ready deliverables including presentations, strategic recommendations, campaign plans and points of view requiring minimal oversight.
Guide digital reputation and intelligence initiatives across social listening, search, GEO, AI visibility and emerging platforms, identifying risks, stakeholder dynamics and opportunities for clients.
Work with paid media, creative and analytics partners to ensure campaigns and digital programs are strategically sound, measurable and aligned with client objectives, without necessarily acting as the hands-on platform operator.
Help build Teneo’s digital advisory offerings, including new methodologies, playbooks and points of view across digital reputation, emerging platforms and AI.
Mentor junior team members, providing direction on research, analysis, reporting and client deliverables while helping build capability across the team.
Stay at the forefront of developments across digital platforms, social, search, AI, LLMs and emerging technologies, proactively bringing new ideas and implications to clients and colleagues.

Qualifications

6+ years’ experience in digital strategy, strategic communications, corporate affairs, reputation management, management consulting or related advisory work.
Experience supporting or advising senior stakeholders on digital strategy, reputation, stakeholder engagement, transformation or other complex business issues.
Demonstrated ability to structure complex problems, develop strategic recommendations and coordinate multidisciplinary teams through execution.
Strong understanding of integrated communications and campaigns spanning owned, earned, shared and paid channels, with experience developing strategy rather than simply executing tactics.
Ability to quickly understand unfamiliar business, reputation and stakeholder issues and identify where digital insight or strategy can add value.
Working knowledge of paid media and ad-buying ecosystems, with the ability to collaborate effectively with specialist agencies and vendors, challenge recommendations and oversee execution.
Strong understanding of digital platforms, search, GEO, AI-driven discovery, social listening and how digital reputation and information environments are evolving.
Experience using digital analytics, research or social listening to identify trends, assess stakeholder dynamics, measure performance and translate findings into strategic recommendations.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to develop clear, executive-ready presentations, recommendations and points of view.
Experience managing client workstreams and mentoring junior team members in a fast-paced, client-driven environment.
Curious, strategically minded and comfortable working in ambiguity, with a demonstrated ability to translate emerging technologies and digital trends into practical client opportunities.
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience.

Job Title: Finance Director
Job Description

The Finance Director leads core financial reporting, regulatory reporting, and FP&A activities while playing a key role in ongoing finance transformation initiatives. This role oversees month-end close, prepares and reviews financial statements and management reporting, and ensures audit-ready documentation and regulatory compliance. The Finance Director also supports IFRS 17 implementation, systems and process improvements, and provides strategic financial analysis and executive reporting in a collaborative, highly visible finance environment.

Responsibilities

Lead and support monthly, quarterly, and annual financial close processes, ensuring timely and accurate completion.
Prepare and review journal entries, account reconciliations, and supporting schedules for balance sheet and income statement accounts.
Analyze balance sheet and income statement fluctuations to identify trends, risks, and opportunities, and communicate findings to leadership.
Prepare financial statements and comprehensive management reporting packages for senior leadership and key stakeholders.
Maintain audit-ready supporting documentation for all financial reporting activities and ensure strong internal controls.
Support internal and external audit requirements, including preparation of audit materials and responding to audit inquiries.
Oversee and support regulatory reporting activities, including OSFI and other regulatory filings.
Prepare reporting schedules, reconciliations, and supporting documentation for regulatory submissions.
Review regulatory filings to ensure reporting accuracy, completeness, and compliance with applicable regulations.
Support finance transformation initiatives, with a particular focus on IFRS 17-related process enhancements and implementation activities.
Participate in testing, controls validation, data verification, and user acceptance testing for new and enhanced finance processes and systems.
Contribute to finance systems and process improvement initiatives, including ERP, reporting, and finance system implementations and integrations.
Lead or support FP&A activities, including budgeting, forecasting, and financial planning processes.
Develop financial models and analytical reporting to support decision-making and strategic planning.
Perform variance analysis on financial results and provide clear, insightful explanations for executive reporting.
Prepare and deliver executive reporting and presentations that summarize financial performance, forecasts, and key insights.
Provide technical accounting guidance, including gap analysis and interpretation of complex accounting standards such as IFRS 17.
Collaborate closely with accounting, reporting, FP&A, and project teams to drive results and support enterprise-wide initiatives.
Demonstrate leadership within a small, highly visible finance team, contributing across multiple areas of finance as needed.
Adapt to changing priorities and work independently while maintaining strong communication and collaboration across the organization.

Essential Skills

Proven experience in financial reporting, including preparation and review of financial statements and management reporting packages.
Strong background in month-end close processes, journal entries, reconciliations, and supporting schedules.
Expertise in forecasting, budgeting, and financial planning and analysis (FP&A).
Demonstrated ability to perform detailed variance analysis and provide clear, actionable insights.
Experience with regulatory reporting, particularly OSFI reporting requirements.
Hands-on experience with IFRS 17 and related technical accounting and process implications.
Strong technical accounting skills, including closing and reporting and gap analysis.
Experience supporting finance transformation and process improvement initiatives.
Proficiency with ERP and finance systems, including SAP, Oracle, and Sun Accounting.
Leadership experience in a finance function, with the ability to work in a small, highly visible team.
Knowledge of Property & Casualty (P&C) insurance financial and regulatory requirements.
Audit experience, including supporting internal and external audits.
Excellent analytical, reporting, and problem-solving skills.
Strong communication skills, with the ability to present complex financial information clearly to executives and stakeholders.

Additional Skills & Qualifications

CPA designation.
Bachelors degree in Accounting, Finance, Commerce, or a related field.
Experience working within Property & Casualty (P&C) insurance organizations.
Hands-on experience with SAP, Oracle, and Sun Accounting systems.
background in audit, either in public accounting or corporate audit functions.
Experience with integration projects and enterprise-wide system implementations.
Proven ability to support finance transformation initiatives and process improvements.
Comfort operating in a hands-on environment and contributing across accounting, reporting, FP&A, and strategic projects.
Ability to navigate changing priorities and work independently while maintaining strong collaboration.
Track record of partnering with senior finance leadership, including CFO-level stakeholders.

Work Environment

This role operates within a small, collaborative, and highly visible finance team where professionals work closely with the CFO and finance leadership. The culture is hands-on, with a strong emphasis on adaptability, clear communication, and a willingness to roll up your sleeves wherever support is needed. The position follows a hybrid work model, with a company policy of three days per week in the office and a standard 37.5-hour workweek. The office is located in Toronto and provides exposure to major finance transformation initiatives, including IFRS 17 implementation, ERP and reporting system enhancements, and enterprise-wide process improvements. Team members partner across accounting, reporting, FP&A, and project teams, gaining broad experience in financial reporting, accounting, FP&A, and strategic projects within a dynamic, transformation-focused environment.

This is a Contract position based out of Toronto, ON.

jobs.title: Cloud Architecture & Engineering, Director
jobs.description:
At PwC, our people in infrastructure focus on designing and implementing robust, secure IT systems that support business operations. They enable the smooth functioning of networks, servers, and data centres to optimise performance and minimise downtime. Those in site reliability engineering at PwC will focus on enabling the reliability, scalability, and performance of organisational technology infrastructure. This will include working to automate processes, monitor systems, and resolve incidents to maintain a seamless user experience.**Meaningful work you’ll be part of**

  

As a Director, Cloud Architecture \& Engineering, you’ll work as part of a team of problem solvers, helping to solve business issues, deliver high\-quality client service and operational efficiency. Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  

* You will play a pivotal leadership role at the intersection of cloud strategy, architecture, engineering, and client engagement.
* This role combines deep technical cloud expertise with strategic leadership, practice development, and team coaching.
* You will shape and scale cloud capabilities, guide clients through complex transformation journeys, and help drive PwC’s cloud first vision.
* You will be responsible for designing and governing enterprise grade cloud architectures while also driving advisory engagements, leading teams, strengthening client relationships, and contributing to the innovation pipeline for cloud\-based solutions and assets.
* This role requires a seasoned cloud leader who can operate fluently across business strategy, modern cloud architectures, and hands\-on technical depth—while mentoring teams and influencing both internal and client executives.

 **Cloud Architecture \& Engineering Leadership**

* Lead the design, governance, and implementation of end\-to\-end cloud architectures aligned to business goals and industry best practices.
* Architect scalable, secure, and cost optimized cloud solutions across AWS, Azure, and GCP.
* Develop cloud foundation blueprints, reference architectures, and reusable patterns.
* Oversee the design and optimization of Kubernetes platforms (EKS, AKS, GKE) and containerized environments.
* Guide the development and automation of cloud infrastructure using Infrastructure\-as\-Code (Terraform, CloudFormation, AWS CDK, ARM, etc.).
* Provide technical guidance on compute, storage, networking, security, identity, data services, and DevOps tooling.

 **Cloud Advisory \& Client Engagement**

* Serve as a trusted advisor to executive\-level stakeholders, helping them define and execute cloud strategies and operating models.
* Assess existing environments, develop modernization roadmaps, and oversee cloud migration programs.
* Lead proposal creation, solutioning activities, statements of work, and client presentations.
* Communicate complex technical concepts to nontechnical audiences clearly and effectively.
* Identify and prioritize client use cases and translate business requirements into architectural approaches and execution plans.

 **Practice \& Team Leadership**

* Build, lead, and mentor teams of cloud architects, engineers, and technical specialists.
* Foster a culture of continuous learning, experimentation, and cloud innovation.
* Recruit and grow diverse technical talent, ensuring strong career development and retention.
* Collaborate with practice leadership to define strategic direction, emerging offerings, and go\-to\-market assets.
* Lead initiatives that strengthen practice foundations: capability models, delivery frameworks, accelerators, patterns, and reusable assets.

 **Innovation, Delivery \& Thought Leadership**

* Lead technical innovation cycles to evaluate, test, and showcase new cloud technologies, tools, and architectures.
* Drive and participate in hands\-on cloud prototyping, labbing, and solution validation.
* Develop technical demos, asset\-driven solutions, and market\-aligned accelerators.
* Present at internal and external events, contributing to PwC’s thought leadership presence.
* Maintain active engagement with cloud provider alliances and product engineering teams to share early insights and influence product evolution.

**Experiences and skills you’ll use to solve**

 **Technical Expertise**

* Extensive experience in cloud architecture and engineering across AWS (primary), Azure, and/or GCP.
* Deep knowledge of Kubernetes, containers, microservices, serverless architectures, and modern DevOps practices.
* Hands\-on experience with IaC tools (Terraform strongly preferred), CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI, Argo, etc.), and automated deployment patterns.
* Strong understanding of cloud security, IAM, network segmentation, encryption, monitoring, cost optimization, and governance frameworks.
* Experience supporting modernization programs such as application migration, refactoring, API strategies, and technical debt remediation.
* AI\-assisted development and prior experience deploying agentic workloads and MLOps pipelines is an asset.

 **Leadership \& Consulting Skills**

* Demonstrated experience leading cloud\-focused teams and initiatives in a complex, multistakeholder environment.
* Strong executive communication skills suitable for client\-facing consulting environments.
* Ability to bridge business and technical perspectives and articulate value propositions, architecture decisions, and tradeoffs.
* Strategic mindset with a bias toward execution, innovation, and measurable impact.

 **Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience).
* Significant cloud architecture and engineering leadership experience.
* Preferred: AWS Solutions Architect (Professional); Azure or GCP Architect certifications; Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) or CKAD; Terraform Associate Certification.
* Ability to obtain Government of Canada **Security Clearance; Level 2 security clearance is an asset**.
*

 About the Opportunity: 
 This is an exciting leadership opportunity within Commercial Banking to shape the future of how data powers business decisions across Canada and the U.S. 
 As Director, Data Foundations, Automation & Information Infrastructure, you will lead a highly technical team responsible for delivering trusted, curated, and scalable data assets that support reporting, analytics, AI, and strategic decision-making across Commercial Banking. You will oversee data engineering, data operations, information infrastructure, and business-managed applications while influencing the broader Commercial Banking data strategy. 
 The role combines banking knowledge, technical leadership, people management, and strategic thinking. As the organization continues its journey toward cloud modernization, AI-enabled automation, Client 360 capabilities, and near real-time data delivery, this leader will play a critical role in shaping the future state of Commercial Banking's data ecosystem. 
 This opportunity is ideal for a banking-savvy technology leader who enjoys building high-performing teams, solving complex data challenges, driving modernization initiatives, and translating business needs into scalable technical solutions. 

 About This Role 
 The Director, Data Foundations leads the team responsible for building, managing and continuously improving the curated data that powers Commercial Banking. This includes client, financial, client activity and master data, along with the other key business data sets that reporting, analytics and AI teams across the organization rely on to make decisions.
 The Director owns the end-to-end data lifecycle, from requirements, data modeling and architecture, through ETL and pipeline development, to the reliable production of trusted data within established service levels. The role partners with business, analytics, AI, Technology and Data Governance partners to ensure data is accurate, well documented and easy to use, and leads the ongoing modernization of data platforms and practices. 
 The ideal candidate combines deep data management expertise with strong people leadership and a high standard for quality. 
 Why This Role Matters 
 Trusted, well-managed data is the foundation for sound decisions, effective and trusted reporting, and the responsible use of AI. This role directly contributes to: 
 ·        Consistent, reliable data that supports executive reporting and business decision-making 
 ·        Curated data assets that allow reporting, analytics and AI teams to focus on insights 
 ·        A scalable, modern data ecosystem that keeps pace with evolving business needs 
 ·        Strong data quality and control practices aligned to BMO’s data governance standards 
 Key Responsibilities 
 Data Strategy and Architecture

 ·        Design and maintain the data architecture and models for curated data assets, including master and reference data, with long-term usability and scalability in mind 
 ·        Establish and uphold standards for data modeling, naming, metadata, integration and data sharing 
 Data Development and Operations 
 ·        Lead the design, development and operation of ETL processes and data pipelines 
 ·        Ensure recurring data production is accurate, timely and reconciled to authoritative sources, within published service levels 
 ·        Monitor data flows, resolve issues promptly and drive root-cause remediation 
 ·        Embed data quality checks, validation and controls throughout the data lifecycle 
 ·        Ensure data is handled securely and protected from loss or unauthorized access, in line with legal and company standards 
 Modernization and Innovation 
 ·        Continuously evaluate and adopt technologies, tools and practices that improve the scalability, efficiency and resilience of the data ecosystem 
 ·        Partner with Technology on platform strategy, infrastructure and the path to production 
 ·        Prepare and structure data to support advanced analytics and AI use cases 
 Data Enablement and Partnership 
 ·        Manage the intake and prioritization of data requests transparently, with clear service levels 
 ·        Promote data literacy and self-service through documentation, data dictionaries and a community of practice 
 ·        Serve as a trusted partner to business, analytics, AI and Technology teams on data definitions, changes and their downstream impacts 
 ·        Partner with Data Governance to meet data quality, metadata, lineage and data risk requirements 
 Business-Managed Applications 
 ·        Oversee a portfolio of business-managed applications that support key business processes, from intake and design through delivery, enhancement and ongoing support 
 ·        Ensure these applications are well controlled and supported, and aligned to BMO technology, data and risk standards 
 People Leadership 
 ·        Build, develop and lead a high-performing team of data professionals, working effectively with vendor partners 
 ·        Set clear goals and accountability, coach for growth, and foster a culture of ownership, quality and continuous improvement 
 ·        Attract, retain and develop top talent, recognizing strong performance and addressing gaps 
 ·        Role model BMO values and foster an inclusive culture connected to our purpose 
 ·        Take measured risks while protecting the bank by applying our Risk Management Framework in the execution of your role, in line with our Risk Culture and within our approved Risk Appetite, making sound and risk informed decisions that align to business strategy, protect assets, and adhere to applicable policy documents (Frameworks, Policies, Standards, Procedures and Supporting documents), laws and regulations. 
 Who You Are 
 ·        Treats data as a product: curated, documented, reconciled and reusable 
 ·        Holds a high standard for accuracy and builds processes that make quality repeatable 
 ·        Balances stability with progress, modernizing while keeping production dependable 
 ·        Understands Commercial Banking and how data flows across clients, products and channels 
 ·        Communicates clearly and builds trust through transparency 
 ·        Influences without authority and aligns diverse stakeholders around shared definitions 
 ·        Thrives in ambiguity and brings creative solutions to complex, interdependent problems 
 Qualifications 
 ·        9+ years of experience in data management, data engineering or a related field, including leadership of data teams 
 ·        Deep expertise in ETL and data pipeline development, data modeling and data quality management 
 ·        Strong proficiency in SQL and modern data programming languages such as Python 
 ·        Experience with cloud and modern data platforms 
 ·        Working knowledge of master data, metadata, semantic layer and data governance practices, including data privacy and integrity 
 ·        Experience operating in a highly regulated environment; Commercial Banking or financial services experience is an asset 
 ·        Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills 
 ·        Post-secondary degree in a related field of study, or an equivalent combination of education and experience 
 Why This Role 
 ·        Lead the Data Foundation that underpins reporting, analytics and AI across Commercial Banking 
 ·        Shape how data is built, managed and used at scale 
 Join a culture that values ownership, collaboration, trust and measurable outcomes

Lifemark Health Group (LHG) is a market leader in customized healthcare solutions.
