Chief Financial Officer

Fresh Prep Foods Inc.

Reports to: Chief Executive Officer
Location: Vancouver HQ (hybrid), with operations in Alberta, Ontario and Quebec
Compensation: $300,000 - $380,000 CAD base + performance bonus + stock options

Who We Are

Fresh Prep is Canada's largest Canadian-owned meal kit company and a certified B Corporation. We deliver chef-created meal kits, prepared meals and a growing grocery marketplace to customers across the country, from production facilities in British Columbia, Alberta, and Quebec, with operations in Ontario. We're a team of over 600 people and over $110M in annual revenue.
Our founders were named EY Entrepreneur Of The Year 2025 winners and we've been recognized as one of Deloitte's Best Managed Companies in Canada, one of BC's Top Employers, and one of Globe and Mail's Top Growing Companies.

The Role

You'll own the financial function of a national, multi-province, physical-operations business with subscription economics, which means you need to be fluent in both cohort and contribution margin analysis and in the operating systems required to manage food costs, labour productivity, last mile delivery and freight.
You'll be accountable for the numbers the Board and our Investors see, capital strategy and the financial rigour that lets the executive team make decisions quickly and correctly.
You'll report to the CEO, sit on the executive team, and be a standing presence in the boardroom. You will also, at points, be the person telling the rest of us that something we want to do doesn't work. We're looking for someone who is comfortable doing that.

What You'll Be Doing

Financial leadership and reporting

Own all financial reporting, including GAAP compliant statements, the annual audit and consolidated reporting across multiple provinces and legal entities.
Own internal management reporting and commentary that gives the executive team and Board timely insight into trends, unit economics, and the drivers behind them: not just what happened, but why.
Own the operating and capital budget process and hold the company to it.
Own the financial metrics framework across the business, including cohort retention, margin, customer payback and facility-level unit economics.

Capital, cash, and financing

Own cash management, working capital, and cash forecasting in a business with meaningful inventory and seasonality.
Manage our lending relationships, credit facilities, and covenant compliance.
Lead financing strategy and execution: debt, asset-based and project finance, equity, and government programs, in partnership with the CEO and founders.
Manage reporting and communication to a capital structure that includes multiple classes of equity and institutional investors, including the obligations that come with it.
Own the government funding agenda, including SR&ED and applicable federal and provincial grant programs.

Transactions and strategic projects

Lead financial diligence, modelling, and integration on acquisitions and other strategic transactions.
Provide modelling and analytical support for growth decisions: new facilities, capacity investment, category expansion, long-term supply contracts, and technology investment.
Bring financial discipline to pricing and promotional strategy in partnership with the CMO, including the margin envelope within which marketing operates.

Operations partnership

Own cost accounting for a manufacturing and logistics business: standard costs, food cost variance, labour productivity, delivery, freight, and waste.
Partner with Operations on the decisions that determine our gross margin and be a genuine second set of eyes on capital projects.
Support technology and automation decisions with credible business cases and honest post-mortems.

Compliance and governance

Ensure legal and regulatory compliance across all financial functions, including multi-province tax (GST/HST, QST, PST), payroll compliance in four provinces including Quebec, and corporate filings.
Maintain the internal controls appropriate to our scale and to the diligence standards our investors and lenders apply.
Support the Board and its committees with materials, forecasts, and the analysis behind major decisions.

Team

Lead, structure, and develop the finance, accounting and supply chain teams
Continue building systems and processes that create more thinking and less data manipulation. This is a company where the finance team should be spending its time on analysis, not on reconciliation.

What We're Looking For

Required

12+ years in finance and/or accounting, including senior finance leadership in a company at or above $75M in revenue.
CPA designation, with a degree in accounting, finance, or business.
Experience in physical-operations businesses: manufacturing, food production, CPG, or logistics, including hands-on cost accounting ownership.
Demonstrated ownership of an external audit and GAAP reporting.
Experience securing debt financing and managing lender relationships and covenants.
Experience with a modern ERP environment and ancillary tech-stack.
Multi-site operating experience in a manufacturing environment.

Strongly preferred

M&A experience with due diligence, deal structuring and integration
Experience with subscription or recurring-revenue economics alongside physical operations.
Experience with institutional equity investors
Experience preparing a company for a liquidity or capital event.
SR&ED and government grant program experience.

How you work

You reason from data and are honest about what the data doesn't tell you.
You can explain complex financial concepts to a room of operators without either condescending or losing them.
You build environments where other people do their best work, and you develop people rather than accumulating tasks.
You are fluent with AI tooling and actively use it in your own work. Not as a talking point, but because you've found it makes your analysis faster and your team's time better spent. You have a view on where it belongs in a finance function and where it doesn't.
You are willing to be the dissenting voice, and you know how to disagree without being obstructive.
You can toggle between daily finance tasks and strategic board conversations comfortably and can operate with precision in both.
You don’t have an ego, you don’t need to be right and you are happy as long as the decision helps achieve the company’s goals.

What You Can Expect

Hybrid work, with our HQ in East Vancouver.
Comprehensive executive health benefits including medical, dental, vision, and life insurance.
A Fresh Prep meal plan
A highly impactful seat at the table of a Canadian company that is at the forefront of food innovation

jobs.title: AVP, Transformation Delivery, Transition and Readiness
jobs.description:
Manulife Canada is transforming how operational work is received, processed, routed, completed and measured across servicing functions. This includes retiring legacy workflow platforms, re-engineering operational processes, modernizing technology architecture, and introducing reusable AI-enabled automation capabilities that improve service, strengthen controls, and create a more scalable operating model. This position will help lead the transformation program supporting this vision while establishing reusable business and technology capabilities that can be applied across future modernization initiatives.

The AVP, Transformation Delivery, Transition & Readiness will play a pivotal leadership role in one of Manulife Canada's largest operational transformation programs. The successful candidate will be accountable for integrated program delivery, transition management, operational readiness, release governance, and execution of the legacy workflow system retirement roadmap across multiple transformation waves.

This role sits at the intersection of operations, technology and delivery. The successful candidate will ensure business capabilities are deployed safely, the organization is prepared to operate through interim states, and transformation outcomes are successfully scaled across the enterprise.

Position Responsibilities

The AVP, Transformation Delivery, Transition & Readiness is accountable for planning, coordinating, governing and executing the transformation roadmap. The role leads the Program Management Office while also establishing the transition strategies, release governance, readiness practices and operating-model controls required to move the organization from current-state operations to future-state operations. The role owns delivery execution and operational implementation of the transformation.

Program and Portfolio Delivery

Own the integrated transformation roadmap.
Govern program schedules, milestones and delivery commitments.
Manage critical path dependencies and inter-workstream coordination.
Lead program governance forums and executive reporting.
Establish delivery performance measures and escalation mechanisms.
Maintain integrated views of scope, timeline, financials and risks.

PMO Leadership

Lead and develop the Program Management Office.
Establish governance processes, standards and controls.
Manage executive reporting, dashboards, status reviews and Steering Committee materials.
Oversee RAID management and dependency tracking.
Coordinate planning across business, technology and delivery workstreams.

Transition Management

Develop the enterprise transition strategy for workflow system retirement.
Define interim-state operating models and deployment approaches.
Establish coexistence strategies for legacy and future-state environments.
Coordinate cutover and rollout planning across business units.
Manage hypercare, stabilization and post-deployment support activities.
Ensure operational continuity throughout transformation waves.

Operational Readiness

Define operational readiness frameworks and checkpoints.
Establish release-level go-live criteria.
Coordinate readiness assessments across business and technology stakeholders.
Ensure operational support models are established and sustainable.
Govern release approvals and deployment decision processes.

Integration Readiness & Ecosystem Coordination

Govern cross-platform dependency management.
Coordinate ecosystem readiness activities across impacted applications.
Track platform onboarding, retirement and transition activities.
Monitor system integration risks impacting rollout schedules.
Partner with Architecture, Engineering and Technology leaders to establish release readiness.
Govern temporary bridge solutions required during transformation waves.

Workflow System Retirement Execution

Maintain workflow system retirement execution plan.
Track retirement dependencies and readiness criteria.
Coordinate enterprise-wide retirement planning activities.
Ensure all retirement risks are identified and managed.
Support final platform decommissioning and transition activities.

Required Qualifications

10+ years leading large-scale enterprise transformation programs.
Experience managing multi-year technology and operations transformation initiatives.
Proven track record establishing PMO and governance functions.
Experience executing phased technology migrations and platform retirements.
Strong understanding of operational readiness, deployment management and transition planning.
Experience managing third-party delivery partners and systems integrators.
Financial services, insurance or operations transformation experience preferred.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with AWD or a comparable workflow platform, such as Pega, Appian, or FileNet, at scale.
Experience establishing reusable automation components or shared engineering services across business units.
Experience delivering transformation in a federally regulated financial institution, including familiarity with OSFI expectations for change and outsourcing.

We’ll empower you to learn and grow the career you want.
We’ll recognize and support you in a flexible environment where well-being and inclusion are more than just words.

Job Description

DePuy Synthes is recruiting for Sr. Director, ERP Supply Chain & SAP Technology Platforms, Orthopedics.

Johnson & Johnson announced plans to separate our Orthopedics business to establish a standalone orthopedics company, operating as DePuy Synthes. The process of the planned separation is anticipated to be completed within 18 to 24 months, subject to legal requirements, including consultation with works councils and other employee representative bodies, as may be required, regulatory approvals, and other customary conditions and approvals.

Should you accept this position, it is anticipated that, following conclusion of the transaction, you would be an employee of DePuy Synthes and your employment would be governed by DePuy Synthes employment processes, programs, policies, and benefit plans. The Sr. Director, ERP Supply Chain & SAP Technology Platforms role provides enterprise leadership including strategy and planning, architecture and execution, and functional and technical operations of ERP Supply Chain solutions and the SAP Technology platform across a complex multi-instance ECC and S/4 global landscape.

This leader will manage multiple conveyed SAP ECC and S/4 instances supporting Day 1 separation, lead transition activities during the TSA period, and execute on the SAP instance consolidation into S/4 supporting TSA exit with focus on Supply Chain ERP capabilities.

Additionally, this role is accountable to establish SAP technology platform services and governance including application development and delivery, and operational support for cross-functional business operations for multiple SAP instances including both finance and supply chain ERP ecosystems and satellite applications.

This position partners closely with Finance, Global Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Quality, Regulatory, and IT leaders to modernize and rationalize platforms, strengthen data and analytics, and drive measurable business value through technology. Establish strong governance, vendor management, and financial oversight for technology investments and operating spend.
Champion continuous improvement, innovation, and standardization to enable a resilient and future-ready SAP ecosystem.

Master's degree, MBA, MS, or equivalent, preferred.

Required

jobs.title: Executive Director - Finance
jobs.description:
Reporting to:
Chief Administrative and Financial Officer (CAFO)
Status:
Executive Leadership
Location:
Alberta / flexible within Alberta

Position Purpose

This is an opportunity to help build something new.
We are looking for an exceptional finance leader who can ensure that today's reporting obligations are delivered with accuracy and credibility, while helping shape what the function becomes tomorrow.

Reporting directly to the Chief Administrative and Financial Officer, the Executive Director, Finance will combine deep public-sector financial expertise with strategic thinking, strong relationship-building skills and a genuine appetite for change. This person will be a trusted advisor to senior leadership, a credible partner to the Ministry and the Office of the Auditor General, and a champion for the people who make up the Finance team.
We are looking for someone who is as interested in people and possibilities as they are in numbers.

Key Accountabilities

1. Financial Reporting Leadership

• Provide executive-level oversight of ALA's monthly, quarterly and year-end financial reporting cycle and ensure deliverables are accurate, complete, well-supported, appropriately reviewed and submitted within required deadlines.
• Provide senior technical leadership on complex accounting matters, financial statement presentation, disclosures, estimates, unusual transactions and other matters requiring professional judgment under Public Sector Accounting Standards (PSAS).
• Oversee preparation and review of financial statements, notes, schedules, Ministry submissions and other internal and external financial reporting requirements.
• Establish a strong reporting discipline around close, reconciliations, review, documentation, issue escalation and resolution.
• Ensure the Finance team is appropriately prepared for year-end reporting and external audit requirements.
• Provide the CAFO and senior leadership with clear advice regarding significant financial reporting issues, risks and emerging matters.
• Maintain an appropriate balance between the immediate requirement to deliver high-quality financial reporting and the longer-term objective of improving the underlying reporting model.

2. Champion of the Future-State Financial Reporting Operating Model

• Serve as a key executive champion for the design and implementation of ALA's new Financial Reporting Operating Model.
• Assist in translating the future-state vision into practical processes, accountabilities, governance structures, resource requirements and capabilities.
• Challenge legacy practices and identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, automate and strengthen financial reporting.

3. Alberta Public-Sector Financial Leadership

• Bring deep knowledge of the Alberta public-sector financial environment to ALA's financial reporting and decision-making.
• Understand and navigate the relationship between ALA, its Ministry, Health Shared Services, the broader Government of Alberta finance community and other public-sector stakeholders.
• Interpret government financial reporting requirements, policies and expectations and translate them into practical requirements for ALA.

4. Executive Interpretation & Financial Advisory

• Act as a trusted financial interpreter for the CAFO and ALA's senior operational leadership.
• Translate complex accounting, financial reporting and financial-management concepts into clear, practical and decision-useful information for non-financial audiences.
• Provide the CAFO with concise, well-reasoned advice on complex financial issues, including the implications of alternative courses of action.
• Exercise sound judgment in determining when an issue can be resolved within Finance, when operational leadership needs to be involved and when consultation with the Ministry, HSS or other government stakeholders is appropriate.
• Build confidence in Finance as a strategic and constructive business partner while maintaining appropriate professional independence and skepticism.

5. Ministry, Auditor General & Senior Stakeholder Relationships

• Develop and maintain strong, credible and trusted relationships with the Ministry and relevant Government of Alberta finance stakeholders.
• Establish a constructive and professional relationship with the Office of the Auditor General of Alberta and serve as a senior Finance contact for financial reporting matters.
• Build strong working relationships with ALA's senior executives and operational leaders across the organization.
• Develop relationships based on credibility, responsiveness, sound judgment and an understanding of stakeholders' perspectives and needs.

6. Leadership of People & Capability

• Lead, develop and inspire a high-performing Financial Reporting team through a period of significant organizational change.
• Establish clear expectations for accountability, quality, responsiveness, collaboration and professional judgment.
• Provide calm, credible leadership when deadlines are tight, information is incomplete or organizational responsibilities are changing.
• Build a culture that combines technical excellence with practical business partnership.

7. Financial Reporting Risk, Controls & Assurance

• Provide executive oversight of financial reporting risk and the control environment supporting financial reporting.
• Identify significant reporting risks and ensure appropriate mitigation, monitoring and escalation.
• Ensure that control deficiencies or audit findings are understood, assigned, remediated and followed through.

8. Cross-Functional & Organizational Leadership

• Work closely with the Ministry to establish clear expectations for financial information, data quality, reporting inputs, timing, service interfaces and issue resolution.
• Partner with operational leaders to improve the quality, timeliness and understanding of information feeding financial reporting.
• Work effectively across organizational boundaries where ALA owns the reporting outcome but depends on other organizations for source information or transaction processing.

• Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation in good standing, with a bachelor's degree in accounting, finance, business or a related discipline; master's degree is an asset.
• Approximately 10 or more years of progressive post-qualification financial experience, including significant senior financial leadership responsibility.
• Extensive experience in financial reporting, corporate controllership, financial management or a combination of these disciplines.

• Deep experience in the Alberta public sector is strongly preferred, including meaningful exposure to Government of Alberta financial processes, reporting requirements, governance structures and accountability expectations.

• Significant experience working with external auditors and responding to complex audit matters; experience working directly with the Office of the Auditor General of Alberta is highly desirable.
• Experience in healthcare, continuing care, social services, government, a public agency or another complex publicly funded environment is strongly preferred.
• Demonstrated experience leading organizational change, operating-model development, process transformation or significant financial reporting improvement.
• Experience working with shared-service organizations or centralized transaction-processing environments is an asset.
• Demonstrated experience working directly with senior executives and providing advice on complex financial and organizational matters.
• Experience leading, developing and motivating professional finance teams.

jobs.title: Director - Geological Data & Database Management
jobs.description:
**Who We Are**
--------------

  

Founded in 1993, Kinross is a Canadian\-based senior gold mining company with operations and projects in the United States, Brazil, Mauritania, Chile and Canada. Our focus on delivering value is based on our four core values of Putting People First, Outstanding Corporate Citizenship, High Performance Culture, and Rigorous Financial Discipline.

  

Mining responsibly is a priority for Kinross, and we foster a culture that makes responsible mining and operational success inseparable. Our values\-based approach ensures that sustainability and our environmental, social and governance commitments are a core part of our strategy and plans for future growth. In line with our values, we also aim to build meaningful partnerships with all of our stakeholders, including communities, shareholders, employees, governments and suppliers.

  

Kinross maintains listings on the Toronto Stock Exchange (symbol: K) and the New York Stock Exchange (symbol: KGC).

  

**Job Summary**
---------------

  

The Director, Geological Data \& Database Management is a senior technical leadership role accountable for designing, implementing, and governing a company\-wide database management system across all exploration, project, and operating sites. This is a hands\-on leadership position: the Director is responsible for maintaining and updating company standards and ensuring sites adopt/adhere to them, ensuring standardization of database software and structures across all sites, and building and managing a team of database administrators and analysts.

  

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

  

* Ensure standardization of the company geologic database platform across all exploration, project, and operating sites, including migration of legacy and existing site databases where required.
* Maintain database standards for structure, content, and required tables at each project maturity point (Setup, Initial Drilling, Infill, Scoping, PFS, FS, and Operations), and ensure sites are equipped to meet them.
* Lead selection, configuration, and lifecycle management of database software and related tools, in partnership with IT.
* Ensure QA/QC protocols are implemented and auditable per internal standards.
* Establish and audit data security controls across all sites: layered/restricted access by user type, edit tracking and audit trails, and automatic, regular backups including offsite storage.
* Define and enforce the separation between dynamic project databases and frozen, dated resource\-model databases used for reserve/resource work.
* Lead systematic, scheduled reviews of database quality across all sites and drive corrective action plans ahead of each project maturity point.
* Initiate and lead internal and external audits as required.
* Build, lead, and develop the company database management function, including hiring and mentoring site and project database administrators and analysts.
* liase with exploration management, KTS, and site geology teams to ensure database structures support geological, resource, and reserve modelling requirements.
* Develop and deliver training and documented procedures for database administrators, geologists, and technical staff on data entry standards, QA/QC execution, and system use.
* Maintain and continuously improve governing documentation (standards guides, database structure references.)
* Report on database health, compliance, and risk to senior technical and executive leadership.
  
**Qualifications and Skills**
-----------------------------

  

**Education and Experience**


* Bachelor's or Master's degree in Geology, Earth Sciences, Geological Engineering, or a related field.
* 10\+ years of progressive experience in mineral exploration or mining geology, including significant experience in geological database design, administration, or data management.
* 5\+ years in a senior or leadership role managing database systems, technical teams, or data governance programs across multiple sites or projects.
* Demonstrated experience implementing or administering industry\-standard geological database platforms (e.g., acQuire, Fusion, Datashed, or comparable systems) at a multi\-site scale.
  

**Technical \& Leadership Skills**


* Deep understanding of relational database structures as applied to drill hole data (collar, survey, lithology, assay, QA/QC, geotechnical, geometallurgical, density, and related tables).
* Strong knowledge of QA/QC protocols, chain\-of\-custody procedures, and data security/access\-control best practices in a geological or mining context.
* Proven ability to lead large\-scale systems and change management initiatives across geographically distributed sites.
* Excellent people\-leadership skills, with experience building and managing teams, including remote or site\-based staff and dotted\-line reporting relationships.
* Strong communication skills, able to translate technical database requirements for both site\-level technical staff and executive leadership.
* Willingness and ability to travel regularly to exploration, project, and operating sites, including remote locations.
  
**Compensation and Total Rewards**
----------------------------------

  

The base salary range for this role is $180,000 to $220,000 CAD plus a target Short\-Term Incentive bonus of 30%, 30% (LTI) and group benefit coverage. The hiring range reflects our targeted compensation framework for the role. The actual offer will be determined through a comprehensive evaluation of each candidate’s experience, capabilities, and potential impact, along with consideration of internal equity, team structure, and benchmark market data for similar positions. In addition to base salary, Kinross offers a comprehensive total rewards package designed to support employee well\-being, performance, and long\-term development.

Notre logiciel est utilisé par certaines des entreprises d'affichage extérieur les plus prospères et alimente des campagnes percutantes et convaincantes vues partout dans le monde. Venez illuminer le monde en tant que Directeur commercial, Ventes de plateforme !

À quoi s'attendre:

En tant que membre de notre équipe commerciale, le Directeur commercial génère plusieurs sources de revenus en identifiant les besoins des clients et en proposant des solutions issues de la gamme variée de produits de Broadsign. Vous serez responsable du développement des affaires et de la gestion des relations stratégiques avec les parties prenantes clés en Amérique du Nord. Plus précisément, vous prospecterez de nouveaux clients sur votre territoire, animerez des démonstrations de produits et développerez des relations avec des cadres dirigeants de comptes clés afin de négocier des conditions commerciales profitables. Essentiellement, vous guiderez et conseillerez vos clients tout au long du processus de vente afin de leur fournir les meilleures solutions possibles !

Ce dont vous avez besoin pour réussir dans ce poste :

5+ ans d'expérience dans la vente de logiciels B2B d'entreprise, avec gestion complète de quotas et un historique prouvé de dépassement des objectifs
Succès démontré dans l'acquisition de nouveaux clients, incluant la prospection sortante, la génération de pipeline et l'élaboration de plans de comptes ciblés
Expérience dans le développement et la gestion d'un pipeline solide tout en établissant des relations stratégiques de confiance avec des cadres dirigeants
Esprit de collaboration et de travail d'équipe, capable de travailler de manière transversale avec les parties prenantes internes de Broadsign pour fournir des solutions centrées sur le client
Compétences exceptionnelles en résolution de problèmes avec la capacité de penser de manière créative, de s'adapter aux situations imprévues et de travailler avec une grande autonomie
Baccalauréat en administration des affaires, en technologie ou dans un domaine connexe (ou expérience équivalente)
Forte présence de leadership avec une compréhension claire de la valeur du travail d'équipe et de la responsabilité partagée
La maîtrise du français et anglais est un atout majeur
Solide compréhension et application pratique de la méthodologie de vente Challenger Sales
Expérience dans la vente axée sur les plateformes adtech ; une familiarité avec l'industrie de la publicité d'affichage extérieur (OOH) est préférée

Ce que nous offrons :

Avantages complets :
Régime d'assurance complet de l'entreprise (soins de santé, soins dentaires, soins de la vue, voyages) en vigueur dès le premier jour (payé à 100 % par l'employeur). Compte de dépenses de santé (HCSA) annuel de 500 $ pour les frais de santé supplémentaires. Accès illimité à la plateforme virtuelle de soins de santé (Telus Health).
Bien-être :
Fonds de bien-être annuel de 500 $ pour la santé mentale/physique et les dépenses liées au bureau.
Congés payés :
Au moins 3 semaines de vacances, 5 jours flottants, 5 jours de maladie/personnel et 2 jours de bénévolat.
Épargne-retraite :
REER collectif avec un abondement de 50 % par l'employeur jusqu'à concurrence de 4 % du salaire.
Avantages financiers :
Remboursement des frais de transport pour les déplacements vers un bureau de Broadsign et subventions pour les repas (du mardi au jeudi).
Soutien à la famille :
Supplément de salaire pour congé parental.
Possibilités de croissance :
Opportunités de formation et de développement avec un budget annuel pour soutenir le développement professionnel.

Chez Broadsign, nous accordons une grande importance à la diversité des identités sociales qui composent notre communauté. Nous reconnaissons que le talent se présente sous différentes formes et nous encourageons donc les personnes aux parcours et aux expériences différentes à nous présenter leur candidature. jobs.title: Head of Data Systems (Google Stack)
jobs.description:
The Head of Data Systems (Google Stack) will play a key role at Stacktics, required to help create and maintain industry-leading quality and efficiency of service and software delivery.

Stacktics will rely on the Head of Data Systems with ownership of the Data Systems function including mentoring and support for our team of engineers, developers, marketing analysts and data scientists. The successful candidate will be expected to meet and exceed Stacktics' quality standards, while helping the organization rapidly expand into increasingly complex application development, data engineering, and related workflows.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Ownership of Stacktics' Data Systems Business Unit

Build and grow your team's capabilities and expertise to be truly platform-agnostic, ever-adapting based on opportunity and business direction
Lead thorough audits of clients'/prospects' Data Systems, and other associated platforms and technologies as applicable including performance and cloud cost-efficiency
Provide proactive recommendations, identifying areas of opportunity and/or improvement for clients based on their underlying business objectives and goals
Maintain continuous focus on work output quality and reliability, acting as the champion of customer satisfaction in a proactive manner and as the final escalation point for technical and delivery issues that cannot be resolved at the Technical Lead level
Act as Stacktics' primary Data Systems expert, ensuring to maintain and continuously grow personal expertise, and sharing information with other Stacktics team members, client stakeholders and prospects
Collaborate with, support, and work closely with cross-functional units to ensure efficient workflow, and realize cross-functional opportunities and enhancements
Maintain responsibility for the Business Unit's growth and success, continuously developing existing engagements, optimizing resourcing and prospecting
Be dedicated to the success and happiness of your team members, optimizing workflow, enabling their personal growth, and acting as a strong team leader overall

Instilling Development Best Practices and Skills/Procedures Advancement

Establishing, maintaining and evolving DevSecOps best practices and tools, and continuously keeping them aligned with current industry best practices and procedures
Understanding, implementing and automating security controls, governance processes, and compliance validation frameworks
Contributing to deployment tooling within the Stacktics team
Contributing to version control technology frameworks and creating/implementing working processes within the Data Systems team, with tools such as Git or SVN
Own and continuously improve the practice's AI coding standards, the AI coding constitution (CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, .cursorrules), PR checklists, and slash commands keeping them current as tools, clients, and the team's needs evolve

Leading in the Software 3.0 Era

AI tools have changed how fast engineering work gets produced. Your job is to make sure that speed shows up as sounder architecture and higher-quality delivery — not just faster shipping of the same judgment gaps.
Recalibrate how the team scopes and estimates work as AI tooling changes what can actually be delivered in a sprint, so timelines and resourcing plans reflect real AI-era delivery speed
Set architecture and coding standards that assume engineers are using AI assistants daily — code review habits, eval frameworks, and quality gates sized to the failure modes of AI-assisted development, not just its speed
Continue evolving Stacktics' AI Development Lifecycle (ADLC) — our AI-native answer to SDLC — piloting new stages against real engagements and driving adoption across the team
Be an active daily user of AI coding assistants yourself, and bring that firsthand experience into how standards and review practices are set for the team
Lead Stacktics’ technical team members through the integration into Agentic AI-first working patterns, and beyond

Code Productization

Migrating the delivery of the most common/universally applicable solutions from custom projects to formally productized software solutions
Advocating for building repeatability, scalability and standardization into how the Stacktics Data Systems team approaches all work, in order to enable the future migration to productization as a general rule

Data Engineering-Specific Responsibilities

Participate in continuous delivery pipelines to fully automate deployment of the highly available cloud platform that supports multiple projects
Design and develop ETL workflows and datasets to be used in data visualization tools
Write complex SQL queries with multiple joins to automate and manipulate data extracts
Perform end to end Data Validation to maintain accuracy of data sets
Build tools for deployment, monitoring and operations
Troubleshoot and resolve issues in the development, test and production environments
Develop re-usable processes that can be leveraged and standardized for multiple instances
Prepare technical specifications and documentation for projects
Stay up to date on relevant technologies, plug into user groups, understand trends and opportunities to ensure we are using the best possible techniques and tools
Understand, implement, and automate security controls, governance processes, and compliance validation

Contribution to Corporate Strategy

Actively and proactively play a key role in steering Stacktics and affiliated companies, considering market developments, competitive maneuvers, unique opportunities, etc.
You will be expected to both bring new ideas to the table and assist other corporate leaders in vetting/developing concepts and tactics
Identification and tracking of performance, coaching, training needs, and motivating members of the Data Systems team — including Senior Technical Leads. Directly or indirectly responsible for hiring, terminating and owning performance evaluations for direct reports and the Data Systems group

Company-Wide Responsibilities

Maintain and exceed client satisfaction with Stacktics’ deliverables, day-to-day work and overall value as a partner
Adapt to ever-changing client needs and expectations
Maintain dedication toward achieving excellence in Stacktics’ delivery against client needs, and overall success as an organization
Ability to provide clear guidance and support for advanced problem solving and system design to large teams at enterprise-level client companies, aiding the evolution of their digital practices

QUALIFICATIONS

Deep expertise in building and managing large-scale data systems on cloud platforms, with a strong preference for Google Cloud Platform (GCP) services
Python, SQL and Cloud Computing
10+ years experience in Data Engineering, including 6+ years in technical leadership or management roles, with experience managing other leads (e.g., Technical Leads or engineering managers).
Strong understanding of and direct experience with managing a team operating in a “Software 3.0” model (Agentic AI-first)
Active user of AI coding assistants (Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code, or equivalent), and fluent in what they change about estimation, architecture, and review
Understanding of digital ecosystems including online data collection, cloud systems and analytics tools (Google Stack, Facebook, Salesforce, Adobe Suite etc.) a strong asset
Strong technical understanding of a range of marketing concepts such as cookie-based data collection, setting and leveraging audience segments, attribution modelling, AB/N & multivariate is an asset
Excellent written & verbal communication skills are essential; candidate should be comfortable presenting and participating in group discussions of concepts with internal and external stakeholders
Candidate must exhibit an analytical, detail-oriented approach to problem solving
Experience with Jira / Atlassian project management tools is an asset

Preferred Qualifications

Google Cloud certifications (e.g., Professional Cloud Architect, Professional Data Engineer) are a strong plus.
Prior experience in a consulting environment, managing and delivering projects for multiple clients concurrently.

jobs.title: Director, Systems & Data Transformation
jobs.description:
HSB Canada, part of Munich Re, is Canada’s premier engineering-driven specialty insurer—bringing deep technical expertise to help clients stay ahead of complex, emerging, and technology-based risks. We blend specialty insurance with inspection, engineering, and technology-enhanced services to redefine what risk protection can be, with leading capabilities across areas such as cyber, equipment breakdown, renewable energy, and IoT technology services.

Backed by Munich Re, one of the world’s most experienced and financially stable insurance and reinsurance groups, HSB Canada combines global strength with deep knowledge of the Canadian market. Building on a long legacy of innovation and technical excellence, we continue to evolve our capabilities to address modern and emerging risks—from cyber and artificial intelligence to connected technologies.

Primary Objectives

The Director, Systems & Data Transformation is accountable for shaping and executing HSB Canada’s enterprise systems, data, and digital transformation agenda. Acting as a strategic partner to the CEO and Executive Leadership Team, the Director translates business priorities into an integrated multi-year roadmap, leads complex cross-functional programs, and delivers measurable improvements in growth, customer and broker experience, operational effectiveness, decision-making, and risk management.

The role provides strategic and operational leadership for the transformation and optimization of the Guidewire ecosystem and its surrounding applications, integrations, data platforms, and controls, ensuring reliable and scalable support for policy, billing, claims, underwriting, and insurance operations.

The Director also leads the delivery of major business-facing capabilities, including Quote, Bind and Issue (QBI), underwriting workflow, digital experiences, enterprise data products, analytics, and responsible AI solutions, in close partnership with business, technology, operations, risk, and global stakeholders.

Success requires an enterprise-minded leader who can connect strategy, architecture, data, delivery, change management, and operational execution; build high-performing multidisciplinary teams; and establish the governance, partnerships, and performance disciplines needed to sustain transformation outcomes.

Job Responsibilities

Transformation Strategy & Portfolio Delivery
Define and maintain an integrated, multi-year systems, data, and digital transformation strategy aligned with enterprise priorities and target business outcomes
Own the transformation portfolio from business case and prioritization through delivery, adoption, value realization, and transition to operations
Establish portfolio governance, roadmaps, investment plans, budgets, resource capacity, milestones, benefits, and executive reporting
Manage cross-program dependencies, delivery risks, organizational constraints, and competing priorities; escalate decisions with clear options and recommendations
Define measurable outcomes and key performance indicators, using performance insights to continuously improve delivery and business value
Core Systems Transformation & Guidewire Leadership
Set the strategy and roadmap for the specialty insurance technology ecosystem, balancing modernization, resilience, scalability, security, cost, and speed to market
Provide accountable leadership for the Guidewire platform and surrounding applications, including architecture, configuration, integrations, data flows, environments, releases, and lifecycle management
Lead major core-platform initiatives, including ClaimCenter transformation, while maintaining service continuity, production stability, support readiness, and effective control design
Digital Insurance & QBI Transformation
Lead end-to-end delivery of Quote, Bind and Issue capabilities and underwriting workflow improvements in partnership with underwriting, product, operations, distribution, and technology teams
Establish a scalable, reusable QBI architecture that supports multiple specialty products, distribution channels, evolving underwriting models, and integration with core platforms
Champion underwriter-centered design, process simplification, automation, and adoption to improve experience, quality, and cycle time
Data Science & Responsible AI
Define and mature HSB Canada’s enterprise data and data science capabilities, including data strategy, governance, quality, architecture, platforms, and reusable data products
Partner with business leaders to identify and deliver AI use cases across underwriting, claims, operations, finance, and distribution
Ensure data and AI solutions are explainable, secure, measurable, and embedded into business processes and decisions
Operating Model & People Leadership
Build, lead, coach, and retain a high-performing multidisciplinary team spanning business systems analysis, product and application leadership, data engineering, analytics, and data science
Define clear mandates, decision rights, accountabilities, delivery standards, and career pathways; create a culture of ownership, collaboration, inclusion, innovation, and continuous learning
Develop workforce and sourcing strategies that balance internal capability, global partnerships, and external expertise while managing capacity and succession risk
Advisory, Change Leadership & Influence
Serve as a trusted advisor translating complex system and data topics into clear choices, trade-offs, recommendations, and decisions
Build alignment across Canadian and global stakeholders, facilitate executive governance, and communicate progress, risks, investment needs, and realized outcomes with clarity
Lead organizational change and adoption for new capabilities, and bring external perspective, emerging practices, and market insight to continuously evolve HSB Canada’s business and technology environment

Qualifications

University-level education in computer science, business administration, risk management, or equivalent professional experience
8–12 years demonstrated experience in business, technology, or product roles; insurance or broader financial services
Structured, hypothesis-driven problem solving: ability to frame ambiguity, develop options, assess trade-offs, and drive to clear decisions.
Strong analytical capability: extracting insights from data and market research and translate them into strategy and action.
Multi-workstream leadership: proven ability to manage multiple initiatives in parallel while maintaining quality, pace, and stakeholder alignment.
Executive communication: ability to produce crisp, compelling materials and present complex topics simply and persuasively to senior audiences.
Strong P&C insurance (or broader financial services) product knowledge—coverage/wordings, underwriting appetite, pricing fundamentals, and regulatory considerations is an asset
Experience building ecosystems/partnerships (vendors, data providers, technology partners) to enable product and service innovation is an asset

Company Benefits:

Together, we engage with everything we have and are, to help humankind act braver and better. Go further with HSB.

We are pleased to offer our employees great benefits and resources to support their mental, physical and financial wellbeing. These include:

An engaging and collaborative environment that promotes continuous learning and development
A hybrid work environment that combines weekly in-office and remote days
A great compensation package including an annual company bonus
Competitive company-paid flexible health and dental benefits, starting on your first day
Flexible dollars provided by the company to put towards a Health Spending Account and/or Wellness Spending Account
Wellness program with tools and resources supporting your mental, physical, and financial wellbeing – on and off the job
Participation in the DC Pension Plan with a progressive employer contribution scale based on tenure starting at 4%, plus optional company match in the RRSP plan
Generous time off including vacation, personal days, unplanned time, Statutory Holidays and company-wide early closure half-days
Learning and development programs and resources, including unlimited access to LinkedIn Learning, Education Assistance Program, and reimbursement for professional fees
Employee Referral Program and Recognition Program

Our base salary range for this role is between $159000 to $186000 per year, plus an opportunity for an annual company bonus based upon a percentage of eligible pay. The salary estimate displayed represents the typical salary range for candidates hired in this position. Factors that may be used to determine your actual salary include your specific skills, how many years of experience you have and comparison to internal equity.

This role is located in our Toronto office on 390 Bay St, and we operate in a hybrid work model. This job posting is for an existing vacancy.

We do not use AI in our recruitment process - applications are reviewed by our team to ensure a fair and personalized experience.

HSB Canada is committed to providing a work environment that is inclusive and free of employment barriers and discrimination. Accommodations will be made for qualified applicants with a disability throughout the recruitment process. If you receive a request for an interview and you have a disability which will require an accommodation to support your participation, please consult with Human Resources or contact hr@hsb.ca as soon as practical so that suitable accommodations can be arranged.

We thank all candidates for their interest; however only those selected for interview will be contacted.

jobs.title: Data Science Chief Expert, CX
jobs.description:
We help the world run better

At SAP, we keep it simple: you bring your best to us, and we'll bring out the best in you. We're builders touching over 20 industries and 80% of global commerce, and we need your unique talents to help shape what's next. The work is challenging – but it matters. You'll find a place where you can be yourself, prioritize your wellbeing, and truly belong. What's in it for you? Constant learning, skill growth, great benefits, and a team that wants you to grow and succeed.

The context engine that makes AI enterprise ready.

Anyone can build an AI agent. What makes SAP's agents different is accuracy grounded in the richest enterprise data and process context in the world. As part of our Data and Applied Science team, you'll build the context engine grounded in SAP’s Business ontology: the semantic infrastructure that transforms raw business data into the knowledge layer powering SAP's AI agents and assistants.

What You'll Build

The Data and Applied Science team will build the semantic and contextual foundation of SAP's AI. While generic AI agents operate on surface-level patterns, SAP agents are accurate because they understand the real semantics of enterprise business master data, process flows, and domain relationships. You will help build and scale the layer that makes that possible. This may include the following:

Leverage deep SAP data and process understanding — including SAP data models, metadata structures, and end-to-end business process semantics across Order-to-Cash, Procure-to-Pay, Record-to-Report, and Plan-to-Produce — to build AI and semantic data solutions using SAP master data domains, SAP One Domain Model, SAP Graph API, and SAP Business Accelerator Hub assets.
Design and maintain enterprise ontologies and semantic models to improve interoperability, entity consistency, and business context across SAP and non-SAP data landscapes, harmonizing sources such as Salesforce, Workday, ServiceNow, MES/IoT systems, and external data providers into unified semantic or analytical layers.
Work with cloud and data platforms such as Databricks, SAP Datasphere, SAP HANA Cloud, AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud Platform to support reliable AI workflows.
Translate ambiguous business challenges into concrete AI use cases, technical designs, and measurable business outcomes.
Design, develop, evaluate, and operationalize end-to-end machine learning and AI solutions — from data preprocessing, feature engineering, experimentation, and validation through to deployment, production handoff, lifecycle support, and continuous improvement.
Apply advanced methods across machine learning, deep learning, statistical modeling, data mining, optimization, and applied AI to solve enterprise-scale problems.
Develop AI capabilities — including generative AI and LLM-based solutions — using enterprise business data, knowledge graphs, business process intelligence, and other structured and unstructured data assets.
Partner closely with product, engineering, business, and customer-facing teams to ensure solutions are scalable, practical, and production-ready.

What You'll Bring

Required Qualifications

Master's degree or PhD in Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, Statistics, Engineering, or related quantitative fields.
10+ years of experience to include deep expertise in machine learning, deep learning, statistical modeling, generative AI, and LLMs, with hands-on experience developing, evaluating, and improving models using real-world datasets — including data preprocessing, feature engineering, and experimentation — and strong analytical and mathematical modeling skills.
10+ years of experience in machine learning, data science, applied AI, AI research, knowledge engineering, or semantic data systems in industry, research labs, or advanced academic environments.
Strong Python and SQL skills, including production-grade Python development and experience with ML libraries such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, and scikit-learn.
Demonstrated experience of deploying, shipping, and operating AI or machine learning solutions in production environments, including production handoff and lifecycle support.
Experience with big data infrastructure, data processing and transformation tools such as Databricks, and cloud environments such as AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud Platform.
Excellent communication, collaboration, and customer-facing skills, with significant experience in agile development environments and a strong curiosity for exploring new AI techniques and their practical applications for SAP customers and products.
Deep working knowledge of SAP data models, metadata structures, and core business processes end-to-end, including how process semantics map to underlying business objects and datasets.
Hands-on experience with the SAP data and AI platform stack — including SAP Datasphere, SAP HANA Cloud Knowledge Graph Engine, SAP Business Data Cloud, SAP One Domain Model, SAP Graph API, and SAP Business Accelerator Hub — with working knowledge of SAP master data domains and Master Data Governance constructs.
Hands-on experience designing and maintaining enterprise ontologies using OWL, RDF/RDFS, SKOS, and SHACL, with proficiency in SPARQL, Cypher, and GQL, and experience evaluating trade-offs between RDF triple stores and labeled property graph databases.
Experience building entity resolution, deduplication, and identity stitching pipelines across SAP and non-SAP systems, with proven ability to harmonize data into a unified semantic layer using federation, virtualization, replication, and shared ontology mapping approaches.
Understanding data product and data mesh principles, including semantic contracts and governed self-service consumption.
Proven experience translating abstract business challenges into concrete AI solutions, delivering from concept through production deployment, production handoff, and business adoption.
Experience working with cross-functional stakeholders — including product, engineering, business, and customer-facing teams — in agile software development environments and enterprise product organizations.
Experience building AI capabilities using enterprise business data, knowledge graphs, or business process intelligence.

Preferred Qualification

Experience with Retrieval-Augmented Generation, vector databases, embeddings, semantic retrieval, and enterprise knowledge grounding.
Experience contributing to reusable AI platforms, foundation model initiatives, shared AI services, or AI capabilities adopted across multiple product areas.
Experience with agentic AI, reasoning frameworks, planning, orchestration, tool use, or multi-agent architectures.
Ability to design upper-level and mid-level ontologies aligned with industry standards, map application-specific schemas to shared ontologies using declarative mapping standards and apply semantic interoperability frameworks and canonical business entity models across complex application landscapes.

Where You Belong

Join a collaborative, forward-thinking team defining how enterprise AI actually works on a global scale. You'll work alongside curious engineers, thoughtful product minds, and applied researchers all focused on building AI that customers can trust in the highest-stakes business processes. There's room to grow into new technical spaces, ship real impact, and shape SAP's AI future. If you value learning, real ownership, and building foundational infrastructure that matters, you'll feel at home here.

Bring out your best

SAP innovations help more than four hundred thousand customers worldwide work together more efficiently and use business insight more effectively. Originally known for leadership in enterprise resource planning (ERP) software, SAP has evolved to become a market leader in end-to-end business application software and related services for database, analytics, intelligent technologies, and experience management. As a cloud company with two hundred million users and more than one hundred thousand employees worldwide, we are purpose-driven and future-focused, with a highly collaborative team ethic and commitment to personal development. SAP’s culture of inclusion, focus on health and well-being, and flexible working models help ensure that everyone – regardless of background – feels included and can run at their best. At SAP, we believe we are made stronger by the unique capabilities and qualities that each person brings to our company, and we invest in our employees to inspire confidence and help everyone realize their full potential. jobs.title: Director, Product Marketing, AI Solutions
jobs.description:
About Us

Sophos is a cybersecurity leader defending 600,000 organizations globally with an AI-driven platform and expert-led services. Sophos meets organizations wherever they are in their security maturity and grows with them to defeat cyberattacks. Its solutions combine machine learning, automation, and real-time threat intelligence with frontline human expertise from Sophos X-Ops to deliver advanced, 24/7 threat monitoring, detection, and response.

Sophos offers industry-leading managed detection and response (MDR) alongside a comprehensive portfolio of cybersecurity technologies — including endpoint, network, email, and cloud security, extended detection and response (XDR), identity threat detection and response (ITDR), and next-gen SIEM. Together with expert advisory services, these capabilities help organizations proactively reduce risk and respond faster, with the visibility and scalability needed to stay ahead of evolving threats.

Sophos goes to market with a global partner ecosystem, including Managed Service Providers (MSPs), Managed Security Service Providers (MSSPs), resellers and distributors, marketplace integrations, and cyber risk partners, giving organizations the flexibility to choose trusted relationships when securing their business. Sophos is headquartered in Oxford, U.K. More information is available at www.sophos.com .

Role Summary

As Director of Product Marketing for AI Solutions, you will lead go-to-market strategy, positioning, and messaging for Sophos' AI security portfolio and the emerging categories reshaping how defenders operate, including Sophos AI Defense and Fusion AI.

This is a build-and-launch role, working across product management, Sophos X-Ops research, sales enablement, demand generation, and channel marketing to turn technical innovation into pipeline and customer outcomes. You must be AI-native in how you work, using AI as a multiplier for your own judgment to research faster, draft sharper, and ship at the pace the market demands.

In your capacity as an Individual Contributor within the Sophos Product Marketing team, you will work closely with your Product Marketing colleagues to develop the AI narratives for our broader solution portfolio, including AI-augmented MDR, AI-native detection and response, and protections built for an AI-accelerated threat landscape.

What You Will Own

Positioning and Messaging

Own positioning and messaging for Sophos' AI solutions portfolio, including the new and emerging categories where Sophos is defining the market.
Build the category narrative around AI-native cybersecurity defense, anchored in Sophos' position that AI handles scale and humans handle judgment and accountability.
Guide the AI-related messaging for the broader Sophos portfolio, ensuring consistency at every point.
Translate deep technical capability into clear, differentiated, channel-ready stories that resonate with security buyers, MSPs, and end customers.
Develop and maintain the messaging frameworks, value propositions, competitive positioning, and proof points that ladder to the broader Sophos narrative.

Launch and GTM Execution

Lead end-to-end go-to-market planning for new AI solutions and category launches, from internal readiness through external announcement, partner enablement, and demand generation.
Partner with Product Management to shape launch scope, sequencing, and tiering decisions that align market readiness with product reality.

The Director leads the modernization of Bird's data platform and analytics ecosystem, establishes scalable AI and automation capabilities, and advances enterprise data governance, data quality, stewardship, and data fluency. Working with executive sponsors, business leaders, Cybersecurity, Privacy, Enterprise Architecture, and delivery teams, this role ensures data and AI capabilities are trusted, secure, adopted, and measurable in business value.

Develop and execute Bird's enterprise Data, AI, Analytics, and Automation strategy, aligned with corporate objectives and the priorities of the Business Systems leadership team, translating business strategy into measurable outcomes across decision-making, operational excellence, and innovation.
Establish and maintain a multi-year roadmap and prioritized portfolio for data modernization, AI adoption, analytics, automation services, and information governance — sequencing initiatives by business value, risk, feasibility, and adoption readiness, and reporting quantified value realization to executive leadership.
Lead the modernization and operation of Bird's enterprise data platform, including lakehouse, Azure Databricks, semantic models, enterprise data models, metadata, data pipelines, and analytics architecture, in partnership with Business Subject Matter Experts, Data Architects, and Business Analysts.

jobs.description:
**POSITION SUMMARY**

Community Living Cambridge (CLC) is dedicated to supporting individuals with developmental disabilities by providing meaningful opportunities and experiences, while upholding their rights, confidentiality, and dignity in alignment with CLC’s mission, vision, and values.

As a key member of the Executive Team, the **Director of Finance Services** provides strategic leadership and fosters a collaborative approach to all financial and revenue\-generating activities. This role ensures the organization’s financial operations comply with all legislative, regulatory, and funding requirements.

The **Director of Finance Services** oversees a wide range of financial functions, including cost and general accounting, budgeting, cashflow and investment management, payroll, accounts payable and receivable, financial analysis, and risk management support, Information Technology, capital assets, internal and external financial reporting, Operations Analysis on vehicle fleet management, compliance with Ministry of Children, Community and Social Services (MCCSS) and risk management.

This is a pivotal leadership position and is responsible for driving revenue generation strategies, optimizing financial models, and enhancing the sustainability and profitability of the organization.

The **Director of Finance Services** collaborates closely with the Executive Director and cross\-functional leaders and teams to align financial goals with CLC’s broader strategic objectives, while cultivating a culture of accountability and performance excellence.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

\* Provide stewardship to the organization in the management of its assets and resources, achieved through the effective use of strong internal controls and compliance with all internal and external reporting obligations

\* Participate as an active member of the Organization’s Senior Management Team

\* Translate complex financial data into actionable insights for organizational leadership, board and committees.

*\** Regularly present financial information to the Board of Directors, Finance Committee and others

\* Planning, directing, coordinating and evaluating all accounting operational functions regularly focusing on the efficiency of business processes and applying improvements, including developing long and short\-term organizational strategies

\* Complete any necessary documentation and reporting required by the *Ministry of Children, Community and Social Services ‘MCCSS’*

\* Review financial statements jointly prepared with the Associate Director, once drafted review with the Executive Director and Treasurer as well as monthly reporting and forecasting to the Board of Directors

\* Lead and facilitate the annual budgeting process, present a draft budget to the Executive Director and once finalized present to the Board of Directors

\* Provide direct managerial support to the Associate Director of Finance and Administration and IT Specialist

\* Establish and maintain effective working relationships with staff at all levels, funders, MCCSS and other external stakeholders to advance financial activities

\* Be an active member of the negotiating team during collective bargaining and participate in CLC meetings where financial support or advice may be helpful

\* Complete supported individual personal financial audits and prepare reports for Associate Directors particularly discrepancies and errors, following that report to the Board of Directors quarterly.

\* Manage procurement processes, oversee all mortgages, vehicle fleet, leases, investments, purchasing and coordinate material and resources allocation

\* Responsible for the oversight into all aspects of information technology, cybersecurity, systems and processes within the organization

\* Recommend, develop and implement financial policies and practices that align with the overall strategic plan and fiscal integrity

\* Act as the Executive Lead for the annual financial audit and ensure all information is prepared in advance and make adjustments as necessary during the process.

\* Ensure adequate insurance coverage on all buildings, equipment and vehicles along with general and liability requirements to protect CLC, the Board of Directors and employees.

\* Analyze market trends and competitive landscape to identify new revenue opportunities and optimize existing revenue streams

\* Develop and execute comprehensive revenue growth strategies focusing on short and long\-term opportunities for increasing revenue

·\* Work closely with cross\-functional teams to ensure alignment between revenue goals and CLC objectives while fostering a culture of accountability and performance excellence.

\* Be thoroughly familiar with and abide by the CLC health and safety policy and procedures, using safe practices at all times and reporting all unsafe conditions, accidents, hazards and practices to management immediately

\* Attend all required training sessions and complete regular recertification programs before expiration (e.g., First Aid \& CPR, Safe Management/Non\-violent crisis intervention, etc.).

\* Be knowledgeable with program specific and CLC policies, procedures and collective agreement and work within applicable frameworks

\* Must be able to perform the essential duties of the position

\* Perform other duties as required

The **Director of Finance Services** must be able to successfully adapt or adjust to continually changing priorities within CLC.

**Pressures:** As this is an executive\-level job, stress is an inherent part of the role. Being able to manage these sometimes\-significant levels of stress is considered an essential duty of the role.

**Working Hours**: The **Director of Finance Services** must be flexible around working hours and be available to work evenings and weekends when needed.

**Location:** This position will work out of CLC Headquarters and local agency designations.

jobs.description:
In your role as a Director, Business Technology and AI
at The North West Company (TNWC); you will be responsible for ensuring technology investments across the organization are prioritized effectively, governed appropriately, and deliver measurable business value.

This role serves as the single enterprise interface between business and IT and owns the end‑to‑end technology demand lifecycle—from idea intake through prioritization, governance, delivery alignment, and value realization.

Joining TNWC gives you the opportunity for development throughout the company, a competitive salary and benefits package, and to be part of a dynamic and diverse culture.

TNWC is a leading retailer to under-served rural communities and urban neighborhood markets in the following regions: Northern Canada, Western Canada, rural Alaska, the South Pacific islands, and the Caribbean. Our stores offer a broad range of products and services with an emphasis on food. Our value offer is to be the best local shopping choice for everyday household and local lifestyle needs. Check out northwest.ca for more information.

Your Role:

Act as the primary Business Relationship Manager (BRM) for all business units, building trusted relationships with executive leaders and serving as the single point of intake for all technology demand.
Partner with business leaders to translate strategic priorities into technology initiatives with defined outcomes, quantified value, clear ownership, and alignment to enterprise objectives.
Lead enterprise demand shaping and prioritization, challenging requests and facilitating trade-off discussions to optimize enterprise value, resource utilization, and strategic alignment.
Own and continuously enhance the enterprise demand management and portfolio governance framework, ensuring transparent and consistent investment decision-making across the organization.
Evaluate and prioritize technology investments across AI and non-AI initiatives, SaaS solutions, enterprise platforms, and custom development opportunities, considering value, risk, complexity, readiness, and capacity.
Maintain a cohesive enterprise technology portfolio by identifying and reducing duplication, fragmentation, shadow IT, and uncoordinated technology investments.
Define, maintain, and evolve the enterprise AI strategy and roadmap, identifying high-value opportunities that support business objectives and competitive advantage.
Establish and oversee AI governance processes to ensure responsible AI adoption and compliance with privacy, security, legal, regulatory, ethical, and risk management requirements.
Lead the governance of enterprise SaaS investments, including demand intake, business case evaluation, prioritization, rationalization, lifecycle oversight, and renewal decision support.
Ensure SaaS solutions have accountable business ownership, measurable value, alignment with enterprise architecture, and appropriate consideration of integration, data, security, and change impacts.
Continuously monitor emerging AI technologies, market trends, vendor capabilities, industry use cases, and regulatory developments, translating insights into actionable recommendations and innovation opportunities.
Partner with architecture, delivery, data, security, procurement, and business teams to ensure technology initiatives are executed in alignment with approved business outcomes and enterprise standards.
Monitor adoption, performance, and realized value of technology investments, providing recommendations to accelerate, redirect, continue, or discontinue initiatives based on business results.
Serve as the primary escalation point for cross-functional technology investment conflicts, facilitating alignment and enterprise-wide decision-making.
Drive organizational maturity in technology demand management, portfolio governance, AI adoption, and value realization through stakeholder engagement, change leadership, and capability development.
Build and foster a network of business partners, technology champions, and AI advocates to support innovation, adoption, and continuous improvement across the enterprise.

Bachelor's degree in Business, Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field; Master's degree considered an asset.

Strong understanding of technology investment management, business case development, benefits realization, and value measurement.
Experience governing enterprise SaaS portfolios, including demand intake, rationalization, vendor evaluation, and lifecycle management.
Proven ability to build trusted relationships with senior leaders and influence decision-making across business and technology functions.
Strong knowledge of enterprise technology delivery, architecture, data strategy, cybersecurity, privacy, risk, and regulatory considerations.
Exceptional strategic thinking, analytical, facilitation, negotiation, and conflict resolution skills.
Demonstrated success leading organizational change, driving technology adoption, and delivering measurable business outcomes in a matrixed environment.
Professional certifications such as BRMP, CBRM, ITIL, COBIT, TOGAF, PMP, Prosci, or AI Governance/Responsible AI certifications are considered assets.

jobs.description:
Company Description

AmpsPump is developing a Canadian-designed EV charging platform that combines modular infrastructure, battery energy storage, edge AI and intelligent energy management. Our architecture is designed to deliver reliable high-power charging while managing grid constraints and improving station economics.
With Canadian manufacturing planned, AmpsPump is preparing to commercialize a repeatable, containerized station model for retail locations, fleet operations and high-demand travel corridors. We are building the team to take this platform from initial deployment to broader expansion in North America, Europe and beyond.
Role Description

AmpsPump is seeking a Chief Financial Officer for a full-time role based in Toronto, Ontario, with flexibility for hybrid working arrangements.
The CFO will partner with the Chairman and executive team to lead financial strategy, support capital raising and establish the financial infrastructure required for growth. This is a hands-on leadership opportunity for someone comfortable building a finance function in an early-stage business with significant infrastructure and technology ambitions.
Key responsibilities include:
Lead financial planning, budgeting, forecasting and cash management, with close attention to liquidity, deployment milestones and capital requirements.
Lead the financial aspects of equity fundraising, including financial models, investor materials, due diligence and investor reporting.
Develop corporate and site-level financing structures, including equipment financing, project debt and other sources of capital.
Evaluate station economics, capital expenditure, pricing, partnerships and expansion opportunities.
Identify and coordinate applications for relevant grants, incentives and other funding programs.
Establish financial reporting, internal controls, accounting policies and tax compliance across the corporate group.
Select and implement financial systems, and build the finance team as the business grows.
Manage relationships with investors, lenders, auditors, tax advisers and other external stakeholders.
Support board reporting and strategic decisions with clear financial analysis.

Qualifications

Demonstrated senior finance leadership experience in a growing business, including experience building financial systems, processes and teams.
A track record of supporting or leading equity fundraising and securing debt or equipment financing.
Strong financial modelling skills, including cash flow forecasting, investment analysis and scenario planning.
Experience with infrastructure deployment, capital-intensive projects or businesses combining hardware and recurring revenue.
Strong command of financial reporting, consolidation, internal controls and Canadian tax and accounting requirements.
Commercial judgment and the ability to translate complex financial information into clear recommendations.
Willingness to work directly on detailed financial and operational matters while providing strategic leadership.
Experience in energy, EV charging, infrastructure, manufacturing or technology is an asset.
Experience in franchising is an asset.
Experience with cross-border operations, government funding programs or public-company reporting is an asset.
CPA designation preferred.
A collaborative leadership style, sound judgment and a high standard of professional integrity.
