jobs.description:
About Citco

JOB DESCRIPTION

The market leader. The premier provider. The best in the business. At Citco, we’ve been the front-runner in our field since our incorporation in 1948 led to the evolution of the asset servicing sector itself. This pioneering spirit continues to guide us today as we innovate and expand, push beyond the boundaries of our industry, and shape its future. From working exclusively with hedge funds to serving all alternatives, corporations and private clients, our organization has grown immensely across asset classes and geographies. For us, this progress is a pattern that we’ll only maintain as we move forward, always prioritizing our performance. So for those who want to play at the top of their game and be at the vanguard of their space, we say: Welcome to Citco.

About The Team & Business Line

Fund Administration is Citco’s core business, and our alternative asset and accounting service is one of the industry’s most respected. Our continuous investment in learning and technology solutions means our people are equipped to deliver a seamless client experience.

Strategic Operations is a dedicated function within Private Assets. It brings transformation delivery, project execution, business analysis, operational initiatives and implementation support into one team, reducing the delivery burden on BAU Operations and maintaining ownership from design through adoption.

The group will be split across three distinct focus areas, aligned under two individual leaders:

Operating Model, Product & Client Solutions: led by the Operating Model & Product leader, this area will define how services should run end to end, shape scalable products and solutions, support complex client implementations, and ensure client commitments are operationally deliverable.

Data, Reporting & Platform Enablement: led by the Technology, Data & Delivery leader, this area will define Operations requirements for data, reporting and platforms, strengthen data quality and lineage, and carry solutions through testing, deployment and adoption.

Digital Workflow, Automation & AI: also led by the Technology, Data & Delivery leader, this area will identify and deliver workflow, automation and AI opportunities, establish appropriate controls, and measure whether the expected benefits are realised.

The group works in close partnership with Operations, the Transformation Office, IT, Tactical Operations and Marquee Client teams. Roles may be permanent or approximately 12-month rotational assignments anchored in strategic locations. Rotational colleagues will join from the business, help shape and deliver change, and return to the line with broader project experience.

Responsibilities

Your Role

You will lead the Operations data, reporting and platform agenda for Private Assets — setting requirements with IT and the Transformation Office, and delivering alongside them.
Own the Operations view of the data and reporting roadmap, including data quality, lineage, ownership and reporting capability.
Set out Operations’ requirements with IT and the Transformation Office, then deliver alongside them rather than handing over.
Lead platform enablement work — ensuring platform change is specified, tested and adopted with Operations in the room throughout.
Establish reporting standards and reusable data products rather than one-off extracts.
Provide the data and evidence base that other focus areas rely on to quantify a problem and measure a benefit.
Coordinate across Operations, IT, the Transformation Office, Tactical Operations and Data Services.
Lead and mentor focus area resources, including rotational colleagues joining from the business.
Report on progress, risks, dependencies and benefits realisation to the relevant leader and senior stakeholders.

Qualifications

About You

You have 12–15 years’ experience in private assets or a comparable financial services environment, with substantial exposure to data and platform initiatives.
Proven delivery of data, reporting or platform programmes, including requirements definition and UAT ownership.
Strong technical knowledge of private assets accounting and operations, and of the data those processes produce and consume.
Practical understanding of data models, lineage, controls and reporting architecture.
Credibility with technology partners — able to challenge a design and hold a delivery date.
Strong leadership skills and supervisory experience of other professionals, including rotational colleagues joining from the business.
Skilled in business planning, budgeting and stakeholder negotiation.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Advanced computer skills (Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint and SharePoint).
Bachelor’s Degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics or a related field; professional accounting designation a plus.

What We Expect Of The Strategic Operations Team

Regardless of role or focus area, everyone in Strategic Operations is expected to demonstrate the following:
Deep technical and operational knowledge — genuine depth in how our processes, data and platforms actually work — the detail that only comes from having run the work.
Curiosity — the instinct to ask why a process looks the way it does, to challenge the answer, and to keep asking whether there is a better way.
A transformational mindset — comfortable redesigning end to end rather than patching, and prepared to see change through past go-live to the point where it is genuinely adopted.
Ownership through to adoption — accountability does not end at delivery; success is measured by whether the change sticks in the business.
Commercial and client awareness — an understanding of what we can genuinely run, so that what we commit to a client is deliverable.
Global mindset — working across regions, jurisdictions and time zones, and designing solutions that scale beyond a single desk, client or location.
Ambition to shape Citco’s future — an appetite to help build the operating model we will run for years, and to be measured on whether it works.

This position is not for an existing vacancy; we are building a candidate pool for future opportunities.

Our Benefits

Your well-being is of paramount importance to us, and central to our success. We provide a range of benefits, training and education support, and flexible working arrangements to help you achieve success in your career while balancing personal needs. Ask us about specific benefits in your location.

We embrace diversity, prioritizing the hiring of people from diverse backgrounds. Our inclusive culture is a source of pride and strength, fostering innovation and mutual respect.

Citco welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available upon request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection.

At Citco, we’ve been the front-runner in our field since our incorporation in 1948 led to the evolution of the asset servicing sector itself. This pioneering spirit continues to guide us today as we innovate and expand, push beyond the boundaries of our industry, and shape its future. From working exclusively with hedge funds to serving all alternatives, corporations and private clients, our organization has grown immensely across asset classes and geographies. For us, this progress is a pattern that we’ll only maintain as we move forward, always prioritizing our performance. So for those who want to play at the top of their game and be at the vanguard of their space, we say: Welcome to Citco.

About The Team & Business Line

Fund Administration is Citco’s core business, and our alternative asset and accounting service is one of the industry’s most respected. Our continuous investment in learning and technology solutions means our people are equipped to deliver a seamless client experience.

Strategic Operations is a dedicated function within Private Assets. It brings transformation delivery, project execution, business analysis, operational initiatives and implementation support into one team, reducing the delivery burden on BAU Operations and maintaining ownership from design through adoption.

The group will be split across three distinct focus areas, aligned under two individual leaders:

Operating Model, Product & Client Solutions: led by the Operating Model & Product leader, this area will define how services should run end to end, shape scalable products and solutions, support complex client implementations, and ensure client commitments are operationally deliverable.

Data, Reporting & Platform Enablement: led by the Technology, Data & Delivery leader, this area will define Operations requirements for data, reporting and platforms, strengthen data quality and lineage, and carry solutions through testing, deployment and adoption.

Digital Workflow, Automation & AI: also led by the Technology, Data & Delivery leader, this area will identify and deliver workflow, automation and AI opportunities, establish appropriate controls, and measure whether the expected benefits are realised.

The group works in close partnership with Operations, the Transformation Office, IT, Tactical Operations and Marquee Client teams. Roles may be permanent or approximately 12-month rotational assignments anchored in strategic locations. Rotational colleagues will join from the business, help shape and deliver change, and return to the line with broader project experience.

Responsibilities

Your Role

You will lead the automation and AI agenda for Private Assets Operations — determining what is worth automating, how it gets deployed, and whether the benefit was real.
Identify and prioritise automation, digital workflow and AI opportunities across the Private Assets estate.
Determine the right approach for each opportunity — workflow, automation tooling or AI — and make the case for it.
Own deployment standards so solutions are reusable and supportable rather than one-off local fixes.
Partner with IT and the Transformation Office through build, deployment and support.
Define how benefit will be measured before build starts, and report on whether it was realised.
Establish the governance and controls around automated and AI-assisted processes, working with Risk and the Control Office.
Coordinate with Tactical Operations on automation already deployed, and pick up solutions worth scaling.
Lead and mentor focus area resources, including rotational colleagues joining from the business.
Report on progress, risks and benefits realisation to the relevant leader and senior stakeholders.

Qualifications

About You

You have 12–15 years’ experience in private assets or a comparable financial services environment, with substantial exposure to automation or digital transformation.
Proven delivery of automation, digital workflow or AI initiatives that were deployed and adopted, not just piloted.
Strong technical knowledge of private assets processes — enough to judge what is genuinely automatable and what is not.
Practical understanding of workflow orchestration, exception-based processing and the control implications of automation.
Sound commercial judgement on effort versus benefit, and the willingness to stop work that will not pay back.
Strong leadership skills and supervisory experience of other professionals, including rotational colleagues joining from the business.
Skilled in business planning, budgeting and stakeholder negotiation.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Advanced computer skills (Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint and SharePoint).
Bachelor’s Degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics or a related field; professional accounting designation a plus.

What We Expect Of The Strategic Operations Team

Regardless of role or focus area, everyone in Strategic Operations is expected to demonstrate the following:
Deep technical and operational knowledge — genuine depth in how our processes, data and platforms actually work — the detail that only comes from having run the work.
Curiosity — the instinct to ask why a process looks the way it does, to challenge the answer, and to keep asking whether there is a better way.
A transformational mindset — comfortable redesigning end to end rather than patching, and prepared to see change through past go-live to the point where it is genuinely adopted.
Ownership through to adoption — accountability does not end at delivery; success is measured by whether the change sticks in the business.
Commercial and client awareness — an understanding of what we can genuinely run, so that what we commit to a client is deliverable.
Global mindset — working across regions, jurisdictions and time zones, and designing solutions that scale beyond a single desk, client or location.
Ambition to shape Citco’s future — an appetite to help build the operating model we will run for years, and to be measured on whether it works.

This position is not for an existing vacancy; we are building a candidate pool for future opportunities.

Our Benefits

Your well-being is of paramount importance to us, and central to our success. We provide a range of benefits, training and education support, and flexible working arrangements to help you achieve success in your career while balancing personal needs. Ask us about specific benefits in your location.

We embrace diversity, prioritizing the hiring of people from diverse backgrounds. Our inclusive culture is a source of pride and strength, fostering innovation and mutual respect.

Citco welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available upon request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection.

jobs.description:
CFO – Canada

Location: Calgary, AB

Company: Hero Canada Foods Inc.

About Hero Canada Foods

Hero Canada Foods is a leading branded food company and part of the international Hero Group, headquartered in Switzerland. In Canada, Hero is known for its successful portfolio of brands including Baby Gourmet, Simply Gourmet, and Goodies. Hero Canada combines local entrepreneurial agility with the scale, expertise, and long-term perspective of an international food group and is investing in systems, processes, commercial capabilities, and organizational maturity to support profitable growth.

Role Summary

Hero Canada Foods is seeking a Chief Financial Officer (CFO) to lead all finance activities in Canada and serve as a key member of the leadership team. Reporting to the General Manager and partnering closely with Hero Group Finance, the CFO provides strategic financial leadership while maintaining a strong connection to the commercial and operational drivers of the business.

The CFO supports the General Manager in shaping strategy, setting priorities, evaluating opportunities, and navigating day-to-day operational decisions. The role provides clear financial guidance and constructive challenges while remaining close enough to the work to turn insight into action quickly.

The CFO will actively partner with the Commercial Finance Manager on pricing, customer profitability, trade investment, forecasting, and business case development, providing both strategic guidance and direct analytical support as needed. At the same time, the CFO will lead a transactional accounting team consisting of a Senior Accountant, an Accounts Payable Accountant, and an Accounts Receivable Accountant, ensuring accurate reporting, disciplined controls, and reliable execution.

Key Responsibilities

1. Strategic Partner to the General Manager

Act as the General Manager’s trusted finance adviser on business strategy, growth priorities, organizational choices, investments, risks, and operational trade-offs.
Provide practical, fact-based guidance on day-to-day business matters, combining strategic perspective with an understanding of operational detail.
Translate financial and commercial information into clear choices, recommendations, scenarios, and actions for the General Manager and leadership team.
Constructively challenge assumptions and help align local decisions with Hero Canada’s objectives and Hero Group expectations.
Support the development and execution of the Canadian strategy, including profitable growth, margin improvement, cash generation, and operating profit protection.

2. Hands-on Commercial Finance Leadership

Lead and actively support the Commercial Finance Manager, providing coaching, prioritization, technical guidance, and direct practical assistance.
Lead financial analysis related to pricing, customer profitability, trade investment, promotions, and margin optimization, personally reviewing and supporting detailed financial models where appropriate.
Personally review, adjust, and, where required, build or manipulate detailed Excel-based pricing and commercial models rather than operating only at review level.
Partner closely with Sales, Marketing, Supply Chain, and Operations to improve decision quality and visibility of margins, cost drivers, pricing impacts, working capital, and profitability.
Ensure financial analysis is commercially relevant, technically sound, timely, and converted into clear recommendations.

3. Planning, Forecasting & Performance Management

Lead the annual budgeting process, rolling forecasts, performance reviews, and longer-term financial projections.
Connect commercial assumptions, supply chain realities, operating costs, and strategic initiatives into an integrated financial plan.
Monitor business performance, identify emerging gaps and opportunities, and establish corrective measures with accountable business owners.
Prepare clear reporting and decision materials for the General Manager, Canadian leadership team, Board, and Hero Group stakeholders.
Use scenario planning and sensitivity analysis to support decisions under uncertainty.

4. Accounting, Reporting & Transactional Finance Leadership

Lead the Senior Accountant, Accounts Payable Accountant, and Accounts Receivable Accountant, establishing clear ownership, priorities, service standards, and controls.
Oversee monthly, quarterly, and year-end close and ensure timely, accurate, and transparent reporting to local management and Hero Group.
Ensure accurate accounting in accordance with applicable accounting standards and Hero Group reporting requirements.
Maintain a strong internal-control environment across order-to-cash, procure-to-pay, record-to-report, payroll, inventory, and treasury processes.
Remain sufficiently close to transactional workflows to resolve issues, remove bottlenecks, improve quality, and provide hands-on support during peak periods or complex matters.
Drive pragmatic process improvements, automation, clear documentation, and stronger use of systems and data.

5. Cash Flow, Working Capital & Risk Management

Own cash flow planning, liquidity, and working capital performance, with focused management of receivables, payables, inventory, and operating commitments.
Identify and manage financial and operational exposures, including insurance, contracts, customer and supplier risk, and foreign exchange where relevant.
Support capital allocation, funding, and investment decisions with disciplined financial analysis and recommendations.
Serve as the primary financial steward of the Canadian business, ensuring decisions support sustainable value creation and alignment with Hero Group objectives.

6. Compliance, Tax & Governance

Ensure compliance with national, provincial, local, and Hero Group financial requirements.
Coordinate external audit, tax, payroll, benefits, legal, insurance, and advisory partners as required.
Oversee statutory filings, tax compliance, transfer pricing support, corporate governance requirements, and Group reporting obligations.
Ensure appropriate documentation, approval authorities, and segregation-of-duties or compensating controls are maintained.

7. Team Leadership & Capability Building

Build one connected finance team across commercial finance and accounting, balancing business partnership with reliable transaction processing and control.
Build finance talent and organizational capability through coaching, development planning, succession management, and cross-functional business exposure.
Develop the Commercial Finance Manager as a strong business partner while remaining available for detailed technical and modelling support.
Create a working culture that values accuracy, pace, ownership, practical problem-solving, continuous improvement, and constructive challenge.
Provide clear goals, coaching, feedback, succession planning, and development opportunities.

Team Structure

Reports to: General Manager, Hero Canada
Functional connection: Hero Group Finance
Direct leadership over: Commercial Finance Manager; Senior Accountant; Accounts Payable Accountant; Accounts Receivable Accountant

Required Qualifications & Experience

CPA designation strongly preferred.
10+ years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including meaningful senior finance leadership responsibility.
Experience serving as a CFO, VP Finance, Finance Director, or equivalent senior finance leader within a growth-oriented, lean operating environment.
Strong commercial finance experience with demonstrated depth in pricing, customer profitability, trade investment, financial modelling, budgeting, forecasting, and performance management.
Advanced Excel capability and willingness to work directly in detailed models and analyses.
Strong technical foundation in financial reporting, accounting, internal controls, cash flow, working capital, audit, tax, and compliance.
Experience leading both commercially oriented finance professionals and transactional accounting teams.
Experience in an international or cross-border business environment; CPG, food, manufacturing, distribution, or branded consumer products experience preferred.
Experience leading finance process improvements, ERP implementations, reporting enhancements, and finance transformation initiatives.

Key Competencies

Strategic and commercial mindset
Hands-on analytical and problem-solving capability
Influence and stakeholder management
Financial stewardship and risk management
Leadership and talent development
Continuous improvement orientation
Executive communication and presentation skills
High integrity and sound judgment
Financial modelling, analytical, and technical accounting capability

And as the largest 100% Canadian-owned and operated professional services firm in our country, we are proud to work alongside our clients to make a positive impact for all Canadians.

By living our Purpose, we will make an impact that matters.

Have many careers in one Firm.
Enjoy flexible, proactive, and practical benefits that foster a culture of well-being and connectedness.
Learn from deep subject matter experts through mentoring and on the job coaching

Deloitte Global is the engine of the Deloitte network. Our professionals reach across disciplines and borders to develop and lead global initiatives. We deliver strategic programs and services that unite our organization.

Work you'll do

The Deloitte Technology Disaster Recovery and Technology Resilience Leader is responsible for establishing, leading, and continuously maturing the technology resiliency framework across Deloitte Technology. Reporting to the Director of Process Optimization and Service Assurance, this role drives the enterprise-wide strategy for IT disaster recovery, in alignment with business continuity and operational resilience to ensure critical technology services remain available, recoverable, and aligned to business priorities. The individual partners closely with technology leaders, architects, engineers, analysts, and cross-functional stakeholders (Global Security Office, Technology Risk Office, member firm BC/DR Leaders) to develop, socialize, and validate comprehensive recovery and resiliency plans through regular testing, governance, and continuous improvement. This leader will design, implement, and integrate recovery & resiliency processes, programs, and procedures using industry best practices and recognized frameworks such as ITIL, COBIT, PMBOK, and CMMI.

What will your typical day look like?

Job Responsibilities:

Develop, implement, and lead a comprehensive Technology Disaster Recovery & Resiliency practice within DT, including governance, standards, planning, testing, reporting, and continuous improvement.
Partner with competency area leads and key stakeholders to identify action owners, define accountabilities, and ensure timely execution, testing, and adherence to IT disaster recovery & resiliency plans.
Design, enhance, and maintain resiliency processes, standards, and controls to protect, sustain, and recover hardware and software operations throughout the full technology lifecycle.
Lead the design, coordination, and execution of Disaster Recovery (DR) capabilities across service & product teams and related, supporting functions.
Collaborate with technology and business leaders to define the resiliency roadmap, strategy, objectives, key performance indicators, and success metrics for BCP, DR, and broader technology resilience initiatives.
Monitor and evaluate the execution and effectiveness of resiliency plans, including periodic exercises, functional recovery testing, tabletop simulations, and remediation of identified gaps.
Ensure alignment of resiliency strategies with the overall information technology strategy, enterprise risk posture, security requirements, and other IT service management processes.
Own and maintain all relevant process documentation, implementation guidance, operating procedures, testing evidence, metrics, and leadership reporting related to technology resiliency.
Produce and deliver key outputs including resiliency strategies, recovery plans, testing schedules, executive dashboards, metrics, and risk or audit reports.
Partner with Controls and Assurance teams to integrate resiliency requirements into audit readiness activities, ensure testing evidence is current, and support internal and external audits through issue tracking and remediation oversight.
Manage the cost, risk, performance, and service quality attributes associated with resiliency-related programs, tools, and capabilities.
Lead, coach, and develop direct reports by fostering a high-performance environment centered on client service, teamwork, accountability, recognition, and mutual respect.
Support employee development through goal setting, performance feedback, succession planning, and training oversight to ensure completion of required departmental and company learning programs.

About The Team

Deloitte Technology works at the forefront of technology development and processes to support and protect Deloitte around the world. In this truly global environment, we operate not in "what is" but rather "what can be" to help Deloitte deliver and connect with its clients, its communities, and one another in ways not previously conceived.

Qualifications

Enough about us, let’s talk about you

Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business, Management, or a related field required
Minimum of 7 years of experience in a complex business and information systems environment.
At least 4 years of experience in a managerial or senior managerial leadership capacity.
Minimum of 5 years of experience in IT Business Continuity Planning, Disaster Recovery, and Technology Resilience.
Demonstrated expertise in IT support processes, operational controls, and service management functions.
Strong understanding of industry frameworks and best practices such as ITIL, COBIT, PMBOK, and CMMI.
Experience leading cross-functional programs, influencing senior stakeholders, and driving enterprise-wide resiliency initiatives.

Preferred Qualifications:

Master’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business, Management or related field.
ITIL v3 or v4 certification is not required but is strongly preferred.
Experience with ServiceNow ITSM or similar service management platforms is a plus.

Total Rewards

The salary range for this position is $104,000 - $215,000, and individuals may be eligible to participate in our bonus program. Deloitte is fair and competitive when it comes to the salaries of our people. We regularly benchmark across a variety of positions, industries, sectors, targets, and levels. Our approach is grounded on recognizing people's unique strengths and contributions and rewarding the value that they deliver.

Our Total Rewards Package extends well beyond traditional compensation and benefit programs and is designed to recognize employee contributions, encourage personal wellness, and support firm growth. Along with a competitive base salary and variable pay opportunities, we offer a wide array of initiatives that differentiate us as a people-first organization. On top of our regular paid vacation days, some examples include: $4,000 per year for mental health support benefits, a $1,300 flexible benefit spending account, firm-wide closures known as "Deloitte Days", dedicated days of for learning (known as Development and Innovation Days), flexible work arrangements and a hybrid work structure.

Our promise to our people: Deloitte is where potential comes to life.

Be yourself, and more.

We are a group of talented people who want to learn, gain experience, and develop skills. Wherever you are in your career, we want you to advance.

You Shape How We Make Impact.

Diverse perspectives and life experiences make us better. Whoever you are and wherever you’re from, we want you to feel like you belong here. We provide flexible working options to support you and how you can contribute.

Be the leader you want to be

Some guide teams, some change culture, some build essential expertise. We offer opportunities and experiences that support your continuing growth as a leader.

Have as many careers as you want.

We are uniquely able to offer you new challenges and roles – and prepare you for them. We bring together people with unique experiences and talents, and we are the place to develop a lasting network of friends, peers, and mentors.

The next step is yours

At Deloitte, we are all about doing business inclusively – that starts with having diverse colleagues of all abilities. Deloitte encourages applications from all qualified candidates who represent the full diversity of communities across Canada. This includes, but is not limited to, people with disabilities, candidates from Indigenous communities, and candidates from the Black community in support of living our values, creating a culture of Diversity Equity and Inclusion and our commitment to our AccessAbility Action Plan, Reconciliation Action Plan and the BlackNorth Initiative.

We encourage you to connect with us at accessiblecareers@deloitte.ca if you require an accommodation for the recruitment process (including alternate formats of materials, accessible meeting rooms or other accommodations) or indigenouscareers@deloitte.ca for any questions relating to careers for Indigenous peoples at Deloitte (First Nations, Inuit, Métis).

When you apply, we will review your application using Deloitte's Global Talent Standards to ensure a consistent recruitment experience. Our recruitment advisors and hiring teams will utilize human screening combined with AI technology to help identify the skills and qualities that matter most to our business, while safeguarding your privacy and using AI responsibly.

Deloitte Canada has 20 offices with representation across most of the country. We acknowledge that Deloitte offices stand on traditional, treaty, and unceded territories in what is now known as Canada. We recognize that Indigenous Peoples have been the caretakers of this land since time immemorial, nurturing its resources and preserving its natural beauty. We acknowledge this land is still home to many First Nations, Inuit, and Métis Peoples, who continue to maintain their deep connection to the land and its sacred teachings. We humbly acknowledge that we are all Treaty people, and we commit to fostering a relationship of respect, collaboration, and stewardship with Indigenous communities in our shared goal of reconciliation and environmental sustainability.

jobs.title: Director - Digital Marketing
jobs.description:
Job Description

Some of what you will do:

The Director, Digital Growth & Media Marketing is responsible for leading Staples Canada's digital growth strategy, media investment, customer lifecycle marketing, and social media ecosystem across B2C and B2B. This role is accountable for driving customer acquisition, engagement, retention, traffic, and revenue through a portfolio of paid, owned, and earned channels.

The Director will lead teams responsible for performance media, SEM, CRM and email marketing, paid and organic social media, marketing technology, and digital marketing effectiveness. This leader will partner closely with Integrated Marketing, Creative & Production, Analytics, eCommerce, Digital Experience, and Business (i.e. B2B, Merchandising, Digital, Services) teams to ensure digital investments drive measurable business outcomes and support enterprise growth objectives.

As a member of the Marketing Leadership Team, this role will champion innovation, customer-centric marketing, personalization, and data-driven decision making while advancing Staples Canada's digital marketing capabilities.

Specifically, You Will

Digital Growth Strategy & Marketing Transformation

Lead the digital growth strategy across B2C and B2B, ensuring paid, owned, and earned channels are aligned to enterprise revenue, traffic, customer acquisition, engagement, and retention goals.
Advance Staples Canada’s shift toward a more digital-first, customer-centric marketing organization through clear roadmaps, capability building, test-and-learn practices, and cross-functional adoption.

Performance Media, SEM & Full-Funnel Investment

Oversee performance media strategy across search, shopping, display, programmatic, paid social, affiliate, retail media, and other growth channels.
Set investment strategy and budget allocation by business objective, audience, funnel stage, and expected return, balancing customer acquisition, demand generation, profitability, and brand-building outcomes.
Lead agency, platform, and partner relationships to ensure media plans are strategically sound, commercially efficient, and aligned to business priorities.

CRM, Email & Customer Lifecycle Marketing

Lead CRM, email, SMS, and lifecycle marketing strategies that deepen customer engagement, increase retention, and drive profitable sales across key customer segments.
Accelerate personalization, automation, segmentation, and triggered communications using customer data, behavioural insights, and marketing technology capabilities.
Develop differentiated lifecycle strategies for B2C and B2B audiences, including business customers (e.g. Preferred Customers, Small Medium Businesses, Enterprise Businesses) and other high-value segments.

Paid & Organic Social Media Ecosystem

Own the strategic direction for paid and organic social media, ensuring Staples Canada builds an integrated, brand-right, performance-oriented social ecosystem.
Partner closely with Integrated Marketing, Creative & Production, PR/Communications, and agency partners to align social content, community engagement, campaign amplification, and performance optimization.

Marketing Technology, Personalization & Digital Effectiveness

Lead the identification, evaluation, business case development, and optimization of marketing technology capabilities that enable personalization, automation, audience activation, measurement, and channel efficiency.
Partner with eCommerce, Digital Experience, Analytics, IT, and external vendors to improve digital marketing effectiveness across the customer journey.

Cross-Functional Planning, B2B/B2C Growth & Business Partnership

Act as a strategic partner to business, marketing, merchandising, eCommerce, digital experience, and services stakeholders to ensure digital investments support enterprise priorities.
Develop scalable approaches that support both B2C and B2B growth, with sufficient focus on business customer acquisition, nurture, retention, and account-based or segment-led marketing opportunities.

Some Of What You Need

University degree in business, marketing, commerce, digital marketing, analytics, or a related discipline.
MBA or advanced education in marketing, business, digital transformation, analytics, or related field considered an asset.
Deep knowledge of digital growth marketing across paid, owned, and earned channels, including performance media, SEM, CRM/email, paid and organic social, and lifecycle marketing.
Strong understanding of B2C and B2B customer acquisition, engagement, retention, demand generation, and full-funnel marketing strategies.
Demonstrated expertise in media investment strategy, budget allocation, channel optimization, agency management, and marketing performance measurement.
Strong analytical capability with the ability to interpret marketing, customer, digital, and financial metrics and translate insights into clear business recommendations.
Knowledge of marketing technology, personalization, segmentation, automation, first-party data activation, and customer journey orchestration.
Familiarity with key digital and marketing platforms such as Google Ads, Google Analytics, paid social platforms, CRM/email platforms, marketing automation tools, and reporting dashboards.
Minimum 10+ years of progressive digital marketing, media, CRM, lifecycle marketing, eCommerce, or growth marketing experience, preferably in retail, omni-channel, B2B/B2C, or customer-led environments.
5+ years of people leadership experience, including leading managers and/or multi-disciplinary teams.
Experience owning significant media, digital marketing, or MarTech budgets with accountability for performance, optimization, and return on investment.
Experience leading agency, platform, vendor, and technology partner relationships.
Experience building or scaling digital marketing capabilities, personalization programs, lifecycle marketing strategies, or test-and-learn operating models.
Experience partnering cross-functionally with eCommerce, analytics, merchandising, creative, integrated marketing, IT, and business stakeholders to deliver measurable business outcomes.

Physical Demands/working Conditions

Office environment – Hybrid, with 4 days onsite in Richmond Hill, subject to the hybrid policy.

Some Of What You Will Get

Associate discount
Health and Dental benefits
RRSP/DPSP
Performance bonuses
Learning & Development programs
And more...

We value transparency in our hiring processes. Please note, artificial intelligence may be used in certain stages to screen, assess, or select applicants, however, a human reviewer makes all final decisions. This posting is for an existing vacancy.

At Staples Canada we are dynamic, inspiring partners to our customers and the communities in which we live. As The Working and Learning Company, we inspire people to work smarter, learn more and grow every day. We’re looking for curious, approachable, and passionate individuals who love finding solutions. If that’s you, let’s work, learn, and grow together.

Staples Canada is continuously working towards creating an inclusive and diverse work environment. jobs.title: Senior Director, Analytics and Data Science, Core Product & Growth
jobs.description:
About Life360

Life360's mission is to keep people close to the ones they love. Our category-leading mobile app, Tile tracking devices, and Pet GPS tracker empower members to protect the people, pets, and things they care about most with a range of services, including location sharing, safe driver reports, and crash detection with emergency dispatch. Life360 serves approximately 102.4 million monthly active users (MAU), as of June 30, 2026, across more than 180 countries.

Life360 delivers peace of mind and enhances everyday family life with seamless coordination for all the moments that matter, big and small. By continuing to innovate and deliver for our customers, we have become a household name and the must-have mobile-based membership for families (and those friends who are basically family).

Life360 has more than 500 (and growing!) remote-first employees. For more information, please visit life360.com.

Life360 is a Remote First company, which means a remote work environment will be the primary experience for all employees. All positions, unless otherwise specified, can be performed remotely (within the US and Canada) regardless of any specified location above.

We are AI Native

We are building an AI native company where AI is an integral part of how we build and operate. AI tool usage during interviews varies by role. You may be asked to demonstrate proficiency with AI tools, discuss how you leverage AI, or complete interview exercises without AI assistance. Your Recruiter will provide clear guidance as you move through the interview process.

Undisclosed use of AI not previously discussed with or approved by your Recruiter may impact your candidacy.

About The Team

The Data & Analytics Team (DnA) is a 60+ person organization spanning data engineering, analytics engineering, analytics/decision science, and data science/ML. The science teams are organized into two sub teams, focusing on MAU and Revenue. This role leads decision science and data science within MAU.

You and your team will be responsible for understanding the drivers behind MAU: why members come, why they stay, and why they return. The team partners with product, marketing, and engineering to put those learnings into everyday work, and that work shapes our roadmaps.

Our data is unusual for a consumer company. Life360 measures families and circles rather than individuals, so one member's behavior affects another's, which makes measurement a different problem than a standard funnel. With billions of location events, driving behavior, crash detection, and Tile and Pet GPS trackers, we get a rich picture of physical behavior that few consumer companies can build.

About The Job

This Senior Director leads MAU Analytics and Data Science.

You and your team will work across acquisition, activation, engagement, and retention on the analysis, models, and experiments behind each. A lot of what this role owns needs to be built rather than maintained: the measurement, the standards, and how the team uses AI. The team is also raising its craft, and coaching people through that is an important part of the job. Within a year, your team members will be operating at an elevated skill level, proactively bringing key questions to light, and serving as trusted advisors whom stakeholders consult for strategic guidance rather than simple task execution.

You will report to the Head of Data and work closely with counterparts leading Revenue Analytics and Data Science, and with the leaders of Data Engineering.

For candidates based in the US, the salary range for this position is $247,000 to $366,000 USD. For candidates based out of Canada, the salary range for this position is $286,000 to $339,000 CAD.
We take into consideration an individual's background, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience in determining final salary. Base pay may also vary based on geographic location, with US work locations falling into one of three geographic tiers.

Total compensation is inclusive of equity compensation in the form of Restricted Stock Units (RSUs)
, as well as a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, vision, financial, and other benefits.

What You'll Do

Lead and develop the decision scientists and data scientists on the team, and set the quality bar for both disciplines.
Own the MAU driver model and the forecast.
Own the exploratory work that drives the strategy to grow MAU.
Establish how an analysis gets scoped, run, reviewed, and written up, so its quality does not depend on who picked up the request.
Partner with your Revenue counterpart and Data Engineering leadership to define common metrics, align on experimentation standards, and introduce unified operating practices across teams.
Build the operating model that gets the team into the roadmap conversation early, with a view on what to build and what to test.
Use agents and automated analysis daily, and expect the same of the team.
Shape how the team works AI-native: what gets delegated to agents, what gets automated, and what stays human judgment.

What We're Looking For

Required Experience & Qualifications

10+ years in analytics, data science, or decision science, including 5+ years in people management in a senior leadership role.
Deep expertise in inferential and causal analytics. Able to lead ML practitioners.
Expert knowledge of engagement, retention, churn, and cohort metrics.
Experience forecasting a company-level metric and being held to it.
SQL, plus Python or R.
Experience with Databricks, third party experimentation tools (e.g. Statsig), Tableau or similar BI tools, and AI native BI tools (e.g. Hex, AI/BI).
Hands-on with coding agents (Claude Code or equivalent) in your own analytical work.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent.

Nice to Have

Familiarity with experiment design to identify and control for network effects.
Master’s degree or PhD with an emphasis in social science, psychology or other behavioral science.
Experience leading a team that reports to you but sits embedded with product and engineering teams.
Experience in a B2C subscription business.

Core Expectations

You have moved an analytics team from reactive to embedded.
You coach and develop people, and you have grown analysts into leaders.
On your teams, analysis starts from a hypothesis rather than a data request.
You have built the standards a team works from, and got people to use them.
You are curious about why people behave the way they do, not just what they did.
You decide what the team does not work on, and you can defend it.

Our Benefits

Medical, dental, vision, life and disability insurance plans (100% paid for US employees). We offer life and disability as well as supplemental plans for medical and dental for Canadian employees.
401(k) plan with company matching program in the US and RRSP with DPSP plan for Canadian employees.
Paid parental leave
Mental Wellness Program & Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for mental well-being
Generous time off: flexible PTO, companywide holidays throughout the year plus summer and winter shutdowns
Learning & Development programs
Equipment, tools, and reimbursement support for a productive remote environment.
Free Life360 Platinum Membership and Tile trackers.

Life360 Values

Our company's mission-driven culture is guided by our shared values to create a trusted work environment where you can bring your authentic self to work and make a positive difference

Be a Good Person - We have a team of high integrity people you can trust.
Be Direct With Respect - We communicate directly, even when it's hard.
Members Before Metrics - We focus on building an exceptional experience for families.
High Intensity, High Impact - We do whatever it takes to get the job done.

Our Commitment to Diversity

We believe that different ideas, perspectives and backgrounds create a stronger and more creative work environment that delivers better results. Together, we continue to build an inclusive culture that encourages, supports, and celebrates the diverse voices of our employees. It fuels our innovation and connects us closer to our customers and the communities we serve. We strive to create a workplace that reflects the communities we serve and where everyone feels empowered to bring their authentic best selves to work.

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at Life360. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status or any legally protected status.

We encourage people of all backgrounds to apply. We believe that a diversity of perspectives and experiences create a foundation for the best ideas. Come join us in building something meaningful. Even if you don't meet 100% of the below qualifications, you should still seriously consider applying!

jobs.description:
Director, Data & Technology

Communitech helps tech companies start, grow, and succeed in Waterloo Region.

We’re building a tech ecosystem that’s proudly local, globally ambitious and powered by community.

Since 1997, Communitech has brought community and tech together to build Canada’s most vibrant innovation ecosystem. We connect local startups and scale-ups to the support they need to grow, compete and lead.

Today, that means helping trusted AI solutions reach the market, turning bold ideas into valuable IP, expanding peer and advisory networks for founders, and uniting voices through the Waterloo Tech Coalition to take on the issues that matter most.

Our goal is to keep Waterloo Region the most connected, collaborative, and resilient tech hub in the country.

We’re looking to grow our team with passionate people – people who believe in our mission and who are willing to do what it takes to help our founders succeed. If you like to work collaboratively, get s#!t done and be a champion for Canadian tech, we want to hear from you. Wonder what it’s like to work at Communitech? Learn more at https://www.communitech.ca/corporate-stuff/careers/.

Communitech is based in downtown Kitchener, Ontario. We work in-office five days a week because great things happen when we're together — creating space for deeper collaboration and stronger relationships with each other and the ecosystem we support.

Role Overview

We are seeking a strategic, forward-thinking, and hands-on leader to oversee Communitech’s Data and Technology functions. Reporting directly to the CFO, the Director of Data & Technology will oversee IT infrastructure, enterprise applications, cyber security, web operations, and data governance.

With our core technical foundation in place, this leader will bring the vision and hands-on expertise needed to transform Communitech’s data assets into actionable strategy, champion responsible AI adoption to streamline internal workflows, and maintain resilient, high-performing IT operations for our staff, facility tenants, and the broader Waterloo Region tech ecosystem.

Key Responsibilities

AI Innovation & Workflow Integration
Lead the identification, evaluation, and adoption of modern AI tools (generative AI, automation scripts, LLM integrations) across internal teams to optimize operations and reduce administrative friction.
Establish clear guidelines, privacy standards, and ethical guardrails for data security and safe AI usage across the organization.
Stay ahead of emerging technology trends to ensure Communitech’s tech stack reflects best practices, positioning our non-profit as a forward-thinking leader in the AI-driven tech landscape.

Strategic Data & Analytics Leadership
Foster a culture of storytelling with data across the organization.
Enable decision making and ensure ecosystem trends, member needs, and non-profit reporting metrics are continuously illuminated through actionable reporting and business intelligence solutions.
Oversee the modernization and integrity of Communitech’s data and analytics infrastructure to maintain data integrity, security, and scalability.

Enterprise IT, Infrastructure, and Web Operations
Lead internal teams and external partners across IT operations, cloud platforms, web development, and application management to deliver high availability and exceptional service quality for our teams and on-site hub tenants.
Act as the primary authority on organizational cyber risk, developing, executing, and monitoring risk mitigation strategies, compliance protocols, and incident response frameworks to protect member and organizational data.

Team Leadership & Operations
Lead, coach and develop high-performing Data and Technology teams.
Maintain a strong track record of completing technical and operational projects on time and within budget through modern project management methodologies and AI-assisted workflows.
Partner closely with internal leaders to align technology roadmaps with overall business objectives and ecosystem needs.
Foster a culture of responsiveness, ownership, collaboration and continuous improvement.

What Success Looks Like

The Director, Data & Technology will make Communitech more valuable, relevant, and indispensable to the members and community we serve.

Success in this role will include:
Successfully introducing AI-driven tooling and automation that noticeably reduces manual overhead across programs, reporting, and internal operations.
Delivering clean, real-time dashboards and impact analytics that clearly measure member engagement and ecosystem health for various stakeholders.
Maintaining an exceptionally reliable, secure, and modern IT environment for the Communitech team and hub facility tenants.
Establish a resilient security posture that protects sensitive startup and organizational data against evolving threats.
Foster an empowered, agile team culture grounded in ownership, responsiveness, continuous learning, and continuous improvement.

Qualifications

5+ years of progressive technology leadership experience across enterprise IT, data engineering, software development, or digital transformation (non-profit or innovation hub experience is a strong asset).
Hands-on understanding of how to practically integrate modern AI tools, automation, and SaaS platforms into workplace processes to maximize non-profit efficiency.
Broad technical grasp across Web, Security, and IT with expertise in data architecture, Business Intelligence, and advanced reporting solutions.
Proven ability to manage, inspire, and develop multi-disciplinary technical teams while remaining willing to dive deep into execution when necessary
Technical Breadth:
Solid architecture understanding of cloud data stacks and web platforms
Deep understanding of networking fundamentals, SaaS platforms, and enterprise cyber security best practices.
Strong track record managing technology vendors, external service providers, and outsourced partners.
Strong business acumen and project management discipline with a history of delivering operational and technical projects on time and within budget.
A strong, member-centric mindset with a deep passion for supporting entrepreneurs, tech start ups, and the local innovation ecosystem.

Compensation

The annual base salary range is $100,000-$115,000. The actual compensation will be based on various factors, including the candidate’s level of skills, experience and education.

To Apply

Please apply online along with your resume and cover letter.

We thank all applicants in advance; however only individuals selected for an interview will be contacted. All applications will be kept confidential. Communitech is a diverse and inclusive environment and encourages applications from all qualified candidates, including aboriginal persons, francophones, members of sexual minority groups, persons with disabilities, visible minorities, and women. We will provide any requested accommodation to candidates with disabilities throughout the recruitment process.

In compliance with Ontario’s Bill 190, we confirm that this posting represents a current, existing vacancy within our organization.

jobs.title: Director, Enterprise Strategy
jobs.description:
Requisition ID: 274044

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

The Scotiabank Enterprise Strategy group is a high-performing central team focused on designing and advancing Scotiabank’s strategic agenda
. The team works closely with the CEO, Group Heads and senior leaders to shape the Bank’s enterprise strategy and its most important business-line priorities.

Reporting to the VP, Enterprise Strategy, the Director will work closely with senior executives, business-line leaders and stakeholders across the Bank to lead complex strategy engagements, generate insights and develop recommendations that shape the Bank’s most important priorities.

Is this role right for you? In this role, you will be responsible for:

Strategy Projects – Must-Win Priorities
Lead a broad range of strategy engagements across the Bank, including business-line priorities and enterprise initiatives. Partner with stakeholders to structure complex problems, conduct qualitative and quantitative analysis, assess strategic and financial implications, and develop and present compelling recommendations to senior leadership.
Design and facilitate problem-solving sessions, workshops, and interviews with cross-functional stakeholders and subject matter experts to generate insights, build alignment, and advance strategic priorities.
Build alignment across business lines and corporate functions to advance strategic priorities and drive enterprise outcomes.
Partner with business-line leaders to shape strategic priorities and support the development of plans aligned to the Bank’s broader strategic objectives.
Synthesize complex findings into clear recommendations, implementation roadmaps, and governance approaches, and present them effectively to senior leaders to drive strategic outcomes.
Serve as a trusted thought partner to senior executives, helping define priorities, assess trade-offs, and navigate complex strategic decisions.
Thought Leadership
Provide thought leadership and constructive challenge on the design and advancement of strategic priorities and must-win opportunities.
Monitor emerging trends, competitive dynamics, and strategic issues to assess their implications for the Bank and its business-line strategies.
Act as a strategic counsel and thought partner for senior executives – both within the context of strategy project and on an ongoing basis
Design and support executive strategy discussions and offsites, helping senior leaders evaluate key priorities, align on strategic direction, and address emerging opportunities and challenges.
Executive Communications
Support the CEO agenda, including all-bank strategy, business line value creation projects, strategic planning, Board-level communications, and being a trusted advisor to senior leaders
Develop clear, compelling presentations and communications that translate complex strategic issues into actionable insights for senior executives, Executive Committee, and Board audiences.
In partnership with Global Communications, develop executive communications and strategic messaging that clearly articulate the Bank's priorities to internal and external stakeholders. Support the planning and delivery of key leadership, employee, and external events.
Team Leadership and Stakeholder Management
Contribute to the growth and development of the Enterprise Strategy team through recruiting, coaching, mentorship, knowledge sharing, and fostering strong partnerships across the Bank.
Ensure the Bank's risk appetite and risk culture are appropriately considered in all activities, recommendations, and decisions.
Champion a high-performance environment and implement a people strategy that attracts, retains, develops, and motivates top talent by fostering an inclusive work environment

Skills

Do you have the skills that will enable you to succeed? We’d love to work with you if you have the following:

MBA, PhD or relevant post-graduate degree from a recognized institution
3-4 years of experience in a top-tier management consulting firm; banking industry expertise is highly recommended
Ability to deliver results in a fast-paced, challenging, and dynamic business environment
Exceptional analytical and problem-solving skills, with ability to manage ambiguity
Superior interpersonal skills, leadership and influencing capabilities on a multi-cultural environment
Self-motivated; ability to work both independently and collaboratively with multi-functional teams
Experience running complex projects, with large group of cross-functional stakeholders
Ability to effectively manage relationships across the Bank, its partners, and external vendors
Exceptional verbal and written communication skills
Collaborative and proven track record of managing and developing high-potential talent
Excellent knowledge of MS Office including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint

Why join us?

The IESO is committed to ensuring Ontario’s electricity system meets the province’s needs today and into the future. We are charged with purpose

Who We Are

Our central role includes managing the provincial power grid in real-time, overseeing and evolving Ontario’s electricity market, engaging with government, municipalities and Indigenous communities, and planning for Ontario’s future electricity needs. Our employees play a key role in driving grid innovation, protecting the system from threats, advancing the province’s energy conservation programs, and forecasting and procuring the electricity resources we’ll need in the decades to come.

This is a non-unionized position that falls within the Corporate Relations, Engagement and Strategy business unit.

What Makes This Role Exciting

The energy sector is rapidly evolving, offering exciting new opportunities for those who want to make a difference.

This is a unique opportunity to help shape the organization's strategic direction and drive initiatives that have enterprise-wide impact. Working closely with senior leaders, the role influences corporate strategy, oversees its implementation, and leads high-profile CEO and organizational priorities. The position offers a rare combination of strategic thinking, cross-functional collaboration, and people leadership, allowing you to see ideas progress from concept to measurable results.

For someone who enjoys solving complex challenges and creating organizational alignment, this role sits at the center of the organization's most important priorities.

What You’ll Do

In this role, you’ll make a meaningful impact by contributing to the IESO team and supporting the electricity needs of the province through:

Leading the development and socialization of the Corporate Strategy, working in close partnership with Directors and senior leaders. Coordinate strategic planning activities, stakeholder engagement, and supporting research, and develop recommendations for Executive Leadership Team (ELT) and Board consideration and approval.
Leading the development of the Strategy Implementation Plan, including prioritization of strategic initiatives, milestones, performance measures, and implementation approaches. Facilitate engagement with business areas and provide recommendations to support ELT decision-making and approval.
Overseeing enterprise-wide monitoring, measurement, and reporting of progress against strategic objectives. Establish and implement reporting approaches, assess organizational performance against strategic commitments, identify emerging risks and issues, and provide insights and recommendations to support leadership decision-making.
Coordinating and aligning corporate strategy activities with other enterprise planning functions, including business planning, enterprise risk management, enterprise change, procurement, workforce planning, etc. Identify opportunities to strengthen the Enterprise Planning Framework and recommend improvements that enhance organizational alignment and execution.
Leading the delivery of CEO-sponsored and strategic initiatives, such as ESG framework, organizational alignment reviews, and other corporate priorities. Direct supporting research, analysis, and project activities; oversee external consultants and contractors where required; and develop recommendations arising from initiative outcomes for consideration by the CEO and Executive Leadership Team.
Provide leadership, direction, and coaching to team members, ensuring the effective delivery of corporate strategy, strategy implementation planning, enterprise reporting, and strategic initiatives through clear priorities, performance expectations, and professional development support.

Decision-Making Responsibilities

Contribute to developing the approach, methodology, and stakeholder engagement process for the development of the Corporate Strategy and Strategy Implementation Plan.
Approve research, analysis, and other work products supporting strategy development, implementation planning, and strategic initiatives.
Determine the approach for strategy performance oversight and enterprise reporting.
Lead the selection and management of consultants and contractors supporting strategy or strategic initiative work, in accordance with organizational policies and procurement requirements.
Make decisions related to the coordination, prioritization, and execution of strategic and CEO-sponsored initiatives.

Recommendations

Recommend the Corporate Strategy, developed in collaboration with Directors and key stakeholders, for consideration and approval by the Executive Leadership Team and Board.
Recommend the Strategy Implementation Plan, including strategic priorities, sequencing of work, performance measures, and resource considerations, for Executive Leadership Team approval.
Recommend enhancements to the Enterprise Planning Framework to strengthen alignment across corporate strategy, business planning, enterprise risk management, enterprise change, workforce planning, procurement, and other enterprise functions.
Develop and present recommendations arising from CEO-sponsored and strategic initiatives, including opportunities, risks, implementation approaches, and organizational impacts, for consideration and approval by the CEO and Executive Leadership Team.
Provide strategic advice and recommendations to senior leadership on organizational performance, emerging issues, risks, trends, and opportunities identified through strategy oversight, reporting, and environmental scanning activities.

Role Requirements

Our team consists of experts from diverse backgrounds, each bringing their unique perspectives and skills.

Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Public Administration, Public Policy, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
12-15+ years of progressively senior experience in government relations, public affairs, strategy, policy, or a related function, preferably within the electricity or broader energy sector.

Proven ability to influence and build relationships with senior leaders, and other internal and external stakeholders.
Exceptional communication, presentation, and facilitation skills, with the ability to convey complex issues effectively and drive alignment.

jobs.title: Director, Data Operations & Analytics
jobs.description:
About Cover Genius

Cover Genius is the global infrastructure for embedded protection. Active in over 60 countries and all 50 US States, we protect the customers of the world’s largest digital companies, including Klarna, Revolut, Stripe, Priceline, Agoda, Booking.com, Turkish Airlines, Tongcheng Travel, eBay, and Uber, with seamless, end-to-end experiences. Cover Genius has protected more than 73M customers globally across 240M policies with USD $3.2BN in gross written sales.

Coming off a stellar year with 40% YoY revenue growth and a recent $100M capital raise, putting our valuation at $1.9BN, we are accelerating into our next phase of growth. As part of our team, you’ll help drive our AI-first roadmap, developing hyper-personalization engines, agentic distribution, and automated claims infrastructure, while building the scalable technology powering the fast-growing $70B embedded protection market.

Our people are:
Accountable, customer-obsessed, collaborative, driven

Our people are not:
Passive, defensive, siloes-driven, hesitant

About The Role

Cover Genius is entering its next phase of growth, and this role is the chance to build the data function that takes us there. You won't be inheriting a finished org chart, you'll be designing how data operations and analytics work as one function: a single, trusted set of definitions for the metrics that matter, and a team the business turns to first.

This is a key contributor role within our data domain, and one of the driving forces behind delivering our data vision. You'll work closely with data engineering, data science, product, and actuaries to turn that roadmap into real value for the business, our customers, and our partners.

You'll lead two teams, one running data operations and analytics, one running merchant partner & regulatory reporting, and you'll sit as the bridge between the business and our technical data teams, translating business questions into asks for data engineering, data science, and our AI adoption function, and making sure what they build actually lands with the people who need it. This also means giving actuaries and other insurance specialists access to data they don't currently have, so they can do their own in-depth analysis rather than working from a finished report.

Key Responsibilities

Own the Data Operations & Analytics Function: lead both the data operations/analytics team and the merchant & partner reporting team, setting priorities that answer real business questions rather than growing the metric count for its own sake.
Business Ownership of the Semantic Layer: define what our core metrics mean and where the source of truth lives (GWP, revenue, claims ratio, and others), and get business sign-off on the logic behind them. When a metric doesn't exist yet, this team builds it.
Data Governance Documentation: own the governance framework behind the semantic layer, metric ownership, definition standards, and change control, so metric trust doesn't depend on someone remembering how a number was built.
Internal BI Ownership: own the internal BI tool end to end and drive adoption across the business. We're the team that gets other teams building their own dashboards and insight, not waiting on a ticket, including training people how to use the tool properly. Where a team can't build what they need themselves in their own domain, we build it for them.
Merchant & Partner Reporting: own reporting accuracy, reconciliation, and regulatory reporting for our merchant and partner relationships, and build the operating rhythm that catches issues before they reach a partner or a regulator.
OKR Instrumentation: translate business and domain OKRs into accurate, trusted data tracking, and make sure every domain has the data assets it needs to measure its own progress.
Drive Data Use Across the Business: look for where data, AI, and automation can remove manual work or replace ad hoc spreadsheets with real systems, ahead of being asked, including automating workflows within our own team.
Team Leadership & Development: grow a team that spans junior analyst to manager, build career paths, and raise data literacy across the business so leaders trust the numbers and ask sharper questions.

Skills And Experience

10+ years in data or reporting operations, including 4+ years leading managers, not just individual contributors.
A track record of fixing unclear ownership and accountability gaps across technical and business teams, in addition to running your own team well.
Fluency in modern data stacks; dbt, BigQuery, semantic layers, BI tools.
Experience defining metrics and governance, what a number means, who owns it, where it lives, in a business with more than one data team.
Comfortable presenting to C-suite and cross-functional leadership on data strategy and risk.
Insurance, insurtech, fintech, or another regulated, data-heavy industry is a plus, particularly experience supporting actuarial or underwriting teams, or running fraud/risk analytics.
Experience building a roadmap with dependencies across multiple technical and business teams, with the project management discipline to scope, sequence, and track it to completion.
Experience running cross-team coordination as a discipline: async updates, meetings with a clear owner, and open items that actually get closed out rather than left in a thread.

Proficiencies And Attributes

Moves fluently between an executive conversation on strategy and a technical one with data engineering, without needing to own the technical call.
Takes ownership of unresolved problems, unclear owners, poor request quality, broken reporting, instead of waiting for someone else to claim them.
Commercially minded enough to know which metrics actually matter to the business.
A people leader who manages managers and invests in a team spanning multiple levels.
Raises the bar on data literacy and requests quality across the whole business, not just within the team.
Understands the business drivers behind each team's numbers, not just the numbers themselves."
Builds trust and alignment through influence, not authority, earning buy-in by showing people the shared benefit rather than asking them to comply.
Takes an ambiguous, cross-system problem and turns it into a clear framework and a workable solution, then operates independently enough to scope and drive it without waiting to be told how.

🤔 Why Cover Genius?

At Cover Genius, We Create Magic By Turning The Archaic Into The Extraordinary. We Take One Of The World’s Oldest And Most Complex Industries And Reinvent It With World-class Technology. Cover Genius Doesn’t Just Disrupt Legacy Insurance; We Make The Impossible Feel Effortless.Our Operating Principles Guide Our Mission

Make today matter: We deliver with urgency and excellence. We act decisively, move with intention, and hold a high bar.
Act with accountability: We own our commitments and take pride in delivering results that move us forward.
Grow together: We are a collective of curious minds. We learn from wins and setbacks, share knowledge generously, and elevate each other every day.
Inspire Each Other: We push each other to think bigger and pull together to go further.
Champion Our Customers: We lead with empathy and center the customer, turning complex disruptions into seamless moments of trust.
Flexible Work Environment - Our teams are hybrid. We work from home on a Wednesday and Thursday and attend the office on Monday, Tuesday and Friday with flexibility around start/finish times.
Don't just take our word for it - hear about our culture straight from our people here: story time.

Ready to make an impact?
If you’re looking for a place where you’ll be challenged, trusted, and empowered, we’d love to meet you.

The Legal & Privacy Stuff

Cover Genius promotes diversity and inclusivity. We don't tolerate discrimination, demeaning treatment of anyone, or harassment due to race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, or any other legally protected status.

Ensure and monitor that the hotel is in compliance with all report deadlines and due dates and react accordingly.
