jobs.description:
Job title: Director, Financial Planning and Analysis


Reporting to: Chief Financial Officer


Years of experience: 10\+ years


Location: This role is based in Toronto and follows a hybrid work arrangement, with three days per week in the Toronto office and the remaining workdays remote.


Position type: Full\-time


Working conditions: Regular collaboration across global time zones and international travel up to 20% of working time, are required.


**About Raising The Village**

Raising The Village's mission is to build and strengthen pathways out of ultra\-poverty through an approach guided by data, designed with communities, and scaled by partnerships. We work with last\-mile communities to implement solutions that raise incomes, sustain impact, and chart sustainable pathways to possibility within 24 months. To date, we have supported more than two million people in Uganda, Rwanda, and the Democratic Republic of Congo, with support from our partners and our team in North America. Find out more about our programs and impact at www.raisingthevillage.org (http://www.raisingthevillage.org/).


**Position overview**


The Director, Financial Planning and Analysis (FP\&A) will play a critical role in leading RTV's forward\-looking finance function and serving as a strategic partner to the CFO, executive leadership, country teams, and functional leaders. The Director will own enterprise planning, rolling forecasts, performance analysis, scenario modelling, and decision support, translating financial and operational data into clear choices, risks, and actions.


As one of three finance pillars reporting to the CFO, the Global FP\&A function provides a forward\-looking planning and performance perspective alongside Controllership and Accounting. The Director will lead this function and establish consistent planning disciplines, management reporting, and business\-partnering practices across the organization.


**Key responsibilities**


*Enterprise Planning, Forecasting \& Scenario Analysis*


* Own the annual consolidated budget, rolling forecast, multi\-year plan, and in\-year reforecasting cycles across countries, departments, programs, and funding sources.
* Develop integrated financial and operational planning models that connect program reach, cost per beneficiary, staffing, capital requirements, funding, and cash needs.
* Lead scenario and sensitivity analysis to assess growth options, funding gaps, foreign exchange exposure, cost pressures, and strategic trade\-offs.
* Maintain clear planning assumptions, version control, decision logs, and reconciliations to approved organizational targets.

*Performance Management \& Executive Insight*


* Own the budget and KPI performance\-management process, including setting review standards, monitoring results against approved targets, and driving accountability for corrective actions;
* Lead quarterly performance reviews at the executive and country levels.
* Translate results into concise commentary on drivers, variances, risks, opportunities, and corrective actions.
* Develop and maintain an enterprise performance framework that integrates financial and non\-financial indicators.
* Prepare CFO, executive leadership, Board, and Finance/Audit/Risk Committee materials with decision\-focused analysis and transparent supporting logic.

*Strategic Business Partnering*


* Act as the senior finance partner to organisational leaders, constructively challenging assumptions and improving the financial quality of decisions.
* Support business cases, program design, workforce planning, country expansion, investment decisions, and resource allocation.
* Partner with Programs, Partnerships, People, IT, Procurement, and country leadership to connect strategy, delivery plans, and financial capacity.
* Provide financial modelling and analysis for donor proposals, cost recovery, funding sustainability, and restricted versus unrestricted resource decisions.

*Cash, Funding \& Sustainability Planning*


* Lead forward\-looking liquidity and cash flow forecasting in partnership with Accounting and Controllership, with clear visibility over restricted and unrestricted cash and reserve requirements.
* Maintain funding\-gap and runway analysis, identifying timing, concentration, and affordability risks for leadership action.
* Ensure planning outputs reconcile to the general ledger, grant records, treasury forecasts, and approved budgets, while preserving appropriate separation between planning and accounting ownership.

*Data, Systems \& Process Improvement*


* Own the FP\&A reporting and analytics roadmap, including dashboards, planning models, data definitions, and management\-reporting standards.
* Advance the effective use of ERP (Sage Intacct/ Dynamics Business central are a plus), Power BI, Excel, and other planning or analytics tools; support finance\-system integration and ERP improvement initiatives.
* Improve forecast accuracy, cycle times, data quality, and self\-service reporting through standardization, automation, and clear controls.
* Establish a single source of truth for management reporting and ensure consistent treatment of currencies, allocations, beneficiaries, and program cost drivers.

*Team Leadership \& Capability Building*


* Lead, coach, and develop the East Africa FP\&A team, setting clear accountability, service standards, and development plans.
* Build FP\&A and financial literacy across budget owners through practical training, templates, guidance, and ongoing coaching.
* Promote a high\-performance culture grounded in collaboration, curiosity, accountability, inclusion, and continuous improvement.
* Create resilient processes with appropriate documentation, cross\-training, succession planning, and coverage for key activities.

*Governance, Risk \& Collaboration*


* Partner with the Controller and Accounting Manager to maintain a clear operating model across planning, technical accounting, controls, reporting, treasury, and count

jobs.title: Director of Product, AI Growth
jobs.description:
1Password is growing.
We’ve surpassed $400M in ARR and we’re continuing to accelerate, earning a spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 for four years in a row and teaming up with iconic partners like Oracle Red Bull Racing.

About 1Password

At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work.

If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future.

Reporting to the Senior Director of Product, the Director of Product, AI Growth grows 1Password's new business in artificial intelligence. In this role, you own driving growth for our AI opportunities by identifying which customers we target, which outcomes we win on, and proving it with design customers. You scale growth through our go-to-market organization and through partnerships with the agent ecosystem and channel partners.

How We’re Using AI Today

Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers.

This is a remote opportunity within Canada and the US.

What We're Looking For

Minimum of 8 years of product management experience, including experience carrying a revenue or adoption target, with a preference for experience in security products, agentic products, or developer tools.
Experience owning the strategy for a new product area or market entry, and taking it from hypothesis to customers running in production.
Experience working directly with enterprise customers on a technical deployment, as the person accountable for the outcome, and turning what those deployments proved into a repeatable motion a sales team can run.
Experience building technology partnerships and integrations, including judging where a product should sit in a larger technology ecosystem and working with business development on commercial terms.
Technical depth to hold a credible conversation with developers and security architects about how AI agents are built, deployed, and given access to systems.
Demonstrated ability to build alignment across go-to-market and engineering teams toward a shared goal, without direct authority over either.
Demonstrated ability to make decisions and move work forward with incomplete information in a fast-changing market.
Takes ownership end to end, including the work that falls between teams.
Works AI-first: uses agents in daily work, and applies their own judgement to decisions, product taste, and customer and internal relationships.
Preferred: familiarity with agentic access products, meaning the products that give AI agents credentials and access to the systems they work in.

What You Can Expect

Growth strategy

Own the growth thesis for 1Password's AI opportunities, covering the customer segments we target, the outcomes we deliver that we win on, and the workflows we get embedded into. Revise it as evidence arrives from customers, partners, and the market.
Form and test hypotheses using customer feedback, product usage data, partner input, and market research gathered with the go-to-market, product, user experience, and product marketing teams.
Lead a weekly business review that brings the voice of the customer, field feedback, and product usage telemetry into one view, so the team can refine targets, forecast the roadmap's impact on growth, and prioritize the blockers that hold adoption back.
Identify what stops customers from adopting, and drive each blocker to a resolution with the product team that owns it.

Design customer program

Run the design customer program for new artificial intelligence opportunities, from selecting customers through to delivered outcomes.
Act as the general contractor for each design customer: the single person accountable for getting that customer deployed on 1Password for their agentic access, and for delivering the security and convenience outcomes they came for. Coordinate every team the deployment touches, and build what it requires together with a forward deployed engineering team.
Bring in solutions engineering, customer success, and product managers to help each customer reach their goal, and run feature betas with the product managers who own those features.
Turn what the program proves into the repeatable signal the company needs to scale, meaning the customer evidence, the deployment pattern, and the measured outcomes that the go-to-market and channel teams build sales plays on.
Improve the program each cycle so it reaches more design customers, raises delivery success rates and customer satisfaction, and shortens the time it takes the company to commercialize a new product.

Partnerships

Decide where 1Password should play in the customer's artificial intelligence stack to deliver the most customer value in securing agent access. Agent access can be controlled at several points in that stack, so weigh those points and choose the ones that solve the most of the customer's problem, rather than the ones we fit into most easily. Base the call on how customers run AI today and on how the industry is evolving.
Identify and pursue the partnerships that let us play at those points and that complete an end-to-end customer outcome, meaning the outcome a customer cannot reach with 1Password alone.
Work with partners to deliver integrations, and find the patterns that let us repeat an integration across similar partners instead of building each one from scratch.
Work with the business development team to structure commercial relationships that grow both companies' business and deliver value to shared customers.

Scale through the field and the developer community

Work with product enablement to build demos and enablement content that the field and our channel partners can use without your involvement.
Work with developer relations to grow adoption organically among developers, through reference architectures, sample code, and open source contributions.

Travel

Travel to design customer sites, partner meetings, and industry events approximately 10 to 20% of a given year.

USA-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $238,000 USD and $357,000 USD, plus immediate participation in 1Password's benefits program (health, dental, 401k and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.

Canada-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $208,000 CAD and $312,000 CAD, plus immediate participation in 1Password’s generous benefits program (health, dental, RRSP and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.

At 1Password, we approach each individual's compensation with a promise of fair market value and internal equity commensurate with experience and specific skill set.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

Our culture

At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first.

You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone . Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results.

How We Work With AI

We are committed to leveraging cutting-edge technology—including AI—to achieve our mission. We also understand that thinking critically about AI in its current forms will help us create better solutions for our customers and ourselves with its future forms, which will help us continue to close the gap between security and privacy and achieve our mission. We want team members at all levels to take the approach of actively learning AI best practices, identifying opportunities to apply AI in meaningful ways, and driving innovative solutions in their daily work. Embracing the future of AI isn't just encouraged—it's an essential part of how we will be successful at 1Password.

This approach extends to our hiring process—candidates are welcome to use AI tools responsibly and thoughtfully during the application process. To us, this means we do ask that you join live interviews without using AI tools so we can get to know how you communicate, solve problems, and collaborate with others.

Our approach to remote work

We believe in the power of remote work, but recognize that in-person connection is important to help us achieve our mission. While we are a remote-first company, travel for in-person engagement is a part of almost all roles, and we require our employees to be ready and willing to take part. Frequency will depend on role and responsibilities, and may include, but is not limited to: annual department-wide offsites, team meetings, and customer/industry events.

What We Offer

We believe in working hard, and rewarding that hard work through our benefits. While not an exhaustive list, here is a glance at what we currently offer:

Health and wellbeing

👶 Maternity and parental leave top-up programs

🩺 Competitive health benefits

🏝 Generous PTO policy

Growth and future

📈 RSU program for most employees

💸 Retirement matching program

🔑 Free 1Password account

Community

🤝 Paid volunteer days

🏆 Peer-to-peer recognition through Bonusly

🌎 Remote-first work environment

Some roles in our GTM team are currently being hired for in-person hybrid work in Toronto and Austin. These roles will specify on the posting.

You belong here.

1Password is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive, diverse and equitable workplace that is built on trust, support and respect. We welcome all individuals and do not discriminate on the basis of gender identity and expression, race, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, colour, religion, creed, gender, national origin, age, marital status, pregnancy, sex, citizenship, education, languages spoken or veteran status. Be yourself, find your people and share the things you love.

Accommodation is available upon request at any point during our recruitme

Job Description

Director, Commercial Strategy

Amica Support Office, Downtown Toronto

Full-Time

3 days in Office (Mon-Wed)

Amica embraces pay- for- performance compensation philosophy and offers a competitive total compensation package designed to reward performance.

Expected Salary Range : 
$124,000-155,000

Maximum Bonus Potential :
20% target bonus, that rewards exceptional performance.

Benefits:
Comprehensive health, dental, and vision coverage, retirement plan contributions, disability, and employee wellness programs.

Vacation:
Generous annual vacation entitlement, aligned with company policy.

Compensation is determined based on skills, experience, and qualifications. Candidates whose experience surpasses the expectations for this role may be eligible for compensation above the advertised range.

About Us

Amica is setting a new standard for senior living in Canada by combining unparalleled premium hospitality and amenities with expert care and support to deliver a personalized senior living experience. Committed to enriching the lives of seniors now and as their needs change, Amica offers Independent Living (IL), Assisted Living (AL) and Memory Care (MC) lifestyle options. Established in 1996, the company operates over 33 residences in British Columbia, and Ontario, with plans to continue expansion in select markets.

The Opportunity

The Director, Commercial Strategy is a senior commercial leader accountable for accelerating occupancy performance across Amica's pre-open, lease-up and occupancy-challenged residences. This role is focused directly on these priority residences - establishing commercial strategy, driving disciplined execution, removing barriers to performance, and partnering with Operations, Sales and Marketing to deliver occupancy results.

Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, the Director acts as an enterprise commercial performance leader for priority residences and provides hands-on support to regional and residence teams. The role also leads selected enterprise commercial effectiveness initiatives that strengthen sales execution across the portfolio.

This position requires strong executive presence, commercial judgment, a bias for action, and the ability to move seamlessly between strategy and hands-on field execution.

What You Will Be Doing

Occupancy Performance - Pre-Open, Lease-Up & Occupancy-Challenged Residences (85%)

Own the commercial performance strategy for pre-open, lease-up and occupancy-challenged residences, with clear occupancy, sales, pipeline and conversion objectives.
Diagnose the commercial drivers of underperformance and translate them into focused residence-level action plans with clear priorities, owners, timelines and expected outcomes.
Establish and lead a rigorous performance cadence for priority residences, including regular business reviews, action tracking, escalation of barriers and executive reporting.
Partner closely with Regional Operations, residence leaders, Sales and Marketing to strengthen lead generation, pipeline health, conversion, pricing and promotional strategy, referral development and local market execution.
Provide hands-on commercial leadership to challenged residences, including direct coaching and challenge of frontline sales teams, targeted field support and decisive intervention where performance is off plan.
Own pre-open and lease-up commercial readiness and execution, ensuring each residence has the demand generation, sales capability, pipeline and market activation required to achieve occupancy milestones.

Performance Intervention & Recovery

Identify emerging occupancy risk early and mobilize targeted interventions before performance materially deteriorates.
Develop and drive 30/60/90-day recovery plans for occupancy-challenged residences, ensuring actions are practical, measurable and executed with urgency.
Challenge existing go-to-market approaches where results are not materializing. Recommend and, with the COO and functional leaders, drive decisive changes to sales resources, pricing, promotions, marketing investment, lead generation, referral strategy and local commercial execution when performance remains off plan.
Coordinate cross-functional support around priority residences and ensure teams remain focused on the few actions most likely to change occupancy trajectory.
Capture and scale successful practices from high-performing pre-open, lease-up and recovery situations across the portfolio.

Commercial Effectiveness & Field Enablement

Support sales force deployment, structure and resourcing decisions based on portfolio priorities and residence needs.
Lead sales incentive compensation strategy and execution, ensuring incentives reinforce enterprise occupancy and commercial objectives.
Partner with Sales and Marketing leaders on CRD capability, sales training and targeted development needs identified through residence performance.
Support CRM and sales process effectiveness, with a focus on field adoption, disciplined lead management and consistent execution.
Assess the effectiveness of key commercial initiatives and recommend where to continue, adjust or redirect investment.

Education & Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Commerce, Marketing, Hospitality, or a related discipline; equivalent relevant experience will also be considered.
8-10+ years of progressive commercial, sales, operations, or revenue leadership experience, ideally in a multi-site consumer, hospitality, seniors living, real estate, or service-based organization.
Demonstrated track record of personally driving measurable revenue, sales and/or occupancy improvement, with clear examples of materially changing the trajectory of underperforming businesses or locations.
Significant experience directly leading, coaching and challenging frontline sales teams; equally comfortable working alongside teams in the field and operating in the executive room.
Experience developing and executing turnaround or performance recovery plans for underperforming locations, including diagnosing root causes and translating them into decisive commercial action.
Experience supporting new openings, market launches, lease-up or other high-growth environments is strongly preferred.

Skills & Capabilities

Commercial operator: Strong instinct for what drives occupancy and revenue, with the ability to quickly identify where performance is breaking down and what needs to change.
Execution-oriented: Moves readily from strategy to action and maintains urgency, accountability and follow-through until performance improves.
Sales leadership: Strong understanding of the full sales funnel, lead management, conversion, referral development, relationship selling, closing and sales leadership.
Performance turnaround: Able to assess an occupancy-challenged residence, establish a focused 30/60/90-day recovery plan, mobilize the right resources and drive measurable improvement.
Market and pricing acumen: Comfortable assessing competitive positioning, pricing, promotions, customer demand, local market dynamics and barriers to purchase.
Cross-functional leadership: Able to bring Operations, Sales, Marketing and other partners together around a clear commercial plan without relying solely on positional authority.
Field orientation: Willing and able to spend meaningful time in residences, working directly with GMs, CRDs and regional leaders rather than managing performance primarily from the corporate office.
Judgment and decisiveness: Knows when incremental improvement is insufficient and can recommend and drive more significant changes to sales resources, pricing, promotions, marketing investment or local execution.
Performance literacy: Comfortable using funnel, conversion, occupancy and financial information to diagnose performance and make decisions; does not need to be an analytics specialist.
Executive communication: Strong presence and ability to communicate performance, risks, actions and recommendations clearly and succinctly to senior leadership.

Working Conditions

Primarily office-based role
Regular interaction with senior leadership, operational leaders, and cross-functional stakeholders across the organization.
Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, highly collaborative environment.
May require travel to residences, or off-site business meetings and planning sessions.
May be required to work additional hours during peak business periods, including annual operating plan development, forecast cycles, and board reporting periods.
Operates in a dynamic, fast-paced environment requiring adaptability, responsiveness, and sound decision-making under pressure.

What You Can Expect From Us

A diverse and inclusive environment where individual differences are celebrated, and you’re encouraged to be your best self
Collaborative environment where we work together to succeed as a team
Learning and development opportunities to help you grow
Comprehensive benefit package including RRSP matching
Office is centrally located in the financial district, on the PATH and the TTC subway line, and provides easy access to downtown amenities
Some travel required ( Hybrid work model, in office 3 times a week

At Amica Senior Lifestyles we are passionate about working together in a supportive and inclusive environment that fosters innovation and turns ideas into action. We remain committed to creating workplaces that reflect the communities in which we operate.  We are actively seeking applicants from all religions and ethnicities, LGBTQ2s+, Black, Indigenous, racialized people, and persons with disabilities and encourage people from all backgrounds to apply for our positions. 

Requests for accommodation can be made at any stage of the recruitment process providing the applicant has met the Bona-fide requirements for the open position. Applicants need to make their requirements known when contacted.

Reporting to the SVP, Pharmacy, the Director, Strategy & Operations is a strategic partner to the Pharmacy Operations & Transformation leadership team, responsible for driving strategic planning, operational excellence, business transformation, and execution of enterprise and divisional priorities.

The Director translates complex business priorities into actionable plans, executive insights, and measurable outcomes. jobs.description:
MaintainX is a leading mobile-first work execution platform
for industrial and frontline teams. More than 13,000 customers
, including Duracell, McDonald's, Shell, DHL and Volvo, use MaintainX to cut unplanned downtime and run better operations, across 13.9 million managed assets and 79.5 million completed work orders.

In August 2026 MaintainX became part of Autodesk, joining
Autodesk Operations Solutions
, the organization unifying Autodesk's operations platform alongside Tandem, FlexSim and Fusion Operations.
Autodesk's strategy is to converge design, make and operate into one continuous lifecycle: design an asset, build it, run it, then feed what you learn running it back into the next design. Autodesk had design and make. Operate is the phase that tells you what actually happened, and it is ours.

The Opportunity

We're looking for an Engineering Director to lead MaintainX's Platform division. Platform owns the seven foundational teams every product engineer builds on: AI Builder, DevOps, Compliance, Testing Frameworks, Backend Frameworks, Mobile Frameworks, and SRE. This is a manager-of-managers role for someone who wants to define how a high-growth engineering org operates at scale.

What You’ll Do

Own the roadmap and operating model for Platform Engineering: set division-level priorities, manage cross-team dependencies, and translate business goals into multi-quarter platform investments.
Lead and develop a team of Software Development Managers - coaching on people development, technical judgment, and organizational effectiveness across seven teams.
Set the engineering standards every product team depends on: framework conventions, reliability targets, compliance posture, and CI/CD health.
Drive MaintainX's AI-native platform strategy - the AI Builder team's agent orchestration, tool registry, and developer environments sit in this division; your job is to ensure the org extracts real leverage from them.
Own division-level reliability: SLO definitions, incident response frameworks, on-call health, and the systemic path from incident to prevention.
Partner with the CTO and peer engineering leaders on org design, architectural decisions, and headcount planning.
Represent Platform Engineering to the business — translating infrastructure investment into engineering velocity, developer experience, and customer trust.
An expert level of English, both spoken and written, is required, as the individual will need to lead platform engineering managers across multiple teams, present technical priorities to executive stakeholders, and align with engineering leaders outside Québec on a daily basis.

About You

10+ years in software engineering with 5+ years in engineering leadership, including 2+ years managing managers across multiple teams.

jobs.description:
About our Client:
Build Canada Homes (BCH) is Canada’s federal housing agency with the mandate to scale up the supply of affordable housing across the country. By leveraging public lands, deploying flexible financial tools, and acting as a catalyst for modern methods of construction, BCH is helping drive a more productive and innovative homebuilding sector. Working in partnership with non-profits, Indigenous organizations, private developers, and all orders of government, BCH is accelerating the delivery of housing Canadians need—faster, smarter, and more affordably.

Their priorities

Leverage public lands and mobilize capital to increase housing supply.
Accelerate large-scale affordable housing projects through partnerships.
Advance modern methods of construction to boost productivity and lower costs.

Following Royal Assent of the Build Canada Homes Act in June 2026, BCH is in a formative stage of transition toward a Crown Corporation. This creates a meaningful opportunity to help establish the governance, accountability, legal, risk, and corporate foundations of a national mission-driven organization with significant scale, visibility, complexity, and public trust responsibilities.

This role is offers a hybrid model. They currently work 2-3 days in office and potentially 4 days in the future.

Position Scope:
The VP, IT and Cybersecurity role, Information Technology (“IT”) leads the strategic direction, governance, and delivery of technology services across Build Canada Homes and its subsidiaries (collectively, the “Corporation” or “BCH”). The role is accountable for technology strategy, enterprise applications, IT operations and infrastructure, cybersecurity, technology risk management, and data governance capabilities that enable BCH to achieve its mandate through secure, reliable, and scalable technology services.

Working across BCH and with internal employees, technology vendors, service providers, and external stakeholders, the VP, IT and Cybersecurity, role ensures technology investments, digital capabilities, and information assets support operational execution, organizational performance, and long-term business priorities. The role establishes technology service delivery frameworks, digital enablement strategies, and governance practices that improve efficiency, innovation, collaboration, and user experience across the Corporation.

The VP, IT and Cybersecurity role provides leadership across IT operations and infrastructure, cybersecurity and technology risk, and data governance, management, and security. The role establishes functional policies, standards, oversight mechanisms, and performance frameworks consistent with the expectations of a Crown corporation, ensuring technology services remain secure, compliant, resilient, reliable and aligned with BCH priorities.

Responsibilities:

TECHNOLOGY STRATEGY, DIGITAL ENABLEMENT AND INNOVATION

Establishes the technology vision, priorities, and multi-year roadmap required to support BCH's mandate, business objectives, and operational requirements.
Aligns technology strategy, investments, and service delivery with organizational priorities and emerging business needs.
Leads or supports, where applicable, digital enablement and technology modernization initiatives that improve organizational effectiveness, scalability, and service delivery.
Identifies opportunities to leverage technology, automation, and innovation to enhance business performance and employee experience.
Provides strategic advice and guidance regarding technology trends, opportunities, risks, and investment priorities.

IT OPERATIONS AND INFRASTRUCTURE

Provides strategic oversight of enterprise applications, platforms, networks, cloud services, workplace technologies, and IT infrastructure.
Establishes service delivery models, operating standards, and performance expectations that support reliable, secure, and efficient technology operations.
Ensures technology services and infrastructure are scalable, resilient, and aligned with business continuity requirements.
Oversees technology lifecycle planning, system availability, capacity management, and service modernization activities.
Monitors technology performance and service outcomes and drives continuous improvement across technology operations.

CYBERSECURITY AND TECHNOLOGY RISK MANAGEMENT

Establishes cybersecurity strategies, policies, frameworks, and controls to protect BCH information assets, systems, and technology environments.
Leads the identification, assessment, monitoring, and mitigation of cybersecurity and technology-related risks.
Oversees IT incident preparedness, response, recovery, and resilience programs to strengthen BCH's security posture.
Ensures compliance with applicable security, privacy, regulatory, and corporate requirements.
Provides strategic oversight of technology risk management practices and promotes security awareness throughout BCH.

DATA GOVERNANCE, MANAGEMENT AND SECURITY

Leads the development and implementation of data governance frameworks, standards, and accountabilities across BCH.
Establishes policies and practices that support data quality, stewardship, integrity, accessibility, and appropriate use of information assets.
Oversees data management, information security, retention, and protection practices in accordance with legislative and corporate requirements.
Enables the effective use of data and information to support reporting, analysis, planning, and decision-making.
Promotes a culture of responsible data management and information governance across BCH.

GOVERNANCE, PERFORMANCE AND LEADERSHIP

Provides leadership, direction, and oversight to Information Technology personnel, programs, and service delivery activities.
Establishes technology policies, standards, governance frameworks, and performance measures that support organizational objectives and regulatory compliance.
Leads technology planning, investment prioritization, resource allocation, and budget management activities.
Oversees technology vendor relationships, contracts, service agreements, and third-party performance management practices.
Establishes or supports, where applicable, reporting frameworks, dashboards, and performance indicators to support executive decision-making and functional accountability.
Ensures technology programs, systems, and information assets are managed in accordance with BCH governance and risk requirements.
Promotes continuous improvement, service excellence, innovation, and operational effectiveness across the Information Technology function.
Supports the development of BCH's annual operating plans, strategic plans, and multi-year business priorities.
Contributes to enterprise planning, performance management, and organizational reporting activities.
Establishes and manages Information Technology budgets and resource plans.

Qualifications and Experience:

Post-secondary degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, Business Administration, or a related discipline.
Relevant professional certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CGEIT, ITIL, PMP, TOGAF, Cloud certifications, or equivalent are considered assets.
Extensive experience of a minimum of ten to fifteen years in progressively senior technology leadership roles.
Proven track record leading enterprise technology, infrastructure, cybersecurity, digital transformation, and data governance functions within complex organizations, public-sector entities, Crown corporations, or similarly regulated environments.
Demonstrated experience developing and executing technology strategies aligned with business priorities.
Strong knowledge of cybersecurity, technology risk management, enterprise architecture, IT operations, cloud technologies, and data governance practices.
Experience overseeing technology vendors, managed services, contracts, and strategic partnerships.
Demonstrated experience advising executive leaders on technology investments, digital enablement, cybersecurity, and information management matters.
Experience managing budgets, resources, and technology performance measures.
Occasional travel required (up to 20% of the time).

jobs.description:
Company Description

About Us:

With a history that dates back over 80 years, Starcom is a global communications planning and media leader. We are an agency still grounded in our founding principle that people are at center of all we do. Each day, we apply this belief to harness the transformative power of data and technology to inspire and move people and business forward. With more than 7,000 employees in over 100 offices around the world, Starcom partners with the world's leading marketers and brands.

Within Canada, Starcom is a part of Publicis Media within Publicis Groupe, one of the world’s leading communications groups. Our team spans across our Windsor, Toronto and Montreal offices. We truly love the world of Media and Advertising. We see the planning and buying process as art. However, it is an art that is always best when backed by the science of empirical data.

You will be joining a well recognised agency with credentials:

Great Places to Work certified three years in a row
Only communications company to be ranked in LinkedIn’s Top 25 Great Places to Work
2022 Media Agency of the Year
2023 Media Agency of the Year finalist

What We Offer

Work Your World program enabling you to experience working from anywhere in Canada or overseas for up to 6 weeks a year
Extended long weekends throughout the year with an additional day off each long weekend
Wellness & Tech benefits to support what’s most important to you
Birthday leave
Extensive Learning & Development opportunities, including more than 15,000 learning programs via our online learning platform as well as a Professional Development Allowance
Local and Global Mobility within the Publicis Groupe network

Overview

We are seeking a strategic, commercially minded Associate Director, Insights & Analytics
to lead and scale our MMM capability across clients and internal teams. This role will shape the agency’s approach to marketing effectiveness measurement, guide clients through data requirements and model design, translate complex model outputs into clear business recommendations, and ensure MMM insights are embedded into planning, optimization, and investment decisions. The successful candidate will bring media strategy knowledge, measurement experience, client consulting skills, and the ability to lead cross-functional teams and external partners through complex analytics engagements.

Responsibilities

Lead MMM Capability: Own the development and evolution of the agency’s MMM offering, including model approach, data collection process, governance, delivery standards, and client-facing best practices.
Guide Model Design & Measurement Strategy: Partner with clients and internal teams to define business objectives, KPI hierarchy, brand/category structure, base versus incremental measurement needs, and testable hypotheses.
Oversee Data Collection & Readiness: Lead data requirement planning across media, sales, revenue, pricing, promotions, seasonality, macro factors, and other business drivers; ensure data inputs are complete, consistent, and model-ready.
Manage MMM Execution: Work closely with internal analytics teams, data science partners, and external vendors to support model development, validation, output review, scenario planning, and optimization recommendations.
Translate Outputs into Action: Turn model results into clear, practical implications for media investment, channel mix, budget allocation, flighting, diminishing returns, and future planning decisions.
Serve as Senior Client Consultant: Lead client conversations on marketing effectiveness, explain model methodology and limitations, present findings with confidence, and build trust with senior stakeholders.
Integrate Insights into Planning: Collaborate with strategy, planning, investment, performance, and client teams to ensure MMM learnings are connected to broader audience, media, and business strategy.
Build Tools, Templates & Standards: Create scalable MMM briefing documents, data collection templates, QA checklists, output interpretation frameworks, and executive-ready reporting formats.
Advance Measurement Thought Leadership: Stay current on MMM, incrementality testing, attribution, media effectiveness, privacy-safe measurement, and AI-enabled analytics to continuously improve the agency’s measurement practice.
Drive AI Capability Adoption & Development: Identify, test, and scale AI-enabled tools, workflows, and best practices that improve research, analytics, reporting, and knowledge-sharing across the agency.
Support Broader Research & Insights Needs: Contribute to research and insights work as needed, including new business pitches, category and consumer POVs, thought leadership, client requests, and cross-agency strategic initiatives.
Lead & Mentor Team Members: Support the growth of managers, specialists, and analysts by providing coaching, quality control, project guidance, and capability-building across MMM and analytics workstreams.

Qualifications

8+ years of experience in marketing analytics, media measurement, research, consulting, or agency/client-side analytics roles.
Strong understanding of Marketing Mix Modeling, including model objectives, business use cases, data requirements, interpretation of outputs, and application to media planning and budget optimization.
Experience managing MMM projects end to end, including scoping, client alignment, data collection, vendor coordination, model review, delivery, and post-model planning recommendations.
Ability to translate technical analytics into concise executive narratives, clear planning implications, and actionable recommendations for senior stakeholders.
Familiarity with paid media channels, including TV, digital video, social, search, display, audio, OOH, retail media, and CTV, and how these channels are measured and optimized.
Strong analytical fluency, with comfort reviewing data inputs, model outputs, response curves, ROI/ROAS, contribution, saturation, and scenario planning outputs.
Proficiency with Excel and PowerPoint expected; familiarity with Power BI, SQL, R, Python, MMM platforms, or other analytics/statistical tools is an asset.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple stakeholders, timelines, and workstreams while maintaining strong attention to detail and quality control.
Ability to lead through influence across strategy, planning, investment, analytics, and client teams.
Strong leadership and mentoring capabilities, with experience guiding team members and building repeatable processes or capability standards.
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience preferred; advanced degree in Marketing, Statistics, Economics, Business Analytics, Data Science, or a related field is an asset.
We welcome candidates with diverse career paths and encourage applicants who meet most of the qualifications to apply.

Additional Information

We’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. Accommodations are available throughout the hiring process upon request.

Salary

Transparency matters to us. The salary range for this position is $80,000- 90,000 per year. Actual compensation within this range will be based on a variety of factors, including relevant experience, knowledge, skills, and applicable certifications. This range reflects what we reasonably expect to offer based on current market data.

You will establish and embed best practice systems, standards and governance frameworks, while championing integrated digital engineering, data and AI-enabled solutions that improve productivity, quality, decision-making and delivery predictability.

This role can be based out of our Montreal, Vancouver or Phoenix offices. 

In this role, you will:

Lead the development and adoption of engineering governance frameworks, systems and standards that enable high-performing engineering delivery globally.

Provide functional leadership for global engineering systems, standards and governance, establishing scalable frameworks that drive consistency, quality and execution discipline across regions without direct operational ownership of engineering delivery teams.

Align engineering systems. processes and tools to enable efficient, seamless delivery at scale across complex project environments.

Champion the adoption of integrated digital engineering, data and AI-enabled capabilities to improve productivity, decision-making and delivery outcomes.

Establish a consistent global approach to engineering execution that enhances predictability, reduces risk and strengthens delivery performance.

Use data and performance insights to continuously improve quality, efficiency and overall project outcomes.

Drive strong commercial outcomes through effective governance of engineering systems, software vendors and strategic investments.

Partner with regional leadership to align engineering capability with business priorities, growth objectives and long-term performance.

What we’re looking for

You’re a strategic and technically credible engineering leader with the ability to operate globally, influence change at scale and build the systems, standards and capability that enable high-performing engineering project delivery.

A degree-qualified engineering leader with 20+ years’ experience in engineering design across minerals processing, oil and gas, chemical or related sectors.

Senior leadership experience across complex, multi-discipline engineering teams.

Strong EPCM experience, including engineering systems integration and delivery governance.

Deep understanding of engineering applications, BIM/CDE environments and emerging digital engineering capability.

Demonstrated experience operating across regions, cultures and matrixed stakeholder groups.

Commercially astute, outcome-focused and confident translating strategy into execution.

Innovative, decisive and adaptable, with a continuous improvement mindset.

A strong communicator who can influence globally and bring teams with you through change.

This is a career-defining opportunity to transform how engineering is delivered globally, with real influence over systems, capability, governance and performance.

If you’re looking for more in your next move, you’ll find it here: more purpose in shaping how global engineering is delivered, more perspective through working across regions and complex projects, more progress through digital innovation, and more impact through measurable performance outcomes.

You’ll be supported by a business that values sustainable performance, wellbeing, flexibility and long-term career development.

Shape engineering at a global scale
by influencing delivery models, governance, capability building, digital innovation and performance across complex, international projects.

Accelerate your career with meaningful impact
in a business that supports flexibility, wellbeing and long-term development, while empowering you to drive measurable outcomes and lasting change.

RRSP matching 

Health and benefits package

Provide technical direction and partner with Product Line Management, engineering, and product development teams to translate validated concepts into scalable planning capabilities and bring them successfully to market.
Partner cross-functionally with hardware teams to model and analyze alternative network architectures, providing data-driven insights that influence product roadmap decisions.

15+ years of telecommunications experience spanning deep technical roles and positions with product, customer, or business leadership accountability.
10+ years expertise in optical and IP transport technologies, including network architecture, control, resiliency, capacity engineering, and optimization trade-offs.

Experience developing, deploying, or governing AI and machine-learning technologies in telecommunications or other complex, high-availability environments.
Customer-facing experience relating to network consultancy services or similar.
Hands-on experience with Python or comparable analytical programming tools for prototyping, data analysis, optimization, or model validation.

Job Description

Leader Amélioration des Données / Data Improvement Lead

English job description follows***

Description De L'emploi

Vous avez une expérience confirmée dans l'analyse de données et la gestion de la performance, vous avez travaillé sur l'amélioration de processus et la digitalisation, et vous souhaitez évoluer tout en développant de nouvelles compétences ? Ce poste est pour vous !

Le programme d'avions commerciaux A220 recherche un Leader en amélioration des données pour rejoindre notre équipe Performance Management basée à Mirabel (Québec, Canada), où vous collaborez étroitement avec les analystes de performance, les équipes des Opérations et l'équipe de digitalisation.

Vous ferez partie de l’équipe Performance Management chargée de développer la standardisation et l'amélioration de la qualité des données de performance pour la chaîne de valeur A220, tout en soutenant la feuille de route de digitalisation. L'organisation de l'équipe est établie de manière à promouvoir la collaboration transversale et l'autonomie, dans un esprit de soutien mutuel et d'apprentissage collectif.

Dans ce rôle, vous agirez en tant que point de contact central et facilitateur entre les analystes de la performance opérationnelle et l'équipe de digitalisation. Votre mission sera d'optimiser l'efficacité des processus d'assemblage de l'A220 en coordonnant l'amélioration des données provenant de divers flux : approvisionnement secondaire, SDO ( Supplier Disruption Over Cost ), coûts récurrents (RC) et CVAT ( Customer Value Added Time ). Vous identifierez les besoins en automatisation, harmoniserez les méthodes d'analyse et assurerez la transition des analyses manuelles vers des solutions digitales robustes pour améliorer la rentabilité globale.

Votre Environnement De Travail

Le siège du programme d'avions commerciaux A220 est situé à Mirabel, dans la région métropolitaine de Montréal, à deux pas de la ville dynamique de Montréal. Réputée pour son environnement paisible et sûr, la région offre une grande qualité de vie aux jeunes professionnels ou aux professionnels expérimentés, ainsi qu'aux familles, en équilibrant parfaitement les opportunités de carrière et les activités de plein air, ce qui en fait un endroit vraiment spécial où il fait bon vivre.

Parce Que Nous Prenons Soin De Vous

Avantages financiers: Salaire attractif, bonus annuel, régime d’assurances collectives, régime de retraite et régime d’achat d’actions.
Équilibre vie privée / professionnelle: Une politique de travail hybride (selon les besoins opérationnels), une cafétéria sur site, une politique de congés très concurrentielle.
Bien-être / santé: Programme d’Aide aux Employé.e.s (PAE), programme de rabais, service médical sur site, accès à un service de navette publique entre Laval (station de métro Montmorency) et Mirabel, et une application de covoiturage.
Développement individuel: des opportunités d’évolution et des possibilités de formations nombreuses (catalogue de plus de 10.000 e-formations disponibles en libre accès pour développer votre employabilité, certifications, programmes de développement accéléré, mobilité nationale et internationale).

Chez Airbus, nous vous aidons à travailler, à vous connecter et à collaborer plus facilement et de manière plus flexible. Partout où cela est possible, nous favorisons la flexibilité dans nos modes de travail afin de stimuler l'esprit d'innovation.

Vos Défis

Assurer le lien principal entre les analystes (Performance, SDO, RC, CVAT) et l'équipe de digitalisation pour traduire les besoins métiers en solutions automatisées;
Garantir la qualité, la cohérence et l'exactitude des données de performance issues des flux d'approvisionnement et de production;
Harmoniser la définition et le suivi des indicateurs clés de performance (KPI) à travers les différents flux pour assurer une vision transverse de la performance;
Identifier les opportunités d'automatisation des rapports de performance (hebdomadaires, mensuels, trimestriels) et superviser leur mise en œuvre par l'équipe technique;
Consolider les points de blocage majeurs identifiés par les analystes du pôle Performance Management afin de prioriser la feuille de route de digitalisation selon l'impact sur la performance des opérations;
Préparer et présenter des feuilles de route claires et des visualisations de données aux parties prenantes pour soutenir la planification stratégique;
Collaborer avec les départements Opérations, Finances et Qualité pour optimiser la performance globale de la chaîne de valeur.

Votre Profil

Vous détenez un baccalauréat en ingénierie;
Vous détenez un minimum de 10 ans d’expérience dans un système industriel;
Vous possédez une expérience pertinente en analyse de données, en gestion de la performance ou en amélioration de processus;
Vous maîtrisez les outils d'analyse et de visualisation de données tels que Power BI, Skywise et Python;
Vous avez une connaissance approfondie des entrepôts de données, de l'analytique en nuage et de l'automatisation des processus;
Vous possédez de solides compétences en résolution de problèmes et une capacité démontrée à collaborer avec des équipes interfonctionnelles;
Vous avez la capacité de vulgariser des concepts de données complexes pour les rendre accessibles aux équipes opérationnelles et de direction;
Vous avez une expérience confirmée dans la définition de cadres de mesure de performance et la création de structures d'analyse complexes.

Ce poste peut impliquer des déplacements professionnels.

Déplacements Requis

Ce travail nécessite une prise de conscience liée à tous les risques potentiels de conformité et à un engagement à agir avec intégrité, ces valeurs sont le fondement du succès, de la réputation et de la croissance durable de l'entreprise.

jobs.description:
Toronto or Waterloo, hybrid | Full-time | Reports to the CEO
Build the finance function at a fast-growing senior care technology company shipping hardware to 24 countries.

The company

We went from a lab in Waterloo to 24 countries in five years. Our sensors detect falls and track sleep, health and wellness, with no cameras, wearables or pendants. Families get peace of mind. Older adults keep their independence. Our CTO, Dr. Yihong Qi, holds 680 patents, and the next few hundred get built here.
Why now

We are scaling. One of the largest deals in our history is in delivery, our consumer product launches in January, and we are preparing our next raise. Every one of those runs on numbers leadership can trust: a close that lands on time, a forecast that ties sales to inventory and cash, and books that hold up in diligence. This is the moment to bring in the leader who owns it.
The role

This is the senior finance role at Pontosense. You own the close, the forecast, controls and the numbers behind our next raise, across our entities in Canada and China. You work directly with the CEO and the leadership team, and you are in the room with investors. This is a builder role first and an operator role second. You set up how finance runs here, then you run it.
What you'll own

A monthly close that is reliable and consolidated across Canada and China, landing by business day 10
A forecast the company actually runs on, with sales, inventory and cash tied together
Product costing that is right: landed cost, COGS and inventory planning for hardware built overseas
The raise: the model, the data room and investor reporting, with you in the room
Annual financials prepared and audited on time, and the relationships with our auditors and tax advisors
Controls that hold up across two countries: approvals, spend and intercompany
A seat at the leadership table

What year one looks like

The books close on time every month, consolidated. The forecast is trusted, and inventory is planned, not guessed. Audited financials are current, and our next raise runs on numbers that hold up in diligence.
How we work

Build it right, then make it better. People's safety rides on what we ship, so we test hard and never settle for good enough.
Say it as it is. Kind and direct, at every level, including the CEO.
Real impact. There is more room to make a difference here than at a company ten times our size.
Do what you said. Trust is built on follow-through, and we return it with real ownership.
Hard, and worth it. What we build keeps someone's parent safe at home. Rest well, it's part of the job.

This is for you if

You'd rather own a problem than be assigned a task
You want the mission to matter and the pace to be real
You're happy to be the person who just fixes it

This isn't for you if

You want a playbook handed to you
You need a big team before you can move

You'll thrive here if

You are a CPA who started in audit, then grew with a product or technology company, with promotions along the way
You have owned the close and built the model yourself, not just reviewed them
You have worked with inventory, COGS and supply chain costing. Multi-entity or international consolidation is a strong plus
You have worked with investors, a board or lenders, or are ready to step into that
You explain the numbers plainly to people outside finance, and decide with incomplete information
You are as happy reconciling an account yourself as setting the strategy

You don't need to check every box. If this sounds like you, we'd like to hear from you.
Where this goes

As we raise and scale, this role grows into leading a finance team of your own.
What you get

A sensor for your parents, on us
Direct access to the leadership team. No layers.
Fair pay, with the opportunity for equity
Impact decides your pay and your path, not tenure
Hybrid in Toronto or Waterloo, remote if that's where you do your best work
Health, dental and vision benefits

The details

Pay: $160,000 to $190,000 CAD base salary
This is a new role, created to grow the team, not a backfill
How we hire: typically an initial interview, a short case, and a final interview in person with our CEO and members of the team. We may adjust this depending on the role
We leverage AI tools in our hiring process, but prioritize human input and manual review

jobs.description:
The Director, Finance Technology & Transformation is a critical enabler of Finance modernization and enterprise scale. This role owns the strategy, architecture, and execution of finance systems, integrations, and automation — ensuring that financial data, workflows, and insights flow seamlessly across the organization and franchise network.

As 1-800-GOT-JUNK? evolves toward a Product Operating Model, this leader will help shift Finance from manual processes to a connected, technology-enabled ecosystem. They will partner closely with Finance, Product, and Technology leaders to ensure financial systems evolve in lockstep with new products, pricing models, payment flows, and operating rhythms.

The Director, Finance Technology & Transformation combines financial process knowledge with systems thinking, technical fluency, and cross-functional leadership. They bring structure to complexity, simplify workflows, and ensure Finance technology supports better decisions — not just better reporting.

This role sits at the intersection of Finance, Technology, Product, and the Field
. The Director, Finance Technology & Transformation enables Finance to move faster, think smarter, and scale confidently — automating the manual, simplifying the complex, and ensuring financial systems support the company’s next phase of growth.

Your Impact & What You'll Own

Finance Systems Strategy & Architecture: Own the end-to-end finance systems architecture, ensuring alignment across ERP, CRM, payments, FP&A, and BI platforms. Design scalable, resilient system landscapes that support growth, product expansion, and franchise complexity. Act as the enterprise steward of how financial data moves, connects, and is consumed.
Integration & Data Flow Enablement: Lead the design and delivery of system integrations using integration platforms and native APIs. Ensure timely, accurate, and reliable data flows between finance, product, and operational systems.Establish data governance principles that support a single source of truth and enterprise confidence in financial data.
Product & Technology Partnership: Partner with Product and Technology teams to ensure finance systems support new products, pricing models, and customer journeys. Translate financial requirements into system capabilities early in the product lifecycle. Support experimentation and iteration while maintaining financial discipline and controls.
Leadership, Delivery & Governance: Lead and develop a high-performing team and vendor ecosystem. Set clear priorities, manage dependencies, and drive delivery with accountability. Establish governance for finance systems changes, enhancements, and adoption.
Automation & Process Modernization: Lead the roadmap to automate and optimize core finance processes, including close, AR/AP, forecasting, and reporting. Reduce manual effort and operational risk by simplifying workflows and eliminating redundant processes. Ensure automation efforts balance efficiency, control, and business usability.
Franchise & Field Enablement: Collaborate with franchise partners and field teams to design integrations and tools that simplify their financial workflows. Ensure finance systems scale across the franchise network while respecting local realities and adoption needs. Act as a bridge between enterprise systems and on-the-ground execution.

8 - 12+ years of experience across software engineering, systems architecture, financial technology, enterprise applications, or finance technology transformation, with a strong track record of building and scaling technology solutions.
Strong engineering and coding foundation — with hands-on experience in JavaScript and/or TypeScript and the ability to write, review, troubleshoot, and understand production code. Comfortable working with APIs, webhooks, databases, data pipelines, and integration frameworks.
Advanced integration and data-flow expertise — proven ability to connect systems and make them work together across platforms, data warehouses, and SaaS applications using APIs, middleware, integration platforms, and custom solutions, while ensuring reliable, accurate, and traceable data flows.
Strong technical understanding of modern data and cloud architecture, including relational databases, SQL, APIs, ETL/ELT pipelines, cloud data platforms, event-driven integrations, and integration technologies. Experience with platforms such as Snowflake, Amazon Redshift, or similar is highly valued.
Systems thinker and problem solver who can look across the entire technology ecosystem, identify gaps and points of failure, and determine whether the right solution is configuration, integration, automation, or custom development.
Comfort operating in ambiguity and building from the ground up — able to simplify complex problems, make pragmatic technology decisions, and create scalable solutions without over-engineering. Ability to work closely with Finance, Product, Engineering, Data, and Operations teams and translate between business needs and technical solutions.
Builder mentality — curious, hands-on, and willing to get into the details. You don't just identify that two systems need to connect; you understand how they should connect and can work with engineers or vendors to make it happen.
Understanding of finance processes such as order-to-cash, procure-to-pay, record-to-report, month-end close, revenue and payments is an asset
Experience working with Netsuite or finance systems and applications is an asset

· Create and maintain stakeholder, governance, communications, change and adoption plans suited to a global, federated delivery model.

· Drive consistent execution across data inventory, risk tiering, security controls, classification, retention, disposition and sustainment workstreams.
· Ensure delivery evidence, controls and reporting are clear, traceable and suitable for senior management, audit and regulatory review.
· Manage vendors and systems integrators, including scope, deliverables, commercial performance, quality and knowledge transfer.

· A credible global roadmap, governance model and integrated delivery plan are established and actively used.

· Priority data risks are addressed through a repeatable model that business groups can sustain.

jobs.description:
Contribute to the City of Hamilton, one of Canada’s largest cities - home to a diverse and strong economy, an active and inclusive community, a robust cultural and dining scene, hundreds of kilometers of hiking trails and natural beauty just minutes from the downtown core, and so much more. Join our diverse team of talented and ambitious staff who embody our values of sensational service, courageous change, steadfast integrity, collective ownership and being engaged empowered employees. Help us achieve our vision of being the best place to raise a child and age successfully. #BeTheReason

Job ID #32268: Director, Development Planning
Union: Non-Union
Job Description ID #: A13715
Close date: Interested applicants please submit your application online at www.hamilton.ca/city-council/jobs-cityby 4:00 p.m. on Wednesday October 21, 2026.
Vacancy type: This posting is for an existing vacancy
Internal applicants should apply with your work e-mail address. External applicants are considered only after the internal posting process has been completed. Only applicants chosen for an interview will be contacted.

DIRECTOR, DEVELOPMENT PLANNING

Summary Of Duties

Reporting to the Director of Planning and Chief Planner in the Planning Division, Planning and Economic Development Department, provides strategic leadership, through subordinate management, to a multi-functional workforce engaged in development review and development approvals.

The Director of Development Planning is one of the City’s foremost city-builders, responsible for a range of services and functions related to managing and ensuring the city’s sustainable growth and development.

The role requires both a strategic, long-term outlook, as well as an ability to meet the demands of a fast-paced environment related to development approvals.

Recommends broad policies and long-range strategies with respect to ensuring the efficiency of the City’s development review process and to meet mandated goals and objectives.

Accountable for establishing and achieving Divisional goals and objectives, as established by the Director of Planning and Chief Planner, through the effective and efficient use of financial and staff resources.

Uses a "best practices" approach in developing and delivering quality services in a timely and cost-effective manner. Instills a customer service focus within the Development Planning Section of the Planning Division.

Pursues continual improvements to ensure that the City’s development review process is timely and efficient.

Evaluates and reports on the Development Planning Section's service, financial, administrative and staff performance against internal and external benchmarks. Designs and implements strategies to improve effectiveness and efficiency. Sets above average standards and leads by example.

Acts and behaves to demonstrate a strong leadership and guidance, customer focus, innovation / creativity, team building / team advocacy, staff delegation, empowerment and staff development and are results oriented.

Is a member of the Planning Division Management Team, providing strategic direction for the Division as a whole.

Responsibilities

Ensure excellence in the quality of new development in the City of Hamilton.

You will assume lead accountability and responsibility for the Development Planning Section within the Planning Division

Develop goals and objectives and ensure delivery of development review and development approvals, including but not limited to Official Plan Amendments, zoning approvals, subdivision/condominium approvals, and part lot control.

Ensure compliance with Provincial and Federal statutes and regulations and Municipal by-laws and policies.

Assist the Director of Planning and Chief Planner in responding to various Corporate, community, Provincial or Federal proposals for service initiatives, changes or enhancements.

Assist the Planning Division and the Planning and Economic Development Department in delivering on the City’s climate change objectives.

Assist the Planning Division and the Planning and Economic Development Department in delivering on the City’s objectives with respect to Equity, Diversity and Inclusion.

Provide professional advice, including reports, to Council and its Committees.

Exercise delegated authorities for development approvals, as authorized by City Council, the General Manager of Planning and Economic Development, and the Director of Planning and Chief Planner.

Ensure cost effective delivery of services and provide regular tracking and reporting on revenues and budgets.

Provide leadership and support to staff, and implement engagement and recognition efforts, within the Development Planning Section.

The Director is accountable to the Director of Planning and Chief Planner for ensuring the development review and development approvals program is provided in accordance with City and Provincial guidelines and in the most effective and efficient manner consistent with the City of Hamilton’s and Department’s Mission, Vision and Values.

GENERAL DUTIES

Participate in strategic planning and direction of the Division as a member of the Division Management Team.

Provide coaching and advice to subordinate managers / supervisors to optimize performance.

Develop and monitor the annual Capital / Operating Budget for the Section.

Ensure compliance with Provincial and Federal statutes and regulations and Municipal by-laws and policies.

Respond to various Corporate, community, Provincial or Federal proposals for service initiatives, changes or enhancements.

Implement customer service improvement initiatives and create a customer-focused culture.

Effectively manage the approved financial and staffing resources of the Section.

Provide professional planning advice and consultation, including reports, to Council and its Committees, the business community and the public.

Establish and complete goals and objectives and initiate projects, including but not limited to those related to the following: community development, Official Plan Amendments, business facilitation, Development Review Team, Plan of Subdivision and Plan of Condominium approvals, Zoning By-law Amendments, Part-Lot Control, Cash-in-Lieu of Parking, Sign By-law Variances, Pits and Quarries, Committee of Adjustment application reviews, comments on Ministry of Environment (MOE) Permits, administration / review of Records of Site Condition, street addressing / street names, and preparation of information and educational materials related development processes.

Provides expert testimony to support the City’s position on planning issues at hearings of the Ontario Land Tribunal.

Attends public meetings and presents the city’s position/actions to the public, media and outside government bodies. Participates, and regularly acts as a public and media spokesperson for the work of the Section.

Direct and manage the general administration of the work areas in the Section by developing and recommending new policies and procedures and monitoring existing ones to maximize utilization of resources and improve customer service.

Establish criteria and priorities for annual work program and performance measures. Prepare work schedules, assign duties to staff, establish priorities, conduct staff hiring, monitor and evaluate staff performance, discipline and train staff, as well as assist in developing staff to their full potential.

Provide strong Corporate leadership by developing strategies to attract and retain more businesses, increase employment opportunities, and financially improve the City’s non-residential tax base.

Provide strategic advice and participate on numerous and various Corporate committees including chairing key committees to ensure financial growth, new development and to increase confidence in investment by the business community.

Ensures that employees are provided with and use the appropriate equipment, material and/or procedures required to perform the assigned duties. Ensures that all employees perform work in accordance with applicable Health and Safety legislation and all City of Hamilton corporate and departmental policies and procedures. Ensures that appropriate action is recommended for those employees who do not work in compliance with legislation, policies and procedures.

Works in accordance with the provisions of applicable Health and Safety legislation and all City of Hamilton corporate and departmental policies and procedures related to Occupational Health and Safety.

Performs other duties as assigned which are directly related to the responsibilities of the position.

`

Qualifications

Proven knowledge of urban and regional planning and urban design, corporate strategic planning, managerial principles, and municipal government administration normally acquired by a University Degree, preferably at a Masters level, in Urban or Regional Planning with progressive relevant work experience at a senior management level, in either the private or public sectors, preferably in the Ontario context.
Full professional membership in the Canadian Institute of Planners (MCIP) or related professional organization, and a Registered Professional Planner (RPP).
Highly developed analytical and business planning skills with a proven track record for long-term visioning and big picture thinking.
Highly developed ability to articulate a vision, to lead and inspire others.
Highly effective leadership, facilitation, communication, interpersonal and organizational skills in a predominantly unionized environment.
Demonstrated mediation / dispute resolution and negotiation skills.
Demonstrated ability to effectively manage a large multi-disciplinary staff in a results-oriented environment and in a predominantly unionized environment. Knowledge of collective bargaining process.
Extensive experience in designing and delivering customer-focused programs and services.
Proven ability to deal effectively with elected officials, media, other levels of government, management, peers, staff and the general public.
Thorough knowledge of Planning Law, Planning Act, Municipal Act, Environmental Assessment Act, Provincial Policy Statements, Zoning By-Laws, Official Plans and Ontario Heritage Act.
Thorough knowledge and understanding of statutes, regulations and by-laws affecting the Division.
Working knowledge of computer software applications.
Proven ability to effectively negotiate complex agreements and excellent facilitation skills in order to build consensus.
Must possess strong organizational and time management skills.
Possess a high level of personal integrity and is an excellent communicator.
Demonstrated knowledge of the Health and Safety Act and applicable regulations as it relates to the position.

HOURS: 35 per week
