jobs.title: Director, AI Platform Engineering
jobs.description:
Director, Enterprise AI Platform Engineering

Job Description

BMO is building a dedicated AI Engineering function to deliver the platform capabilities that make enterprise AI safe, governed, and scalable across our business domains and regulatory regimes. We are seeking an experienced technical leader to own the core infrastructure that governs and enforces how AI runs at BMO
- the AI Gateway, Policy Engine, Identity Fabric, AI Registry, Guardrails Runtime, and AI Observability.

This is a build-and-run
leadership role. You will lead a team that designs, ships, and operates the control and orchestration infrastructure sitting between policy authoring and inline enforcement — the capabilities every AI workload at BMO consumes to be secure, compliant, and observable. You will not own the AI models or applications themselves (those are domain-owned); you own the governed platform they run on
, and the runtime evidence that proves they run within policy.

You are a hands-on technical leader who has built platform capabilities at scale, operates what you build, and designs for operability and regulatory defensibility from day one. You blend deep engineering credibility with the executive presence to partner across Security, Architecture, DevOps, and domain teams. You are energized by taking real engineering assets — an existing developer portal, AI registry, a body of policy-as-code, and gateway integrations — and formalizing, scaling, and governing them into an enterprise-grade platform.

What You'll Own

Enterprise Control Plane

Developer Portal & AI Registry - productionize the developer portal; deliver a federated AI Registry spanning agents, models, tools, channels, and evaluations, with self-service onboarding and lifecycle workflows.
Policy Engine - policy-as-code infrastructure (Cedar/OPA), a policy compilation and GitOps distribution pipeline, risk-tiered approval workflows, and a policy simulation environment.
Observability & Audit - a multi-pipeline architecture spanning operational, security, and compliance telemetry; OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions; cross-pipeline trace correlation; and a tamper-evident audit lake producing regulator-ready evidence.
Governance & Lifecycle - certification workflows, automated compliance scoring, decommission governance, and evidence generation for architecture and model-risk review.

Domain Orchestration

Gateway Runtime - domain-hub deployment across multiple clouds; an inline enforcement engine with request-time policy evaluation, routing, residency, budget/quota controls, and circuit breakers, operating within strict latency budgets.
Guardrails Runtime - a multi-stage safety pipeline (input moderation, prompt-injection defense, PII handling, output validation, hallucination detection, policy enforcement) with bilingual (EN/FR) parity and behavioral guardrails for agentic workloads.
Identity Fabric - workload identity for AI (SPIFFE/SPIRE), token-exchange bridging, per-domain trust boundaries, enterprise identity integration, and cross-cloud token federation with zero-trust attestation.

What You'll Deliver (First 12 Months)

A production-hardened Developer Portal and federated AI Registry with sub-5-day self-service onboarding.
An AI Gateway operational in a selected business domain, meeting tiered latency targets.
Policy-as-code infrastructure distributing domain-scoped policy bundles via GitOps, with a working simulation sandbox.
A runtime evidence pipeline producing lineage-stamped, audit-ready traces aligned to model-risk and regulatory expectations.
A team scaled from an initial core (8–12 FTE) toward steady-state through a blend of net-new hiring and reallocation of experienced internal engineers.

How You'll Work

Build-run integrated - your team operates what it builds; there is no separate run team. You design for operability and Engineering support from the start.
Federated - you own the enforcement infrastructure domains consume; domains own their workloads. You enable, you don't centralize execution.
Evidence-first - regulatory evidence (e.g., OSFI E-23, OCC model-risk expectations) is produced at runtime through instrumented infrastructure, not assembled retroactively.
Capability-aligned - your teams own outcomes ("Identity Fabric works across all platforms"), not specific technologies.

Required Core Skills

Organizational & People Leadership

8+ years in technical platform, infrastructure, or AI/ML engineering roles in a large enterprise, including 4+ years leading and managing engineering teams.
Proven organizational leadership: building and scaling engineering teams from a small core to steady-state, including workforce planning, hiring, succession planning, and structuring squads for clear ownership and accountability.
Demonstrated team building across blended teams — integrating net-new hires with reallocated and seconded internal engineers into a single high-performing team with shared identity and standards.
Strong mentoring and coaching track record: developing engineers and technical leads, growing depth and bench strength, giving effective performance feedback, and creating clear technical growth pathways.
Ability to establish and sustain a healthy, inclusive team culture that promotes psychological safety, mutual respect, recognition, and employee engagement, aligned to BMO Values.
Experience leading through change and ambiguity — standing up a new function, aligning a team to a fast-evolving mandate, and maintaining momentum under tight timelines.
Conflict resolution and cross-team influence, including partnering with peer Directors on shared roadmaps and resolving competing priorities.

Platform & AI Engineering Depth

Demonstrated experience building and operating platform capabilities at scale — API gateways, policy/authorization systems, identity/workload-identity infrastructure, observability pipelines, or equivalent shared services.
Strong knowledge of GenAI platform engineering: LLM/AI gateways, model routing and abstraction, RAG and agentic patterns, guardrails, and AI evaluation approaches.
Hands-on experience with policy-as-code and authorization systems (Cedar, OPA/Rego, or equivalent) and GitOps-based distribution.
Experience with workload identity and zero-trust patterns (SPIFFE/SPIRE, mTLS, token exchange, federated identity) — or strong adjacent identity/security engineering depth.
Strong observability engineering background: OpenTelemetry, distributed tracing, and telemetry pipelines across operational, security, and compliance domains.
Multi-cloud fluency (AWS and Azure preferred), cloud-native architecture, containerization/Kubernetes, and Infrastructure as Code.
Hands-on familiarity with modern AI/ML tooling (e.g., Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, SageMaker, Databricks, MLflow, LangChain, or equivalents) sufficient to lead technical direction.
Proven CI/CD, DevSecOps, and MLOps/LLMOps delivery experience.

Governance, Strategy & Communication

Solid grounding in Responsible AI, AI/data governance, privacy, and — ideally — model-risk management and financial-services regulatory expectations.
Executive-grade communication and relationship management across technical and senior-leadership audiences (written, verbal, and presentation).
Strategic and organizational management skills, including multi-year roadmap planning, budgeting, forecasting, and vendor engagement in partnership with Vendor Management.
A critical thinker with strong analytical, problem-solving, and prioritization abilities across a complex, multi-stakeholder portfolio.

Education & Certifications

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical discipline (Master's preferred).
Relevant certifications an asset: cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP) architecture or ML/AI certifications, Kubernetes (CKA/CKAD), security/identity certifications, or enterprise architecture (TOGAF or equivalent).

Join ABC Fitness and become part of a culture that’s as ambitious as it is authentic. Let’s transform the future of fitness—together!

Our Values

Best Life

We believe great work begins with great people. That’s why our culture is built on respect, trust, and belonging. We create an inclusive environment where every team member can bring their authentic self to work—because diverse perspectives drive innovation and meaningful impact.

Growth Mindset

We are doers, thinkers, and dreamers. At ABC Fitness, your growth is our investment. Through continuous learning, mentorship, and professional development opportunities, we empower you to reach new heights—personally and professionally.

One Team

From day one, you’ll be part of a team that collaborates, celebrates, and cares. We move fast, support one another, and have fun along the way. Because when you thrive, we all thrive.

ABC Fitness is becoming the intelligent operating system for the global fitness industry — the infrastructure that powers how 40M+ members are discovered, joined, engaged, and retained across 40,000 operators in 100+ markets. The layer that makes this possible is our API and AI orchestration platform: the control plane that governs how data, agents, partners, and external AI assistants securely access ABC's system of record, payments rails, and member intelligence.

As Director of Product for API & AI Orchestration, you will own this platform end-to-end and build the team and strategy behind it. You will set the vision for how ABC exposes its capabilities — to our 400+ integration partners, to internal teams building embedded AI experiences, and to a new generation of AI agents and assistants via the Model Context Protocol (MCP) — and stand up the roadmap, operating model, and commercial engine to deliver it. This is a rare mandate to build a new platform business at ABC: the interface between our data moat and the AI-native fitness economy, and a durable, monetizable revenue line contributing to our 2030 target of 10% of revenue from AI, API , and data.

What You’ll Do

Own the vision, strategy, and roadmap for ABC's API and AI orchestration platform — the control plane for access, permissions, audit, and monetization across the company — and align it with ABC's intelligent-OS and IPS platform strategy.
Build, lead, and grow a team of product managers, setting direction, coaching for growth, and establishing the operating rhythm and ways of working for the platform organization.
Define and own ABC's MCP strategy: how external AI assistants and agents discover and act on ABC capabilities (availability, pricing, booking, billing, member context) safely, with the right authentication, scoping, governance, and audit.
Own the platform P&L thinking and commercial model: usage-based and tiered monetization, entitlements, metering, and packaging that turn platform access into a scalable revenue line.
Treat the API as a flagship product — set the standard for developer and partner experience across documentation, onboarding, versioning, SDKs, sandbox, and self-serve so partners and internal teams build faster and stay on the platform.
Partner with engineering, security, and compliance leadership to make access governance a first-class capability — granular permissions, consent, audit trails, and compliance (GDPR, CCPA, PCI, SOC) built into the platform.
Act as a senior cross-functional leader across product, engineering, data, payments, GTM, and partnerships — building alignment, managing dependencies, and representing the platform in executive and board-level forums.
Shape the 400+ partner ecosystem strategy with business development, prioritizing the integrations, endpoints, and orchestration patterns that unlock the most partner and member value.
Define and own the KPIs and success metrics for the platform — adoption, partner activation, API reliability, and monetized consumption — and drive data-informed prioritization amid ambiguity and competing demand.
Serve as the internal and external evangelist for the platform, representing ABC with partners, prospective developers, analysts, and strategic customers.

What You’ll Need

15+ years in product management, including experience leading and growing product teams (managing PMs or managers).
A track record of owning API, platform, or developer-facing products end-to-end — from strategy through delivery — and treating them as products others build on.
Demonstrated success building or scaling a platform, API, or ecosystem business, including its commercial and monetization model.
Strong technical fluency: able to set direction on REST/GraphQL APIs, authentication and authorization (OAuth, scopes, tokens), webhooks, versioning, and API governance with senior engineering leaders.
Proven ability to translate a high-level platform vision into strategy, business cases, org design, and prioritized delivery across multiple teams.
Executive presence and communication skills — comfortable influencing at the leadership and board level and negotiating with stakeholders at all levels.
A degree from an accredited university or college, or equivalent relevant experience.

AND IT’S GREAT TO HAVE

Familiarity with the Model Context Protocol (MCP), AI agent tooling, function/tool calling, or LLM orchestration — and a clear point of view on how AI assistants should safely act on platform data.
Experience building monetization for platform or API products: usage-based pricing, metering, entitlements, and packaging.
Exposure to payments, fintech, CRM, or other systems-of-record where compliance, security, and data governance are core to the product.
Experience operating in a private-equity-backed or high-growth software environment with a focus on durable, profitable growth.
Strong leadership and team-player qualities, adept at building relationships and collaborating across functions and geographies.
Deep understanding of agile methodology and ceremonies, and the ability to lead multiple initiatives simultaneously with ownership and accountability.
A growth mindset and familiarity with the fitness industry and modern fitness consumers.

Compensation for this role will be determined based on a variety of factors, including relevant experience, qualifications, skills, geographic location, and market considerations. The anticipated compensation range for this position is -

$174,000.00 - $202,000.00 CAD or 530,000.00 - 540,000.00 PLN- annually. In addition to base compensation, eligible employees may be offered other forms of compensation, such as bonuses, commissions, equity, or other incentive programs, where applicable. Compensation and benefits may vary by location and are subject to applicable legal, business, and market requirements.

WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU
:

Purpose led company with a Values focused culture – Best Life, One Team, Growth Mindset
Time Off – with our open PTO policy, we offer flexibility in how and when you take PTO!
Days of Disconnect – once a quarter, we take a collective breather and enjoy a day off together around the globe. #oneteam

Best Life Perk – we are committed to meeting you wherever you are in your fitness journey with a quarterly reimbursement
Medical/Dental/Vision coverage
EAP – we get you help when you need it. Period.
Premium Calm App – enjoy tranquility with a Calm App subscription for you and up to 4 dependents over the age of 16
And more! – so many benefits we couldn’t even fit them all here!

At ABC Fitness, we don’t just build technology—we build communities and transform lives. Your work matters here, your growth is supported, and your voice is heard. We welcome diverse talent and encourage you to apply, even if you don’t meet every requirement.

jobs.title: Director-Data Retention
jobs.description:
TekStaff's Client has a current vacancy for a 'Director-Data Retention"

Job Description
The opportunity

We are seeking a senior global delivery leader to establish and lead the program office for the Global Data Retention Management Program. The program will coordinate enterprise efforts to identify, secure, classify and remediate over-retained structured and unstructured data, using a risk-based approach and a common global framework. The role is accountable for turning a complex cross-enterprise mandate into an executable roadmap, strong governance, transparent reporting and measurable outcomes.
This is a hands-on leadership role for a self-starter who creates clarity, builds momentum and takes ownership. The successful candidate will work across business groups and control functions, lead a team of project managers and workstream leads, and engage senior business and technology leaders to resolve issues and maintain alignment.

Key accountabilities

· Own integrated delivery across discovery, planning, execution and transition to sustainable business-as-usual controls.
· Establish and run the program management office, including the integrated roadmap, and master schedule. Coordinate with regional delivery teams on their work breakdown structure, resource plan, financial controls and delivery standards.
· Design and operate program governance, including steering committee, governance committee and working-team forums, with clear decision rights, escalation paths and accountabilities.
· Lead multiple project managers, workstream leads, internal teams and external delivery partners. Set expectations, remove barriers and drive timely decisions.
· Develop executive communication and reporting models covering progress, outcomes, milestones, dependencies, risks, issues, decisions, financials and capacity.
· Create and maintain stakeholder, governance, communications, change and adoption plans suited to a global, federated delivery model.
· Partner with business groups to sequence work based on risk, readiness, dependencies and capacity while avoiding duplication with related initiatives.
· Drive consistent execution across data inventory, risk tiering, security controls, classification, retention, disposition and sustainment workstreams.
· Ensure delivery evidence, controls and reporting are clear, traceable and suitable for senior management, audit and regulatory review.
· Manage vendors and systems integrators, including scope, deliverables, commercial performance, quality and knowledge transfer.
Measures of success
· A credible global roadmap, governance model and integrated delivery plan are established and actively used.
· Senior leaders have clear, concise and timely visibility into outcomes, trade-offs, risks and decisions.
· Workstreams have accountable owners, realistic plans and disciplined execution rhythms.
· Priority data risks are addressed through a repeatable model that business groups can sustain.

Experience and expertise

Stakeholder leadership

· Operate confidently with Business Group CIOs and senior business leaders at VP and SVP levels.
· Build alignment across Technology, Data, Cybersecurity, Enterprise Architecture, Risk, Privacy, Compliance, Legal, Records Management, Audit and business teams.
· Frame complex issues simply, present clear options and secure timely decisions without overloading leaders with detail.
· Influence across organizational boundaries, manage competing priorities and maintain constructive challenge when commitments are at risk.
· Create trusted relationships while preserving clear accountability for outcomes, decisions and follow-through.

Leadership competencies

Ownership and drive
Acts as the accountable leader, anticipates needs and follows issues through to resolution.
Self-directed execution
Creates structure from ambiguity, mobilizes quickly and works effectively with limited direction.
Enterprise perspective
Connects delivery choices to risk reduction, business outcomes and long-term sustainability.
Executive communication
Communicates with precision, adapts to the audience and makes decisions easy to understand.
People leadership
Sets high standards, develops team members and creates a culture of accountability and collaboration. (No direct people management)
Pragmatic judgment
Balances pace, control, cost, capacity and quality to keep a complex program moving.

Why this role matters

The Global Data Retention Management Program addresses a material enterprise need: reducing cyber, privacy and regulatory risk while creating stronger and more sustainable control over data assets (structured and unstructured). This role will shape how the organization mobilizes, governs and executes a complex global transformation, while building a delivery model that can be sustained across business groups.

Critical Skills / Must-Haves:

1. 10+ years of progressive experience leading large, complex enterprise programs, including global or multi-business transformation.
2. Demonstrated success building and running a large program office with multiple project managers, workstreams, delivery partners and senior sponsors.
3. Strong command of program governance, integrated planning, dependency management, RAID management, financial oversight, resource planning and executive reporting.
4. Experience delivering programs in data governance, data management, records and information management, cybersecurity, privacy, regulatory remediation, technology risk or related domains.
5. Ability to translate strategy and risk objectives into practical work packages, milestones, measures and accountable execution.
6. Experience leading federated programs where central standards and governance support execution by business or regional teams.
7. Working knowledge of structured and unstructured data environments, data lifecycle practices, classification, retention and disposition concepts.
8. Experience managing consulting firms, systems integrators and specialist vendors in outcome-based engagements.

Dig Insights unites strategy, human understanding, and technology to help brands move decisively, in a world that won’t wait. We work with insights and marketing professionals at some of the world’s most well-loved brands, powering their brand and innovation decision-making. Dig One is our agile technology platform, used by our people and our clients, to deliver smarter and faster decisions.

Our clients span verticals including CPG, QSR, retail, technology, financial services, and telecommunications. Our work is led by a team of over 250 strategists, insights consultants, developers, and data scientists. We work for a global client base out of offices in Toronto, Chicago, London, and Singapore.

Since we started in 2010, we’ve been focused on setting a new standard for the insights industry – challenging the traditional model and building for what comes next. That means hiring people who are bright, creative, resourceful, and kind. People who succeed at Dig are curious, question established norms and are passionate about helping our clients to move their businesses forward. If you want to join a team that takes themselves just seriously enough to produce great work, we’d love to welcome you.

As we continue to grow, both geographically and in our expertise, we are looking for people who want to join a high-growth and highly collaborative company.

Dig insights is looking for a dedicated and passionate Director, Insights to join our growing Toronto office.

Director, Insights – About this role

Working closely with the Analysts, Managers and VP on their team, the Director provides essential support to their team to help execute and deliver client projects. The Director is responsible for delivering a final report including strategic insights/ research findings, summaries, and recommendations to the VP. The Director has demonstrated their research skills and knowledge and is a key contact for clients on any questions or clarifications. They can be relied on for project updates, recommendations on additional analysis required, working with other Dig team members to develop solutions to any project related problems and troubleshoot any issues that arise. The Director also acts as the day-to-day manager of the Analysts and Managers on the team, providing feedback, establishing goals, and helping to train the team on fundamentals, advance research techniques and report writing. In addition to growing their skill set as a researcher, the Directors at Dig are encouraged to take part in our company’s exciting culture and enjoy this dynamic stage in their career.

Your primary responsibilities will include, but are not limited to:

Supporting the sales process through proposal development, including methodology design, costing, scheduling and design considerations.
Overseeing project management in its entirety ensuring timely, quality deliverables according to project design.
Managing a team by guiding data analysis and results communication to ensure projects are delivered with excellence.
Analysing results and creating a "story" that delivers insightful, strategic and actionable answers for clients.
Confidently presenting results to all levels of client organizations in a clear and compelling manner.
Providing advice, guidance and counselling to Research Analysts and Research Managers, including assessment and identification of training needs.
Developing and maintaining client relationships while identifying growth opportunities within existing accounts and consulting/participating in the selling process.

Able to work within a fast-paced dynamic environment.

jobs.title: Director, Enterprise Strategy - Global Banking & Markets
jobs.description:
Requisition ID: 273705

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

Purpose

The Scotiabank Strategy group is a central team focused on shaping the Bank’s strategic agenda, considering both enterprise-wide and business / function-specific strategic questions and opportunities.

Reporting to the Vice President, Enterprise Strategy, the Director, Enterprise Strategy
is a key representative for GBM at the Enterprise Strategy level. GBM encompasses Corporate and Investment Banking and Global Markets, offering clients a range of financial services including lending, transaction services, investment banking advice, and access to capital markets. The Director plays a critical role in supporting the contextualization of GBM strategy within the context of the Bank’s overall strategic framework. The Director also works closely with GBM leadership, Enterprise Strategy partners, and Corporate Functions to deliver strategic insights and, support strategic planning and execution as needed across GBM. The role focuses on shaping strategic direction, translating strategic direction into actionable initiatives, providing analytical rigor, and ensuring strategies are practical, measurable, and executable.

The incumbent combines strong strategy development capabilities and experience in a top-tier strategy consulting or corporate strategy environment with either experience in Corporate & Investment Banking, Capital Markets, and/or related businesses, or a demonstrated ability to rapidly build domain expertise in complex industries. The successful candidate will be expected to quickly develop a deep understanding of GBM businesses, products, clients, and market dynamics and engage credibly with senior business leaders on strategic priorities.

Is this role right for you? In this role, you will be involved in:

Strategy Development & Planning Support

Support the development and refresh of GBM strategy in alignment with the Bank’s enterprise strategy, helping to “connect the dots” across business lines and corporate functions.
Lead discrete strategic workstreams and targeted deep dives across GBM strategic priorities, including growth, profitability, client experience, and operating model initiatives.
Identify, assess, and evaluate strategic opportunities and issues specific to GBM, including implications of market trends, competitive dynamics, regulatory developments, and emerging risks.
Support the annual GBM strategic planning process, including preparation of analysis and materials for Executive Management and the Board, ensuring alignment with enterprise processes and requirements.
Provide structured analytical support and strategic recommendations to senior leaders, under the guidance of the VP.

Strategy Execution, Monitoring & Insights

Design and oversee execution roadmaps for GBM strategic initiatives, working closely with cross-functional partners to ensure alignment, momentum, and delivery against milestones.
Design strategic KPIs and tracking mechanisms to monitor progress against GBM strategic objectives.
Conduct benchmarking and competitive analysis against local and global peers to identify performance gaps, opportunities, and emerging best practices.
Monitor execution risks, dependencies, and trade-offs, and escalate issues with clear options and recommendations.
Support periodic assessments of GBM’s strategic positioning, operating model, and performance outcomes.

Thought Leadership & Strategic Advisory

Act as a thought partner to GBM and enterprise leaders by providing effective challenge, fresh perspectives, and fact-based insights on strategic priorities and must win initiatives.
Facilitate strategic discussions with business leaders, challenge assumptions where appropriate, and drive alignment on priorities and investment decisions.
Synthesize complex analysis into clear, compelling stories and recommendations tailored to executive audiences.
Operate as a strategy advisor to GBM leadership, applying a structured problem solving approach, hypothesis-driven analysis, and executive-level communication to complex business challenges.
Contribute to the preparation and facilitation of GBM and enterprise strategy offsites, planning sessions, and leadership workshops.
Stay current on global capital markets, investment banking trends, and broader financial services developments to inform strategic thinking.

Stakeholder Management & Collaboration

Establish credibility with senior GBM executives by combining structured problem solving, data-driven analysis, commercial insight, and an understanding of client, market, and competitive dynamics.
Build strong working relationships with GBM leadership, enterprise strategy colleagues, and partners across finance, risk, technology, and other corporate functions.
Bridge silos and enable alignment across teams to support execution of GBM priorities.
Act as a trusted partner to senior executives, helping them clarify priorities and translate strategy into execution.

Team Leadership, Culture & Risk

Lead and mentor junior strategy resources and contribute to building a high-performing, inclusive strategy team.
Support talent development through coaching, feedback, and knowledge sharing.
Perform all activities in accordance with the Bank’s risk culture, risk appetite, and control environment.
Ensure strategy work incorporates appropriate consideration of financial, operational, regulatory, and conduct risks.
Foster a customer-focused mindset by embedding client impact and outcomes into strategic analysis and recommendations.

Dimensions

Leads multiple complex strategy workstreams with cross-functional teams across GBM and the broader Bank.
Exercises independent judgment within defined scope on high impact initiatives; escalates key decisions and trade-offs appropriately.
Regular interaction with senior leaders (SVPs, EVPs) within GBM and enterprise functions, with less frequent direct exposure to Group Heads and Board-level forums.
Operates in a highly collaborative environment requiring strong influencing skills without direct authority.

Skills

Do you have the skills that will enable you to succeed? We’d love to work with you if you have the following:

University degree in Business, Finance, Economics, or a related discipline; MBA or equivalent post graduate degree strongly preferred.
Typically 7–12 years of relevant experience, including strategy roles within financial services and/or top-tier management consulting.
Solid working knowledge of Global Banking and Markets, Capital Markets, and Investment Banking businesses and products.
Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional strategy or transformation initiatives
Exceptional structured problem-solving, critical thinking, and quantitative analytical capabilities
Ability to synthesize complex information into clear, compelling recommendations for executive audiences.
Proven ability to communicate complex ideas clearly and concisely to senior audiences.Demonstrated success building credibility quickly with senior business leaders and navigating highly matrixed organizations.
Collaborative leadership style with experience developing high potential talent.
Strong interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills.
Proficiency in MS Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
Proficiency in French and/or Spanish is an asset.

jobs.title: VP, Finance & Controllership
jobs.description:
Banyan Software is the best permanent home for software businesses that serve specialized industries, their employees, and their customers. With a buy-grow-and-hold-for-life approach and a permanent capital base, Banyan acquires and grows companies worldwide, honoring founder legacies and helping portfolio companies modernize through shared AI expertise and operational discipline. Founded in 2016, Banyan operates more than 120 portfolio companies across North and South America, Europe, and APAC, and has appeared on the Inc. 5000 list for six consecutive years. The Banyan Software Foundation, endowed with $100 million in Banyan stock, leverages technology to build a greener and more equitable world.
The Opportunity This is the operational core of our global Finance function. You will own the close, the consolidation, the audit, and the reporting rhythm that turn a growing portfolio of acquired software companies into a coherent whole.
Banyan acquires vertical software businesses and holds them permanently. We don’t buy to flip. We buy to grow. That permanence shapes how we build Finance: it rewards investment in process, systems, and people that compound over years. You will inherit a function in motion, healthy and growing, and set the trajectory for the next layer of operational maturity across HQ and the operating companies.
You will lead a team across Controllership, Global Payroll, and ERP & Reporting, partner closely with FP&A, Tax, and Treasury at HQ, and work directly with Finance Directors at the operating companies.

Why Banyan A permanent-hold model changes how Finance is built.

Most controllership leaders inherit a function being optimized for a sale or transition. Here, you’re building for the long arc: maturing close, consolidation, and reporting practices that compound with every acquisition we add. The work you do this year is still relevant five years from now.
Real scale, real complexity, real velocity.

Many legal entities globally. A growing collection of vertical software businesses, each with its own data and accounting nuances, rolling up into one coherent group. Acquisitions flow through the close on a regular cadence.
Direct partnership with the CFO.

You’ll operate as a thought partner, not a back-office function. The CFO is looking for someone who can translate the numbers into narrative, surface implications, and bring discipline to how Finance shows up across the group.

What You Own The global close and consolidation cycle.

Own the monthly close across HQ and operating companies under US GAAP. The current close runs about ten days; the working target is five. You will set the path to get there, holding integrity as the floor.
The year-end audit.

Manage the external audit relationship and deliver a cleanly run year-end. Coordinate audit asks across HQ and operating companies. Hold the function to a standard an auditor can lean into.
Group-level technical accounting.

Bring deep US GAAP fluency, particularly around software industry topics. Translate technical positions into practical, operational outcomes. Partner with the CFO on judgment calls that need an executive view. You understand the grey, not just the rule.
Standardization across operating companies.

Partner with OpCo Finance Directors to align chart of accounts, reporting packages, close timelines, and day-to-day accounting practice as we continue to migrate operating companies onto a common ERP environment. Bring coherence without flattening what makes each business work locally.
Controllership, Payroll, ERP & Reporting, and AR / AP leadership.

Lead a team of approximately ten, including a Director of Controllership, a Director of Global Payroll, and a Head of ERP & Reporting. Hire, develop, and stretch the team. Build a culture of delegation, ownership, and accountability so the function scales without you becoming the bottleneck.
HQ Finance partnership.

Work alongside the VP, FP&A on reporting infrastructure; with Tax on compliance cadence; and with Treasury on cash and FX support. Bring connective tissue.
Systems and automation.

NetSuite is the group ERP, with adjacent close-management, AP, and expense tooling in place. Identify and introduce automation, AI, and system enhancements that create efficiency as the portfolio scales.
Acquisition integration.

Integrate newly acquired operating companies into the close and reporting rhythm. Make onboarding repeatable.

 Who You Are An experienced controllership leader.

12+ years of progressive controllership experience, including approximately 5+ years in a senior Controllership role.
Public-company-grade reporting rigor.

You've operated in an environment where audit, internal controls, and disclosure discipline are taken seriously. Whether at a public company, a PE-backed platform with audited GAAP financials, or a leveraged credit reporting to an institutional lender group. Public-company background is welcome.
Multi-entity, multi-currency, multi-jurisdiction consolidation. Required

. You've owned a consolidation across 100+ legal entities, many currencies, and multiple jurisdictions. You know what breaks first when an acquisition lands in the close, and you know how to fix it permanently.
A Big 4 (or comparable firm) foundation. Required.

Big 4, or a strong, reputable firm equivalent.
Software industry experience. Required.

Either in-industry or as a software-focused practice at a public-accounting firm.
Hands-on NetSuite experience. Required.

NetSuite is the group ERP. We need someone who has worked in it directly, not someone planning to learn it on the job.
Strong on technical accounting, with commercial sense.

Deep US GAAP applied to software industry topics. You navigate technical positions and audit requirements fluently, and you balance the technical view with what is practical and operational.
An “altitude” leader.

You move from the close-cycle detail to the implications conversation with the CFO without losing either. You tease out the “so what”: not just what the numbers say, but what they mean and what should change because of them.
A team leader who empowers and trusts.

You hire well, develop people, hold a high bar, and run a team without needing to be in the middle of every detail.
Humble and collaborative.

Ego doesn’t show up in the work. You partner across functions without elbows.
Energized by execution.

You drive things to done. You don’t wait for a perfect playbook before you move. The pace is real, and it’s a reason strong operators thrive here.
Intellectually curious about AI and automation.

You evaluate tools. You bring an early-adopter mindset, even if you haven’t yet led a transformation program. AI is helpful here, not critical.

 Strongly Preferred Private equity-backed, holdco, or serial-acquirer environment.
Track record leading or supporting Finance systems improvements: NetSuite migrations or expansions, close-management tool implementations, AI-enabled tooling.
Acquisition integration experience: volume of integrations matters more than complexity of any single deal.
Experience compressing a close cycle.
Global team experience, including managing or partnering with offshore teams

 Location & Compensation Location:

Toronto, ON, Canada (hybrid - 3 days / week in-office)
Travel:

periodic (~10%)
Compensation:

CAD $200,000-$250,000 base salary, excluding annual bonus and equity (when applicable). Salary is based on a number of factors including market conditions, location and may vary depending on job-related skills and experience.

Titre du poste :
Chef du Centre d’Excellence PGI

À propos de & Whitney Canada

Pratt & Whitney Canada (P&WC) est un leader mondial de l’innovation aérospatiale, dont le siège social est situé à Longueuil, au Québec, depuis 1928. Nous concevons et fabriquons des moteurs d’aéronefs de nouvelle génération qui propulsent la plus grande flotte mondiale d’avions et d’hélicoptères dans les segments de l’aviation d’affaires, de l’aviation générale et de l’aviation régionale.

Depuis près de 100 ans, nos équipes sont à l’avant-garde des technologies de propulsion, repoussant les limites afin de rendre nos moteurs plus performants et fiables. Nos moteurs soutiennent des missions essentielles, du transport de passagers et de marchandises aux services médicaux d’urgence, aux opérations humanitaires et à la lutte contre les feux de forêt, partout dans le monde.

Un employeur de choix

Pratt & Whitney Canada a été reconnue comme l’un des meilleurs employeurs au Canada en 2026 selon Forbes, et ce, pour une 11e année consécutive. L’entreprise s’est également classée au premier rang des employeurs de l’industrie de l’aérospatiale et de la défense au pays. De plus, notre siège social figure toujours parmi les meilleurs employeurs de la région de Montréal.

Ensemble, ces distinctions confirment notre réputation d’employeur de choix à Montréal, au Canada et à l’échelle mondiale.

Pourquoi rejoindre l’équipe des Technologies Numériques de Pratt & Whitney Canada ?

Nous sommes en pleine transformation numérique, redéfinissant notre manière de travailler, optimisant nos opérations et transformant nos produits et services pour améliorer les expériences des employés et des clients.

En tant que membre de notre équipe de Technologie Numérique, vous contribuerez à façonner l’avenir en travaillant avec des outils avancés, en automatisant les processus et en innovant dans toutes les fonctions de l’entreprise.

Notre organisation mondiale est déterminée à cultiver une équipe autonome et compétente afin d’apporter des solutions avancées et des capacités numériques à la pointe de la technologie à nos clients.

Sommaire du poste :

Il s’agit d’un rôle de leadership stratégique à fort impact au sein de nos opérations mondiales complexes et orientées mission dans la fabrication et la maintenance après-vente. Le poste bénéficie d’une haute visibilité et implique des interactions à la fois stratégiques et opérationnelles avec les équipes Digital Technologies (DT) et Business Leadership, y compris les cadres supérieurs.

À quoi ressemblera votre quotidien?

Diriger le COE (centre d’excellence) du ERP (PGI – Progiciel de Gestion Intégré) mondial, en définissant la vision, le modèle de gouvernance et la structure organisationnelle alignés sur les principes directeurs clés de l’organisation des Technologies Numériques de Pratt & Whitney.
Conseiller les parties prenantes en tant que leader stratégique et technologique, mobiliser l’expertise et les benchmarks industriels, et influencer au sein d’une organisation matricielle complexe.
Stimuler l’innovation et l’amélioration continue, anticiper les tendances technologiques et catalyser le changement pour améliorer l’expérience utilisateur et l’efficacité opérationnelle.
Gérer budgets, capacité et planification financière en collaboration avec les finances sur une base mensuelle.
Communiquer avec l’équipe de direction (SLT) et les cadres pour aligner les priorités.
Gérer les escalades, agir comme point de contact principal pour les problèmes prioritaires et coordonner leur résolution.
Contribuer à la satisfaction des employés, suivre l’engagement et le moral, et collecter les retours via des enquêtes de satisfaction.
Collaborer étroitement avec tous les groupes DT, y compris RTX, pour assurer l’alignement transversal.
Communiquer clairement les problématiques complexes en termes non techniques, tout en guidant l’équipe dans la collecte des besoins, l’analyse des processus et le développement de solutions globales.
Gérer et livrer un portefeuille complexe d’initiatives d’exploitation et de transformation ERP, et maintenir des feuilles de route stratégiques pluriannuelles avec les parties prenantes.
Concevoir et exécuter une stratégie de transformation SAP S/4 HANA spécifique à P&W, alignée avec le programme RTX.
Superviser les opérations quotidiennes du COE : relations fournisseurs, gestion budgétaire et des ressources, suivi de performance et évaluation des risques, en appliquant les méthodologies projet cascade et agile.
Gouverner la gestion du changement ERP, la planification des versions, la gestion de la demande, de la capacité et de la priorisation.
Piloter l’harmonisation des processus globaux et assurer l’alignement avec les objectifs métier pour la planification, fabrication, chaîne d’approvisionnement, qualité, logistique et finance (OEM et Aftermarket).
Maîtriser les ERP et processus métier de bout en bout (Opportunity-to-Cash, Record-to-Report, Source-to-Pay, Plan-to-Sustain) dans un environnement réglementé.
Superviser et optimiser un paysage ERP complexe (SAP et non SAP), incluant PLM, MES, portails fournisseurs, QMS et applications sur mesure.
S’adapter rapidement aux priorités changeantes tout en gérant risque et impacts sur le portefeuille.
Diriger une équipe performante et développer une stratégie de talents : montée en compétences, attraction de nouveaux talents, adoption de SAP S/4 HANA, Analytics et IA générative.
Gérer une équipe mondiale de leaders SAP et experts fonctionnels, promouvoir l’amélioration continue et le partage de connaissances.
Coacher et encadrer les membres de l’équipe pour soutenir leur développement professionnel et renforcer leurs compétences.
Garantir la conformité aux réglementations IT et A&D, aux normes de sécurité (ITAR, DFARS), à la loi SOX et aux contrôles internes.
Soutenir les opérations d’infrastructure pour maintenir les solutions à grande échelle et garantir une couverture 24/7, y compris jours fériés et week-ends.

Ce poste a été désigné comme « sur site
», avec un travail régulier en personne dans nos locaux situés à Longueuil, QC. Il nécessitera également des déplacements vers différents sites selon les besoins pour participer à des sessions de travail et collaborer directement avec différents intervenants de l’entreprise. Les déplacements sont estimés à au moins 25 %. Le poste est basé dans notre site principal à Longueuil, QC.

Quest-ce qu’il vous faut pour réussir ?

Qualifications requises :

Baccalauréat en ingénierie, informatique, technologies de l’information ou systèmes d’information avec 14+ années d’expérience dans les systèmes ERP ; OU diplôme supérieur dans les mêmes domaines avec 12+ années d’expérience dans les systèmes ERP.

Qualifications recherchées :

Solide capacité de management – expérience démontrée dans la conduite et la gestion de projets ERP DT complexes et à grande échelle.
Orientation résultats – focalisé sur l’atteinte des objectifs malgré les obstacles internes ou externes.
Aptitude business forte – capacité à apprendre rapidement, comprendre et interpréter les processus métier, agir en tant que partenaire de confiance et être reconnu comme contributeur de valeur.
Compétences interpersonnelles solides – capacité à collaborer efficacement avec différentes équipes pour atteindre des objectifs communs.
Maîtrise des processus de cycle de vie logiciel.
Autonomie et proactivité – capacité à prendre en charge des missions et à livrer des résultats de manière fiable.
Excellentes compétences en communication – aptitude à transmettre clairement des informations complexes, tant à l’écrit qu’à l’oral.

Ce poste s’inscrit dans un milieu de travail francophone, néanmoins il nécessite une très bonne connaissance de l’anglais pour lire et comprendre, sur une base quotidienne, de la documentation et des termes techniques qui peuvent émaner d’organisations internationales, ainsi que pour écrire et communiquer en anglais avec des clients, des fournisseurs ou des collègues internationaux.

Ce que nous offrons

Programme de régime de retraite et d’épargne avec cotisation de l’employeur
Programme d’assurance collective
Possibilités d’avancement (progression de carrière)
Programme de mérite ou programme de reconnaissance
Programme de santé et bien-être, y compris la télémédecine
Club récréatif et sportif
Garderies à proximité
Accessibilité en transport ou programme de transport en commun et stationnement gratuit

Travailler chez Pratt & Whitney Canada

Le masculin est utilisé sans discrimination et uniquement dans le but d’alléger le texte. Nous étudierons la demande d’emploi de tous les candidats qualifiés.

Chez Pratt & Whitney Canada, nous allions avec passion, audace et rigueur pour concevoir, fabriquer et entretenir les moteurs d’aéronefs les plus avancés et les plus fiables au monde.

Notre travail et la qualité de nos produits contribuent au succès de nos clients, qui à leur tour sauvent des vies, soutiennent le commerce, connectent les communautés et protègent les libertés.

Chez Pratt & Whitney Canada, vous avez l’occasion de faire une différence tous les jours ; il suffit de lever les yeux. Êtes-vous prêt à vous dépasser ?

jobs.title: Senior Director, Product - Threat Intelligence & Detections
jobs.description:
At Arctic Wolf, you won’t just watch the cybersecurity industry evolve – you'll help lead the change. Our global Pack is made up of people who thrive on solving hard problems, moving fast, and building technology that protects organizations around the world. We’re proud to be recognized by Forbes, CNBC, Fortune, CRN, Gartner Peer Insights and IDC MarketScape – but what matters most is the work behind it: delivering real outcomes for customers through award winning innovation like our Aurora Platform.

If you’re looking for meaningful work, smart teammates and the chance to make a real impact in a high-growth company that’s redefining security operations, Arctic Wolf is the right place for you!

Our mission is simple: End Cyber Risk. We’re looking for Senior Director, Product - Threat Intelligence & Detection
to be part of making this happen.   

LOCATION
: This role is open to Remote-United States, Remote-Canada, Hybrid-Eden Prairie-MN-USA, Hybrid-Waterloo-ON-CAN.

This senior product management lead role for Arctic Wolf defines and evangelizes the commercial strategy and product roadmap for threat intelligence & threat hunting along with delivering on the platform strategy to drive detection efficacy and efficiency for the latest threats keeping our customers safe. You will collaborate with Architecture, Engineering, Security Research, and cross-functional teams to align product vision with company goals, guide strategic planning, and drive innovation and outcomes in threat intelligence, threat hunting and detection engineering. You will lead initiatives to map strategy to execution, commission research, define OKRs, and maintain alignment across product lines and stakeholders. As a respected leader in the cybersecurity space, you will influence organizational structure, drive cross-team buy-in, mentor others, and represent your group with transparency and integrity.

Role Scope

Presents at stakeholder meetings to communicate the vision and alignment with corporate strategy
Works with product principals and engineering leaders to communicate strategy and high-level roadmap for threat intelligence, detections, and AI related initiatives to Leadership, PM and Engineering teams
Participates in cross-functional efforts and co-design to ensure product initiatives leverage existing security research capabilities and avoid redundant development
Decides (with Architecture and Security Research leadership) when new threat detection or intelligence capabilities are sufficiently differentiated to create new products or platforms and deliver highest value in efficacy and efficiency
Creates vision and strategy presentations and documents that address high-level cybersecurity problems, emerging threat landscapes, and AI-driven solutions
Defines and drives the strategic vision for threat intelligence and threat hunting while overseeing the incubation of breakthrough threat detection capabilities that improve effectiveness of our products (MDR, EDR) and the SOC
Leads cross-functional teams through product development, fostering a culture of experimentation, rapid iteration, threat validation, and customer-centric innovation in security
Partners with executive leadership to align threat intelligence and AI initiatives with long-term business goals, ensuring resource allocation and portfolio management driving high-impact security outcomes

Knowledge & Experience

Deep expertise in threat intelligence, threat hunting, detection engineering, and security research practices and their application to product development
Demonstrated understanding of conversational AI, large language models (LLMs), and machine learning applications in cybersecurity and threat intelligence and or detections is a plus
Collaborate and run cross-functional backlog reviews for threat intelligence and detections; participate in other product line reviews to contribute to overall organizational prioritization
Commission research into possible strategies to address customer security problems and evolving threat landscapes
Identify OKRs for threat intelligence, threat hunting and detections in support of wider corporate goals
Identify follow-up analysis and insights into emerging threat patterns and their implications for product strategy

Complexity and Problem Solving

Communicates to teams about process changes and the value these bring—provides clarity and answers questions about threat detection innovation priorities
Works with Engineering and Labs leadership to align threat intelligence, detection, and AI strategies with company direction, then breaks out specific initiatives to implement and support the strategy
Propagates priorities and "big rocks" to product principals and technical leaders to create an overall threat intelligence and detection product roadmap
Helps other product teams understand how threat intelligence, detections, and AI capabilities enable faster, more effective threat response in their solutions
Identifies projects that shift priorities and communicates with stakeholders across threat intelligence, security operations, and engineering teams

Collaboration & Interaction

Aligns cross-functional teams (Security Research, Engineering, Sales, Go-to-Market) on threat intelligence product strategies & roadmap to successfully meet the business needs
Drives buy-in and support from the SOC, security research, engineering, sales, and broader organization improving our threat intel and detection efficacy and efficiency
Creates documentation required for calibration efforts and prepares for reviews with evidence of achievements to represent the threat intelligence and detection portfolio

Required Qualifications

7+ years of progressive experience in cybersecurity, with deep expertise in threat intelligence, threat hunting, detection engineering, incident response, or security research—this is non-negotiable
10+ years of product management experience, including 3+ years at a director level or equivalent managing complex, cross-functional teams delivering enterprise security products at scale
Proven track record of taking products from strategy through successful market launch, with quantifiable results in revenue growth, customer adoption, or competitive market share expansion
Executive presence with ability to speak credibly to technical and non-technical audiences about cybersecurity strategy, emerging threats, and security innovation

Preferred Qualifications

Background in Threat Intelligence, managed security services (MSS), managed detection and response (MDR), or security operations centers (SOCs)
Experience within a fast-growth cybersecurity company or within a security labs/innovation division focused on emerging threats or technologies
Active presence and network within the cybersecurity community, threat intelligence organizations, security research ecosystem, or industry consortiums is a plus

What We're Looking For

A seasoned cybersecurity leader and product strategist who brings deep technical credibility and hands-on threat intelligence experience combined with strong executive product management acumen. You understand evolving threat landscapes and advanced adversary tactics, have direct experience with threat intelligence analysis and threat hunting, and are passionate about applying emerging AI technologies to revolutionize how organizations detect and respond to threats. You can operate effectively at the executive level, balance strategic vision with execution discipline, and drive organizational alignment on complex, multi-year threat defense initiatives. You thrive in a fast-paced, innovation-focused environment and have the credibility to influence executive decision-making on security investments.

About Arctic Wolf

At Arctic Wolf, we foster a collaborative and inclusive work environment that thrives on diversity of thought, background, and culture. This is reflected in our multiple awards, including Top Workplace USA (2021-2025), Best Places to Work – USA (2021-2025), Great Place to Work – Canada (2021-2024), Great Place to Work – UK (2024-2026), and Kununu Top Company – Germany (2024-2026). Our commitment to bold growth and shaping the future of security operations is matched by our dedication to customer satisfaction, with over 10,000 customers worldwide and more than 2,000 channel partners globally. As we continue to expand globally and enhance our technology, Arctic Wolf remains the most trusted name in the industry.

Our Values

Arctic Wolf recognizes that success comes from delighting our customers, so we work together to ensure that happens every day. We believe in diversity and inclusion, and truly value the unique qualities and unique perspectives all employees bring to the organization. And we appreciate that—by protecting people’s and organizations’ sensitive data and seeking to end cyber risk— we get to work in an industry that is fundamental to the greater good.  

We celebrate unique perspectives by creating a platform for all voices to be heard through our Pack Unity program. We encourage all employees to join or create a new alliance. See more about our Pack Unity here.   

We also believe and practice corporate responsibility, and have recently joined the Pledge 1% Movement, ensuring that we continue to give back to our community. We know that through our mission to End Cyber Risk we will continue to engage and give back to our communities.  

All wolves receive compelling compensation and benefits packages, including:  

Equity for all employees 
Flexible time off and paid volunteer days 
RRSP contribution and matching
Training and career development programs 
Comprehensive private benefits plan including medical, mental health, dental, disability, life and AD&D, and value-added services 
Robust Employee Assistance Program (EAP) with mental health services 
Family-forming benefits, enhanced maternity benefits, and paid parental leave

Arctic Wolf is an Equal Opportunity Employer and considers applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, orientation, national origin, age, disability, genetics, or any other basis forbidden under federal, provincial, or local law. Arctic Wolf is committed to fostering a welcoming, accessible, respectful, and inclusive environment ensuring equal access and participation for people with disabilities. As such, we strive to make our entire experience as accessible as possible and provide accommodations as required for candidates and employees with disabilities and/or other specific needs where possible. Please let us know if you require any accommodation by emailing recruiting@arcticwolf.com.   View our Hiring Page to learn more about our application process.

Security Requirements

Conducts duties and responsibilities in accordance with AWN’s Information Security policies, standards, processes, and controls to protect the confidentiality, integrity and availability of AWN business information (in accordance with our employee handbook and corporate policies). 
Background checks are required for this position.  
This position may require access to information protected under U.S. export control laws and regulations, including the Export Administration Regulations (“EAR”).  Please note that, if applicable, an offer for employment will be conditioned on authorization to receive software or technology controlled under these U.S. export control laws and regulations.

jobs.description:
AI-DNA VP, North America Channel — GFI Software

Are you a hands-on channel operator who can run a real book of business — not a slide about one? Do you use GenAI daily as a working method, not a talking point? If so, come own the North America channel for GFI Software.

GFI Software
is a global vendor of security and IT operations products — Kerio Control (firewall), Kerio Connect (business mail), GFI MailEssentials, GFI LanGuard, GFI HelpDesk, and Exinda — sold to small and mid-sized businesses in over 100 countries. Two-thirds of our revenue is outside the United States.

We go to market 100% through the channel — GFI to distributor to reseller to end customer. Our North America distributor is one of our strongest global partners, and we recently refreshed the distributor relationship to raise the bar on how the US business is run. Our North America reseller base is hundreds of partners strong — a mix of large DMRs and a long tail of smaller MSPs, VARs, and regional partners. Some are excellent. Many are not.

Your Job, In Order

Steward the renewals. Do not let a dollar of the existing book leak during the distributor transition. When a customer is up for renewal on June 30th and their reseller has not issued a quote by June 20th, that is your fire.
Segment the reseller base into Group A and Group B. Group A adds value — MSPs, installers, active demand-gen. Group B recycles paper and pockets margin. Move Group B's business to Group A partners and retire Group B relationships. This will create noise. You must have the stomach for it.
Drive AI product attach across Group A. Once the book is stable, unlock the AI-driven capabilities we have built in Kerio and GFI across the reseller base.

You will use AI tools daily
— Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot — to review reseller performance, prepare partner conversations, extract patterns from renewal data, and codify what Group A partners do that Group B partners don't. We want a concrete working method, not a philosophy.

This is an individual-operator role
. You will have no direct reports. You will have the full GFI global pre-sales, post-sales, marketing, and product organization behind you, plus our distributor's US team. The entire GFI company is a channel team.

Fixed compensation
: USD $200,000 per year, $100 per hour (2000 hours) — 1099 contractor, no quota, no commission, weekly Payoneer pay. Fully remote, US-based, ~80% availability during North America business hours.

Requirements

Must be based in the United States, Canada, or Mexico.
7+ years of sales or channel account management experience, with a track record as an individual operator rather than solely as a people manager.
Direct experience running, stabilizing, or consolidating an existing reseller or distributor channel; prior experience segmenting or culling a partner base is a strong plus.
Demonstrated ability to use GenAI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Copilot, Claude) to analyze data and improve work quality and productivity.
Fluency in GRR vs. NRR, and building partner segmentation off ARR concentration, is a must.

This Role Is Not For You If

Remote,

LocalOne is a technology company preparing multiple products for the North American services market. The first commercial product is a universal services marketplace. Planned capabilities also include protected buyer–seller transactions, AI that structures requests and compares providers, and LocalOne's own AI agents operating within permissions set by users.
LocalOne is pre-launch. We have the product concept and project documentation. The technical foundation and the engineering team are still to be built, and you will lead that work from the start.

Lead technical architecture and engineering standards across LocalOne products.
Work with product management to turn approved priorities into an MVP plan and sequenced engineering work, with estimates and dependencies across teams.
Work with HR to build the engineering team: define role requirements, conduct technical interviews and assess candidates' skills and suitability. LocalOne leadership approves final hiring decisions.
Lead and coordinate specialists in backend, payments, iOS, Android, web, AI/data, DevOps/security/SRE and QA as the team grows.
Write and review backend code and resolve complex problems across connected systems.
Make technical decisions on cloud services, providers and AI tools, weighing product requirements, security, integration effort and operating costs.
Oversee release readiness, reliability, incident escalation, backups and recovery.
Maintain technical documentation, clear responsibilities and knowledge transfer.

Required experience

Hands-on backend development in at least one modern language, with software delivered and supported in production.
Strong backend/API design and relational database skills, including PostgreSQL-class systems, transactions, concurrency, migrations and data integrity.
Order and payment state machines: durable events, idempotent operations, webhooks, retries and recovery after failures.
Payment provider integrations (account verification, payout states, refunds, chargebacks), plus internal ledger design and reconciliation with provider records.
Launching a product from initial development into production, ideally a marketplace, fintech or SaaS product with orders and payments.
Managing and mentoring engineering teams, conducting technical interviews and assessing the quality and timeliness of engineers' work.
Turning product priorities into engineering plans and estimates, and explaining technical decisions in terms of delivery dates, costs, security and service reliability.

Nice to have

Working knowledge of cloud services, CI/CD, monitoring, secrets management, security controls and safe release and rollback practices.
Practical experience with AI model integration: structured outputs, evaluations and fallbacks when a model fails.
Familiarity with marketplace payment flows: seller verification (KYC/KYB), holding and releasing funds.
Designing permissions and audit trails for AI agents that act on behalf of users, including protection against prompt injection.

Suitable backgrounds include CTO, Head/VP of Engineering, or Staff/Principal Backend or Platform Engineer with engineering leadership experience.

Full-time employee role, fully remote. Candidates may be based in any country; how employment is structured in each country is agreed individually.
Expected annual base salary for the initial full-time employment: US$150,000.
LocalOne is pre-launch and raising financing, expected to close within three months. Paid employment begins after financing is secured and terms are agreed. Apply through LinkedIn. Please include:

your CV or professional profile;
examples of relevant products you have built or led;
your potential availability;
a short answer (a few sentences): what is the most difficult payment or data-consistency failure you have investigated, and how did you resolve it?

Applications are treated confidentially.

Provide clear, concise, commercially focused communication on how the business achieves its financial, strategic, and operational outcomes

Drive value through local, regional, and global initiatives, from new market acceleration to pricing strategy

Distributed team leadership

The Director, Financial Reporting & Internal Controls is responsible for the Company’s consolidated financial reporting, technical accounting, global statutory reporting and audit activities, and oversight of the internal control environment. This role will oversee a small team, providing day-to-day leadership, coaching, workload prioritization and performance support while ensuring high-quality execution of key reporting and control deliverables. The role partners closely with senior finance leadership, regional finance teams, cross-functional stakeholders and external auditors.

Key Responsibilities

Prepare the Company’s quarterly and annual consolidated financial statements and related disclosures in accordance with IFRS.
Support quarterly and annual reporting processes and review significant accounting entries and adjustments.
Ensure consistency and accuracy of financial reporting across the organization.
Lead the consolidated financial statement audit, acting as the primary relationship manager with external auditors, coordinating key deliverables, reviewing and participating in the negotiation of audit fees, and resolving audit and accounting matters.
Serve as a key technical accounting resource and lead the assessment and documentation of complex and non-routine transactions under IFRS, including revenue recognition, share-based compensation, leases, pensions, restructuring and provisions, impairments, business combinations, legal entity restructuring and other complex accounting matters.
Monitor new accounting standards and developments and assess their impact on the Company’s financial reporting and accounting policies.
Oversee global statutory financial statements, audits and required filings across multiple jurisdictions, including managing the statutory audit calendar, coordinating with local finance teams, external auditors and service providers, monitoring progress and driving timely completion.
Oversee the financial internal control environment, including monitoring key controls, identifying control gaps and supporting remediation activities.
Partner with Tax, Treasury, Legal and other functions on significant transactions, restructurings and other accounting matters.
Support acquisitions, integrations, legal entity restructurings and other strategic initiatives from an accounting and financial reporting perspective.
Drive continuous improvement and standardization of financial reporting, statutory audit and related finance processes.
Lead, coach and develop a small team, including setting priorities, assigning work, providing timely feedback and supporting professional growth.
Promote a collaborative, high-performance team environment with clear expectations, effective communication and accountability for deliverables.

Must hold a recognized professional accounting designation (CPA, ACA, or ACCA).
10+ years of progressive accounting and financial reporting experience, preferably including experience in a large multinational organization and/or public accounting.
Strong knowledge of IFRS.
Experience in preparing consolidated financial statements and related disclosures.
Strong technical accounting research and documentation skills.
Experience managing external audits and global statutory reporting requirements.
Experience working across multiple legal entities, jurisdictions and finance teams.
Strong project management skills with demonstrated ability to manage multiple concurrent deadlines.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills and ability to communicate complex accounting matters clearly to both finance and non-finance stakeholders.
Demonstrated people management experience, including coaching, developing and managing the performance of direct reports in a finance or accounting environment.

jobs.title: Director, Enterprise Managed Services Sales
jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Director, Enterprise Managed Services Sales based in Canada.

This is a senior enterprise sales opportunity focused on transforming how large organizations build, manage, and operate media infrastructure.

You will target Fortune 1000 organizations with in-house studios, production teams, internal networks, and live event operations.

The role combines consultative selling with deep media operations expertise, requiring you to diagnose operational challenges before shaping the right solution.

You will engage senior communications, marketing, technology, procurement, and finance stakeholders and build relationships across complex buying groups.

Success means creating recurring, multi-year managed services relationships while expanding existing accounts from individual projects into ongoing operations.

Working closely with engineering and operations teams, you will help design scalable solutions spanning production, cloud, remote workflows, staffing, facilities, and 24/7 operations.

The position offers significant autonomy, executive visibility, uncapped commission, and the opportunity to influence the growth of an enterprise-focused media services business.

Accountabilities

Build and manage a new-logo pipeline of Fortune 1000 enterprises with in-house media, studio, or live event operations, prioritizing multi-year managed services agreements over one-time projects.
Engage the full enterprise buying group, including communications and marketing executives, media production leaders, IT and network stakeholders, procurement, and finance.
Conduct operational assessments covering staffing, facilities, production workflows, uptime risks, and costs, then translate findings into tailored managed services solutions.
Collaborate with engineering and operations teams to package end-to-end offerings covering consulting, facility design and build, embedded staffing, cloud and remote production, and 24/7 network operations.
Own proposals and RFP responses, including solution scope, staffing models, service-level agreements, and commercial structures.
Identify opportunities to expand existing enterprise accounts from individual events or projects into recurring managed operations.
Represent the organization at industry events and executive forums while bringing market intelligence back to inform sales positioning and service development.
Maintain an accurate sales forecast in HubSpot, including pipeline stages, expected close dates, opportunities, and next steps.

Requirements

10+ years of experience in media production and operations within enterprise environments or live broadcast news.
5+ years of experience leading media production or media operations at Director level or above.
Proven experience managing large production teams, vendors, budgets, and multi-site facilities, including purchasing and managing comparable services.
Strong knowledge of broadcast and digital media environments, including live production, studio operations, content workflows, cloud and remote production, and distribution across television, streaming, and social platforms.
Demonstrated success transforming production workflows or operating models with measurable improvements in cost, speed, efficiency, or reliability.
Strong executive presence and experience engaging C-suite communications, marketing, and technology leaders.
An established professional network across enterprise media and broadcast.
A consultative sales mindset, with the ability to diagnose operational challenges and translate technical architectures into clear business outcomes.
Proven ability to carry a sales quota, develop pipeline from target account lists, and drive complex enterprise sales cycles.
Experience in telecommunications, financial services, or other enterprise environments operating internal networks, brand studios, or executive communications at scale is a plus.
Previous sales, business development, or client-facing agency experience is desirable.
Background in creative content strategy and corporate communications alongside technical operations is an advantage.
Familiarity with managed services commercial models, including SLAs, staffing-as-a-service, and multi-year MSAs, is preferred.
Existing relationships within enterprise media communities in major U.S. markets are a plus.

Benefits

Base salary plus uncapped commission.
Full-time employment.
Remote work option, with Washington, DC identified as a primary location.
Approximately 30–40% travel to client sites, facilities, and industry events.
Senior-level opportunity with significant enterprise sales ownership and executive exposure.
Opportunity to work across managed services, media infrastructure, cloud production, remote workflows, and 24/7 operations.
Exposure to large-scale enterprise clients across technology, telecommunications, financial services, consumer brands, and other industries.
Opportunity to build long-term recurring revenue relationships and influence strategic service offerings.
