We’re an AI-powered learning platform that helps organizations create, deliver, and manage training all in one place. But our real mission goes deeper: we help teams move faster, work smarter, and focus on the work that truly matters. Our platform is built with intelligent, time-saving tools that personalize learning, eliminate busywork, and turn training from a checkbox into a superpower. The result? Better experiences for learners and real results for businesses.

We’re shaping the future of learning with a team that isn’t afraid to challenge the status quo. If you're excited by the idea of using AI to make work-life better for real people–you’ll feel right at home here. And it’s not just what we build, it’s how we show up. At Docebo, our values aren’t just posters on the wall—they guide how we work every day. We call it the Docebo Heart
: trust by default, assume positive intent, and create space for different perspectives to thrive.

So… what are you waiting for? Join 900+ Docebians around the world and help us reinvent the way people learn, because learning never stops.

The Adventure Ahead 🚀

As our Vice President, Information Security, you will step up as the de facto security leader owning Docebo’s global security strategy across product, cloud, GRC, and AI. This is not an advisory tower role; you will operate at executive altitude while staying close to real architecture, engineering decisions, threat modeling, and control execution. You will drive hard, measurable risk reduction while pioneering AI-first security practices that empower our business to move fast with complete confidence.

The Day-to-Day 🗓️

Architect Global Strategy: Own and evolve Docebo’s enterprise security roadmap across product security, cloud hardening, GRC, privacy, and incident response to achieve measurable control maturity.
Embed Security by Design: Partner deeply with Product and Engineering to integrate threat modeling, secure SDLC, CI/CD security, identity controls, and vulnerability remediation into core engineering workflows.
Pioneer AI-First Security: Build robust governance and controls for AI products and internal tooling while harnessing AI to automate detection, vulnerability management, and threat response.
Champion Customer Trust: Lead compliance programs (SOC 2, ISO 27001) backed by real controls, and represent Docebo with executive credibility in board updates, audits, and enterprise customer due diligence.
Elevate Defense Operations: Strengthen security telemetry, threat intelligence, and detection across cloud and corporate environments to protect against emerging modern attack patterns.
Empower High-Impact Teams: Lead and coach a talented security team, building a high-accountability culture focused on clear outcomes, rapid execution, and continuous learning.

Your Superpowers ⚡

Proven Executive Leadership: Significant experience leading information security programs in a software, SaaS, or tech product environment with a track record of executive and board collaboration.
Deep Technical Foundations: Hands-on mastery of application security, cloud security (AWS), infrastructure, identity systems, secure SDLC, and modern vulnerability management.
Mandatory Certification: Active CISSP credential backed by a deep understanding of SOC 2, ISO 27001, privacy regulations, and enterprise SaaS security standards.
Collaborative Business Driver: Exceptional ability to forge trusted partnerships across Product, Engineering, Legal, and Sales, acting as an enabler who balances security with business velocity.
Outcome-Focused Execution: A clear track record of using metrics and business risk language to make decisive, risk-informed choices in complex, ambiguous environments.

Bonus Points 🎯

AI Security Expertise: Hands-on experience securing AI-enabled products and LLMs, or utilizing AI tools to scale security operations and automated testing.
Advanced Technical Certifications: Additional credentials such as CISM, CISA, CCSP, AWS Security Specialty, or GIAC, combined with offensive security or red teaming experience.
Enterprise & Public Sector Reach: Proven experience navigating FedRAMP standards, public-sector requirements, and high-growth global SaaS expansion.

Our Hybrid Work Philosophy 🤝

Great work can happen anywhere but coming together helps us go further. Our team spends three days a week in the office (Tuesday-Thursday) to collaborate, solve problems, and learn from each other. With flexibility the rest of the week, it’s a balance designed to help everyone do their best work and keep growing.

Our Total Rewards Philosophy
🎉

Our Total Rewards Philosophy centers around three core areas to reward and care for our People:

Rewarding Impact: We lead with competitive pay to reward the impact, skills and traits that fuel our success.
Fostering Holistic Wellbeing: We care deeply about and invest in the whole person with programs that support our people’s physical, mental, and financial well-being.
Empowering Our Talent Culture: We build a culture of trust and empowerment by designing our rewards and benefits with transparency, equity, and flexibility, enabling our people to do their best work and stay for the long haul.

Our Promise to You
😍

Financial Wellness: Own a piece of Docebo through our Employee Share Purchase Plan (ESPP) at a 15% discount, plus a competitive compensation package.
Your Well-Being, Covered: You’ll get access to health benefits, so you can get the care you need when you need it.
Rest, Relax, Repeat: Rest and recharge with paid vacation days, two company-wide Docebo Days, floating holidays for cultural celebrations, and your birthday off!
Family First: We provide coverage offering you time with your little one(s) so you can soak up all those precious moments. Fun fact: we had 30 Docebian babies join the family in 2025!
Connections That Count: Connect with global communities through our Employee Resource Groups (including PRIDE, DWA, BIDOC, and Green Ambassadors) and company-wide events that keep the fun rolling all year long.

About Docebo 💙

At Docebo, we create seamless, AI-powered learning experiences for over 3,000 customers worldwide. We have successfully achieved two IPOs (TSX: DCBO & NASDAQ: DCBO), been recognized as a top SaaS e-learning solution, and are growing exponentially in the process. We're a global company, with office across North America, EMEA, APAC, and beyond. Our team is guided by five core values— Grow Together Win Together, Build with Our Customer, Clear is Kind, Own Outcomes, Progress Over Perfection
—that shape everything we do. If this resonates with you, now is the perfect time to join one of the fastest-growing learning technology companies in the world.

Docebo is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. We are committed to diversity and inclusion in our workforce. All qualified applicants and employees will receive consideration for employment regardless of their race, colour, religion, sex (including pregnancy, gender identity, and sexual orientation), national origin, citizenship status, age, disability, genetic information, or any other category protected under applicable law.

As a federal contractor, Docebo is committed to the principles of affirmative action and equal employment opportunity for protected veterans and individuals with disabilities. Docebo does not discriminate because of protected veteran status or on the basis of disability, and Docebo takes affirmative action to employ and advance in employment qualified protected veterans and individuals with disabilities.

jobs.title: Director of Strategic Finance
jobs.description:
About Forma.ai:
  Forma.ai is a Series B startup that's revolutionizing how sales compensation is designed, managed and optimized. We handle billions in annual managed commissions for market leaders like Edmentum, Stryker, and Autodesk. 
Our growth has been fuelled by our passion for fundamentally changing and shaping how companies use sales intelligence to drive business strategy.  
We’re welcoming equally driven individuals who are excited about creating something big!  
DIRECTOR OF STRATEGIC FINANCE

Strategic FP&A, AI Automation, & Executive-Level Storytelling
ABOUT THE ROLE:

We are looking for an exceptional, hands-on Director of Strategic Finance to act as the strategic right-hand lead to our VP of Finance. Operating alongside our Controller (who leads accounting close, statutory compliance, tax, and ERP administration), you will own our forward-looking financial strategy. You will lead our corporate modelling, deploy AI and modern automation workflows across Finance and RevOps, execute on M&A and capital markets transactions, and use generative AI or AI applications to build out high-performance analytics frameworks as the company scales.
WHAT YOU'LL DO (KEY RESPONSIBILITIES):

1. Hands-On Strategic FP&A & Corporate Modeling
• Corporate Financial Architecture: Build and maintain our dynamic 3-statement models, weekly/monthly/quarterly operating plans, revenue forecasting, multi-year operating forecasts, and scenario analyses from the ground up without relying on junior analysts.
• Executive & Board Presentation: Spearhead the quantitative financial narrative, analysis, and materials for Board of Directors meetings, executive quarterly reviews, and investor reporting.
• Corporate Planning: Lead the annual budgeting process by working with the executive team to develop an annual plan with near real-time reporting on plan progress.
• Future Team Foundation: Establish rigorous modeling standards and analytical infrastructure today, with the mandate to hire, mentor, and build out an FP&A and FinOps team over the next 1–2 years.
2. Financial Engineering & AI Workflow Automation
• AI Agent & Workflow Deployment: Identify manual bottlenecks across billing, contract parsing, data extraction, and commercial operations; build and deploy LLM workflows, custom prompts, and automated scripts.
• Data Pipeline & Systems Integration: Architect and optimize data flows connecting CRM (Salesforce/HubSpot), CPQ, Billing, and ERP systems to automate revenue operations and eliminate reconciliation friction.
• Modern Automation Tooling: Use tools like Python, SQL, Zapier/Make, and API integrations to establish self-sustaining, real-time reporting layers.
• AI Analytics & Insights: Leverage AI to drive deeper analysis and insights throughout the organization (i.e. QBR’s, MMR’s, BvA’s)
3. RevOps & Commercial Structuring
• GTM Engine Analytics: Partner with RevOps to track and analyze sales capacity, pipeline velocity, CAC/LTV dynamics, and retention cohorts.
• Deal Structuring & Deal Desk: Serve as the primary strategic finance partner to Sales and RevOps on deal structuring, pricing models, margin analysis, discounting schedules, and commercial contract terms.
4. M&A / Capital Markets Execution & Compensation Modelling

• Transaction & Valuation Execution: Own the operational execution for M&A / capital market transactions, including due diligence financial modelling, virtual data room (VDR) setup, and cap table administration
• Compensation Architecture: Model and maintain corporate compensation bands, incentive structures, and equity option pool dilution economics.

WHO YOU ARE (QUALIFICATIONS):

- 7–10+ years in Strategic Finance, FP&A, BizOps, or Investment Banking / Management Consulting followed by high-growth B2B SaaS operational experience. Strong business acumen with a high intellectual curiosity.
- FP&A Mastery:
Spreadsheet wizard with demonstrated mastery of complex revenue modelling, 3-statement modelling, operational modelling, SaaS metrics (ARR, NRR, GRR, CAC payback), and executive-level financial storytelling.
- Engineering & AI Mindset:
Practical experience architecting the finance tech stack and working with data, deploying AI/LLM tools, automation platforms (Python, SQL, Zapier/Make), and SaaS toolchains (Salesforce, Stripe/Chargebee, NetSuite) to eliminate manual workflows.
- Commercial Depth:
Proven deal desk and commercial contract experience, with a solid grasp of pricing models, billing schedules, and equity compensation economics.
- Autonomy & Drive:
High-autonomy builder who thrives with ambiguity and enjoys executing hands-on work from scratch with the leadership aptitude to manage direct reports as the team grows.

WHY THIS ROLE IS DIFFERENT:

You won't be managing month-end reconciliations, audits, tax filings, or HR administration—our Controller leads those domains with excellence. You are joining to be an operational architect and strategic partner: designing intelligent financial infrastructure, building board-level models, and leveraging AI to scale our operational engine.

ADDITIONAL JOB INFO:

This position is for an existing vacancy
Salary range: 150-180K

What you can expect from us Meaningful compensation.
In addition to your base salary, you’ll join our employee stock ownership plan to further recognize your contributions to Forma.ai’s success.
Healthcare coverage.
We have a full benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, disability and life insurance, and a paid parental leave program.
Learning and development.
Access the resources you want to help you grow in your role by utilizing our $750 yearly training stipend.
Growth.
You’ll have a huge opportunity to build a career for yourself and gain the type of experience you’re looking for, whether that’s as an individual contributor or as a people leader.
Our Values:
  Work well, together.
We’re real. We have kids and pets. Mortgages and student loans. We’re in this together, so no matter how brilliant any one of us is, we always play nice with one another – no exceptions.  
Be precise. Be relentless.
We believe complacency breeds failure, so we set new goals as quickly as we achieve them. We persist in the face of adversity, learn from our mistakes, and push each other to continuously improve. The status-quo is kryptonite.
Love our tech. Love our customers.
Our platform solves a very complex problem in a currently underserved market. While everyone at Forma isn’t customer-facing, we’re all customer-focused. Maybe even slightly customer-obsessed. ­  

Use of AI for Recruitment
Currently, Forma.ai does not use artificial intelligence as part of our recruitment process, specifically but not limited to the screening, filtering and shortlisting of applicants.  
Our commitment to you:
  Forma is a proud equal opportunity employer that is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment.   Every effort to accommodate candidates for accessibility will be made upon request. Information received related to accommodations will be addressed confidentially. We know that applying to a new role takes a lot of effort. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. There are many paths to a successful career and we’re looking forward to reading yours.
We thank all candidates for their interest however only qualified applicants will be shortlisted.

jobs.description:
**Toronto Pearson is transforming. Now’s the time for your career to fly.**



The Greater Toronto Airports Authority (GTAA) is a unique and dynamic place to work, with a bold plan to make Toronto Pearson, Canada’s leading global hub airport, a global leader in airport performance, customer care and sustainability. Together with our partners, approximately 2,100 GTAA employees are working to create a next\-generation airport by innovating in all we do and striving for the most uplifting, safe and efficient experience for our passengers – all while championing the prosperity of our people, the community we call home, and our aviation partners. Join us on our journey together, as we put the joy back into travel and make Toronto Pearson the chosen place to fly and work.


**What's in it for you?**


* An opportunity to grow, develop, and thrive within a dynamic, and fast\-growing company alongside thoughtful and passionate individuals dedicated to their work and community.
* Comprehensive benefits, including a flexible retirement program with employer matching, along with voluntary savings options (RRSP, TFSA, and Non\-Registered Savings Plans).
* A flexible hybrid work environment, continuous internal and external learning opportunities, and a meaningful reward and recognition program.


**What can you expect from this position?**



Reporting to the Executive Director, Capital Planning, the Associate Director, Capital Investment Strategy will lead the Capital Investments function and help determine where and why Toronto Pearson invests. You will provide financial leadership across the front end of the capital investment lifecycle by supporting strategic initiative business cases, portfolio prioritization, project intake, investment governance, and benefits realization. Working with business units, the Transformation Office, Strategy, Finance business partners, and program teams, you will translate strategic priorities into decision\-ready investment recommendations for executive consideration. You will establish consistent methodologies, standards, and controls so that capital investments are strategically aligned, financially sound, affordable, and supported by reliable data and robust business intelligence.


**As an Associate Director, Capital Investment Strategy, you will:**


* Lead the development and financial evaluation of business cases for major strategic initiatives, while establishing the standards and methodologies applied across the broader capital portfolio.
* Develop complex financial models incorporating NPV, IRR, ROIC, cash flow, sensitivity, scenario, and risk\-adjusted investment analyses.
* Challenge assumptions and translate complex analysis into decision\-ready recommendations for executive and Board\-level consideration.
* Lead quarterly financial forecasting and reporting for multi\-year strategic initiatives.
* Support the enterprise capital allocation and prioritization process with a multidisciplinary team, applying consistent strategic, financial, affordability, risk, and delivery\-capacity criteria to recommend investments, sequencing decisions, trade\-offs, and off\-ramp actions to executive governance forums.
* Establish and maintain enterprise investment\-governance standards, including business\-case methodologies and templates, evaluation criteria, capital allocation frameworks, hurdle rates, risk premiums, stage\-gate requirements, and decision records that support consistent and transparent recommendations.
* Lead the enterprise project intake and triage process partnering with the appropriate teams to confirm strategic alignment, scope maturity, resource capacity, accounting treatment, funding pathway, and business\-case requirements before investments advance for prioritization or approval.
* Establish benefits and cost baselines for approved investments, integrate expected outcomes into portfolio planning, monitor realization across all programs, and lead post\-investment evaluations that identify variances, lessons learned, and implications for future capital allocation decisions.
* Support the evaluation of public\-private partnerships and alternative delivery models, including financial returns, affordability, financing approaches, and risk allocation.
* Lead, coach, and develop a high\-performing team while fostering accountability, collaboration, analytical excellence, and continuous improvement.


**This is the role for you, if you have:**

* A university degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related discipline.
* A CPA, CFA, CBV, MBA, or other relevant professional designation or graduate degree is considered an asset.
* Five or more years of relevant experience in investment analysis, corporate finance, infrastructure finance, business\-case development, portfolio planning, or major capital programs, including experience leading complex, cross\-functional investment decisions in a leadership capacity.
* Advanced expertise in financial modelling, scenario analysis, sensitivity testing, and investment evaluation methodologies.
* Expertise in developing decision\-ready business cases for major strategic or capital initiatives.
* Demonstrated experience designing or operating capital allocation, project intake, stage\-gate, investment\-governance, or benefits\-realization processes across a complex portfolio.
* Experience evaluating public\-private partnerships or alternative capital\-project delivery and financing models.
* Advanced stakeholder management and influencing skills, with the ability to work effectively across senior leadership and business functions.
* Strong executive communication skills and the ability to translate complex financial analysis into clear business implications and recommendations.
* Strategic thinking, sound judgement, and strong problem\-solving and decision\-making capabilities.
* Experience leading, coaching, and developing finance professionals in a collaborative environment.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Enterprise Execution
jobs.description:
Join a Challenger

At EQ, we're remaking banking so every Canadian gets ahead, every day. Serving nearly 4 million Canadians from coast to coast, we offer a wide variety of financial services from banking and lending, to trust and credit union solutions.

We've been at this since 1970, challenging the conventions of traditional banking with smarter, faster, and more connected financial experiences.

What's kept us moving?
The people behind it all: challengers who ask better questions, push back on old assumptions, and look for a better way forward.

If you're driven to help reshape how banking works for Canadians and the businesses that power our economy, this could be your next big opportunity.

We can’t wait to get to know you!

The Work

The Senior Director, Enterprise Execution is responsible for helping EQB translate strategic priorities into business outcomes.

Working directly with executive leaders across the organization, this role leads a focused portfolio of the Bank's most important enterprise initiatives and strategic priorities. These are high-impact, cross-functional efforts that are critical to delivering EQB's strategy, growth ambitions, and financial objectives. The role serves as a bridge between strategy, execution, and outcomes, ensuring that the Bank's biggest priorities maintain momentum, overcome obstacles, and deliver the impact they were intended to achieve.

Enterprise Execution acts as an execution partner to leadership, bringing structured problem-solving, strategic thinking, and execution discipline to a select group of enterprise priorities. The role combines elements of strategy execution, enterprise leadership, organizational effectiveness, and executive problem-solving, helping translate strategic ambition into measurable results.

The ideal candidate combines the structured problem-solving capabilities of a top-tier strategy consultant with the practical execution mindset of an experienced operator. They are highly comfortable working in ambiguous situations, quickly building credibility with senior stakeholders, and driving progress on complex challenges that cut across multiple business units. They are intellectually curious, commercially minded, and action-oriented. They know how to move seamlessly between strategy and execution, challenge and support, analysis and action. Most importantly, they have a demonstrated ability to help organizations deliver on their most important priorities and achieve meaningful outcomes.

Strategic Initiative Leadership & Enterprise Priorities (55%)

Lead a portfolio of EQB's highest-priority enterprise initiatives and strategic priorities, including CEO- and CFO-sponsored programs.
Partner directly with executive sponsors and act as a trusted advisor to mobilize, accelerate, and deliver initiatives that are critical to achieving the Bank's strategic and financial objectives.
Provide hands-on leadership for complex cross-functional initiatives requiring enterprise coordination, senior stakeholder alignment, and disciplined execution.
Shape implementation approaches, execution strategies, operating models, and delivery plans to maximize organizational impact.
Challenge assumptions, strengthen plans, and improve decision-making through structured problem solving and rigorous analysis.
Identify and resolve issues, risks, dependencies, and organizational barriers that could impede successful execution.
Bring an enterprise-wide perspective that helps ensure initiatives advance broader corporate objectives.

Strategic Execution & Outcome Realization (25%)

Ensure approved business cases and strategic objectives translate into measurable business, customer, operational, and financial outcomes.
Partner with initiative leaders to strengthen execution plans and improve the likelihood of successful outcomes.
Identify emerging risks, dependencies, and barriers requiring intervention and help drive resolution.
Provide executive visibility into initiative progress, key decisions, and areas requiring leadership attention.
Work closely with Finance, initiative owners, and business leaders to understand expected versus realized outcomes and identify opportunities to improve performance.
Conduct initiative reviews and post-implementation assessments to reinforce accountability and continuous improvement.
Promote a culture of disciplined execution and ownership across enterprise priorities.

Enterprise Planning & Prioritization (10%)

Lead the annual enterprise initiative prioritization process as part of EQB's strategic planning cycle.
Partner with business leaders, Finance, and Strategy teams to identify, evaluate, and prioritize initiatives requiring investment and organizational capacity.
Facilitate discussions regarding sequencing, trade-offs, resource allocation, and execution readiness.
Develop an integrated view of enterprise priorities, dependencies, and investment requirements to support executive decision-making.
Help ensure organizational focus remains concentrated on initiatives that create the greatest strategic impact.

Executive & Board Effectiveness (10%)

Help ensure EQB's most important strategic priorities, enterprise initiatives, and investment decisions are supported by clear, aligned, and decision-ready executive and Board materials.
Partner with senior leaders across the organization to elevate the quality, consistency, and strategic coherence of materials presented to Executive Leadership Team and Board forums.
Ensure major strategic discussions are informed by a cohesive enterprise perspective and supported by fact-based, well-structured recommendations.
Challenge gaps, inconsistencies, duplication, and disconnects across strategic updates, investment proposals, and enterprise initiatives before they reach decision-making forums.
Support major strategic planning sessions, Board strategy discussions, and executive reviews by helping ensure discussions remain focused on decisions, outcomes, and enterprise priorities.
Act as a steward of excellence for the Bank's most important leadership discussions and governance forums.

Let's Talk About You!

8-10 years of experience in strategy consulting, corporate strategy, enterprise execution, strategic initiatives, business transformation, operating leadership, or related fields.
Demonstrated track record leading complex cross-functional initiatives that deliver measurable business outcomes.
Experience partnering with executive leadership teams and influencing decisions in highly matrixed organizations.
Strong commercial, financial, and operational acumen.
Proven ability to drive alignment, solve complex problems, and deliver results without direct authority.
Exceptional communication and executive presentation skills.
Experience developing executive and Board-level recommendations and materials.

Preferred Experience

Experience in private equity value creation roles or at a top-tier management consulting firm a significant asset.
Experience within financial services, banking, fintech, or other complex regulated industries.
Experience leading enterprise-wide strategic initiatives, operating model changes, integration programs, or growth-focused initiatives.
Familiarity with strategic planning, capital allocation, benefits realization, and organizational prioritization processes.
MBA or equivalent graduate degree considered an asset.

What we offer [For full-time permanent roles]

💰 Competitive discretionary bonus

✨ Market leading RRSP match program

🩺 Medical, dental, vision, life, and disability benefits

📝 Employee Share Purchase Plan

👶🏽 Maternity/Parental top-up while you care for your little one

🏝 Generous vacation policy and personal days

🖥 Virtual events to connect with your fellow colleagues

🎓 Professional development and comprehensive Career Development program

💛 A fulfilling opportunity to join one of the top FinTechs and help create a new kind of banking experience

The incumbent will be working hybrid and in office time will be spent working from EQ Bank’s additional office space located at 2200-25 Ontario Street, Toronto, ON
.

Equity, Diversity & Inclusion

EQ is committed to building an inclusive, accessible environment where every employee feels valued, respected, and supported. We believe our organization is stronger — and our people thrive — when we honour and celebrate diverse experiences, identities, and perspectives. We’re equally committed to supporting your growth, both professionally and personally.

All candidates considered for hire must successfully complete a criminal background check and credit check. Turner & Townsend is a global professional services company with over 22,000 people in more than 60 countries.

Working with our clients across real estate, infrastructure, energy and natural resources, we transform together delivering outcomes that improve people’s lives. As a Turner & Townsend Project Management Director, you’ll be responsible for client management and department-related management services within multiple geographic markets, programs, and asset classes to achieve the company's strategic business objectives by delivering outstanding results to our client.

They are responsible for the management of projects from initiation through completion for dedicated client groups as part of a multi-service outsourcing contract. Who are you?

You are an expert Real Estate
Project Management Director
with a minimum of 12+
years post-graduate experience
in real estate project management
looking for the next step or are currently undertaking a similar role in a similar environment.

Job Description

Communicate with the client and manage client expectations on resourcing needs, project and programme performance, risks, status reporting, and issues escalation
Direct all phases of the delivery process for large and high-profile clients including procurement, contracting, planning, tracking, and execution
Provide formal supervision to direct report employees in Canada, the US and EMEA. Monitor the training and development of staff. Conduct performance evaluations and coaching. Oversee the recruiting and hiring of new employees.

Conceptualize new methods, techniques, processes, and standards across job disciplines or functions.
Direct the resolution of highly complex or unusual business problems by applying advanced critical thinking.

jobs.title: Associate Director, Capital Investment Strategy
jobs.description:
Toronto Pearson is transforming. Now’s the time for your career to fly.

The Greater Toronto Airports Authority (GTAA) is a unique and dynamic place to work, with a bold plan to make Toronto Pearson, Canada’s leading global hub airport, a global leader in airport performance, customer care and sustainability. Together with our partners, approximately 2,100 GTAA employees are working to create a next-generation airport by innovating in all we do and striving for the most uplifting, safe and efficient experience for our passengers – all while championing the prosperity of our people, the community we call home, and our aviation partners. Join us on our journey together, as we put the joy back into travel and make Toronto Pearson the chosen place to fly and work.

What's in it for you?

An opportunity to grow, develop, and thrive within a dynamic, and fast-growing company alongside thoughtful and passionate individuals dedicated to their work and community.
Comprehensive benefits, including a flexible retirement program with employer matching, along with voluntary savings options (RRSP, TFSA, and Non-Registered Savings Plans).
A flexible hybrid work environment, continuous internal and external learning opportunities, and a meaningful reward and recognition program.

What can you expect from this position?

Reporting to the Executive Director, Capital Planning, the Associate Director, Capital Investment Strategy will lead the Capital Investments function and help determine where and why Toronto Pearson invests. You will provide financial leadership across the front end of the capital investment lifecycle by supporting strategic initiative business cases, portfolio prioritization, project intake, investment governance, and benefits realization. Working with business units, the Transformation Office, Strategy, Finance business partners, and program teams, you will translate strategic priorities into decision-ready investment recommendations for executive consideration. You will establish consistent methodologies, standards, and controls so that capital investments are strategically aligned, financially sound, affordable, and supported by reliable data and robust business intelligence.

As an Associate Director, Capital Investment Strategy, you will:

Lead the development and financial evaluation of business cases for major strategic initiatives, while establishing the standards and methodologies applied across the broader capital portfolio.
Develop complex financial models incorporating NPV, IRR, ROIC, cash flow, sensitivity, scenario, and risk-adjusted investment analyses.
Challenge assumptions and translate complex analysis into decision-ready recommendations for executive and Board-level consideration.
Lead quarterly financial forecasting and reporting for multi-year strategic initiatives.
Support the enterprise capital allocation and prioritization process with a multidisciplinary team, applying consistent strategic, financial, affordability, risk, and delivery-capacity criteria to recommend investments, sequencing decisions, trade-offs, and off-ramp actions to executive governance forums.
Establish and maintain enterprise investment-governance standards, including business-case methodologies and templates, evaluation criteria, capital allocation frameworks, hurdle rates, risk premiums, stage-gate requirements, and decision records that support consistent and transparent recommendations.
Lead the enterprise project intake and triage process partnering with the appropriate teams to confirm strategic alignment, scope maturity, resource capacity, accounting treatment, funding pathway, and business-case requirements before investments advance for prioritization or approval.
Establish benefits and cost baselines for approved investments, integrate expected outcomes into portfolio planning, monitor realization across all programs, and lead post-investment evaluations that identify variances, lessons learned, and implications for future capital allocation decisions.
Support the evaluation of public-private partnerships and alternative delivery models, including financial returns, affordability, financing approaches, and risk allocation.
Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team while fostering accountability, collaboration, analytical excellence, and continuous improvement.

This is the role for you, if you have:

A university degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related discipline.
A CPA, CFA, CBV, MBA, or other relevant professional designation or graduate degree is considered an asset.
Five or more years of relevant experience in investment analysis, corporate finance, infrastructure finance, business-case development, portfolio planning, or major capital programs, including experience leading complex, cross-functional investment decisions in a leadership capacity.
Advanced expertise in financial modelling, scenario analysis, sensitivity testing, and investment evaluation methodologies.
Expertise in developing decision-ready business cases for major strategic or capital initiatives.
Demonstrated experience designing or operating capital allocation, project intake, stage-gate, investment-governance, or benefits-realization processes across a complex portfolio.
Experience evaluating public-private partnerships or alternative capital-project delivery and financing models.
Advanced stakeholder management and influencing skills, with the ability to work effectively across senior leadership and business functions.
Strong executive communication skills and the ability to translate complex financial analysis into clear business implications and recommendations.
Strategic thinking, sound judgement, and strong problem-solving and decision-making capabilities.
Experience leading, coaching, and developing finance professionals in a collaborative environment.
The ability to obtain and retain Transportation Security Clearance at the designated level for the position.

The GTAA is committed to Employment Equity and maintaining a diverse, equitable and inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive.

This position is exempt from Ontario's 2026 pay transparency requirements under Regulation 476/24.

jobs.title: AI Product Scaling Director
jobs.description:
We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients. 

 At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute. 

 To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com 

 What you'll be doing 

 Our AI team builds enterprise capabilities that support a wide range of users across the organization, from end users to technology teams and low-code or no-code builders. As a Principal Product Scaler – AI Engineering, you'll build the engineering foundation that helps us repeatedly deliver high-quality AI products safely, efficiently, and at scale. You'll architect and develop the reusable components, software development kits, testing frameworks, and delivery patterns that move us from individual implementations to a mature product engineering model. You'll establish the standards for how AI products are designed, built, tested, packaged, released, and monitored in production. Working closely with data scientists, engineers, and technology partners, you'll help turn strong prototypes into reliable enterprise products while strengthening the team's overall engineering capability.

 At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. Details on your work arrangement (proportion of on-site and remote work) will be discussed at the time of your interview. 

 How you'll succeed 

 Build scalable engineering foundations - Design and develop software development kits, libraries, reusable components, templates, and reference implementations that accelerate delivery across the AI portfolio and reduce repeated effort across teams.
 Establish engineering excellence - Define and implement standards for code structure, testing, code review, versioning, packaging, documentation, release management, and production readiness for AI and Generative AI products.
 Advance AI quality and reliability - Create automated testing, evaluation, regression, monitoring, and observability patterns that support both traditional software quality and the unique behavior of probabilistic AI systems.
 Drive efficient delivery - Establish continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) patterns, quality gates, and repeatable workflows that help teams move from experiment to production with greater speed and consistency.
 Enable adoption across teams - Design interfaces and developer experiences that make enterprise AI capabilities easy to consume for technology teams, other AI teams, and low-code or no-code solution builders.
 Elevate team capability - Review architecture and code for critical products, coach AI practitioners on engineering best practices, and help the team adopt effective agentic development workflows, tooling, and guardrails.

 Who you are 

 You are a hands-on senior engineering leader. You have atleast 5+ experience operating at a Staff, Principal, Lead Engineer, or equivalent level, and you enjoy both designing systems and writing production-quality code.
 You can demonstrate experience in system design, application programming interface (API) and software development kit (SDK) design, testing, CI/CD, versioning, observability, and production operations. It’s an asset if you have built platforms, frameworks, developer tooling, or reusable services used by multiple teams.
 You give meaning to data. You understand the engineering challenges of taking AI and Generative AI solutions from experimentation into production, and you know that quality for AI systems requires more than traditional unit testing.
 You look beyond the moment. You're excited by the opportunity to shape how agentic software development evolves, including workflows, repository design, testing approaches, review practices, context management, and governance for increasingly autonomous delivery.
 You're motivated by collective success. You influence engineers, data scientists, technology partners, and leaders through strong partnership, sound judgment, and a commitment to raising the capability of the broader organization.
 You act like an owner. You naturally identify repeated patterns, remove friction from the development lifecycle, and build practical solutions that help teams deliver faster, more safely, and with greater consistency.
 Values matter to you. You bring your real self to work, and you live our values - trust, teamwork, and accountability.

 What CIBC Offers 

 At CIBC, your goals are a priority. We start with your strengths and ambitions as an employee and strive to create opportunities to tap into your potential. We aspire to give you a career, rather than just a paycheck.
 We work to recognize you in meaningful, personalized ways including a competitive salary, incentive pay, banking benefits, a benefits program*, defined benefit pension plan*, an employee share purchase plan, a vacation offering, wellbeing support, and MomentMakers, our social, points-based recognition program.

 Our spaces and technological toolkit will make it simple to bring together great minds to create innovative solutions that make a difference for our clients.

 We cultivate a culture where you can express your ambition through initiatives like Purpose Day; a paid day off dedicated for you to use to invest in your growth and development.

 *Subject to plan and program terms and conditions

 What you need to know 
 CIBC is committed to creating an inclusive environment where all team members and clients feel like they belong. We seek applicants with a wide range of abilities and we provide an accessible candidate experience. If you need accommodation, please contact Mailbox.careers-carrieres@cibc.com 

 CIBC is committed to clarity in our hiring process. All roles posted are opportunities we’re actively recruiting for, unless stated otherwise.

 We may ask you to complete an attribute-based assessment and other skills test (such as simulation, coding, French proficiency). 

 We use artificial intelligence tools during the recruitment process. Our goal for the application process is to get to know more about you, all that you have to offer, and give you the opportunity to learn more about us.

jobs.title: Director of Data Center Operations
jobs.description:
Director of Data Center Operations

The Director of Data Center Operations serves as a strategic leader responsible for enabling Salute’s site teams to focus on customer delivery. This role will support administrative, compliance, and employee development responsibilities, ensuring operational consistency across sites and building a highly skilled, engaged workforce. The Director will manage operational governance, talent development, process improvement, and cross-site coordination, leading a multi-campus operations account.

Key Responsibilities

1. Operational Oversight & Administrative Management

Own and manage all non-billable (internal) operational duties to reduce administrative workload on billable site managers.

Maintain centralized oversight of policies, procedures, and documentation standards for all assigned sites.

Ensure compliance with safety, security, and regulatory requirements through regular audits and reporting.

Coordinate multi-site operational planning, scheduling, and resource allocation in alignment with client needs.

Track and report operational performance metrics, providing actionable insights to client site leadership.

Observe customer operational workflows, documentation, and reporting templates and recommend improvements to client site management to drive consistency and performance across locations.

2. Employee Development & Talent Management

Lead talent development programs for site leadership teams, including onboarding, training, mentoring, and career progression planning.

Conduct regular performance reviews, provide coaching, and create individual development plans for site managers.

Facilitate leadership readiness programs to prepare emerging leaders for future management roles.

Ensure new leaders are equipped with the skills and tools needed before assuming management positions.

3. Process & Quality Improvement

Identify operational bottlenecks and implement process improvements to enhance efficiency and service quality.

Develop and maintain a knowledge base of best practices, lessons learned, and standard operating procedures.

Coordinate cross-site initiatives to align maintenance, safety, and operational excellence programs.

Oversee root cause analysis and lessons-learned documentation following incidents, ensuring consistent follow-up.

Maintain relationship with client site management for quality assurance feedback.

4. Stakeholder Communication & Coordination

Act as the primary liaison for operational matters between the VP of Data Center Operations, site managers, and corporate teams.

Act as primary account manager for a data center operations client.

Support internal communications, ensuring that site managers receive timely updates and clear direction.

Collaborate with HR, Finance, and other support functions to resolve site-level personnel or process issues.

Receive client feedback and escalations on team performance.

Report data, metrics, and feedback to client in support of reporting and collaboration.

Qualifications

5+ years in operations leadership, preferably in critical infrastructure or technical services.

Proven experience in employee development, team leadership, and performance management.

Strong organizational, planning, and project management skills.

Exceptional communication and stakeholder engagement abilities.

Experience implementing process improvements and operational standards across multiple locations.

Deep understanding of data center infrastructure and operations.

Position Impact

Under the Director of Data Center Operations, site managers will be empowered to focus on, and be supported in, delivering exceptional service to our customers. This role will be instrumental in strengthening our leadership pipeline, improving operational efficiency, and ensuring long-term customer satisfaction.

jobs.title: Directeur régional des technologies de l’information - Région de Montréal/Information Technology Regional Director - Montreal
jobs.description:
MDA Space (TSX : MDA) est un partenaire de mission de confiance de l’industrie spatiale mondiale qui crée l’espace entre ce qui est prouvé et ce qui est possible. À titre de pionnier de la robotique, des systèmes satellitaires et du renseignement géospatial, avec une histoire de 55 ans de premières mondiales et de plus de 450 missions, MDA Space est un chef de file mondial dans les domaines des satellites de communication, de l’observation de la Terre et de l’espace, ainsi que de l’infrastructure et l’exploration spatiale. L’équipe de MDA Space, qui compte plus de 4 000 experts du secteur spatial au Canada, aux États-Unis et au Royaume-Uni, possède les connaissances et le savoir-faire nécessaires pour transformer la vision audacieuse du client en une mission réalisable, grâce à une combinaison unique d’expérience, d’excellence technique et d’émerveillement qui fait partie de notre ADN depuis le premier jour. Pour ceux qui rêvent grand et repoussent les limites sur terre et dans les étoiles afin de changer le monde pour le meilleur, nous vous y emmènerons.

Le Rôle

MDA Space connaît une croissance fulgurante, et nous sommes à la recherche d’un dirigeant technologique visionnaire pour piloter l’expérience informatique de plus de 2 000 collaborateurs
répartis entre Montréal, Kirkland, Sainte-Anne-de-Bellevue et d’autres emplacements stratégiques. Vous serez responsable de l’expérience utilisateur de bout en bout, mènerez des projets d’amélioration des services, gérerez les contrats avec les fournisseurs et veillerez au respect des normes ITIL/ITSM, de cybersécurité et de plan de continuité des activités (PCA). Si vous vous épanouissez dans des environnements dynamiques et à fort impact, et que vous aimez transformer des environnements techniques complexes en services fluides et centrés sur l’utilisateur, ce poste vous permettra de propulser votre carrière vers de nouveaux horizons.

Le directeur régional des technologies de l’information (TI), région de Montréal, supervisera la prestation des services informatiques locaux pour l’emplacement de Montréal et les emplacements environnants, en veillant à offrir une expérience employé de qualité, à garantir la fiabilité des opérations et à respecter les normes de MDA Space. À ce titre, il travaillera en collaboration avec les dirigeants locaux, les équipes de TI régionales, les fournisseurs et les intervenants de l’entreprise afin d’améliorer la qualité des services, de soutenir la croissance, de gérer les risques et de s’assurer que les services de TI répondent aux besoins actuels et futurs de l’entreprise.

Principales Responsabilités

Favoriser une excellente expérience des collaborateurs de TI sur les sites relevant de sa responsabilité / entrant dans son champ d’action
Favoriser l’implication des services de TI au sein du site – en veillant à ce que les collaborateurs des TI travaillent comme une seule et même équipe
Diriger les services de TI locaux afin d’offrir une expérience employé homogène et de grande qualité à Montréal et aux emplacements environnants.
Collaborer avec les dirigeants du site et les équipes des TI régionales afin de soutenir la croissance, de résoudre les problèmes et d’améliorer le rendement des services.
Communiquer de manière claire et concrète sur les services des TI, les normes, le rendement et la sensibilisation à la cybersécurité au sein du site.
Surveiller les performances des services locaux, les risques et les plans d’amélioration à l’aide de rapports et de tableaux de bord standardisés.
Veiller à ce que l’infrastructure, les outils et les services locaux respectent les normes de MDA Space et garantissent la continuité des activités.
Servir de point de contact local pour les incidents informatiques, les projets et les problèmes liés aux services, en assurant la coordination avec les équipes concernées pour trouver des solutions.
Soutenir les équipes de production et d’exploitation en garantissant que les services de TI sont fiables, cohérents et alignés sur les priorités de l’entreprise.
Superviser les ressources de TI locales, les services des fournisseurs, les contrats et la mise en œuvre des projets liés aux modifications ou aux extensions des sites.
Veiller au respect des exigences en matière de TI, de sécurité, de gestion des actifs, de la norme SOX et d’assurance qualité.

Direction Et Relations

Établir d’excellentes relations avec les dirigeants locaux, les partenaires commerciaux, les équipes de TI et les fournisseurs afin de garantir que les services répondent aux besoins de l’entreprise.
Diriger, encadrer et soutenir l’équipe des TI locale tout en encourageant la collaboration, la responsabilisation et l’amélioration continue.
Représenter le service des TI au niveau local et aider les employés à comprendre l’assistance, les services et les interlocuteurs à leur disposition.

Priorités

Expérience des employés: Donner l’exemple et donner le ton au sein de la direction des TI en mettant l’accent sur la promotion d’une expérience des employés exceptionnelle à travers l’ensemble des services des TI; diriger et faire évoluer l’infrastructure, les outils et les services de TI du site afin de soutenir le personnel; garantir une prestation de services de grande qualité et une amélioration continue, en accord avec les stratégies mondiales de MDA Space.
Direction d’équipe: constituer, diriger et développer une équipe locale de professionnels des TI qualifiés; être responsable du recrutement et de l’intégration des nouveaux membres de l’équipe, ainsi que de la mise en place de méthodes de travail efficaces.
Gestion technologique: maintenir une compréhension approfondie des technologies et des services de MDA Space; documenter et maintenir l’environnement technique du site afin de garantir que les performances actuelles et futures répondent aux besoins de l’entreprise.
Implication des collaborateurs: Représenter l’équipe technique des TI du site au sein d’une communauté de partenaires et de collaborateurs professionnels; veiller à la cohérence des prestations, conformément aux feuilles de route et aux normes mondiales.
Opérations et conformité: Gérer les contrats et les services des fournisseurs locaux; veiller au respect des normes informatiques, de la sécurité et des exigences de conformité.
Défense des intérêts des utilisateurs finaux: adopter une approche proactive et concrète en matière d’assistance et d’expérience utilisateur; identifier les possibilités d’exploiter les capacités existantes pour obtenir de meilleurs résultats.
Calendrier et lieu: Dans un premier temps, le titulaire du poste aura pour mission de garantir une excellente expérience employé en pilotant divers projets de manière transversale.

Compétences Et Expérience Requises

Passion pour la prestation d’un service d’excellence, en cherchant constamment à améliorer l’expérience utilisateur et à optimiser la performance.
Expérience dans un poste de direction à titre de responsable de services, avec une expérience avérée dans la prise en charge, la gestion et la responsabilité d’un service, d’une plateforme ou d’outils informatiques
Maîtrise parfaite de l’anglais et du français, à l’écrit comme à l’oral.
Expérience avérée dans le secteur de l’industrie ou des services
Expérience avérée dans la prestation et l’exploitation de services
Une compréhension technique approfondie couvrant un large éventail de technologies et de domaines.
Bonnes compétences en communication et en engagement, et expérience avérée dans la gestion des relations professionnelles
Excellentes compétences en matière de collaboration pour gérer les attentes locales et trouver des solutions
Excellentes compétences en matière d’influence, de réseautage et de travail d’équipe
Expérience approfondie dans un environnement normatif, réglementé et conforme
Excellente connaissance pratique de l’ITIL, des outils ITSM ou équivalents
Expérience avérée dans la gestion des fournisseurs locaux, des contrats, des renouvellements et des appels d’offres
Dirigeant et coéquipier : donne l’exemple à l’équipe ou encadre les autres; collaboration efficace avec ses pairs dans toute la région.
Expérience en gestion et en développement d’équipes, dans un environnement de travail ouvert, honnête, responsable et collaboratif.

Compétences Et Expérience Souhaitées

PMP
Six Sigma Ceinture noire
Certification ITIL
Une certification en expérience client serait un atout

Commentaires/Considérations Particulières

Les candidats retenus doivent obtenir et détenir une autorisation de et réussir Secret OTAN
l’évaluation de sécurité pour le Programme des marchandises contrôlées (PMC) et ITAR.

Avantages Sociaux

MDA offre une rémunération et des avantages sociaux compétitifs à ses employés à tous les emplacements. À titre de membre de l’équipe de MDA, vous et vos personnes à charge admissibles pouvez bénéficier d’un régime d’avantages sociaux qui assure un niveau de protection complet grâce à des soins de santé concurrentiels, y compris des régimes d’assurance-maladie complémentaire et de médicaments flexibles, des prestations dentaires et de vision, une protection du revenu en cas d’invalidité, une assurance-vie, des régimes d’épargne-retraite collectifs et un programme d’aide aux employés et aux familles.

Égalité Des Chances

MDA est un employeur qui prône l’égalité des chances, la diversité et l’inclusion. Nous nous engageons à traiter tous les employés et candidats à l’emploi avec respect et dignité. Si vous avez besoin d’une assistance ou d’un accommodement raisonnable en raison d’un handicap pendant le processus de candidature ou de recrutement, n’hésitez pas à nous en informer.

jobs.title: Associate Director-AI&Data
jobs.description:
We Are:

Accenture Data & AI — the people who love using data to tell a story. We're the world's largest team of data scientists and experts in machine learning and AI. A great day for us means solving big problems using the latest tech, serious brain power, and deep knowledge of just about every industry. We believe a mix of data, analytics, automation, and responsible AI can do almost anything — spark digital reinvention, widen the range of what humans can do, and breathe life into smart products and services.

You Are:
A thought leader and practitioner at the intersection of AI strategy and data delivery — As a senior leader in the Data & AI practice, you will coach and mentor up-and-coming leaders, guide diverse multi-disciplinary teams, and help clients embed AI and data capabilities as a lasting part of their organisational culture — with a strong focus on responsible AI, data governance, and public trust

An executive who never stopped being a practitioner. You have built and shipped AI systems that run in production, and you are as credible in a technical design review as in a board-level investment conversation. You have led at scale — teams, portfolios, commercial results — and you can tell a CEO why their AI ambition will stall against their existing systems, then show them what to do about it.

What You'll do:

Role Summary

You will own Accenture's AI agenda in the Québec market: what we take to clients, how we deliver it, and the capability that sustains it.

Clients here are not short of AI ambition. They are short of the foundation underneath it — systems nobody fully understands, knowledge that lives in people rather than in artifacts, architectures never designed for autonomous software to act inside them, and no safe way to let AI touch a system of record. Closing that gap is the work: making the existing enterprise legible to AI, designing the architecture and controls that let AI be trusted with consequential decisions, encoding the domain meaning that makes a solution reflect the business, and building systems that hold up in production.

It also means making it last. You will help clients set the architecture and operating model their AI estate will run on, prove and improve those systems once live, keep the economics defensible to a CFO, and deploy privately or sovereignly where data cannot leave their control. The standard we are accountable for is AI that is enterprise-grade: in production, measurable, economically sustainable and defensible to a regulator.

Key Responsibilities:

Grow the Québec AI business

Own the market strategy, value propositions and commercial constructs for AI in Québec, adapted to local industry priorities, regulatory context and buying behaviour — in Québec-ready form, not translated global collateral.

Develop and personally hold executive relationships (CEO, CIO, CTO, CDAO, COO, CFO and business-unit leaders) across priority accounts.

Lead the shaping of proposals and RFP responses; own solution architecture, estimating, commercial construct and risk posture on the pursuits you lead.

Carry an originated-sales objective and contribute to managed revenue growth across the portfolio.

Lead delivery

Lead agentic and generative AI systems end to end: value case, architecture, model and pattern selection, evaluation design, integration with systems of record, deployment and transition to run.

Lead the work of recovering what a client's estate actually does and what the organization actually knows — legacy code, undocumented logic, institutional knowledge — and making it usable by AI systems.

Establish the architecture and control patterns that let autonomous systems operate against production environments with appropriate isolation, authorization, traceability and oversight.

Ensure domain meaning is engineered deliberately — ontology, semantics, business context — rather than approximated.

Lead the hardest engagements personally, including forward-deployed work where small, senior, embedded teams work directly against client outcomes.

Own quality, risk, margin and delivery health across the Québec AI portfolio, including architecture review on engagements you do not lead.

Industrialize and sustain

Establish the reference architectures, engineering standards and operating patterns that take clients from isolated solutions to a governed AI estate: lifecycle management, evaluation and regression discipline, observability, and continuous optimization once live.

Bring economic discipline to AI at scale — unit economics, tiered model selection, cost attribution and consumption controls.

Codify what we learn into reusable accelerators and delivery playbooks.

Responsible AI, privacy and sovereignty

Embed responsible AI practice into every engagement: risk classification, evaluation and red-teaming, bias and safety testing, traceability, human oversight and auditability.

Ensure solutions meet Québec and Canadian obligations, including Law 25, privacy impact assessment practice, data residency expectations, and applicable sectoral supervision such as model risk and third-party risk in financial services.

Lead client conversations on private and sovereign AI, including the architectural and economic trade-offs of keeping models, data and inference inside client or national boundaries.

Advise on quality and fairness in French-language AI systems: model performance in Québec French, terminology and register, and the service-language obligations that apply to our clients' own customers.

Build the team

Build, lead and retain a bilingual team of AI engineers, architects, data scientists and delivery leads; own capability planning, skills strategy and career progression for the Québec AI community.

Recruit from the Québec talent market and partner with universities and research institutes on talent pipeline and applied research.

Stay close enough to the technology to review architecture, critique evaluation design and challenge weak assumptions.

Ecosystem and eminence

Represent Accenture across the Québec AI ecosystem — research institutes, industry clusters, accelerators, public-sector innovation bodies — and convert those relationships into joint work.

Partner with our platform, infrastructure and frontier model alliance partners to bring new capability into Québec accounts first.

Speak and publish in both languages, and engage analysts and media on what AI looks like once it reaches production.

Bachelor's degree or completion of a college program in computer science, or a related technical discipline.

15+ years of relevant experience in AI/ML, data and software development or enterprise technology delivery, including hands-on architecture and production operationalization — not advisory work alone.

Executive-level leadership experience: leading a practice, portfolio, business unit or major program at scale, with accountability for commercial outcomes, quality and people, and credibility with C-suite and board-level stakeholders.

Demonstrated experience delivering generative and agentic AI systems into production, including model selection and adaptation, evaluation methodology, guardrails, and integration with enterprise systems and data.

Strong grounding in enterprise architecture and legacy estate modernization, and in the lifecycle practice required to run AI systems in production.

Track record of originating and closing services work with personally attributable sales, including proposal shaping, solution design and commercial construct.

Experience leading multi-disciplinary teams on complex, multi-year programs with measurable business outcomes, and a record of hiring, coaching and growing technical people.

Working knowledge of responsible AI practice and of the Canadian and Québec regulatory landscape relevant to AI and data, including Law 25.

English is required for this position as this role will regularly interact with stakeholders across Canada, US and other countries across our Global footprint where English is the common language. Due to the significant high volume of interactions with these English-speaking stakeholders, which is inherent to this position, it is not possible to reorganize the company's

activities to avoid this requirement.

Preferred Qualifications:

Established network in the Québec market — clients, ecosystem institutions, or the local AI and engineering talent community.

Depth in one or more Québec-weighted industries: financial services and insurance, aerospace, transportation and travel, energy and utilities, retail, telecommunications, natural resources, or public sector.

Experience with private, sovereign or residency-constrained AI deployments and the trade-offs they impose.

Experience making the economics of AI legible to a CFO: inference cost, unit economics and benefits realization.

Practical experience evaluating and tuning model performance in French.

Hands-on fluency with modern AI engineering tooling: agent frameworks, orchestration, retrieval and knowledge infrastructure, evaluation harnesses, observability, and agentic coding tools.

Experience with major cloud and AI platforms and with frontier model providers.

Applied research background, published work, patents, or open-source contribution in AI/ML.

Travel and Working Conditions

Based in Montréal, with regular presence at client sites across Québec.

Travel elsewhere in Canada and occasionally internationally, concentrated around pursuits, delivery milestones and ecosystem events.

Blend of on-site client collaboration, in-office team leadership and remote delivery.

About SandboxAQ

SandboxAQ is a high-growth company delivering AI solutions that address some of the world's greatest challenges. The company’s Large Quantitative Models (LQMs) power advances in life sciences, financial services, navigation, cybersecurity, and other sectors.

We are a global team that is tech-focused and includes experts in AI, chemistry, cybersecurity, physics, mathematics, medicine, engineering, and other specialties. The company emerged from Alphabet Inc. as an independent, growth capital-backed company in 2022, funded by leading investors and supported by a braintrust of industry leaders.

At SandboxAQ, we’ve cultivated an environment that encourages creativity, collaboration, and impact. By investing deeply in our people, we’re building a thriving, global workforce poised to tackle the world's epic challenges. Join us to advance your career in pursuit of an inspiring mission, in a community of like-minded people who value entrepreneurialism, ownership, and transformative impact.

About The Team

The SandboxAQ AI Generation Engine (SAIGE) team’s mission is to accelerate SandboxAQ’s mission of “Deep Impact at Scale”
with a focus on quantitative AI and rapid innovation. More specifically, the SAIGE team aims to:

Build next-generation AI capabilities that establish SandboxAQ as the global pacesetter in quantitative AI.
Identify, incubate, prototype, and launch new AI products for high-potential and longer-term use cases, proving (or disproving) their viability as high-impact, highly profitable business lines.

The SAIGE team operates on the following principles: Prototype with Velocity, Explore Boldly, Fail Smart, Learn Fast, Look Forward, and Share Knowledge.

Our current top priority use case is leveraging AI and LQMs to solve some of the most impactful problems in the Finance and Insurance industries.

The Opportunity

As The Director Of Product Management For The AI Generation Engine (SAIGE), You Will Be The PM Lead For The Team And a Key Partner To Engineering, Research, And User Research. You Will

Own the product strategy and execution for our efforts in Finance & Risk Modeling, partnering closely with financial services and insurance customers to understand their workflows, risk models, and decision-making processes.
Lead rapid prototyping and innovation across a broad range of new ideas and domains, driving 0→1 product discovery, experimentation, and incubation of high-potential use cases.
Operate in a highly ambiguous, fast-changing environment, providing clarity on priorities, making pragmatic trade-offs, and ensuring we ship impactful prototypes and products.

This role is ideal for a seasoned product leader who is energized by uncertainty, enjoys working across disciplines (UXR, engineering, research, business), and is excited to build new AI and quantitative products from the ground up.

Key Responsibilities

Lead product strategy in Finance & Risk Modeling

Own the product vision, roadmap, and execution for our Finance/Risk portfolio, with a focus on financial services and insurance (e.g., portfolio risk, capital modeling, risk analytics, underwriting, and related workflows).
Develop a deep understanding of customer contexts, including current tools, models, and data flows (e.g., portfolio / risk modeling systems, vendor platforms, internal analytics stacks).
Partner with quantitative researchers, ML engineers, and domain experts to translate customer problems into clear product requirements and model/data needs.
Define success metrics and validation strategies to compare our approaches against existing PML/ERM and portfolio views, and to demonstrate differentiated value.

Drive rapid prototyping and 0→1 innovation

Identify, evaluate, and prioritize new AI / LQM use cases across multiple domains (beyond Finance/Risk), from early signals to clearer opportunities.
Lead 0→1 product discovery: problem framing, hypothesis development, lightweight customer validation, and rapid iteration on prototypes.
Work with engineering and research to scope experiments that are small enough to move quickly but meaningful enough to answer key questions.
Establish and champion a rigorous but pragmatic approach to ruthless prioritization, ensuring the team focuses on the highest-impact opportunities.

jobs.description:
Job Description

As Director, Planning, you will be responsible for the strategic leadership, governance, and performance of all planning activities across shipbuilding and ship repair programs. This role will ensure that integrated, credible, and risk-informed plans are developed, maintained, and used as key management tools to support on-time and efficient project delivery.

You will provide functional leadership to the planning organization, establish standards and best practices, and work closely with the Project Management, Operations, Engineering, and Finance Departments, as well as senior management, to support decision-making at both the project and portfolio levels.

More Specifically, You Will

Define and lead the enterprise planning strategy, including standards, methodologies, tools, and governance across all programs.
Ensure project and program plans accurately reflect execution strategy, contractual commitments, scope, and project maturity, while maintaining planning integrity, consistency, and compliance throughout the organization.
Provide executive oversight of integrated program and project planning activities, including milestones, sequencing, critical interfaces, constraints, and recovery strategies.
Assess planning performance, trends, and risks at the portfolio level, proactively identifying leading indicators and escalating material issues with clear, actionable recommendations to senior management.
Establish and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) to measure planning quality, predictability, readiness, and delivery performance.
Ensure robust progress measurement, forecasting, and alignment with cost, earned value, and project controls reporting to support informed management decisions.
Oversee the evaluation of planning impacts related to changes, delays, claims, and replanning activities, ensuring risks, assumptions, and recovery scenarios are clearly articulated and supported by credible analysis.
Lead and develop the planning organization, ensuring appropriate capabilities, capacity, and succession planning are in place to support current and future programs.
Set clear expectations for performance, accountability, and continuous improvement, and attract, retain, and develop senior planning talent.
Act as the senior planning authority and trusted advisor to senior management.

Qualifications

Ten to fifteen (10–15) years of progressive experience in planning, project controls, or a related field, including at least five (5) years in a supervisory role.
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Business Administration, or a related field is preferred.
Significant experience supporting large‑scale shipbuilding and/or ship repair projects is a strong asset.
Strong knowledge and demonstrated ability to apply project controls principles and methodologies aligned with AACEI and PMI (PMBOK) standard practices.
Sound understanding of project delivery phases and associated activities and deliverables.
Working knowledge of Earned Value Measurement (EVM – ANSI/EIA-748-B) in engineering, procurement, and construction.
Working knowledge of risk management principles and methodologies.
Demonstrated understanding of the interrelationships between good technical project scope definition, planning quality, estimating, construction sequencing, execution strategy, procurement and contracting strategies, commissioning, and start-up.
Ability to manage the impact of changes and trends related to budget control and ETC and EAC analysis.
Strong understanding of cross-functional interfaces with engineering, supply chain (materials and subcontracts), construction, safety, quality, finance and accounting, and operations.
Ability to work effectively as an integral part of a large team, including the client, engineering disciplines, the senior management team, and third-party suppliers.
Effective verbal and written communication skills with superiors, colleagues, and internal and external individuals.
Bilingualism (French and English). Proficiency in english and french is required for this position, as the incumbent will interact in both languages with our clients, partners, and suppliers.
High degree of teamwork and collaboration with other team members, including fast-paced deadline pressures.
Excellent knowledge of Excel, including pivot tables, formulas, and import/export features.
Proficiency in Primavera P6, or at a minimum, comprehensive knowledge of its use and capabilities in integrated planning and project controls environments.
Good working knowledge of financial systems and project management techniques (planning, budget control, etc.).
Ability to prioritize assignments, deal with interruptions, and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment, while producing high-quality work.
Attention to details.
Successful completion of the investigation and security clearance process required under the federal government’s Contract Security Program.

About Us

Founded in 1825, Davie is Canada’s largest shipyard. We build and repair specialized, essential vessels for government and commercial clients.

Working at Davie means embracing vast possibilities every day and taking part in an adventure where every project leads to something monumental. It’s about tackling big challenges with creativity, determination, and passion.

There’s a real sense of pride in being part of the Davie team. It’s not just about delivering major projects—it’s about innovation and pushing boundaries to accomplish something truly remarkable.

!
