Job Description:

Director, Management Equity Finance and Tax – SLC Management

WHAT IS IN IT FOR YOU:

As a Director, Management Equity Finance and Tax you will support the financial and tax operations of its Management Equity Plan (MEP). This role plays a critical part in ensuring accurate financial reporting, tax compliance, and stakeholder communication across SLC. The ideal candidate will support the development and implementation of robust reporting and communication processes, within tight deadlines, for the management equity plan at SLC Management. The role will ensure that management receive the information they need to complete their personal tax obligations arising from the MEP program and that the Sun Life group receives the information it needs for corporate tax purposes. As the MEP is complex, the role will require close collaboration with internal and external business partners to ensure the required information and filings are delivered in an efficient and well-controlled environment. An understanding of the different tax treatments for flow through entities (such as partnerships/LLCs), corporations and hybrid entities will be an advantage in being able to deliver in this role.

WHAT YOU WILL DO:

Financial Reporting & Analysis

Develop deep understanding of the drivers of income vs taxable income for individuals and corporates in the SLC group to support the MD in preparing MEP-related financial commentary based on taxable income and distributions across the US, Canada and RoW.
Analyze and reconcile accounting vs. taxable income differences and prepare simplified summaries for internal and external stakeholders.

Tax Compliance & Advisory

Coordinate with internal and external tax advisors and operational tax teams to ensure timely and accurate tax filings and payments, on behalf of, or to individuals, including US state composite returns for Non-Residents, PTET elections.
Ensure information from SLC affiliates and corporate entities are properly accurate and complete to enable both corporate tax and personal tax reporting purposes.
Support the tax settlement process and partner with SLC and Corporate Treasury on the timing and amount of cash needs.

Stakeholder Engagement

Act as a liaison between HR, Finance, Corporate Tax, Affiliate Tax, and external advisors to gather and disseminate financial and tax data.
Coordinate with affiliates, external tax advisors and SLF Corporate Tax team to understand the various data needs and develop a robust data repository to efficiently and effectively share information between parties.
Prepare quarterly tax analysis and commentary to support MEP participant communication, filings and payments on account.

Process Optimization

Contribute to the development and implementation of streamlined reporting and communication processes. Systems have already been selected and are being implemented, you must ensure systems generate synergies.
Identify opportunities to enhance the efficiency and accuracy of tax provision and settlement workflows.

WHAT YOU WILL NEED TO SUCCEED:

CPA or equivalent designation strongly preferred.
8+ years of experience in finance or tax roles, ideally within asset management or financial services and ideally with a strong tax component to their work
Strong curiosity, desire to learn and resilience - this is a multi-disciplinary role requiring understanding of finance, tax and legal structures across different jurisdictions (mainly US and Canada but also others, particularly the UK)
Experience working with tax-transparent entities and the tax reporting associated with them is a strong benefit

Excellent analytical, communication, and stakeholder management skills.

At OpenText, AI is at the heart of everything we do—powering innovation, transforming work, and empowering digital knowledge workers. We are hiring talent AI can't replace to help us shape the future of information management. Join us.

Senior Director, AI Product Strategy - On-Site - Full Time, Permanent Role.

Location:
OpenText Headquarters – Waterloo, Ontario

The Opportunity

OpenText manages information for the largest organizations worldwide — and we're now rebuilding that foundation around AI. As enterprises embrace a new era of intelligent automation and generative AI, we are building the next generation of content, data, and AI-driven solutions that empower organizations to unlock knowledge, drive efficiency, ship AI that enterprises actually trust.

Your Impact

We are seeking a Senior Director, AI Strategist and Product Management to lead our initiatives for Generative AI and Agentic AI product portfolios within the Content Management Business Unit. This senior leadership role will shape OpenText’s AI product roadmap and execution, driving innovation at scale across our enterprise SaaS solutions.

The ideal candidate is a product leader and hands-on AI strategist — someone who combines deep technical expertise in AI and data science with proven experience leading global product and development teams to deliver transformative business outcomes. You will own both the 'why' and the 'what' — not just the roadmap document.

What The Role Offers

Define and execute the AI strategy for all our Content Management products.
Lead and mentor a global AI product organization, fostering innovation, accountability, and deep client empathy.
Architect and deliver production-grade agentic systems using LangChain, LangGraph, A2A (Agent-to-Agent) protocols, and other transformative AI frameworks to create adaptive, multi-agent enterprise solutions.
Partner with Development, Data Science, and Data Cloud teams to develop scalable, secure, and high-performing AI-driven products.
Shape OpenText's point of view on AI — representing the company at industry events, client forums, and analyst briefings — including Gartner, Forrester, and major client advisory boards — as a thought leader in enterprise AI.
Report into and co-own strategy with the Content BU leadership and C-level executives to align AI strategy with business goals and ensure measurable outcomes.
Ensure product roadmaps align with modern data architectures and leverage knowledge graphs and unstructured data management to enhance AI model grounding and reduce hallucinations.

What You Need To Succeed

7+ years of proven experience in data science, AI, and ML — with at least 3 years leading product organizations at enterprise scale — and hands-on exposure to building and optimizing Agentic AI systems.
Deep expertise in Agentic AI frameworks, including MCP, A2A protocols, Google ADK, LangChain, and LangGraph (critical).
Demonstrated success leading Product Management organizations in enterprise software or cloud platforms.
Strong background in AI/ML, data management, and modern data architectures (Lakehouse, Data Fabric, knowledge graphs).
Experience with unstructured data management, grounding AI models, and context engineering to reduce hallucinations in generative AI systems.
Proven track record delivering enterprise-scale SaaS solutions through collaboration with global, cross-functional teams.
Exceptional communication, storytelling, and executive presence — with the ability to influence strategy and engage C-level stakeholders.
Track record of shipping: you can point to specific AI products you've taken from concept to production, with measurable outcomes.

One Last Thing

OpenText is more than just a corporation, it's a global community where trust is foundational, the bar is raised, and outcomes are owned.

Join us on our mission to drive positive change through privacy, technology, and collaboration. At OpenText, we don't just have a culture; we have character. Choose us because you want to be part of a company that embraces innovation and empowers its employees to make a difference.

About Versapay

Versapay is the platform that rewires AR by removing barriers to collecting and reconciling B2B payments, providing end- to-end cash flow clarity, ensuring businesses can manage working capital on their terms. By closing the loop for finance teams and their business systems, customers, and payment activity into a single intelligent ecosystem, Versapay transforms money matters into a data-driven advantage. With 10,000 customers and 5M+ companies transacting, Versapay facilitates 110M+ transactions and processes $300B+ in payments volume annually.

About The Role

We are looking for a strategic, builder-minded Senior Director of Enterprise Data Management to own and execute Versapay’s enterprise data strategy at a pivotal moment in our evolution. This leader will drive the convergence of our transactional, operational, behavioral, relational and intent data layers into a unified operational backbone — the foundational unlock for AI- powered product features, semantic data models, externalized data products, and autonomous AR workflows.

This is a high-visibility, high-impact role directly tied to our product and commercial roadmap, with a clear mandate and executive alignment behind it.

What You’ll Do

Data Strategy & Architecture

Define and drive Versapay’s enterprise data strategy, aligning the data roadmap to product, AI, and commercial objectives.
Lead the architectural convergence of our transactional, operational, and analytical data layers into a unified, bi-directional operational backbone.
Own a multi-year data maturity roadmap with clear milestones across architecture, semantics, governance, and accessibility.
Champion a business-first data modelling philosophy: canonical hierarchies, enterprise ontologies, and shared metric catalogues that allow humans and AI agents to interpret data consistently.

Data Governance & Quality

Operationalize data governance as a first-class concern — automated classification, RBAC enforcement, platform SLAs, and certified data objects.
Formalize the Enterprise Data Catalogue, replacing institutional knowledge with a searchable, self-service discovery layer.
Deploy and maintain an executive data health dashboard to provide ongoing visibility into the health and integrity of our data estate.
Enforce the data procurement gate, ensuring new tools and systems are reviewed and classified before entering the estate.
Build and own the Enterprise Data Asset Registry to enable secure, frictionless data sharing internally and with commercial partners.

AI Enablement & Agentic Readiness

Drive data infrastructure readiness to support Versapay’s AI roadmap — from ML pipelines and LLM serving layers to agentic serving tiers.
Establish formal schema contracts and semantic modelling standards that guarantee deterministic outputs for safe, scalable agent deployment.
Partner with Product and Engineering to enable agentic capabilities: reverse data flow, predictive model productization, and real-time data serving.
Govern data and AI exposure — ensuring sensitive data stays within approved platforms and all external data products meet strict quality, lineage, and privacy standards.

Data Accessibility & Commercialization

Evolve the function from ad hoc data requests to a design-first, product-oriented organization with a governed, discoverable asset registry.
Operationalize external data products for commercialization, delivering clear value to customers within consent and compliance frameworks.
Partner with the commercial team on data product strategy — turning Versapay’s proprietary network data into defensible, recurring revenue.
Expand self-service data access for internal teams while protecting compute capacity and governance standards.

Team Leadership

Act as the cross-functional bridge between Product, Engineering, Commercial, Finance, and Legal/Compliance- ensuring data serves every function from a shared, trusted foundation.
Build a culture of data discipline — standardizing how information is captured and governed so insight is consistent, discoverable, and trusted across the organization.
Represent the data function at the executive level, partnering closely with the CTO and contributing to the broader AI and product roadmap.

Required

10+ years of experience in data leadership, with at least 5+ years at the Director level owning enterprise data strategy, architecture, or governance.
Demonstrated track record of modernizing and unifying complex, multi-source data environments at scale — ideally in a SaaS, fintech, payments context.
Deep expertise in modern data stack: cloud data warehouses (Snowflake preferred), lakehouse architectures, ETL frameworks, and semantic/canonical modelling.
Strong evidence of application of AI and ML infrastructure — including how data governance, observability, and semantic standards underpin safe, scalable AI deployment.
Proven ability to build and lead high-performing technical teams and partner effectively across Product, Engineering, and Commercial functions.
Experience governing data for commercial use: external data products, consent frameworks, lineage standards, and privacy compliance.
Exceptional communication skills — able to translate complex data and architectural concepts for executive audiences and build alignment across functions.
Experience with managing the cost of data warehouses and cost forecasting.

Reporting directly to the President and Vice-Chancellor, the Vice-President, Finance & Administration and Chief Financial Officer (VPFA & CFO) is a key member of the Executive Council and a strategic leader.

As a trusted strategic advisor to the President, the Board of Governors, and the executive leadership team, the VPFA & CFO plays a central role in shaping MacEwan University's future by providing strategic financial leadership that enables institutional growth, advances academic priorities, and strengthens long-term sustainability.

As the University's senior finance executive, the Vice-President, Finance & Administration provides strategic leadership that strengthens financial sustainability, drives enterprise transformation, and enables long-term institutional growth.

This is an exceptional opportunity to lead a broad and impactful portfolio spanning finance, information services, human resources, and facilities and sustainability services. As MacEwan's senior financial executive, the VPFA & CFO will contribute to enterprise-wide strategy, champion operational excellence, lead transformative initiatives, and identify innovative approaches to revenue generation, resource optimization, and long-term financial resilience. With responsibility for financial stewardship, enterprise risk management, capital planning, strategic resource allocation, and the systems that support these functions, the VPFA & CFO will help position the University for its next phase of growth and success.

Working closely with students, faculty, staff, government, unions, and community partners, the VPFA & CFO will help shape an institution with significant momentum, ensuring MacEwan University continues to deliver an exceptional student experience while achieving its bold ambitions for the future.

Ideal Candidate Profile

Success in this role requires more than financial expertise. It calls for a collaborative, forward-thinking leader who thrives in complex environments, builds trusted relationships across diverse constituent groups, and inspires innovation and continuous improvement.

The ideal candidate is an accomplished executive who combines strategic vision with sound judgment, collaborative leadership, and exceptional relationship-building skills. They will bring deep financial expertise, a strong record of leading complex organizations through growth and change, and the ability to serve as a trusted advisor on financial stewardship, enterprise risk, governance, and institutional strategy. They combine strategic vision with exceptional financial acumen and are recognized for challenging assumptions, identifying opportunities, and delivering meaningful organizational change.

They have demonstrated success leading enterprise-wide transformation across finance, human resources, information technology, and other administrative functions, building integrated teams that work collaboratively toward shared institutional outcomes rather than operating in functional silos.

A confident and forward-thinking leader, they inspire trust through integrity, transparency, and accountability while fostering a culture of innovation, continuous improvement, and evidence-informed decision-making. They are an effective collaborator who builds strong relationships across diverse constituent groups and thrives in complex, highly regulated environments.

The successful candidate will be passionate about developing people, building organizational capacity, and helping position MacEwan University for continued success and long-term impact.

Relevant university degree required and Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation highly preferred. Equivalent senior financial leadership experience as the organization's chief financial executive may be considered.
Significant executive leadership experience leading finance within a large, complex organization, preferably in the post-secondary sector.
Demonstrated success leading enterprise transformation, organizational redesign, technology-enabled modernization, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Demonstrated success leading finance and administrative functions, including financial stewardship, budgeting, forecasting, enterprise risk management, and organizational transformation.
Demonstrated success leading multidisciplinary portfolios that include finance, human resources, information technology and other corporate services.
Experience providing strategic advice to executive leadership and boards within complex governance environments.
Proven ability to lead multidisciplinary portfolios and build high-performing teams through periods of growth and change.

We're looking for a senior leader to join the Affirm Global Operations team as the Director, Vendor Strategy & Operations
to lead Affirm's global BPO and vendor operations program and serve as a true partner in reinventing how we serve customers at scale across our large global vendor network. This leader owns the customer operations vendor strategy, performance, and outcomes of our global servicing network vendor program — customer experience, compliance, operational excellence, resiliency, and cost-to-serve — across a rapidly growing and complex business. The role will be taking ownership and providing programmatic oversight of the vendor program for operations.

This is a senior leadership role for someone who thinks like an owner, not an administrator. The ideal candidate pairs deep expertise in fintech and financial-services customer operations and vendor programs with genuine fluency in applying AI and human call center culture to reinvent servicing across the vendor network. They are relentlessly customer-centric, dive deep into both the customer and front-line vendor agent experience, and know how to build a winning combination of culture and data-driven operations across vendors and our internal team. This role is scoped to grow: the right leader will expand into broader operational scope as our transformation matures and play a key leadership role in shaping the future of Affirm Operations and customer centric company culture.

You'll lead a team of Vendor Managers and In-Country Vendor Managers, partner closely with cross-functional stakeholders, and shape the future of Affirm's global servicing network.

What You'll Do

Strategy, Governance & Reinvention

Define and execute the long-term strategy for Affirm's global customer operations vendor network, balancing customer experience, operational efficiency, resiliency, compliance, and business continuity across all global vendors.
Reinvent how we resolve customer issues and deliver experience across the vendor network, treating the BPO vendor network as an innovation hub rather than a cost center.
Establish governance frameworks, performance standards, and accountability mechanisms across the global vendor ecosystem.
Lead executive-level vendor governance forums, including Quarterly Business Reviews, strategic planning, and escalation management.
Partner with Financial Partnerships on vendor selection, expansion, remediation, and network design, evaluating capabilities, geographic footprint, and concentration risk to inform future-state decisions.

AI & Operational Innovation

Partner deeply across product, engineering and operations teams to deploy agent and customer facing AI and automation across servicing workflows within the vendor network — agent assist, quality, forecasting, and customer resolution — to reinvent cost-to-serve and elevate vendor agent and customer experience.
Bring an experimentation mindset, using AI in everyday problem-solving to reimagine the vendor operating model and program, not just optimize the current one.

Performance & Operational Excellence

Own overall vendor network performance across servicing functions, including CSAT, SLA, compliance, QA, productivity, and efficiency outcomes.
Build mechanisms for vendor performance management, escalation handling, and vendor accountability, and drive systemic improvements across vendors and functional PODs.
Lead recovery efforts for high-risk or underperforming vendor relationships.
Drive target cost optimization programs across all global vendors.

Analytics & Decision Enablement

Partner with Analytics to define vendor reporting requirements, scorecards, and operational health metrics.
Translate operational trends into actionable recommendations for senior leadership, ensuring decisions are grounded in data and measurable outcomes.

Cross-Functional Leadership

Build a global "one team" mentality that treats the vendor network as strategic partners rather than order-takers.
Serve as the primary operational leader for vendor-supported servicing functions, partnering with Product, Engineering, Workforce Management, QA, Training, Risk, and Compliance.
Lead large-scale initiatives — vendor migrations, specialization efforts, operating-model transformations, and regulatory implementations.
Act as the executive escalation point for complex vendor, operational, and customer-experience issues.

People Leadership

Lead and develop a team of Vendor Managers and In-Country Vendor Managers, embodying a customer-centric culture and Affirm's values by example.
Establish role clarity, operating rhythms, and performance expectations across the organization.
Coach leaders to strengthen analytical rigor, strategic thinking, vendor-management capability, and cross-functional influence.
Build a high-performing organization anchored in accountability, ownership, and continuous improvement.

What We Look For

15+ years in customer operations — including large-scale global vendor BPO program management, operations strategy, or consulting for fast-paced, multi-million-customer businesses using vendor networks (or demonstrated equivalent leadership trajectory).
10+ years leading managers and/or complex global operational and vendor organizations.
Proven success managing large-scale outsourced operations and global vendor networks across multiple international geographies.
Experience leading and optimizing supply and demand management with global work force management teams.
Demonstrated experience deploying AI or automation to improve customer operations or BPO environments at scale.
Strong analytical background, using data to drive strategic decisions and operational outcomes.
Track record leading large cross-functional initiatives with measurable business impact.
Deep cultural fluency across global geographies — a proven ability to lead and motivate diverse international teams and to build a customer-centric, high-performing culture across varied call-center and BPO environments.
Exceptional communication, executive presence, and stakeholder management.

Responsibilities

Develop and implement information management strategies and polices to ensure the secure and efficient handling of Court information.
Project management, change management and strategic planning processes for the effective delivery and management of both short and long-term information technology goals set by the judiciary.
Represent the interests of the judiciary recognizing judicial independence in their day-today operations of and/or projects involving implementing and/or updating software, databases and digital tools used by the judiciary or involving judicial data and court information.
Must operate with full confidence of the Chief Justices and the Chief Judge, be discreet as required and understand the highly confidential and sensitive nature of the work that they perform.
The Chief Court Information Officer (“CCIO”) must have the ability to work cooperatively and harmoniously with all members of the judiciary and both senior and front-line court administration staff, as we as internal and external stakeholders.
Lead the modernization of court information systems, including case management, e-filing, digital evidence, and courtroom technology.

Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively with stakeholders at all levels of the organization.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to develop and implement effective information management strategies for an increasingly digital legal work environment.
Extensive experience conducting IT and information security research and providing advice and opinions, preferably at a senior executive level.

jobs.title: Director, HRBP - Operations and Technology
jobs.description:
The Director, HR Business Partner partners with the Partnerships & Alliances and Commercial System Acceleration leadership teams to drive people strategies that enable business growth, organizational effectiveness, and high performance. As a trusted advisor and member of the leadership team, this role leads talent, workforce, and organizational initiatives that support business objectives and enhance the employee experience.

Operating in a highly matrixed environment, the HRBP collaborates closely with business leaders, regional HR teams, and Centers of Excellence to develop and execute integrated people solutions. The role also plays a key part in leading organizational change, shaping talent strategy, and driving an interconnected people agenda that contributes to both operational and financial success.

Preferred Location: MSP, Toronto

About The Role

In this opportunity as Director, HRBP,
you will be responsible for:

Partnering and Innovating Across the Enterprise

Act as a thought partner and coach to senior leadership, able to contribute on all aspects of growing and managing the business (not restricting themselves to talent-related discussions).
Support leaders with organizational change.
Drive the strategic people agenda in a highly matrixed and collaborative environment.
Partner with key teams across Partnership & Alliances and Commercial System Acceleration to align HR strategies with business objectives.
Lead change management initiatives, acting as a change agent to foster innovation and transformation within the organization.

Talent Strategy & Strategic Workforce Planning

Work in tandem with business leaders to develop business strategy and translate this into a people strategy, deriving short- and long-term talent needs from strategic business plans, with an emphasis on strategic workforce planning — understanding the talent needs of these functions, including skill gaps and forecast needs.
Provide strategic workforce and top talent succession planning by engaging with leaders to identify top talent needs and translating those needs into discrete projects and initiatives that flow smoothly to the HR Professionals Pool for execution.
Identify future capabilities and align talent strategies with industry trends and business needs.
Develop and implement talent strategy and strategic workforce plans using predictive analytics and scenario modeling.

Organizational Design and Talent Management

Provide functional-specific talent change management strategy (e.g., a hiring strategy for go-to-market in a growth region).
Design effective operating models and talent management activities to support the business strategy.
Strengthen the talent pool through succession planning, talent flow, and career management.
Lead talent acquisition strategies to attract and onboard future capabilities.

Organizational Health and Effectiveness

Partner with and coach leaders on delivering a talent-first culture.
Improve business effectiveness through operational enhancements aligned with the business model.
Promote an inclusive and values-driven culture.

Understanding Our Customers, Industry, and Thomson Reuters

Stay current on industry trends to inform HR practices and drive innovation.
Build a professional network and represent Thomson Reuters HR at external events.

Understanding Data and Creating Insight

Utilize metrics and analytics to guide management decisions and improve organizational performance.
Leverage Workday as a key platform for operational efficiency.

Linking Financial Performance to People Planning

Monitor financial performance to understand people implications and design HR responses accordingly.

About You

You're a fit for the role of Director, HRBP
if your background includes:

Required Knowledge & Skills

Business or HR degree preferred; a relevant Master's degree is a plus.
Track record of designing and being accountable for the delivery of a global people strategy.
Track record of leading the HR response to changing industry and business environments.
Experience partnering with senior business leaders.
Experience working in global, complex, matrixed environments.
Experience actively managing the health of an organization (engagement, culture, etc.).
10+ years of experience with broad HR responsibilities preferred; less experience will be considered depending on the scale and scope of the experience.
Strong consulting skills and strategic advisory capability, with the ability to influence senior stakeholders.
Expertise in organizational design and change management.
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic, multicultural, international environment.
Influential storyteller with strong interpersonal and communication skills.
Innovative mindset with experience in talent management and acquisition.
Demonstrates learning agility and strong business acumen.
M&A or strategic partnership experience is a plus.

Critical Leadership Capabilities

Collaborating and Influencing: build genuine partnerships and consensus across diverse teams.
Leading Change: advocate for innovation and support leadership through business shifts.

New Position: This position is open due to an existing vacancy to support our evolving business needs.

What’s in it For You?

Hybrid Work Model: We’ve adopted a flexible hybrid working environment for our office-based roles while delivering a seamless experience that is digitally and physically connected.
Flexibility & Work-Life Balance: Flex My Way is a set of supportive workplace policies designed to help manage personal and professional responsibilities, whether caring for family, giving back to the community, or finding time to refresh and reset. This builds upon our flexible work arrangements, including work from anywhere for up to 8 weeks per year, empowering employees to achieve a better work-life balance.
Career Development and Growth: By fostering a culture of continuous learning and skill development, we prepare our talent to tackle tomorrow’s challenges and deliver real-world solutions. Our Grow My Way programming and skills-first approach ensures you have the tools and knowledge to grow, lead, and thrive in an AI-enabled future.
Industry Competitive Benefits: We offer comprehensive benefit plans to include flexible vacation, two company-wide Mental Health Days off, access to the Headspace app, retirement savings, tuition reimbursement, employee incentive programs, and resources for mental, physical, and financial wellbeing.
Culture: Globally recognized, award-winning reputation for inclusion and belonging, flexibility, work-life balance, and more. We live by our values: Obsess over our Customers, Compete to Win, Challenge (Y)our Thinking, Act Fast / Learn Fast, and Stronger Together.
Social Impact: Make an impact in your community with our Social Impact Institute. We offer employees two paid volunteer days off annually and opportunities to get involved with pro-bono consulting projects and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) initiatives.
Making a Real-World Impact: We are one of the few companies globally that helps its customers pursue justice, truth, and transparency. Together, with the professionals and institutions we serve, we help uphold the rule of law, turn the wheels of commerce, catch bad actors, report the facts, and provide trusted, unbiased information to people all over the world.

About Fulfillment IQ

Fulfillment IQ (FIQ) is a supply chain technology and consulting company helping retailers, brands, and 3PLs solve complex fulfillment and logistics challenges.

Our work spans three core practices: Supply Chain Consulting, Technology Delivery & Transformation, and Implementation. We help customers assess and design supply-chain strategies, select and implement technology, modernize fulfillment operations, and build technology solutions that solve complex operational challenges.

The Opportunity

FIQ is looking for an experienced VP of Sales, Enterprise to drive growth across our full portfolio of services.

This is a hands-on, quota-carrying enterprise sales role for someone who knows how to sell complex professional services, not simply software licenses.

You will work with senior executives at large retailers, brands, 3PLs, and other supply-chain organizations to understand complex business and operational challenges, shape solutions with FIQ's consulting and technical teams, and own opportunities through commercial close.

As FIQ grows, you will also contribute to building the sales organization, including sales methodology, account strategy, forecasting, coaching, and future team development.

What You'll Do

Own complex enterprise opportunities from prospecting and qualification through discovery, solution development, proposal, negotiation, and close
Sell across FIQ's Supply Chain Consulting, Technology Delivery & Transformation, and Implementation practices
Build relationships with C-suite and senior leaders across supply chain, logistics, operations, fulfillment, and technology

Why Fulfillment IQ

OpenText is a global leader in information management, where innovation, creativity, and collaboration are the key components of our corporate culture. As a member of our team, you will have the opportunity to partner with the most highly regarded companies in the world, tackle complex issues, and contribute to projects that shape the future of digital transformation.

AI-First. Future-Driven. Human-Centered.

At OpenText, AI is at the heart of everything we do—powering innovation, transforming work, and empowering digital knowledge workers. We are hiring talent AI can't replace to help us shape the future of information management. Join us.

Workforce Strategy & Talent Development Director (HRBP)

Shape the future of the organization through workforce, talent, and organizational strategy. What You Will Do

Partner with senior leaders to align people strategies with business priorities and organizational needs.
Lead global workforce planning, organization design, talent strategy, succession planning, and leadership development initiatives.
Provide executive coaching, consultation, and trusted counsel to leaders, influencing decisions and constructively challenging thinking when needed.
Drive organizational transformation and change initiatives from planning through execution.
Use workforce and talent analytics to identify trends, risks, and opportunities and translate insights into actionable recommendations.
Lead complex, cross-functional people initiatives with strong program and stakeholder management discipline.
Drive alignment and consistency on function-specific priorities and global HR programs across all regions.
Partner with HR Centers of Excellence (COEs), including Talent Acquisition, Total Rewards, and HR Shared Services, to deliver integrated solutions and talent advisory to business leaders.

What Success Looks Like

Senior and executive leaders see you as a trusted advisor and strategic partner.
Business strategy, workforce plans, and talent priorities are strongly aligned.
Leadership pipelines are strengthened and succession plans are robust and future-ready.
Organizational changes and transformation initiatives are delivered effectively and on schedule.
Complex people initiatives are managed with clear governance, milestones, stakeholder alignment, and measurable outcomes.
Risks and dependencies are anticipated early, enabling faster, better-informed decisions.
Workforce and talent insights translate into recommendations that improve business performance and organizational effectiveness.
Strong collaboration and alignment across the HR team and broader organization.

What It Takes

Significant HR Business Partner experience supporting senior and executive leaders in complex, global organizations.
Expertise in workforce planning, talent management, succession planning, leadership development, and organizational design.
Strong business acumen, executive presence, and consulting capability.
Ability to coach, influence, and constructively challenge leaders.

Strong project and program management skills, including planning, prioritization, stakeholder management, governance, and execution.

Enterprise mindset with strong collaboration and relationship-building skills.

If you’re ready to shape the workforce, develop talent, and help drive meaningful organizational changes, we’d love to hear from you. Join us and help shape the organization, the talent, and the future of the business.

jobs.title: Director, PathWise Actuarial Implementation and AI-Enabled Process Transformation
jobs.description:
The Life Solutions division at Aon is seeking a Director to lead large-scale PathWise implementation projects. This role also supports AI-enabled process transformation initiatives for life and annuity insurers across North America. This client-facing role combines actuarial expertise, implementation leadership, and technology-enabled transformation to help insurers modernize modelling, reporting, workflow automation, AI-enabled systems, and operational workflows.

The Director will work within Aon Life Solutions, part of Aon’s Reinsurance Strategy and Technology Group to translate business needs into practical implementation plans, scalable operating models, and measurable delivery outcomes. This role will be based in Canada.

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in Canada. This role is not eligible for sponsorship, and we are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa or work permit.

Aon is in the business of better decisions

At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world.

As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.

What The Day Will Look Like

Implementation and Client Delivery

Lead and support large-scale PathWise implementation projects for life and annuity insurers across North America.
Handle key implementation workstreams, including model migration, data integration, testing, reconciliation, workflow design, documentation, training, and production deployment.
Translate client business objectives and current-state processes into clear delivery plans, target-state solutions, and implementation roadmaps.
Develop and migrate actuarial models and production processes for valuation, pricing, financial reporting, capital, ALM, and risk management use cases.
Support delivery governance, issue resolution, risk management, collaborator communication, post-implementation stabilization, and client knowledge transfer.

AI-Enabled Process Transformation and Innovation

Identify, prioritize, and continuously refine opportunities to use automation and AI-enabled capabilities to improve actuarial modelling, reporting, reconciliation, documentation, and analysis processes across the PathWise lifecycle.
Collaborate closely with the PathWise AI and development teams to translate business difficulties into clear AI use cases, feature requests, and improvements.
Help clients redesign legacy actuarial workflows into more efficient, scalable, governed, and technology-enabled operating models.
Contribute to reusable implementation assets, process transformation playbooks, documentation templates, workflow designs, and AI-enabled delivery accelerators.
Lead or support pilots of new PathWise AI features, capturing user feedback and performance metrics, and consolidating insights into actionable recommendations for the PathWise AI roadmap
Promote responsible and controlled use of AI-enabled capabilities, including review, validation, traceability, documentation, and governance, and contribute to standard guidance on AI-enabled workflows

Business Development and Market Support

Support PathWise growth in the North American life and annuity market through client solutioning, demonstrations (including AI-enabled capabilities), proposals, implementation estimates, and project planning.
Partner with senior leaders in client discussions on actuarial modernization, implementation strategy, process automation, AI-enabled transformation, and business value.
Develop proof-of-concept materials and presentations on PathWise capabilities, implementation guidelines, and emerging insurance industry issues.
Develop and share case studies, training materials, and thought leadership that showcase successful AI-enabled PathWise use cases and evolving capabilities

How this opportunity is different

PathWise is Aon’s high-performance actuarial software platform, enabling insurers to model liabilities, assets, capital, and related business processes with speed, transparency, flexibility, and control. The platform supports modern actuarial modelling, scenario analysis, financial reporting, ALM, risk management, and enterprise-scale production processes.

In this role, you will help clients migrate models and processes into PathWise, improve actuarial production workflows, and apply automation and AI-enabled capabilities across requirements, model development, testing, reconciliation, documentation, workflow monitoring, and reporting. You will also help identify new AI applications within PathWise, develop improvements with the PathWise AI team, and promote adoption of emerging capabilities across client and internal teams.

Skills And Experience That Will Lead To Success

10+ years of experience in life insurance, life reinsurance, actuarial consulting, financial technology, actuarial modelling, or enterprise platform implementation.
Experience with valuation, pricing, ALM, hedging, capital, financial reporting, risk management, model governance, or related actuarial functions.
Experience supporting or leading implementation, modernization, migration, or transformation projects within actuarial, finance, risk, or insurance technology environments.
Solid understanding of life and annuity products, reserves, capital, financial reporting, ALM, and risk management.
Practical experience with actuarial modelling platforms, model migration, data transformation, testing, reconciliation, workflow automation, documentation, and production process improvement.
Experience identifying and shaping AI-enabled transformation opportunities (e.g., automation, analytics, AI-assisted development, or generative AI applications) in actuarial or financial services processes, including working with development teams to refine and implement new features
Knowledge of programming, data workflows, Python, APIs, cloud infrastructure, or automation concepts is preferred.
Comfort acting as a bridge between actuarial users and technical AI / software teams, including providing structured feedback on prototypes and helping define success metrics and acceptance criteria for new capabilities
Strong project delivery, customer management, communication, and team leadership skills.
Member of the Society of Actuaries, Canadian Institute of Actuaries, or equivalent actuarial organization preferred.

jobs.title: Associate Director, CRM Platforms & Data Governance
jobs.description:
About Us

SickKids Foundation, with over 50 years of philanthropic impact is Canada's largest charitable funder of child health research, learning and care, raising over $200 million last year. As a national charity, SickKids Foundation invests in national and international initiatives to benefit children in Canada and around the world. As the fundraising partner to The Hospital for Sick Children (SickKids), we are aligned in supporting Precision Child Health (PCH), the future of tailoring medicine to each child's unique traits so SickKids can diagnose faster, treat smarter, and predict better.

We are driven by our core values of integrity, collaboration, excellence, innovation, and inclusion, with goals of delivering a superior donor experience, investing in our people and culture, driving innovative and sustainable fundraising, and disrupting the market through data and technology.

SickKids Foundation is committed to an inclusive culture by embedding equity, diversity and inclusion in our policies, practices, and behaviours. We aim to build awareness and skills in this area, both internally and with our partners. Our commitment extends to creating a safe, positive work environment. For details on our Equity, Diversity & Inclusion commitment, please click here.

We’re committed to attracting and retaining passionate individuals to help create a healthier future. That’s why SickKids Foundation is looking for a new Associate Director, CRM Platforms & Data Governance
.

Description of the Position

The AD, CRM Platforms & Data Governance is accountable for the Foundation’s CRM and fundraising platform ecosystem, ensuring it operates as a reliable, secure, scalable, and well-governed enterprise product. This role leads CRM modernization, platform performance, donor and gift data governance, fundraising and payment capabilities, and the use of automation and AI to improve donor experience, operational efficiency, and business outcomes. As a hands-on technical leader, the Associate Director translates enterprise priorities into roadmaps, disciplined delivery, measurable outcomes, and continuous improvement. Working across IMT, Fundraising Operations, Finance, Digital, Marketing Technology, Cybersecurity, Privacy, and business partners, this role ensures platforms and data are aligned and sustainable.

Key Responsibilities

CRM Platform Product Ownership, Modernization, and Delivery

Own the CRM and fundraising platform ecosystem, including roadmap, backlog, releases, service performance, technical debt, adoption, and lifecycle management.
Lead CRM modernization and ongoing platform delivery through governed intake, prioritization, release planning, process redesign, configuration, migration, testing, cutover, stabilization, and transition to steady-state operations.
Translate enterprise priorities into clear delivery plans, measurable outcomes, and continuous improvement within the CRM and data governance portfolio.
Rationalize platforms and capabilities to reduce duplication, complexity, cost, customization, and vendor dependency.
Ensure CRM platforms and related capabilities comply with enterprise architecture, cybersecurity, privacy, data governance, and delivery standards.

Donor Data Governance and Platform Integrity

Establish and enforce governance for donor, gift, relationship, consent, preference, campaign, and engagement data maintained within CRM and fundraising platforms.
Define data ownership, stewardship, business rules, quality standards, retention requirements, and authoritative system-of-record responsibilities in partnership with business and technology teams.
Implement automated controls and remediation processes that improve data accuracy, completeness, consistency, traceability, and availability for reporting, analytics, automation, and AI.
Identify and manage material operational, technology, data, and delivery risks related to CRM platforms and donor data.
Support strong data governance practices that enable trusted decision-making, reliable reporting, and improved donor experience.

Fundraising Operations and Payment Capability

Own the technology capabilities supporting gift processing, recurring giving, pledges, donor servicing, transaction processing, receipting inputs, and reconciliation.
Partner with Fundraising Operations and Finance to maintain transaction integrity, auditability, service levels, and alignment across donor, gift, payment, and financial records.
Define CRM and reconciliation requirements for digital payment migrations led by Website & Digital Platforms.
Approve operational readiness for payment-related changes and assume steady-state payment platform ownership following transition.
Ensure fundraising and payment capabilities are scalable, secure, well-documented, and aligned with business requirements.

Automation, AI, and Operational Excellence

Identify and implement automation and AI opportunities across fundraising operations, donor servicing, data stewardship, workflow management, and platform administration.
Use automation and applied technical leadership to simplify work, accelerate delivery, improve data quality, and reduce reliance on incremental staffing.
Maintain reliable, secure, scalable, and recoverable platforms through effective monitoring, change control, incident management, documentation, and root-cause remediation.
Measure improvements in productivity, cycle time, quality, adoption, platform performance, and business value.
Drive continuous improvement through standardization, documentation, benchmarking, and disciplined operational practices.

Cross-Functional Collaboration and Enterprise Leadership

Partner across IMT and business functions to deliver Foundation-wide outcomes related to CRM modernization, fundraising operations, data governance, digital payments, analytics, automation, and AI.
Work closely with Fundraising Operations, Finance, Digital, Marketing Technology, Data Integration, Infrastructure, Cybersecurity, Privacy, Enterprise Architecture, and business partners to ensure cohesive platform delivery.
Provide clear direction, coaching, accountability, and development for team members and future leaders.
Support enterprise planning by providing accurate capacity, demand, risk, dependency, and value information to inform decisions.

Vendor and Financial Management

Manage vendors, contracts, licensing, service performance, and operational costs within delegated authority.
Maximize value from existing platform investments while identifying opportunities to reduce cost, duplication, and operational risk.
Monitor vendor performance, platform costs, and contract obligations to ensure value realization and sustainability.

Qualifications

While we know that for any job posting no one candidate will possess the qualifications being sought in equal measure, below is an outline of the qualifications we believe are important for a candidate to bring to the position or for the successful candidate to develop while in the role:

Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business Systems, Data Management, or a related field; a relevant advanced degree or certification is an asset.
Eight to ten years of progressive experience leading enterprise CRM, fundraising, constituent relationship, or comparable business platforms in a complex environment.
Demonstrated experience delivering a major CRM implementation, replacement, or modernization, including process redesign, data migration, testing, cutover, stabilization, and adoption.
Strong knowledge of platform product management, CRM configuration and releases, donor or customer data governance, gift processing, payment operations, and financial reconciliation.
Working knowledge of cloud platforms, integrations, application programming interfaces, data platforms, cybersecurity, privacy, and enterprise architecture principles.
Applied experience using automation and AI to improve workflows, data quality, analysis, productivity, and business outcomes.
Proven ability to translate enterprise priorities into roadmaps, delivery plans, measurable outcomes, and continuous improvement.
Strong vendor management, financial stewardship, risk management, communication, stakeholder engagement, and decision-making skills.
Experience leading, coaching, and developing team members with clarity, accountability, and a focus on enterprise outcomes.

We’re looking for a passionate individual who is interested in moving the dial and making a difference. We are an environment that looks to attract hardworking and committed people; people who want to challenge themselves and grow with a globally recognized brand that continues to change the world. If this describes you, consider joining our team. We look forward to reviewing your application.

Total Compensation Package

Expected Hiring Salary Range:
$99,297.00 – $124,121.00; with the ability to progress to a maximum of $142,739.00. To ensure fair and equitable pay at SickKids Foundation, placement on the salary range will be based on your years of experience, skills, and qualifications relevant to the Associate Director, CRM Platforms & Data Governance
.

To help you lead in the fight for kids’ health and to support your health, wellness, and career growth, in addition to competitive compensation, we offer a comprehensive benefit package including a flex benefit plan, tuition reimbursement, flexible work arrangements, pension plan and birth parent/parental top up – to name a few!

jobs.title: Finance Director - MacKay Contracting
jobs.description:
This is not a Finance Director role where you sit above the numbers.

MacKay is looking for a finance leader who can think strategically, work directly with Operations and executive leadership, and still get close enough to the accounting to know whether the numbers are right.

You will lead finance operations for MacKay in heavy civil construction, mining, aggregates and related businesses. The environment is project-driven, equipment-intensive and growing. Cash moves quickly. Capital decisions matter. Project forecasts matter. Bonding capacity matters.

Your job is to make sure the financial side of the business gives the company the information, discipline and capacity it needs to make good decisions and execute.

The Work

MacKay delivers complex civil, mining and infrastructure work across Western Canada, with operations developing in the United States.

That creates a finance environment very different from a conventional corporate accounting role.

You will be dealing with project forecasts, WIP, equipment economics, capital planning, banking, surety, cash flow, multiple entities and operational decisions that can move millions of dollars.

You will work closely with the COO, CEO, General Manager, Operations, Estimating and Equipment teams. You will lead the Corporate Controller and help build the finance team, systems and controls behind the business.

And when something needs to be figured out, you will be expected to get into the detail.

What You'll Get to Lead

Give leadership a clear view of where the business is going.

Build the budgeting, forecasting and financial planning processes that allow leadership to see revenue, margin, overhead, cash requirements, backlog and capital needs before decisions have to be made.

Strengthen project financial performance.

Work directly with project leaders on monthly job-cost reviews, forecast-at-completion, WIP and variance analysis. The goal is not simply to report what happened. It is to identify problems early enough that Operations can do something about them.

Own cash, banking and bonding capacity.

Maintain a forward view of cash requirements, working capital, financing and covenant compliance while developing strong relationships with lenders and sureties. You will be directly involved in the financial packages and decisions that support MacKay's ability to pursue and execute larger projects.

Bring discipline to major capital decisions.

MacKay operates an equipment-intensive business. You will work with Operations and Equipment to evaluate fleet investments, utilization, lifecycle cost, financing alternatives and return on capital before significant purchases are made.

Build financial reporting people can actually use.

Turn accounting information into clear P&L, margin, cash, project and KPI reporting that helps the executive team understand what is changing, why it is changing and what requires attention.

Strengthen the finance function as the company grows.

Develop the Controller and broader finance team, improve systems and processes, strengthen internal controls and build enough depth that the department does not depend on one person knowing everything.

This Is a Hands-On Finance Director Role

You will set financial strategy, work with lenders and sureties, advise the executive team and contribute to major business decisions.

But you also need to understand the accounting underneath those decisions.

There will be times when you need to review an accrual, trace an intercompany balance, understand a journal entry, work through a loan payment or help resolve a payroll or receivables issue.

You do not need to do everything yourself.

You do need to understand it well enough to know when it is right, when it is wrong and what needs to happen next.

You'll Probably Fit Here If

You have spent enough time inside project-based businesses to understand that construction finance cannot be managed entirely from financial statements.

You understand job costing, WIP, percentage-of-completion accounting, cash flow and the relationship between project execution and financial performance.

You are comfortable moving between executive-level conversations and detailed accounting questions.

You can sit with a Project Manager and challenge a forecast, work with an Equipment Manager on a capital purchase, talk bonding capacity with a surety, then explain the financial implications clearly to the executive team.

You also know how to build a finance team without creating unnecessary bureaucracy around the people trying to run the work.

Your experience includes:

A CPA designation.
10+ years of progressive finance experience, including at least 5 years in senior financial leadership.
Experience in construction, infrastructure, mining or another project-based industry.
Strong project accounting, cash flow, financing and commercial-risk knowledge.
Experience leading finance teams and working directly with banks, lenders, sureties or insurers.

Even Better If You Bring

Experience with multi-entity organizations, cross-border Canadian/U.S. operations, equipment-intensive businesses or aggregates would translate well here.

Experience with construction ERP, job-costing, budgeting and project-control systems would also be useful.

What You Can Expect From MacKay

You will have direct access to the people making operational and business decisions.

You will be expected to challenge assumptions, bring problems forward early and contribute your perspective rather than simply report results after the fact.
This is an established business with real projects, significant equipment, multiple operating entities and an experienced leadership team. At the same time, there is meaningful work still to be done in strengthening systems, reporting, accountability and the financial infrastructure required for the company's next stage.

As the business grows, so will this role. The scope, responsibilities and influence of the finance function will expand alongside the company, creating real opportunity for the right person to grow with it.

The role is based on-site in Cranbrook, British Columbia
.

The normal schedule is Monday to Friday, with additional time required around month-end, year-end, budgeting and major banking or bonding deadlines. Occasional travel to projects and meetings with financial partners will be required.

About MacKay

MacKay Contracting is a heavy civil, mining and aggregates contractor based in the Kootenays.

Since 1986, our teams have delivered challenging infrastructure, earthworks, mining and environmental projects across Western Canada. Today, MacKay continues to build its capabilities and operating footprint while staying focused on the fundamentals that built the company: practical problem-solving, accountable execution and strong people.

Our values are simple:

Be Safe Always

Unified as a TEAM

Integrity & Accountability

Lead with Innovation & Excellence

Drive Positive Impact

Interested?

If you are a finance leader who wants to be close to the business, influence real operating decisions and help build the financial platform behind a growing contractor, we'd like to hear from you.

jobs.description:
Description

University Audit Services
in VP Finance
is currently seeking a Full-time Regular Senior IT Auditor
.

Reporting to the IT Audit Manager, the Senior IT Auditor plays a key role in delivering the University's technology audit program. This position is responsible for executing and leading IT audit engagements and providing independent, objective assurance over the effectiveness of IT processes and controls.

Operating within a complex and decentralized academic environment, the Senior IT Auditor will work closely with business and IT stakeholders to identify risks and practical improvements that support organizational objectives. The successful candidate combines strong technical knowledge with business acumen to evaluate both technology and business risks, provide advisory services, and contribute to the continuous improvement of the organization's control environment.

Summary of Key Responsibilities
(job functions include but are not limited to):

Technology Audit Delivery (Primary Focus)

Lead and execute complex IT assurance engagements, from planning through reporting.
Identify and assess risks related to cybersecurity, privacy, business continuity, system implementations, and third-party providers.
Develop risk-based audit programs and test procedures to assess IT general controls, application controls, and emerging technology risks using relevant frameworks.
Evaluate the design, implementation, and operating effectiveness of controls across ERP systems, research systems, cloud platforms, and critical infrastructure.
Prepare clear, concise audit reports and present actionable solutions to Management.
Resolve complex audit issues and escalate key risks and control gaps to senior leadership in a timely manner.
Ensure audit work meets professional standards with high-quality documentation and reporting.
Build effective working relationships with IT Services, cybersecurity teams, and administrative units

Audit Planning & Risk Assessment

Support the development and ongoing refinement of the risk-based internal audit plan with a focus on technology risks and digital transformation initiatives.
Conduct IT risk assessments in emerging risk areas such as Al, cloud computing, and cybersecurity, to inform audit priorities.
Provide insights into institutional risk exposures and control maturity across IT domains.

Audit Systems, Tools & Innovation

Support administration of our audit and compliance platforms (e.g., OpsAudit and CrossComply), ensuring effective configuration, data integrity, and usability.
Maintain and enhance audit tools and systems to support efficient audit execution and stakeholder reporting.
Collaborate with IT and business to ensure alignment between audit tools, governance frameworks, and institutional systems.

Data Analytics & Continuous Monitoring

Support the IT Audit Manager in leading the development and application of data analytics to enhance audit coverage, efficiency, and insight generation.
Analyze large datasets to identify trends, anomalies, and risks, supporting both individual audits and continuous monitoring initiatives.
Enable and mentor audit staff in the use of data analytics tools and techniques.

Business Intelligence & Reporting

Support the administration of the Internal Audit Power Bl environment, including governance, data models, and reporting assets.
Design and deliver dashboards and reports that provide meaningful insights into risk, audit results, and performance metrics.
Communicate findings clearly to technical and non-technical audiences, including senior leadership.

Operational Contributions

Contribute to the continuous improvement of Internal Audit processes, methodologies, and templates.
Participate in departmental initiatives, special projects, and cross-functional work as required.

Qualifications / Requirements:

Education & Credentials

Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Information Systems, Computer Science, Information Security, Business Administration, or a related discipline.
Professional certifications such as CISA, CIA, CISSP, and/or CPA is strongly preferred.

Experience

Minimum 3-6 years of relevant experience in IT audit, Internal Audit, cybersecurity, or related areas.
Experience executing IT audits, including testing general and application controls.
Experience working in complex or decentralized environments (public sector or higher education considered an asset).

Skills & Competencies

Deep knowledge of IIA Global Internal Audit Standards (GIAS) and IT control frameworks (e.g., COBIT, NIST, ISO 27001, ITIL).
Strong understanding of cybersecurity, data governance, privacy, and digital risk management.
Expertise in IT general controls, application controls, and system implementation reviews.
Advanced analytical and problem-solving skills with experience in data analytics tools (e.g., Power BI, ACL, Python).
Strong communication skills with the ability to translate technical risk into business impact.
Proven ability to build relationships and influence stakeholders in a decentralized environment.
Collaborative team player with strong interpersonal skills.

jobs.description:
About the Role

We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients.

At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute.

To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com

What you'll be doing

Our Applied Artificial Intelligence (AI) team within Operations helps turn high-value opportunities into practical solutions that improve how work gets done across the business. As the Director, AI Delivery, you'll lead the end-to-end delivery of a growing portfolio of AI and Generative AI initiatives, from opportunity identification and prioritization through implementation, adoption, and value realization. You'll lead and develop a team of data scientists while creating the structure, operating rhythm, and accountability needed to deliver consistently in a complex enterprise environment. Working closely with Operations leaders and cross-functional partners, you'll translate business problems into clear, well-scoped initiatives with measurable outcomes. You'll also manage competing priorities across the portfolio, remove barriers to progress, and help ensure solutions are successfully embedded into business workflows. Success in this role means building a delivery organization that scales effectively, delivers predictably, and creates measurable business impact.

At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. Details on your work arrangement (proportion of on-site and remote work) will be discussed at the time of your interview.

How you'll succeed

Lead delivery excellence
- Own the end-to-end delivery of the Operations AI portfolio, from intake and prioritization through development, production, adoption, and realized value. Create clear ownership, execution discipline, and accountability across initiatives.
Build trusted business partnerships
- Partner closely with Operations leaders and teams to understand business needs, identify high-value AI opportunities, and shape a sustainable pipeline of use cases with clear outcomes and success measures.
Manage the portfolio
- Continuously assess and prioritize concurrent AI initiatives based on business value, feasibility, capacity, dependencies, and evolving insights. Make pragmatic decisions on scope, sequencing, resourcing, and delivery approach to maintain momentum.
Navigate enterprise delivery
- Drive initiatives forward with partners across data science, engineering, technology, risk, governance, and the business. Anticipate blockers and dependencies early, and work across the organization to resolve them.
Embed solutions for impact -
Ensure AI solutions don't stop at production and are effectively adopted into business workflows to achieve intended outcomes. Create transparency into delivery progress, risks, capacity, portfolio health, and business value.
Develop your team -
Lead, coach, and support a team of data scientists across multiple levels of experience. Help team members build ownership, strengthen stakeholder management, and increase delivery effectiveness over time.

Who you are

You are a caring and accountable leader
. You have experience developing and leading teams responsible for delivering complex technology or AI initiatives. You create clarity and accountability while empowering talented people to take ownership of their work.
You can demonstrate experience in
delivering Generative AI solutions in a business environment, portfolio delivery, and cross-functional execution across business and technology teams. It’s an asset if you also bring broader experience in artificial intelligence and machine learning delivery.
You give meaning to data
. You understand enough about AI and Generative AI delivery to challenge assumptions, identify delivery risks, and work effectively with data scientists and engineers. You balance technical understanding with strong business judgment.
Your influence makes a difference
. You're comfortable working directly with senior business leaders and building trusted relationships across diverse partner groups. You can challenge priorities, scope, and expectations in a constructive and effective way.
You act like an owner
. You focus on business outcomes, adoption, and value realization rather than activity alone. You make thoughtful trade-offs, know when to accelerate or reshape work, and can stop initiatives that aren't delivering enough value.
Values matter to you
. You bring your real self to work, and you live our values - trust, teamwork, and accountability.

What CIBC Offers

At CIBC, your goals are a priority. We start with your strengths and ambitions as an employee and strive to create opportunities to tap into your potential. We aspire to give you a career, rather than just a paycheck.
We work to recognize you in meaningful, personalized ways including a competitive salary, incentive pay, banking benefits, a benefits program*, defined benefit pension plan*, an employee share purchase plan, a vacation offering, wellbeing support, and MomentMakers, our social, points-based recognition program.
Our spaces and technological toolkit will make it simple to bring together great minds to create innovative solutions that make a difference for our clients.
We cultivate a culture where you can express your ambition through initiatives like Purpose Day; a paid day off dedicated for you to use to invest in your growth and development.

CIBC is committed to creating an inclusive environment where all team members and clients feel like they belong. We seek applicants with a wide range of abilities and we provide an accessible candidate experience. If you need accommodation, please contact Mailbox.careers-carrieres@cibc.com

In support of the Mission and Vision of Motor City Community Credit Union, the Chief Financial and Risk Officer (CFRO) is responsible for leading and managing the financial stewardship of the organization to ensure fiscal responsibility and maintain financial readiness. The CFRO is also responsible for the oversight of Motor City Community Credit Union’s Enterprise Risk Management regime and will be the contact person to the Board of Directors as it relates to risk.

Major Duties and Responsibilities:

Provide leadership, direction and financial/risk expertise to the organization, with responsibility for corporate finance structure, financial reporting, forecasting and business planning, risk management, setting financial policies and establishing financial targets to effectively measure success
Direct the overall forecasting, planning & analysis, accounting, budgeting, financial reporting and the overall evaluation of the business
Ensure timely and accurate financial and compliance reports for management and the Board of Directors, external auditors and regulators
Accountable for Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) practice, ensuring all programs are in compliance including capital risk management, structural risk management, market risk management and liquidity risk management
Collaborate with the senior leadership team and Board of Directors in establishing key risk indicators, tolerance levels and monitoring trends
Oversee the compliance function including anti-money laundering and all Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada ( FINTRAC) requirements
Responsible for the compliance governance function including all support for the Board, Committees and individual directors
Serve as key point of contact for the Financial Services Regulatory Authority (FSRA) relationship manager including responding to all requests
Act as the point person between the Credit Union and the Board of Directors as it relates to risk,
Develop the long-term financial forecast plan that aligns with the Credit Union’s strategic and business plans
Oversee the finance and compliance departments and provide strategic leadership and mentorship to the team
Perform other duties as assigned

Qualifications:

Bachelor’s Degree in Business or Equivalent
Accounting Designation (CPA)
10-15 years’ experience in a Financial Services environment (Credit Union experience an asset)
4-5 years of Senior Management experience
Anti-money laundering/Anti-terrorist financing experience an asset
Enterprise Risk Management facilitation considered an asset
Must be bondable

Strong knowledge of IFRS reporting standards
Strong knowledge of the Credit Union and Caisse Populaires Act, 2020
Development and/or maintenance of administrative and financial policies and procedures
Senior level oversight of AML/ATF regime
Proven ability to work closely with a Board of Directors and Regulators

Proficient in time management, written and verbal communication skills
