The Opportunity
Our client, an established and growing third-party logistics organization in the Greater Toronto Area, is looking for an experienced Director of Finance
to join its leadership team.
This is a hands-on senior finance position for someone who enjoys being close to the business. In addition to leading the accounting and finance function, the Director of Finance will work closely with operations, transportation, sales, and senior leadership to improve financial performance, strengthen reporting, and provide greater visibility into costs and profitability.
The successful candidate will bring strong financial leadership along with an understanding of the operational side of a logistics, transportation, or distribution business.

Key Responsibilities
Financial Leadership & Reporting
Lead the day-to-day accounting and finance function and provide direction to the finance team.
Oversee financial reporting, general ledger activities, accounts payable, accounts receivable, payroll, and period-end closing.
Deliver timely and accurate monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reporting.
Lead the budgeting and forecasting process and maintain ongoing cash flow projections.
Analyze business performance, operating expenses, customer profitability, and gross margins.
Provide senior leadership with meaningful financial analysis to support business decisions.
Maintain appropriate financial controls, policies, and processes.
Manage relationships with external auditors, financial institutions, tax professionals, and other external partners.

Commercial Finance & Profitability
Work closely with operational and commercial teams to understand the financial performance of customers, lanes, services, and contracts.
Provide financial oversight related to transportation costs, pricing, and margin performance.
Review costing information and identify areas where profitability can be improved.
Support pricing decisions, customer proposals, bids, and contract renewals.
Develop reporting that provides greater visibility into customer and operational profitability.
Help establish consistent processes for reviewing pricing, costs, and margins.

Business & Operational Partnership
Partner with Operations and Transportation leaders to ensure financial information accurately reflects business activity.
Provide financial guidance on operational decisions, service costs, and customer requirements.
Work with Sales on the financial components of new business opportunities and customer agreements.
Develop and monitor KPIs related to financial and operational performance.
Identify trends, risks, and opportunities and translate financial data into practical recommendations for the leadership team.

Payroll, Compliance & Risk
Provide oversight of payroll administration and related reporting requirements.
Ensure appropriate remittances, tax filings, and regulatory requirements are completed accurately and on time.
Maintain strong financial documentation and ensure the organization remains audit-ready.
Monitor areas of financial and operational risk and ensure appropriate controls are in place.

Leadership & Continuous Improvement
Coach, develop, and support members of the finance team.
Evaluate existing financial processes and identify opportunities to improve efficiency, accuracy, and reporting.
Support improvements to accounting, transportation, and business systems.
Participate in system implementations and integrations, with a focus on data integrity and effective financial reporting.
Introduce tools, reporting, and automation that provide leadership with better and faster business information.

Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, or a related discipline.
CPA designation strongly preferred.

Progressive experience in accounting and financial leadership within 3PL, transportation, logistics, distribution, or a similar operational environment
.
Strong understanding of financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, cash flow, and internal controls.
Experience analyzing costing, margins, pricing, and profitability
within an operational business.
Previous experience leading and developing a finance or accounting team.
Strong Excel skills and experience working with accounting and ERP systems.
Exposure to transportation management systems (TMS) or other logistics technology is considered an asset.
Experience supporting system implementations, integrations, or finance process improvements is an asset.
Strong analytical, leadership, and communication skills with the ability to work effectively across multiple departments.

The Ideal Candidate
You are a finance leader who wants to understand why the numbers look the way they do
, not simply report them.

You are comfortable moving between financial statements and operational conversations and can work collaboratively with Operations, Sales, and senior leadership. You understand the importance of costing and margin visibility in a high-volume logistics environment and can turn financial information into practical business decisions.

This opportunity is well suited to someone who has built their career within a 3PL, transportation, logistics, distribution, or similarly fast-paced operational business
and is looking for a role where Finance has a meaningful seat at the table.

jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Director, CRO & Analytics based in Canada.

This role leads a conversion rate optimization practice with a strong focus on data, experimentation, and behavioral science.

You will translate quantitative and qualitative insights into revenue-driving improvements across Shopify ecommerce experiences.

The position combines client strategy, analytics, statistical modeling, experimentation, personalization, and performance reporting.

You will work with DTC and omnichannel brands, partnering closely with UX, Design, Development, and other specialists.

A major focus is building reliable analytics foundations and turning funnel, cohort, and segmentation data into actionable priorities.

You will also help evolve CRO through AI-enabled experimentation and real-time personalization.

The role offers broad ownership across strategy, execution, client relationships, and the continuous improvement of CRO practices.

Accountabilities

As Director, CRO & Analytics, you will own strategic CRO engagements and the analytics backbone supporting experimentation, optimization, and measurable business outcomes.

Lead strategic CRO engagements for ecommerce brands, including discovery, ongoing retainers, and consulting initiatives.
Serve as a data-driven strategy partner across site experience, merchandising, acquisition, retention, analytics, UX, and digital product roadmaps.
Develop strategies aligned with short- and long-term business objectives using funnel and cohort analysis.
Identify optimization opportunities across the customer journey, from landing pages and product pages through checkout and post-purchase experiences.
Develop data-backed hypotheses and prioritized testing roadmaps in collaboration with UX, Design, and Development teams.
Design, execute, and analyze A/B and multivariate experiments using appropriate statistical methods, including sample size, significance, and power calculations.
Monitor test and site performance, identify data anomalies, and continuously refine recommendations.
Lead the evolution toward AI-enabled experimentation and real-time personalization using behavioral and transactional data.
Apply AI throughout the experimentation lifecycle to improve insight generation, test design, velocity, and performance analysis.
Own monthly client analytics reporting covering traffic, conversion, revenue, channel mix, and experiment results, with prioritized recommendations.
Oversee analytics implementation and data integrity, including GA4, Google Tag Manager, Shopify Customer Events and pixels, consent mode, bot and spam filtering, and reconciliation with Shopify order data.
Build automated BI dashboards that visualize conversion trends, test impact, and revenue attribution for client leadership.
Conduct funnel, cohort, segmentation, statistical, ROI, revenue growth, and customer lifetime value analyses.
Combine quantitative analysis with qualitative research such as user testing, surveys, interviews, persona development, journey mapping, and competitive or heuristic audits.
Translate complex, multi-source data into clear narratives and actionable recommendations.
Perform final quality assurance on analytics and CRO deliverables and oversee CRO contractors and vendors.
Maintain the central CRO task board and support delivery coordination.
Collaborate with UX, Design, and Technical Delivery teams across new site builds, migrations, redesigns, feature launches, optimization, and maintenance.
Contribute to internal CRO, UX, and ecommerce best practices, frameworks, and thought leadership.

Requirements

The ideal candidate is a data-first CRO leader who combines advanced ecommerce analytics and experimentation expertise with strong client leadership, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills.

Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Business, Analytics, UX, or a related field; Master’s degree is a plus, or equivalent professional experience.
Proven experience leading CRO initiatives as a data-driven practice, mentoring team members, guiding cross-functional teams, and owning client strategy from discovery through execution.
Advanced ecommerce analytics expertise with the ability to turn raw data into clear insights and prioritized, revenue-focused actions.
Hands-on experience with statistical modeling for web experimentation, including hypothesis testing, sample size calculations, significance testing, and segmentation.
Experience with A/B testing and experimentation platforms such as Intelligems, VWO, Optimizely, Shoplift, Visually, or similar tools.
Advanced hands-on proficiency with Google Analytics 4, including custom reporting, funnel analysis, and segmentation.
Experience building prioritized and resourced testing roadmaps based on quantitative impact estimates.
Experience with the Shopify platform.
Experience partnering with UX, Design, and Development teams to bring insights and experiments into execution.
Experience conducting UX analysis, usability testing, and heuristic evaluations.
Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the ability to explain data and statistical findings to both clients and internal stakeholders.
Strong organizational and attention-to-detail skills, with the ability to manage multiple client engagements in a fast-paced environment.
Prior agency experience supporting multiple brands and workstreams is preferred.
Experience with Klaviyo or other email and retention platforms is an advantage.
Understanding of paid social and paid search, including how traffic quality and acquisition data can affect experiment reliability, is preferred.
Working proficiency with BigQuery and SQL for independent, ad hoc analysis is a plus.

Benefits

Opportunity to lead a specialized CRO and analytics practice across multiple ecommerce brands.
Broad ownership spanning analytics, experimentation, AI-enabled optimization, client strategy, and business impact.
Exposure to DTC and omnichannel ecommerce environments and complex Shopify experiences.
Collaboration with UX, Design, Development, and Technical Delivery specialists.
Opportunity to work with modern analytics, experimentation, BI, and AI-driven optimization tools.

Overview

At KPMG in Canada, our people bring their unique perspectives to Canada’s most important challenges. Here, you can build momentum that reaches beyond our business, develop skills for the future, and take ownership of your career with support at every stage. Join a firm where your career can make a difference.

KPMG Corporate Finance Inc. is the Ontario Securities Commission (OSC)-regulated entity through which KPMG LLP provides investment banking services in Canada. KPMG Corporate Finance services are principally comprised of merger, acquisition and divestiture services and financing services, including raising debt and equity capital. We offer independent financial advisory and investment banking services to both private and public companies.

With over 100 professionals across Canada and a global network of 3,000+ bankers in 160 offices, we combine local execution expertise with global reach. KPMG Corporate Finance is consistently ranked the #1 mid-market investment bank in Canada.

Our growing diversified investment banking team is seeking an Associate Vice President (Manager) to join our team in Calgary, Edmonton or Winnipeg to play a key role across all aspects of transaction delivery.

What You Will Do

Assume responsibility for the day-to-day execution and delivery of service on a range of corporate finance projects.
Draft pitch books, teasers, confidential information memorandums (CIM) and other transaction process documentation.
Manage, mentor and train junior corporate finance professionals (Analysts & Associates).
Prepare and review various forms of financial analysis, including complex financial models.
Conduct market and industry research, detailed financial analysis and business valuations.
Assist in the identification of potential acquisition targets, purchasers and/or investors.
Undertake engagement and practice management responsibilities, including billings and adherence to professional practice requirements.
Lead proactive business development and deal initiation activities.

This role provides significant learning opportunities and increasing responsibility over time. At times, business needs arise, and employees are required and agree to work beyond their normal workday or work week to fulfill the accountabilities required for their job. Likewise, employees need time to devote to personal matters, and our approach to flexibility provides for this.

An undergraduate degree in finance, commerce, business, accounting, economics or other related field.
4-6 years of relevant post-graduate experience, in Corporate Finance, or a related field e.g. transaction advisory, investment banking, private equity, or corporate development.
Proven track record of M&A transaction initiation/execution in a fast-paced professional setting – as exhibited by your deal credential list which should accompany your cover letter.
CPA, CBV or CFA designations are all considered assets.
Strong technical finance proficiency, including knowledge of financial statements and general accounting principles.
Demonstrated experience or ability in training and developing junior staff members.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills (English).

Support for candidates enrolled in professionally accredited designation programs (CPA, CBV, CFA, etc.) including paid enrollment costs, paid study / exam days, ongoing coaching and third-party courses / materials for exam preparation.
Meaningful roles on a variety of Corporate Finance assignments for some of Canada’s premier companies, with support and coaching from senior Corporate Finance executives that promote professional growth and development.
Assignment of a Performance Manager on day one to help guide and grow your career as a Corporate Finance professional.
Deal Advisory team events throughout the year to help build a strong team culture.
Modern office space in our recently renovated downtown offices in Calgary, Edmonton and Winnipeg.

The Director of CRO leads ehouse's conversion optimization practice as a data analyst and behavioral scientist first, translating quantitative signals into revenue-driving changes across client Shopify experiences. This role owns the analytics backbone of experimentation, statistical modeling, segmentation, and reporting and converts that data into testing hypotheses, prioritized roadmaps, and measurable outcomes for DTC and omnichannel brands.

The ideal candidate treats every optimization decision as a data question: what the funnel and cohort data show, whether a result is statistically significant, and what segment-level analysis recommends next. Design, execute, and analyze A/B and multivariate tests, applying appropriate statistical methods (sample size, significance, power) to translate results into prioritized recommendations

Lead the evolution of CRO from traditional A/B testing to AI-enabled experimentation and real-time personalization, grounded in behavioral and transactional data

Own analytics implementation and data integrity: GA4 and Google Tag Manager configuration, Shopify Customer Events and pixels, consent mode, bot and spam filtering, and regular reconciliation of analytics data against Shopify orders.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Risk Data Strategy
jobs.description:
We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients.

At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute.

To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com

What You'll Be Doing

The Risk Data Management Office plays an important role in enabling strong risk management through trusted data, modern architecture, and effective governance. As Senior Director, Risk Data Strategy, you'll lead the vision, design, and delivery of a large, complex, multi-year transformation of CIBC's risk data ecosystem to deliver measurable improvements in decision-making, data quality, scalability, efficiency, and user experience across the bank. You'll develop and execute the short-, medium-, and long-term strategy for risk data architecture, aligning risk management priorities with enterprise business, data, and technology capabilities. In this leadership role, you'll drive modernization across cloud architecture, data governance, integration, reporting, automation, and advanced analytics, while helping strengthen regulatory readiness and enterprise alignment. You'll work closely with senior leaders across Risk Management, Technology, Finance, Compliance, and Operations to translate complex priorities into a clear roadmap, mobilize cross-functional teams, and deliver sustainable business outcomes. You'll also lead and develop a high-performing team, fostering a culture of collaboration, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement.

At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. You’ll have the flexibility to manage your work activities within a hybrid work arrangement where you’ll spend 2-3 days per week on-site, while other days will be remote.

How You'll Succeed

Lead strategic direction - Develop and execute Risk's data architecture strategy, ensuring alignment with CIBC's business priorities, enterprise data strategy, and risk management framework.
Strengthen data, data governance, and reporting - Oversee initiatives that improve risk data aggregation, governance, lineage, controls, and reporting. Apply a practical understanding of BCBS 239 and Enterprise data governance requirements to ensure the target state supports reliable capital and risk reporting while also creating broader business value.
Drive technology and cloud architecture modernization - Lead the assessment, design, and evolution of risk data architecture, including data modelling, data warehousing, pipelines, cloud platforms, integration patterns, security, resiliency, and data controls. Bring sufficient technology depth to partner with engineering and architecture teams, and ensure solutions are scalable, sustainable, and aligned with enterprise standards.
Advance innovation - Identify opportunities to streamline and automate manual processes and evaluate the use of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and advanced analytics to enhance risk data capabilities and decision-making.
Deliver a large, complex, multi-year transformation - Own end-to-end program delivery, from strategy and investment case through roadmap, execution, adoption, and benefits realization. Establish clear outcomes, milestones, governance, dependencies, resource plans, and delivery controls; proactively resolve risks and trade-offs; and maintain accountability across multiple workstreams and senior stakeholders. Success will be measured by tangible business value and sustainable capability improvements, not only by regulatory compliance.
Build strong partnerships - Collaborate with leaders across Risk, Finance, Compliance, Operations, Technology, Internal Audit, and enterprise data functions to align priorities, support governance, and advance strategic initiatives.

Who You Are

You're an experienced people leader. You have a strong track record of leading and developing high-performing, multi-functional teams. You know how to create clarity, build capability, and foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
You bring deep technology and risk data architecture expertise. You have technology experience and a strong command of modern data architecture, including cloud architecture, data platforms, integration, data modelling, security, resiliency, and controls. You can engage credibly with architects and engineers, connect technology choices to business outcomes, and guide the design of scalable, resilient, and well-governed solutions within a complex financial institution.
You are a proven transformation and program delivery leader. You have successfully delivered large, complex, multi-year programs spanning business and technology, with multiple workstreams, significant dependencies, and senior stakeholder visibility.
You understand OSFI CAR and BCBS 239 requirements. You bring a practical understanding of OSFI's Capital Adequacy Requirements guidelines, BCBS 239 principles, and the data, governance, aggregation, lineage, control, and reporting capabilities required to support them. You can translate regulatory expectations into pragmatic design and delivery decisions without losing focus on the broader business value of the transformation.
You are an exceptional and influential communicator. You communicate complex business, technology, architecture, and regulatory concepts with clarity and confidence across technical teams, business leaders, senior executives, governance committees, and Board-level stakeholders. You create alignment, make decisions and trade-offs transparent, tailor messages to the audience, and use compelling written and verbal communication to sustain momentum through a multi-year transformation.
Values matter to you. You bring your real self to work, and you live our values - trust, teamwork, and accountability.

What CIBC Offers

At CIBC, your goals are a priority. We start with your strengths and ambitions as an employee and strive to create opportunities to tap into your potential. We aspire to give you a career, rather than just a paycheck.

We work to recognize you in meaningful, personalized ways including a competitive salary, incentive pay, banking benefits, a benefits program*, defined benefit pension plan*, an employee share purchase plan, a vacation offering, wellbeing support, and MomentMakers, our social, points-based recognition program.
Our spaces and technological toolkit will make it simple to bring together great minds to create innovative solutions that make a difference for our clients.
We cultivate a culture where you can express your ambition through initiatives like Purpose Day; a paid day off dedicated for you to use to invest in your growth and development.
Subject to plan and program terms and conditions

What You Need To Know

CIBC is committed to creating an inclusive environment where all team members and clients feel like they belong. We seek applicants with a wide range of abilities and we provide an accessible candidate experience. If you need accommodation, please contact Mailbox.careers-carrieres@cibc.com

The market leader. The premier provider. The best in the business. As a product-focused lead within the Data Transformation Office, you will partner with the Transformation Office leadership team to bring structure, governance, and product thinking to our API platform initiative. Drawing on your project governance background and hands-on analytics exposure, you will translate high-level business needs into a clear product roadmap, user stories, and delivery milestones. You will help shape how our APIs are designed, consumed, and evolved — turning a technical asset into a well-managed product that internal teams and clients can depend on.

Contribute to the API product vision and align the roadmap to strategic goals
Establish and maintain governance structures (intake, prioritization, change control, versioning) for the API portfolio
Create and maintain extensive documentation — including API catalogs, consumer guides, and decision logs — to enable self-service knowledge dissemination
Identify opportunities to improve processes and generate new product ideas informed by analytics and usage patterns
Work with the Product Owner and stakeholders to prioritize enhancements and manage the backlog
Anticipate, identify, manage and mitigate risks and cross-project dependencies
Manage expectations of senior management and stakeholders, facilitate steering committees, and provide regular status reports
Help to break down organizational silos and promote collaboration between business, engineering, and operations
Ensure quality of work being delivered by being involved in testing efforts, including API contract and UAT validation
Through partnership with the business, define, sponsor and steer API product initiatives
Influence and guide technology, project management, and operations teams in solution delivery
Translate light-touch data analysis (SQL, basic scripting) into product hypotheses and feature ideas
Maintain and develop expertise and keep abreast of market trends, API standards, and competitor offerings
Collaborate with other product teams on prioritization, reuse of endpoints, and shared components
Define success metrics (adoption, latency, error rates, consumer satisfaction) and use them to steer the roadmap
Work with Platform and Application teams to design API solutions in alignment with our business objectives

Qualifications

About You

5+ years hands-on experience in project/program governance, product ownership, and documentation
Working knowledge of SQL and/or basic scripting/analytics tools (e.g., Excel, Power Query, or Python fundamentals)
Experience with Power BI, Qlik, or similar reporting/visualization tools is an advantage
Collaborates effectively with individuals of varying technical ability and business acumen
Learns quickly and thrives in a fast moving, dynamic atmosphere
Strong project governance skills — intake processes, prioritization frameworks, risk/change control — with attention to detail and proven ability to multi-task
Strong knowledge of Atlassian products (Jira, Confluence)
PMP, Certified Scrum Master, or Certified Scrum Product Owner a plus
Skills in negotiation, influencing, stakeholder management
Track record of organizing and structuring technical initiatives (e.g., API programs) from a product/governance perspective
Strong written and verbal communication skills
Strong visual communication skills (PowerPoint, Visio, Smart Sheets)

We provide a range of benefits, training and education support, and flexible working arrangements to help you achieve success in your career while balancing personal needs. The Group focuses on management and origination of banking relationships within the Financial Services sector, with a focus on senior debt financing opportunities with non-regulated lenders or long-term lessors as well as full banking relationships with specific financial services sub-sectors.  The team assesses financing opportunities representing $10MM or more, both on a syndicated and bilateral basis, for both private and public companies in Canada. The Group is based in Toronto and has national coverage in the sector.

 Job Overview   
 The Director will join the FSG team that is responsible for senior secured loan origination and account management of a growing portfolio of clients. The Director will have direct portfolio management responsibilities of an existing portfolio comprised of lending relationships with complex credit structures and important cash management needs. This includes making credit approval recommendations and working collaboratively with various Corporate Finance representatives to best serve and manage these existing client relationships as well as grow the portfolio by adding new relationships.  

 Job Description   
 The selected candidate:  
 Manages the risk of the assigned complex portfolio in a timely and precise manner.  
 Acts as daily sales contact for clients on sales related questions such as product information, pricing, implementation timeframes and requirements.  
 Directly manages the annual review process, interim reviews, specified quarterly reports and resolution of exceptions.  
 Assists team in pre-sales activities such as pitch preparation, client research, preparation of prospect and client files for further action.  
 Assists with sales and service administration and processing to ensure client experience is seamless and opportunities are identified and met.  
 Gathers data to advance sale process and completes all required documentation.  
 Manages transaction requests to keep the process on track with timelines.  
 Tracks internal reports and recommends improvements to sales support materials based on findings and feedback.  
 Maintains accurate documentation and ensure adherence to prescribed policies and procedures and overall safety of the Bank’s position.  
 Maintains current client information on Bank system/files to ensure client history is accurate and complete.  
 Applies expertise and thinks creatively to address unique or ambiguous situations and to find solutions to problems that can be complex and non-routine.  
 Broader work or accountabilities may be assigned as needed.  

 Qualifications:   
 Typically, 10+ years of relevant experience and post-secondary degree in related field of study or an equivalent combination of education and experience. An MBA, CPA, CFA or other relevant professional designation or advanced/graduate degree, ongoing or completed, is an asset.  
 Credit Qualifications and associated credit knowledge and skills according to the established qualification standards  
 Demonstrated knowledge of relevant industry verticals and market’s competitive environment  
 Experience in contract negotiations with both clients and legal counsel  
 Computer literacy and technical skills as it relates to basic Microsoft Office applications (Excel, Word, PowerPoint) – In-depth / Expert  
 Relationship Management - In-depth / Expert  
 Collaboration & team skills; with a focus on cross-group collaboration - In-depth / Expert  
 Verbal & written communication skills - In-depth / Expert  
 Financial and Working Capital Understanding – In-depth / Expert  
 Analytical and problem-solving skills - In-depth / Expert  
 Data driven decision making - In-depth / Expert  
 Risk Management - In-depth  
 Sales and Service Management –In-depth  
 Business Acumen – In-depth

$85,500.00 - $185,000.00

Salaried

jobs.title: Directeur(trice) principal(e) de l’architecture de solutions/Senior Director, Solution Architecture
jobs.description:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

 What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

 Directeur(trice) principal(e) de l’architecture de solutions/Senior Director, Solution Architecture

 À propos du poste

 McKesson recherche un(e) Directeur(trice) Principal(e), Architecture d’Entreprise et Expérience Numérique pour diriger la stratégie d’architecture couvrant l’architecture de solutions, l’architecture applicative, la modernisation des solutions héritées (legacy) et la gestion de l’expérience numérique. Ce leader définira la vision de solutions technologiques modernes, évolutives, sécurisées et centrées sur le client afin de soutenir les priorités de l’entreprise et d’améliorer les résultats opérationnels.
 Dans ce rôle, vous dirigerez les pratiques d’architecture qui relient la stratégie d’affaires à l’exécution technologique. Vous collaborerez avec les dirigeants, les équipes produits, ingénierie, sécurité, opérations et les parties prenantes métier afin de moderniser les plateformes, simplifier les environnements hérités, orienter la stratégie d’expérience numérique et renforcer la gouvernance architecturale. Vous développerez également les talents, influencerez les décisions à l’échelle de l’entreprise et aiderez les équipes à livrer des solutions technologiques à fort impact dans un environnement complexe et réglementé.

 Ce que vous ferez
 Diriger la pratique d’architecture d’entreprise couvrant l’architecture de solutions, l’architecture applicative, la modernisation et la gestion de l’expérience numérique.
 Définir les normes d’architecture, les feuilles de route, les modèles de gouvernance et les cadres décisionnels permettant une livraison technologique sécurisée et évolutive.
 Collaborer avec les dirigeants et les responsables métier afin d’aligner la stratégie d’architecture sur les objectifs d’affaires, les besoins des clients et les priorités de l’entreprise.
 Diriger les stratégies de modernisation des applications et plateformes héritées, y compris la rationalisation applicative, la migration vers le cloud, l’intégration, l’automatisation et la réduction de la dette technique.
 Orienter l’architecture de l’expérience numérique afin d’améliorer l’utilisabilité, l’accessibilité, la performance, la fiabilité ainsi que les parcours clients et employés de bout en bout.
 Conseiller les équipes sur les modèles d’architecture modernes, notamment les API, les microservices, les plateformes cloud natives, l’intégration de données, la gestion des identités, la sécurité et l’observabilité.
 Superviser la planification du portefeuille d’architecture, la stratégie fournisseurs, les recommandations d’investissement et la création de valeur mesurable.
 Développer les responsables et les équipes d’architecture grâce au mentorat, à la gestion des talents, à l’évaluation de la performance et à un leadership inclusif.

 Exigences de base
 13 ans ou plus d’expérience professionnelle en technologie, dont au moins 6 ans dans des fonctions de leadership en architecture, ingénierie, livraison d’applications, plateformes numériques ou transformation technologique. 
 Diplôme universitaire en informatique, systèmes d’information, ingénierie ou domaine connexe, ou expérience équivalente.
 Expérience dans la direction d’architectures d’entreprise, de solutions ou applicatives dans des environnements technologiques de grande envergure.
 Expérience de la conception et de la modernisation d’architectures de solutions d’entreprise en s’appuyant sur des plateformes intégrant l’intelligence artificielle et des technologies émergentes afin de stimuler l’innovation, l’évolutivité et la création de valeur.
 Expérience dans l’élaboration de stratégies d’architecture, de feuilles de route, de normes, de modèles de gouvernance et de recommandations destinées aux dirigeants.
 Expérience dans la modernisation d’applications, de plateformes ou de capacités numériques héritées.
 Expérience en gestion de responsables, d’équipes d’architecture ou d’équipes technologiques multidisciplinaires.
 Expérience de collaboration avec des parties prenantes métier et technologiques de haut niveau pour influencer la stratégie et l’exécution.
 Expérience en planification budgétaire, gestion des fournisseurs, priorisation de portefeuille ou prise de décisions d’investissement technologique.

 Compétences et expériences privilégiées
 Expérience avec les plateformes cloud, les stratégies API, les microservices, l’architecture événementielle (event-driven), le DevSecOps ou l’ingénierie de plateformes.
 Expérience en gestion de l’expérience numérique, plateformes d’expérience client, portails, applications mobiles/web ou solutions omnicanales.
 Expérience dans les secteurs de la santé, de la distribution pharmaceutique, de la chaîne d’approvisionnement, du commerce de détail ou d’autres environnements d’entreprise réglementés.
 Expérience des cadres d’architecture d’entreprise, des comités de revue d’architecture, de la modélisation des capacités ou de la gestion de portefeuille applicatif.
 Expérience de direction de programmes de transformation à grande échelle impliquant plusieurs équipes, fonctions ou unités d’affaires.
 Excellentes compétences en communication avec les dirigeants et capacité à simplifier des décisions technologiques complexes pour des audiences métier.
 Capacité démontrée à améliorer la performance opérationnelle, réduire la dette technique et accélérer la mise sur le marché.
 Style de leadership axé sur la collaboration, la vision stratégique, la conduite du changement, l’orientation client et le développement des talents.

 Déplacements, présence au bureau et exigences physiques
 Le modèle de travail peut être à distance, hybride ou en présentiel selon les besoins de l’entreprise et de l’équipe.
 Des déplacements occasionnels peuvent être requis pour des réunions de leadership, des sessions de planification, des rencontres avec des fournisseurs ou des activités de collaboration d’équipe.
 Le poste requiert une utilisation régulière de l’ordinateur ainsi qu’une participation à des réunions virtuelles et en personne.

 About the Role 
 McKesson is seeking a Senior Director, Enterprise Architecture & Digital Experience to lead architecture strategy across solution architecture, application architecture, legacy solution modernization, and digital experience management. This leader will set the vision for modern, scalable, secure, and customer-centered technology solutions that support enterprise priorities and improve business outcomes.
 In this role, you will lead architecture practices that connect business strategy to technology execution. You will partner with senior leaders, product, engineering, security, operations, and business stakeholders to modernize platforms, simplify legacy environments, guide digital experience strategy, and strengthen architecture governance. You will also develop leaders, influence enterprise decisions, and help teams deliver high-impact technology solutions in a complex, regulated environment.

 What You’ll Do 
 Lead the enterprise architecture practice across solution architecture, application architecture, modernization, and digital experience management.
 Define architecture standards, roadmaps, governance models, and decision frameworks that enable scalable and secure technology delivery.
 Partner with executive and senior business leaders to align architecture strategy with business objectives, customer needs, and enterprise priorities.
 Lead legacy application and platform modernization strategies, including rationalization, cloud migration, integration, automation, and technical debt reduction.
 Guide digital experience architecture to improve usability, accessibility, performance, reliability, and end-to-end customer and employee journeys.
 Advise teams on modern architecture patterns, including APIs, microservices, cloud-native platforms, data integration, identity, security, and observability.
 Oversee architecture portfolio planning, vendor strategy, investment recommendations, and measurable value delivery.
 Build and develop architecture leaders and teams through coaching, talent planning, performance management, and inclusive leadership practices.

 Basic Requirements 
 13+ years of professional technology experience, including 6+ years of leadership experience in architecture, engineering, application delivery, digital platforms, or technology transformation. 
 Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or related field, or equivalent experience.
 Experience leading enterprise, solution, or application architecture across large-scale technology environments.
 Lead the design and modernization of enterprise solution architectures, leveraging AI-enabled platforms and emerging technologies to drive innovation, scalability, and business value.
 Experience developing architecture strategy, roadmaps, standards, governance, and executive-level recommendations.
 Experience leading modernization of legacy applications, platforms, or digital capabilities.
 Experience managing leaders, architecture teams, or cross-functional technology teams.
 Experience partnering with senior business and technology stakeholders to influence strategy and delivery.
 Experience with budget planning, vendor management, portfolio prioritization, or technology investment decisions.

 Preferred Skills/Experience 
 Experience with cloud platforms, API strategy, microservices, event-driven architecture, DevSecOps, or platform engineering.
 Experience with digital experience management, customer experience platforms, portals, mobile/web applications, or omnichannel solutions.
 Experience in healthcare, pharmaceutical distribution, supply chain, retail, or other regulated enterprise environments.
 Experience with enterprise architecture frameworks, architecture review boards, capability modeling, or application portfolio management.
 Experience leading large-scale transformation programs across multiple teams, functions, or business units.
 Strong executive communication skills with the ability to simplify complex technology decisions for business audiences.
 Demonstrated ability to improve operational performance, reduce technical debt, and increase speed-to-market.
 Leadership approach aligned to collaboration, strategic insight, change leadership, customer focus, and talent development.

 Description of Travel or In-Office and Physical Requirements 
 Work model may be remote, hybrid, or office-based depending on business and team needs.
 Occasional travel may be required for leadership meetings, planning sessions, vendor engagements, or team collaboration.
 Role requires regular use of a computer and participation in virtual and in-person meetings.

 We are proud to offer a competitive compensation package at McKesson as part of our Total Rewards. This is determined by several factors, including performance, experience and skills, equity, regular job market evaluations, and geographical markets. The pay range shown below is aligned with McKesson's pay philosophy, and pay will always be compliant with any applicable regulations. In addition to base pay, other compensation, such as an annual bonus or long-term incentive opportunities may be offered. For more information regarding benefits at McKesson, please  click here.

jobs.description:
We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients.

At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute.

To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com

What You'll Be Doing

As Director, Strategy & Reporting for the Enterprise Anti-Money Laundering (EAML) team, you'll play a pivotal role in shaping and advancing the division's strategic priorities. Reporting to the VP, Strategy, Governance & Advisory, you'll collaborate with senior leaders to define the purpose, vision, and core strategy for EAML, while implementing frameworks to track progress against divisional goals. You'll oversee the development and production of senior executive and board reporting for the AML/Anti-Terrorist Financing (ATF) Program, ensuring accuracy, completeness, and timely delivery. Your strategic insights will help optimize operational capacity and workforce planning, and you'll lead a team dedicated to maintaining high standards in reporting and governance. Building strong relationships across CIBC, you'll be a key connector between EAML and partner departments, supporting compliance and driving continuous improvement.

At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. You'll have the flexibility to manage your work activities within a hybrid work arrangement where you'll spend 1-3 days per week on-site, while other days will be remote.

How You'll Succeed

Strategic Planning & Execution – Collaborate with senior leadership to define EAML priorities, develop strategic roadmaps, and monitor progress against objectives, providing updates and identifying areas for improvement.
Reporting & Metrics Management – Lead the team responsible for producing monthly, quarterly, and annual reports for Boards, Committees, and senior executives; ensure data accuracy, consistency, and visually clear presentation.
Capacity Planning & Forecasting – Analyze operational workflows and resource allocation, present insights to inform workforce planning, and continuously refine forecasting models to align with evolving business needs.
Governance & Compliance – Build and maintain governance frameworks for EAML metrics, manage access to reports, and ensure compliance with CIBC policies and controls.
Team Leadership & Development – Provide effective management and mentorship to staff, set context for assignments, build team capabilities through development opportunities, and foster a positive, inclusive work environment.
Cross-Functional Collaboration – Establish and nurture strong relationships with key internal partners across Risk Management, Finance, Internal Audit, Human Resources, Chief Administration Office, and Corporate Secretary.

Who You Are

You have expertise in AML, Compliance, or Risk Management. Your experience enables you to navigate complex regulatory environments and contribute to strategic planning.
You're a strategic thinker. You bring a university degree and a strong understanding of value creation, options analysis, and business performance metrics.
You're an analytical problem solver. Your excellent analytical skills support data interpretation, risk management, and informed decision-making.
You're a skilled communicator. You have exceptional written and presentation skills, and can clearly document and convey complex concepts to diverse audiences, including senior executives and board members.
You're an effective team leader. You have proven experience managing high-performing teams, providing mentorship, and aligning individual roles with business priorities.
You're highly organized and detail-oriented. You consistently deliver accurate and comprehensive reports, maintaining strong attention to detail.
You value collaboration and influence. You build strong relationships across departments and can influence outcomes to support divisional goals.
Values matter to you. You bring your real self to work, and you live our values - trust, teamwork, and accountability.

What CIBC Offers

At CIBC, your goals are a priority. We start with your strengths and ambitions as an employee and strive to create opportunities to tap into your potential. We aspire to give you a career, rather than just a paycheck.

We work to recognize you in meaningful, personalized ways including a competitive salary, incentive pay, banking benefits, a benefits program*, defined benefit pension plan*, an employee share purchase plan, a vacation offering, wellbeing support, and MomentMakers, our social, points-based recognition program.
Our spaces and technological toolkit will make it simple to bring together great minds to create innovative solutions that make a difference for our clients.
We cultivate a culture where you can express your ambition through initiatives like Purpose Day; a paid day off dedicated for you to use to invest in your growth and development.

We use artificial intelligence tools during the recruitment process. Our goal for the application process is to get to know more about you, all that you have to offer, and give you the opportunity to learn more about us.

What We’re Looking For:

As the Director, AI Operations, you will be the operational force behind the scaling and integration of Artificial Intelligence across Omnicom’s Canadian portfolio Reporting directly to the Head of AI, Omnicom Advertising Canada, you will bridge the gap between cutting-edge technical innovation and real-world agency execution.

What You’ll Do:

Operational Scaling
: Working the VP, Agency Operations, implement standardized frameworks for AI deployment across departments to ensure consistency, efficiency, and compliance.
Workflow Integration
: Audit existing agency workflows to identify AI-ready touchpoints, deploying use cases that reduce manual overhead and elevate human creativity.
Infrastructure Management
: Oversee the operational health of AI platforms, ensuring seamless access to the Omnicom AI ecosystem and approved third-party tools.
Performance Tracking
: Define and track key metrics (i.e. ROI, time-savings, output volume) to quantify the impact of AI initiatives on agency growth.
Innovation Pipeline
: Proactively scout for emerging AI tools and lead rapid Proof of Concept experiments to test agency applications before scaling.
Onboarding & Approvals
: Navigate end-to-end the internal vetting process for new AI tools.
AI workflows
: Shape the workflows and internal experience with
Node-based tools (n8n, Figma Weave, Magnific).

What You Bring:

7+ years of experience in operations, project management, program management, account leadership, innovation, digital transformation, or a related field.
Experience working in an advertising, marketing, creative, media, technology, or agency environment strongly preferred.
Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional projects from strategy through implementation.
Experience managing multiple workstreams, timelines, priorities, and stakeholders in a fast-paced environment.
Strong understanding of AI technologies, platforms, tools, and emerging capabilities, with a genuine interest in how AI is transforming the creative and marketing landscape.
Practical experience using or implementing generative AI tools and platforms such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, Adobe Firefly, or similar tools.
Experience identifying opportunities to improve workflows, automate processes, increase efficiency, and enhance team capabilities through technology.
Experience working with senior leadership and influencing stakeholders across multiple disciplines.
Demonstrated ability to translate complex technology concepts into clear, actionable recommendations for non-technical audiences.
Experience developing processes, frameworks, playbooks, guidelines, or operating models that help teams adopt new tools and ways of working.
Comfortable working in an environment where technology, platforms, and best practices are constantly evolving.

Who We Are:

TBWA is The Disruption® Company, a global agency collective of 10,000+ creative minds operating in over 80 countries. Named one of the World's Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company four years in a row, we are a disruptive brand experience company that uses creativity to help businesses acquire a greater share of the future.
We believe in doing the brave thing.

Doing the brave thing
is about courage. It’s about never being a spectator. Speaking up with clarity and conviction and kindness. Not hedging our points-of-view with clients or each other. Saying what we think when it’s in the best interest of the idea or the people, even if it’s uncomfortable. Being willing to take smart risks. Making tough decisions without agonizing. And, being transparent and vulnerable in search of the best. This is the expectation for all of us. In turn, we commit to perpetuating a culture where bravery is rewarded and support is always within reach. TBWA\Canada develops strategies, advertising and brand experiences for some of the world's most iconic brands, with offices in Toronto, Edmonton and Montreal.

The Company:

At TBWA\Canada, Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging (DEIB) are our core values. We are committed to a diverse workforce and aim to maintain an inclusive and equitable workplace where employees feel valued, respected, and supported. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and lived experiences. If you require an accommodation during the recruitment process, please contact our Human Resources team and we would be happy to work with you to meet your needs.

The salary range for this position is $100,000 - $120,000 per year. Compensation will be determined based on qualifications, relevant experience, and internal equity. This posting represents an active vacancy that we are currently hiring for.

These tools assist our recruitment team but will never replace the human judgement that guides our hiring decisions. We will only contact shortlisted candidates for this role.

Job Description

Area Vice President, AI Data Platform – Canada Enterprise

Come and Join Us!

Oracle is seeking a strategic, customer-focused Area Vice President, AI Data Platform – Canada Enterprise to lead our AI Data Platform business across Canada.

This executive leadership role will have responsibility for Oracle's AI Data Platform business across all Commercial and Enterprise customer segments and industry verticals throughout Canada, helping organizations modernize their technology environments, accelerate AI adoption, unlock the value of their data, and transform mission-critical workloads.

Leading a national organization of Sales and partnering with Sales Engineering professionals, you will develop and execute the go-to-market strategy for Oracle's AI Data Platform portfolio across Canada. You will be responsible for building a high-performance culture, developing exceptional talent, driving predictable growth, and strengthening Oracle's position as a strategic technology partner to Canada's leading organizations.

Working closely across Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), Applications, Consulting, Customer Success, Product, Marketing, and Alliances, you will bring together the full power of Oracle to help Canadian customers accelerate transformation through AI, data, cloud, and multicloud innovation.

What You'll Do

Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing national organization of Sales and Sales Engineering leaders and professionals responsible for Oracle's AI Data Platform business across Canada.
Own and execute the Canada Enterprise go-to-market strategy across Commercial and Enterprise customers spanning all major industry verticals, including Telecommunications, Media, Technology, Retail, Manufacturing, Transportation, Energy, Professional Services, and other strategic industries.
Drive consistent execution against bookings, cloud consumption, pipeline, revenue, market growth, and customer success objectives while establishing a culture of accountability and predictable performance.
Help Canada's leading organizations modernize legacy technology environments, consolidate and simplify data platforms, migrate mission-critical workloads, and accelerate the adoption of AI and next-generation data architectures.
Champion Oracle's multicloud strategy, helping customers take advantage of Oracle technology across OCI and Oracle's strategic partnerships with Microsoft Azure, Amazon Web Services (AWS), and Google Cloud.
Build trusted relationships with CEOs, CIOs, CTOs, CDOs, CISOs, business executives, and other senior decision-makers, positioning Oracle as a strategic partner for their most important technology and business transformation initiatives.
Lead strategic account planning, executive engagement, pipeline development, forecasting, territory strategy, and business reviews to create disciplined execution and sustainable growth across the Canadian market.
Partner closely with OCI, Applications, Consulting, Customer Success, Product, Marketing, Alliances, and other Oracle organizations to deliver a unified strategy for customers and maximize opportunities across Oracle's portfolio.
Develop and expand strategic relationships with Global Systems Integrators (GSIs), Independent Software Vendors (ISVs), cloud providers, and technology ecosystem partners to increase market reach and accelerate customer adoption.
Build a strong partnership between Sales and Sales Engineering, ensuring technical strategy, customer value, executive engagement, and commercial execution are tightly aligned throughout the customer lifecycle.
Recruit, develop, retain, and inspire exceptional talent while creating a culture centered on customer success, collaboration, innovation, accountability, and high performance.
Represent Oracle at executive customer engagements, industry forums, conferences, partner events, and strategic engagements while serving as executive sponsor for some of Oracle's most important Canadian customers.

What You'll Bring

jobs.title: Vice President, Strategy & Innovation
jobs.description:
HSB Canada, part of Munich Re, is Canada's premier engineering-driven specialty insurer and provider of inspection, engineering and technology services that set the standard for excellence in the market. Our constantly evolving offerings lead the market in cyber, equipment breakdown, renewable energy, technology services, engineering based risk management and inspection services. We bring technical expertise to help our clients stay ahead of complex, emerging, and technology-based risks. We dare to think big, and we are continuously innovating on behalf of our clients. We recognize Diversity, Inclusion, and Belonging as key priorities and a culture that welcomes different thoughts and opinions.

HSB is much more! It’s insurance. Engineering. Technology. To learn more about us, please visit www.hsb.ca (opens in new window)

Primary Objectives

HSB Canada is seeking a Vice President, Strategy & Innovation to help shape the company's long-term direction and turn strategic ambition into measurable business results. Reporting directly to the President & CEO and serving as a member of the Executive Leadership Team, this leader will bring quantitative rigor to enterprise strategy, strengthen execution discipline, and build a focused portfolio of innovation opportunities that create customer and business value.

Operating as an internal strategy and innovation consultant, the Vice President will work across business units and functions to frame complex issues, synthesize data and market insight, challenge assumptions, align senior stakeholders, and mobilize cross-functional teams. The role will also refresh HSB Canada's Internet of Things (IoT) strategy and go-to-market approach, strengthening the connection between technology-enabled services, insurance solutions, distribution opportunities, and customer needs.

The successful candidate will build strong cross-functional partnerships with HSB and Munich Re Group business leaders and enterprise partners to align priorities, remove barriers, and accelerate priorities ensuring understanding of relevant strategy, standards and philosophy.

Internal Applicants please apply online and submit your candidacy by October 14, 2026.

External Applicants please apply online and submit your candidacy by October 31,2026.

Job Responsibilities

Enterprise Strategy and Strategic Planning
Lead enterprise strategic planning with the President & CEO and Executive Leadership Team, including strategy refreshes, scenarios, priorities, and roadmaps.
Shape evidence-based choices on growth, portfolio priorities, partnerships, investments, and emerging risks.
Translate strategy into measurable objectives, initiatives, milestones, accountabilities, and resource priorities.
Advise and challenge senior leaders, and develop clear Board materials on choices, trade-offs, progress, and decisions.
Business Performance and Execution Discipline
Co-lead quarterly business reviews with FP&A, linking strategic priorities to financial and operating performance.
Hold business leaders accountable for commitments, indicators, dependencies, corrective actions, and outcomes.
Establish practical execution disciplines, including scorecards, governance, benefits tracking, and escalation.
Use quantitative analysis to identify gaps, size opportunities, evaluate trade-offs, and recommend action, while respecting FP&A ownership of core financial processes.
Innovation Portfolio and Commercialization
Build and manage an innovation portfolio aligned with strategy, customer needs, financial goals, risk appetite, and capacity.
Identify and incubate new products, services, digital and data solutions, partnerships, and business models.
Govern opportunities from validation and business case through pilot, commercialization, and value realization.
Equip business leaders with disciplined innovation practices and recommend when to advance, pivot, pause, or stop initiatives.
IoT Strategy and Go-to-Market Leadership
Refresh HSB Canada’s IoT strategy, positioning, target segments, value propositions, ecosystem, and investment priorities.
Develop a go-to-market roadmap linking IoT-enabled risk solutions to underwriting, distribution, client needs, service delivery, and value creation.
Mobilize business, functional, and Group partners to move priority IoT opportunities from strategy to market.
Define measures for adoption, customer value, risk improvement, revenue, and profitability.
Market Insight, Executive Advisory and Group Integration
Turn customer, broker, competitor, technology, regulatory, and economic insights into actionable recommendations.
Align HSB Canada, HSB, and Munich Re Group stakeholders around shared outcomes, decisions, and timelines.
Lead high-priority cross-enterprise projects requiring structured problem solving, executive sponsorship, and coordinated execution.
Deliver Board-ready communications, represent HSB Canada in Group forums, and translate Group capabilities into Canadian opportunities.
People Leadership
Lead, coach, and develop up to five professionals across strategy, innovation, market insight, and portfolio management.
Set clear priorities, delegate ownership, provide timely feedback, and hold the team accountable for results.
Build diverse talent and foster curiosity, constructive challenge, experimentation, and learning.
Influence and mobilize matrixed teams beyond direct reporting lines.

Qualifications

Experience and Education

Approximately 12 or more years of progressive experience in enterprise strategy, corporate strategy, management consulting, innovation, business transformation, corporate development, or a related field, including significant leadership experience.
A record of advising CEOs and senior executives, leading enterprise planning, solving ambiguous business problems, and converting strategy into execution.
Experience building and governing innovation portfolios and bringing products, services, or new ventures from insight through commercialization.
Demonstrated people leadership, including coaching strong talent, setting priorities, and driving accountability across multiple concurrent workstreams.
Prior experience with a leading management consulting firm is a strong asset.
Experience in property and casualty insurance, reinsurance, or broader financial services is an asset; experience in another regulated, data-intensive sector may also be relevant.
A bachelor’s degree in business, economics, finance, engineering, mathematics, or a related discipline is required. An MBA or other relevant graduate degree is an asset.

Leadership Capabilities

Strategic agility: Quickly grasps complex concepts, identifies the critical question, connects disparate information, and develops clear strategic choices.
Quantitative and commercial acumen: Extrapolates insight from financial, operating, customer, and market data; builds robust business cases; and understands value drivers and trade-offs.
Executive influence: Engages confidently with the Board, CEO, Executive Leadership Team, business-unit leaders, and Group stakeholders; constructively challenges senior colleagues while building trust and alignment.
Execution orientation: Converts ideas into priorities, workplans, governance, milestones, and measurable outcomes; maintains momentum across multiple projects.
Innovation leadership: Balances curiosity and experimentation with underwriting discipline, customer value, operational feasibility, regulatory considerations, and financial return.
Communication excellence: Distils complex analysis into concise, compelling narratives and adapts communication for Board, executive, technical, and business audiences.
Enterprise mindset: Optimizes for HSB Canada as a whole, navigates a matrixed global organization, and integrates diverse perspectives without losing pace or accountability.
People leadership: Creates clarity, develops talent, fosters constructive debate, and builds a collaborative, high-performance culture.

Company Benefits

Together, we engage with everything we have and are, to help humankind act braver and better. Go further with HSB.

Benefits

We are pleased to offer our employees great benefits and resources to support their mental, physical and financial wellbeing. These include:

An engaging and collaborative environment that promotes continuous learning and development
A hybrid work environment that combines weekly in-office and remote days
A great compensation package including an annual company bonus
Competitive company-paid flexible health and dental benefits, starting on your first day
Flexible dollars provided by the company to put towards a Health Spending Account and/or Wellness Spending Account
Wellness program with tools and resources supporting your mental, physical, and financial wellbeing – on and off the job
Participation in the DC Pension Plan with a progressive employer contribution scale based on tenure starting at 4%, plus optional company match in the RRSP plan
Generous time off including vacation, personal days, unplanned time, Statutory Holidays and company-wide early closure half-days
Learning and development programs and resources, including unlimited access to LinkedIn Learning, Education Assistance Program, and reimbursement for professional fees
Employee Referral Program and Recognition Program

Citi is looking for a hands on Technical Lead to shape the engineering foundation of its Services AI Platform a multi\-tenant, production\-grade ecosystem where agentic AI meets enterprise scale. * Design precise prompt and intent classification logic that prevents workflow collisions and ensures each agent instruction is handled with high accuracy.
* Partner directly with subject matter experts to translate deep domain knowledge into automated, agent\-driven solutions, and collaborate with UI and API teams to deliver seamless end\-to\-end integrations.

* 10 or more years of software engineering experience, with at least 5 years focused on AI and machine learning solutions delivered in production environments.

* 3 or more years leading technical teams and owning delivery of complex software or AI platforms end to end.

* Hybrid working model with 3 days in the office and 2 days working remotely, giving you structure alongside genuine flexibility.
* Access to cutting\-edge AI infrastructure, tools, and frameworks that keep you at the leading edge of the field.
* Continuous learning and development support, including access to technical training, industry conferences, and structured career growth pathways.
* The opportunity to lead high\-impact engineering at global scale, with your work directly influencing how Citi builds and deploys intelligent automation across the enterprise.
* Competitive compensation and a comprehensive financial wellbeing package reflective of a Vice President\-level position at a leading global institution.
* Wellbeing support programs that help you maintain balance and perform at your best over the long term.

Build the AI platform that powers Citi's next generation of intelligent automation — apply now and bring your engineering leadership to one of the most technically ambitious platforms in global financial services.

About The Wawanesa Mutual Insurance Company

Founded in 1896, The Wawanesa Mutual Insurance Company is one of Canada’s largest mutual insurers, fully owned by its more than 1.8 million members. Headquartered in Winnipeg, Wawanesa is the parent company of WSI™, a specialty insurer delivering tailored solutions built around unique needs; Wawanesa Life, a provider of life insurance products; and Western Financial Group, a leading national distributor of personal and commercial insurance.

Wawanesa is committed to helping communities thrive in a changing world. The company invests more than $4 million annually in charitable initiatives, including $2.5 million each year to support people and communities on the front lines of climate change. Learn more at wawanesa.com.

We are currently seeking dedicated, driven, and enthusiastic individuals who thrive in a dynamic environment, embrace change, and are eager to gain diverse experience while advancing their careers as part of a growing team.

Job Overview

The Director, Personal Lines, Business Planning & Performance is responsible for coordinating business strategy and planning development, providing trusted advice, insights and performance management across the Personal lines of business and key business partners.

This role provides critical support to the SVP & Chief Personal Lines Officer by monitoring market developments and gathering internal and external performance metrics and business insights to enable informed decision-making, identifying opportunities for improvement, and ensuring enterprise-level alignment in planning, reporting, and execution. This role also brings together pertinent information (performance metrics, business insights and market data) into a cohesive view and narrative for the Line of Business for Executive and Board reporting. With direct leadership of cross functional business planning and market monitoring, this role is instrumental in building a performance-focused and member-centric culture. This role requires balancing high-level strategic work with tactical execution, ensuring focus on achieving Wawanesa’s critical goals in the coming years.

Serve as an advisor to the Chief Personal Lines Officer, delivering confidential counsel and perspective on matters of priority to Personal Lines planning and performance across the line of business.
Coordinate the Personal Lines strategic and tactical business planning process, gathering the relevant operational reporting/performance monitoring inputs, ensuring alignment with enterprise planning processes and priorities.
Collaborate closely with executive leadership to translate strategic objectives into measurable initiatives and performance indicators. Oversee the design and execution of executive reporting dashboards, business reviews, and decision-support analytics for the SVP and senior leadership.
Monitor and analyze external competitor and market developments, industry benchmarks, and risk, to present actionable information to support decision-making and prepare the organization to adapt effectively and proactively to changes.
Foster a collaborative environment that brings together sales, operations, finance, compliance, legal, and strategy to address performance and planning needs holistically.
Drive cross-functional initiatives and deliver results by executing through influence, effectively navigating a matrixed structure without direct authority.
Create and manage agendas and execute logistics for Personal Lines Senior Leadership meetings (including strategy and offsite sessions), Personal Lines communication forums (e.g., Townhalls, Ask Anything sessions, etc.) and track follow-ups.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in business, insurance, actuarial science, analytics, or a related field; MBA or equivalent advanced education is an asset.
Minimum 8–10 years of experience in strategic or business planning, performance reporting, operational leadership or regulatory compliance in the P&C insurance industry.
Proven leadership experience managing cross-functional teams and delivering results in a matrixed environment.
Strong understanding of insurance operations, risk management and industry financial and non-financial performance drivers.
Demonstrated ability to translate strategy into action, drive execution, and measure impact through well-structured performance frameworks, including analyzing complex issues from multiple angles and provide sound counsel among competing priorities.
Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills, with a high degree of comfort working with data, financials, and reporting tools.
Exceptional versatility, agility, situational awareness, and composure. Proven ability to navigate multiple issues concurrently and prioritize critical work.
Demonstrated ability to analyze complex issues from multiple angles and provide sound counsel among competing priorities, including experience in financial literacy and quantitative analysis, with the ability to distill actionable insights.
Effective communicator and collaborator, with strong storytelling and presentation skills and the ability to influence senior stakeholders.
Deep alignment with Wawanesa’s values and purpose, with a passion for supporting people, protecting members, and improving the way we work.
Flexibility to travel within Canada and work variable hours, including overtime, as required.
Agile business mindset with a focus on innovative problem-solving and interdepartmental collaboration.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including executive-level correspondence.

Refine Finance provides AI-powered fractional CFO and outsourced accounting services that deliver expert financial guidance at a fraction of the cost of a full-time in-house team. The company helps small and mid-sized businesses automate routine financial tasks, access real-time strategic insights, and make data-driven decisions to support efficient growth. With advanced AI-driven analytics, clients can optimize cash flow, forecast trends, manage risk, and maintain compliance and financial accuracy. Refine Finance serves entrepreneurs and business owners across North America, taking leadership of their finances, operations, and strategy so they can focus on scaling their businesses and ensuring long-term financial health.
Role Description
The Director of Finance and Accounting is a full-time, hybrid role based in the Greater Toronto Area, Canada, with flexibility for some work from home. This role oversees financial planning and analysis, budgeting, forecasting, and the preparation and review of financial statements and reports. The Director will manage accounting operations, ensure accuracy and compliance with relevant standards and regulations, and optimize internal controls and financial processes. Day-to-day responsibilities include leading and mentoring a finance and accounting team, providing strategic financial insights to support decision-making, partnering with leadership on growth initiatives, and leveraging data and technology to improve efficiency and financial visibility. The Director will also communicate financial performance and risks to stakeholders and contribute to long-term financial strategy and governance.
Qualifications

Strong expertise in Finance and Financial Planning, with experience in budgeting, forecasting, and strategic analysis.
Proficiency in preparing and reviewing Financial Statements and Financial Reporting, including compliance with accounting standards and regulatory requirements.
Demonstrated Analytical Skills and the ability to interpret complex financial data to provide clear, actionable insights.
Proven leadership experience managing finance and accounting teams, including coaching, performance management, and team development.
Advanced skills with financial systems, spreadsheets, and data analysis tools; experience with AI-driven or automated finance platforms is an asset.
Solid understanding of internal controls, audit processes, risk management, and best practices in corporate governance.
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to present financial information to non-financial stakeholders and build strong cross-functional relationships.
Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, or a related field; CPA, CFA, or equivalent professional designation strongly preferred.
QBO experience is a must
Project based accounting is a plus
