jobs.description:
Type de poste :
Permanent Modèle de travail :
Hybride Numéro de demande:
133501 Lieu principal :
Toronto, ON Emplacements additionnels :
Toronto, ON; Brossard, QC; Burlington, ON; Calgary, AB; Edmonton, AB; Fredericton, NB; Halifax, NS; Kitchener, ON; Laval, QC; Moncton, NB; Montréal, QC; Ottawa, ON; Régina, SK; Saint John, NB; Saskatoon, SK; St. John's, NL; Vancouver, BC; Victoria, BC; Winnipeg, MB; ville de Québec, QC

Notre raison d’être

Chez Deloitte, notre raison d’être est d’avoir une influence marquante. Nous existons pour inspirer et aider nos gens, nos organisations, nos collectivités et nos pays à prospérer en créant un avenir meilleur. Notre travail soutient une société prospère où les gens peuvent s’épanouir et saisir des occasions. Il renforce la confiance des consommateurs et des entreprises, aide les organisations à trouver des moyens créatifs de déployer des capitaux, habilite des institutions sociales et économiques justes, fiables et efficaces, et permet à nos amis, à nos familles et à nos collectivités de profiter de la qualité de vie qui accompagne un avenir durable. Étant le plus grand cabinet de services professionnels détenu et exploité à 100 % par des Canadiens dans notre pays, nous sommes fiers de travailler aux côtés de nos clients pour avoir une influence positive sur tous les Canadiens.

En incarnant notre raison d’être, nous aurons une influence marquante.

Diversifiez votre carrière au sein du Cabinet.
Tirez parti d’avantages souples, proactifs et pratiques qui favorisent une culture de bien-être et la création de liens solides.
Approfondissez vos connaissances grâce au mentorat d’experts et à du coaching au travail.

--

À quoi ressemblera votre journée type

En tant que leader principal(e) d’Oracle EPM Planning (directeur(trice) principal(e)), vous serez responsable des programmes de planification d’entreprise et de transformation de la fonction finance pour façonner des solutions, de la gestion de relations avec des clients et de l’exécution de nombreuses missions.

À ce titre, vous devrez faire ce qui suit :

Superviser simultanément la prestation de bout en bout de l’architecture de solutions et de nombreuses missions Oracle EPM Planning, y compris l’étendue, le plan de travail, la gestion des risques et des problèmes (RAID), la gestion financière, la gestion de la qualité et les résultats globaux de la prestation.
Fournir des conseils sur les stratégies de transformation de la fonction finance et de planification d’entreprise.
Assumer la responsabilité de la conception de la solution et des décisions en matière d’architecture.
Diriger la définition des processus de planification pour l’état futur et des modèles d’exploitation en tirant parti des capacités d’Oracle EPM pour rehausser l’efficacité et les perspectives d’affaires.
Favoriser l’harmonisation entre les finances, les TI et les parties prenantes de la direction pour favoriser des processus décisionnels efficaces et veiller à la réussite des programmes.
Assurer la direction fonctionnelle des solutions Oracle EPM Planning, y compris la gamme complète de modules EPBCS.
Superviser la conception du modèle de planification et l’architecture des solutions (catalyseurs, hypothèses, scénarios, flux des travaux, production de rapports) et s’assurer que les solutions sont adaptables, durables et harmonisées aux objectifs du client.
Veiller à l’exécution de cas d’utilisation de grande qualité sur le plan de la planification, des prévisions et de la gestion du rendement.
Superviser les activités de test et de déploiement, notamment la stratégie de test, le tri des défectuosités, l’état de préparation aux essais d’acceptation par l’utilisateur et la planification du déploiement, afin de s’assurer que les solutions sont adoptées avec succès et créent la valeur commerciale attendue.
Favoriser le développement des affaires en faisant preuve de leadership sur le plan des offres de service, en effectuant des présentations auprès des clients et en assurant la gestion des relations.
Contribuer aux stratégies de mise en marché, à l’élaboration d’offres de service et au leadership d’opinion au sein de l’équipe Oracle EPM.
Diriger et encadrer des équipes de prestation dans le cadre de nombreuses missions, afin de promouvoir une solide discipline d’exécution et leur perfectionnement grâce au coaching, au mentorat et à une rétroaction de qualité.
Contribuer au recrutement, à l’intégration et au développement de capacités au sein de l’équipe Oracle EPM.
Demeurer au courant des nouveautés liées au produit Oracle EPM et intégrer les innovations pertinentes à la prestation de services, en particulier les capacités d’IA/IGR telles que la planification prédictive, Auto Predict et IPM Insights.
Aider les clients à mettre en œuvre des capacités de planification habilitées par l’IA pour améliorer l’exactitude des prévisions, automatiser la création de perspectives et améliorer les processus décisionnels.
Façonner les réflexions de clients sur le rôle de l’IA dans le cadre de la planification d’entreprise, et la création d’un équilibre entre l’innovation et la mise en œuvre de mesures pratiques qui créent de la valeur.

La personne retenue aura l’occasion de faire partie de notre premier cabinet de services-conseils qui travaille à la fine pointe de mises en œuvre d’Oracle Cloud. Vous travaillerez auprès d’une grande variété de clients et jouerez un rôle important dans certaines des mises en œuvre les plus stimulantes à l’échelle mondiale.

Renseignements sur l’équipe

L’équipe adopte et incarne la raison d’être du Cabinet – c’est-à-dire avoir une influence marquante –, tout en vous poussant à vous surpasser, vous-même et votre équipe, afin de trouver des solutions aux problèmes les plus importants de nos clients, de nos gens et de la société.

Veiller au perfectionnement de gens et d’équipes hautement performantes en leur offrant des occasions stimulantes et pertinentes.
Offrir un service à la clientèle exceptionnel en obtenant un rendement élevé, tout en favorisant la collaboration entre les équipes et les régions.
Exercer une influence positive sur les clients, les équipes et les gens en donnant l’exemple et en établissant de solides relations.
Veiller à ce que les gens soient sur la même longueur d’onde et à ce que les priorités soient harmonisées aux objectifs d’affaires des clients et de Deloitte.

Assez parlé de nous, parlons de vous

Vous Avez Le Profil Suivant

Au moins huit années d’expérience dans la prestation de solutions Oracle EPM Planning dans des environnements de consultation ou d’entreprise.
Expérience dans la supervision de programmes de transformation de la fonction finance et de la planification d’entreprise pour améliorer les processus de budgétisation, de prévision et de présentation de l’information.
Expérience éprouvée dans la mise en œuvre de bout en bout d’Oracle EPM Planning tout au long du cycle de vie du projet, des exigences au déploiement et à la stabilisation.
Expérience éprouvée en gestion de missions de grande envergure ou simultanées, ainsi qu’en gestion de l’exécution, des parties prenantes et des aspects financiers des missions.
Excellente expertise fonctionnelle liée aux plateformes Oracle EPM Planning, y compris les systèmes EPBCS, PBCS et Hyperion Planning), et aux modules associés (Workforce, Capital, Project, Strategic Modelling).
Compréhension approfondie des processus de planification et d’analyse financières, y compris la budgétisation, les prévisions, la planification à long terme et la gestion du rendement.
Expérience de la gestion des aspects financiers des projets, de leur étendue et des risques liés aux missions complexes.
Connaissances pratiques des intégrations, de l’architecture des métadonnées et des technologies connexes (p. ex., gestion des données, FDMEE, règles d’affaires Essbase, création de scripts dans Groovy, et IPA REST).
Solides compétences en résolution de problèmes et capacité d’analyser et de résoudre des problèmes d’affaires complexes au moyen d’approches structurées.
Excellentes aptitudes pour la communication et les relations interpersonnelles, capacité de produire du contenu prêt à l’emploi et de communiquer avec les parties prenantes de haut niveau avec assurance.
Compréhension des capacités de planification propulsées par l’IA dans Oracle EPM, telles que Auto Predict et IPM Insights, capacité à les utiliser de manière responsable afin d’améliorer l’exactitude des prévisions et l’efficacité de la planification, et expérience de leur application (ou soutien de l’application).
Baccalauréat en finances, en comptabilité, en technologies de l’information ou dans un domaine connexe; une maîtrise ou un titre professionnel (p. ex., CPA, MBA) est un atout.
Certifications Oracle EPM (p. ex., certification Oracle Cloud EPM) : considérées comme un atout important.

Le bilinguisme en français et en anglais est requis pour ce poste en raison de la nature du rôle ayant des interactions avec les clients et les équipes de projet nationaux et mondiaux.

Rémunération totale

L’échelle salariale pour ce poste est de 105,000 $ à 234,000 $. Certaines personnes peuvent être admissibles à notre programme de prime. Sur le plan salarial, Deloitte se concentre sur l’équité et la compétitivité. Nous établissons régulièrement des comparaisons aux données de référence du marché établies pour divers postes, secteurs, cibles et niveaux. Notre approche est fondée sur l’importance de reconnaître les forces et les contributions uniques de chaque personne et de récompenser celle-ci pour la valeur qu’elle apporte.

La rémunération totale offerte par Deloitte s’étend bien au-delà des programmes traditionnels de rémunération et d’avantages sociaux et est conçue pour reconnaître les contributions des employés, favoriser le mieux-être personnel et soutenir la croissance du Cabinet. En plus de nos jours de congé payés réguliers, quelques exemples incluent : 4 000 $ par an pour les avantages de soutien en santé mentale, un compte de dépenses flexibles de 1 300 $, des fermetures à l'échelle de l'entreprise connues sous le nom de "Jours Deloitte", des journées dédiées à l'apprentissage (connues sous le nom de Jours de Développement et d'Innovation), des arrangements de travail flexibles et une structure de travail hybride.

Notre promesse à nos gens : Deloitte est là où vous pouvez propulsez vos ambitions.

Vous, et plus encore.

Évoluez au sein d’une équipe passionnée et déterminée à apprendre et à développer de nouvelles compétences. Bâtissez votre réseau et faites le plein d’expériences qui vous permettront de vous épanouir et vous mèneront vers la prochaine étape de votre carrière.

Vos chemins nous portent plus loin.

La diversité de vos compétences, perspectives et expériences nous rend meilleurs. Nous voulons que vous vous sentiez comme chez vous, qui que vous soyez et d’où que vous veniez. Nous vous oﬀrons des options de travail ﬂexibles et personnalisées pour répondre à vos besoins, peu importe votre mode de vie.

Devenez le leader que vous désirez être.

Certains dirigent des équipes, d’autres sont au cœur d’un changement de culture, d’autres encore bâtissent une expertise de pointe. Nous soutiendrons votre croissance en tant que leader par l’entremise d’expériences, d’occasions et de défis variés et enrichissants.

Ayez autant de carrières que vous le souhaitez.

Nous sommes en mesure de vous offrir de nouveaux rôles et de nouvelles responsabilités, et de vous aider à vous y préparer. Notre objectif est de conjuguer vos aspirations à vos compétences et à l’excellence de votre savoir-faire. Nous sommes l’endroit pour développer un réseau durable d’amis, de pairs et de mentors.

La balle est dans votre camp

Chez Deloitte, nous avons à cœur de faire des affaires de manière inclusive – cela commence par une diversité parmi les collègues de toutes les compétences! Deloitte encourage tous les candidats qualifiés qui représentent la diversité des collectivités partout au Canada

jobs.title: Sr. Director, Product Strategy (AI, Data, Advertising)
jobs.description:
Publicis Groupe Canada
is the Canadian subsidiary of Publicis Groupe, the second largest communications group in the world and a global leader concentrated within four main activities: Communication, Media, Data and Technology. Publicis Groupe Canada represents the vision of a set of collaborative and integrated agencies that offer expertise and insightful services to many of the biggest brands in North America.

Canadian brands include:
Publicis Canada (Publicis Canada, Hawkeye, Razorfish, Publicis Health, ThePubProductions, Nurun, Moov AI, Publicis Sports & Entertainment), Publicis Media (Starcom, Spark Foundry, Zenith), Leo Burnett (Leo Burnett Canada, Ove Brand Design, Leo Burnett Design), Saatchi & Saatchi (Saatchi & Saatchi Canada, Synergize, TPM), MSL Canada/North Strategic and Publicis Sapient.

Overview

The Senior Director, Product Strategy
owns the enterprise vision, business roadmap and market adoption strategy for Connected Solutions (Publicis Groupe’s core AI and data products). This leader connects client business priorities, agency needs and product capabilities, turning complex opportunities into a clear portfolio direction and sequenced roadmap.

Operating as a senior individual contributor and trusted executive advisor, this person shapes strategic decisions across clients, agencies and internal leadership. They establish the narrative, commercial logic and adoption model for Connected Solutions, ensuring that individual client opportunities translate into repeatable products, scalable growth and sustained market relevance.

Responsibilities

Enterprise Product Vision & Portfolio Strategy

Set and champion the long-term product vision for Connected Solutions, aligning AI and data capabilities with client priorities, agency strategy and market opportunity.
Own the enterprise business roadmap and rollout sequencing for the core agentic solution, while identifying adjacent products and portfolio opportunities that can expand impact and revenue.
Establish portfolio-level prioritization criteria that balance client demand, feasibility, commercial potential, differentiation and strategic fit.
Make clear recommendations on where to invest, accelerate, pause or reposition, and build executive alignment around those choices.

Executive Leadership & Governance

Serve as the senior strategic voice for Connected Solutions in executive forums, client leadership meetings and cross-agency planning discussions.
Create decision frameworks and governance rhythms that keep business, product, delivery and technology leaders aligned on priorities, risks and expected outcomes.
Hold the strategic boundary between product vision, tactical product design and technical execution, ensuring accountability without dictating architecture.
Partner closely with the Product Lead and Delivery and Technology leadership to translate strategic intent into an executable plan.

Commercial Growth & Market Positioning

Identify and shape growth opportunities across existing and prospective client relationships, connecting product capability to meaningful business value.
Define positioning, packaging, adoption pathways and service models that enable agencies and account teams to bring Connected Solutions to market consistently.
Partner with growth and account leaders on pitches, proposals and strategic pursuits, strengthening the commercial story and value proposition.
Turn high-value client use cases into repeatable offerings that can scale across accounts, markets and agency disciplines.

Client Advisory, Storytelling & Influence

Act as a trusted advisor to C-level clients and senior internal executives, helping them understand where AI, data and automation can create measurable value.
Shape and deliver compelling narratives for pitches, demonstrations, executive presentations and strategic workshops.
Translate complex product and technical capabilities into clear business choices, outcomes and trade-offs for non-technical audiences.
Build consensus across clients, agencies, product, technology and delivery teams, especially when priorities compete or strategic pivots are required.

Adoption, Impact & Continuous Learning

Define what successful adoption and rollout look like, including client outcomes, adoption signals, repeatable use cases and indicators of commercial scale.
Develop executive-level measures of product value and use them to guide roadmap decisions, investment conversations and market expansion.
Establish structured feedback loops with clients and agencies to identify friction, unmet needs and emerging opportunities.
Serve as the senior escalation point for product-related concerns or strategic pivots, coordinating resolution with the Product Lead and relevant partners.

What Success Looks Like

Connected Solutions has a clear, prioritized and commercially grounded roadmap understood by senior stakeholders.
Clients and agencies understand the portfolio’s value and how to adopt it.
Product decisions reflect client feedback, adoption signals and market opportunity.
Individual client needs become repeatable use cases, scalable offerings and sustained commercial momentum.

Qualifications

What we are looking for:

12+ years of progressive experience in product strategy, marketing strategy, innovation or commercial growth, including significant leadership at the Director, Group Director or equivalent level.
Experience owning enterprise product or portfolio strategy, business roadmaps and rollout plans across external clients, agency networks or complex organizations.
Deep understanding of the agency ecosystem, ideally across creative, media, CRM and data disciplines.
Strong knowledge of marketing and media workflows and a practical understanding of how agentic AI and automation can improve them.
Proven ability to advise C-level stakeholders, simplify complex topics and influence cross-functional decisions in a matrixed environment.
Strong commercial mindset, with experience connecting product capabilities to packaging, adoption, client value and scalable growth.
Ability to partner credibly with engineering and technical leadership while owning business strategy rather than technical delivery.
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Marketing, Product, Strategy or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.

Stand-Out Experience

Launching or scaling agentic AI, automation, data or marketing technology solutions within CRM, media or creative organizations.
Familiarity with agency commercial models, including licensing, packaging, service tiers and value propositions.
Experience leading product advisory boards, executive workshops, innovation councils or structured client discovery programs.
New business, growth strategy or enterprise transformation experience across multiple agencies, markets or global stakeholder groups.

Additional Information

Eligibility: Candidates must be based in the Greater Toronto Area (GTA), possess valid Canadian work authorization, and be willing to commute to our downtown Toronto office.
Hybrid schedule: Rotating 2-day / 3-day in-office schedule (Tue/Thu one week, Mon/Wed/Fri the next).
Competitive annual vacation program, enhanced between Christmas and New Year’s when our offices are closed.
Extended statutory holidays (we give our employees the Mondays and Fridays of provincial holidays so you can enjoy long 4-day weekends).
6 sick days per year and 2 personal days per year.
Monthly cell phone allowance
Employer RRSP matching contributions of up to 2%
“Work Your World” program, allowing you to work remotely for up to 6 weeks in any country where we have an office (50+ countries).
Comprehensive group insurance benefits (medical and dental care, vision care, psychological and paramedical services, disability insurance, fertility support, and gender-affirming care).
Internal support and guidance program for cancer, fertility, and gender transition.

The salary for this position is $160,000 - $210,000 per year. Actual compensation will be based on a variety of factors, including relevant experience, knowledge, skills, and applicable certifications. This reflects what we reasonably expect to offer based on current market data.

We use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of our hiring process. These tools assist our recruitment team but never replace human decision-making. We believe in a human-first approach, where your experience and potential are recognized by people.

Publicis Canada is committed to building a diverse workforce representative of our community. We encourage and are pleased to consider all qualified candidates, without regard to race, colour, citizenship, religion, sex, marital / family status, sexual orientation, gender identity, aboriginal status, age, disability or persons who may require an accommodation, to apply. If you require a specific accommodation, please contact Human Resources at inquiries@publicisna.com.

jobs.title: Directeur Financier | Finance Director
jobs.description:
Description

Qui sommes-nous : Manos

Manos Software Group fait partie de Valsoft Corporation, un investisseur à long terme dans les entreprises de logiciels de marchés verticaux. Valsoft acquiert et exploite des sociétés de logiciels avec une vision de détention permanente, en mettant l’accent sur l’autonomie, une croissance disciplinée et la création de valeur à long terme. Manos se concentre sur des secteurs connexes à la santé, notamment les logiciels dentaires, médicaux et vétérinaires.

Description Du Poste

Dans le cadre de l’expansion continue de notre portefeuille d’entreprises de logiciels spécialisés par secteur d’activité, nous recherchons une personne dynamique et expérimentée pour rejoindre notre équipe en tant que Directeur.trice Financier·ère. Relevant directement de l’un des Partenaires d’Investissement, la personne retenue sera responsable de la supervision de la performance financière et du développement stratégique de notre portefeuille. Ce rôle implique une prise en charge complète de la planification financière, du reporting et de la gestion de la performance.

La personne idéale est un.e leader stratégique doté.e d’une forte expertise financière, capable de favoriser l’excellence opérationnelle, d’optimiser la rentabilité et d’assurer un flux de trésorerie positif. Cette personne travaillera en étroite collaboration avec des équipes interfonctionnelles, en favorisant la coopération pour exécuter avec succès les stratégies d’entreprise tout en maintenant des contrôles financiers rigoureux et une conformité exemplaire.

Responsabilités principales

Piloter la planification financière en analysant la performance et les risques du portefeuille
Définir les objectifs et superviser l’ensemble du personnel comptable et financier (comptabilité, FP&A, comptes clients, comptes fournisseurs)
Préparer les rapports financiers mensuels, trimestriels et annuels
Élaborer et gérer les prévisions financières mensuelles, trimestrielles et annuelles ; suivre les indicateurs clés de performance (KPIs)
Surveiller et analyser les performances pour identifier des axes d’amélioration et mettre en œuvre des plans d’action permettant d’atteindre ou de dépasser les objectifs financiers
Suivre la santé financière du portefeuille et garantir un flux de trésorerie positif
Diriger et organiser les audits légaux annuels, en veillant au respect de toutes les obligations réglementaires
Développer des stratégies pour améliorer la rentabilité et le retour sur investissement
Superviser et réviser les activités comptables, y compris la fiscalité et la conformité
Veiller à l’efficacité des contrôles financiers internes et évaluer en continu les politiques et procédures en place
Collaborer avec l’équipe chargée de l’intégration des entreprises nouvellement acquises, notamment pour la production des bilans d’ouverture, des états financiers complets, et pour assurer leur intégration aux processus financiers de Valsoft
Maintenir une communication régulière avec le département Finance du groupe
Participer activement aux processus d’acquisition et de cession d’entreprises
Accomplir toutes autres responsabilités confiées par l’employeur, que la personne s’engage à exécuter avec diligence, conformément aux termes de l’accord

Prêt(e) à joindre une équipe collaborative et innovante où vous pourrez avoir un impact immédiat?

#Manos

Manos Overview

Manos Software Group is part of Valsoft Corporation, a long-term investor in vertical market software businesses. Valsoft acquires and operates software companies with a permanent ownership mindset, emphasizing autonomy, disciplined growth, and long-term value creation. Manos focuses on healthcare-adjacent verticals, including dental, medical, and veterinary software.

Position Description

As we continue to expand our portfolio of vertical market software businesses, we are seeking a dynamic and experienced professional to join our team as Finance Director. Reporting directly to one of our Investment Partners, the Finance Director will be responsible for overseeing the financial performance and strategic development of our portfolio. This role involves full ownership and accountability for financial planning, reporting, and performance management. The ideal candidate is a strategic leader with a strong financial acumen, capable of driving operational excellence, optimizing profitability, and ensuring positive cash flow. They will work closely with cross-functional teams, fostering collaboration to execute business strategies successfully while maintaining rigorous financial controls and compliance.

Key Responsibilities

Drive the financial planning of the company by analyzing portfolio performance and risks
Set targets for and supervise all accounting and finance personnel (Accounting, FP&A, AR, AP)
Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reports
Build and manage monthly, quarterly, and annual forecasts; track KPIs
Monitor and analyze performance strategies to identify areas of opportunity and implement action plans to meet or exceed financial targets
Monitor the financial health of the portfolio and ensure positive cash flow
Lead and organize annual statutory audits and ensure all required filings are completed
Develop strategies to increase return on investment and profitability
Oversee and review accounting tasks, including tax and compliance
Ensure effective financial internal controls and continuously evaluate established policies and procedures
Collaborate with the integration team of newly acquired companies by producing opening balances, complete financials, and onboarding on Valsoft finance procedures
Maintain high-level interaction with the corporate finance department
Actively participate in processes related to the sale or acquisition of companies
Perform all other applicable responsibilities as delegated by the Employer, which the Employee agrees to carry out diligently under the terms of the Agreement

Ready to join a collaborative and innovative team where you can make an immediate impact?

jobs.title: Director, Wealth Strategy & Research - 12-month contract - Tangerine
jobs.description:
Requisition ID
: 273102

At Tangerine, we’re redefining banking. As Canada’s leading digital bank, we thrive on innovation, agility, and bold thinking, tackling every challenge head-on with leading technology and the unstoppable power of collaboration.

Our client-obsessed teams deliver flexible, accessible banking solutions, breakthrough products, and award-winning service. Beyond banking, we’re committed to making an impact in the communities we serve and across our organization. We foster a culture built on integrity, inclusion, and fearless ambition – where diverse perspectives are valued, and people are empowered to do their best work.

Are you ready to disrupt the status quo? Do you crave challenges that push boundaries? If you’re a high performer looking to accelerate your career and reimagine the banking landscape, this is your moment.

Let’s shape the future of banking together!

What You Will Be Doing

The Director, Wealth Strategy & Research will lead the development and execution of strategic initiatives that shape the future of our wealth offerings. This role carries enterprise-level accountability, executive decision support, and stakeholder influence across the organization. The Director will serve as a thought leader, driving insights that inform product strategy, market positioning, and long-term growth.

Is this role right for you? In this role, you will be:

Define and execute the Tangerine Wealth product roadmap in alignment with business strategic objectives.
Provide strategic insights and recommendations to senior executives, influencing enterprise priorities and business decisions.
Represent Tangerine Wealth in executive forums and prepare board reports, C-suite briefings, and steering-committee updates.
Work closely with market research and competitive intelligence teams to identify actionable insights to inform product development and business decisions.
Continuously monitor the traditional wealth, digital wealth, and fintech landscape for emerging trends, competitor moves, regulatory developments, and technology innovations.
Translate research findings into actionable strategies that drive innovation and client-centric solutions.
Develop and manage structured frameworks for competitor benchmarking, client segmentation, pricing, and go-to-market strategies.

We Are:

Accenture Data & AI — the people who love using data to tell a story. We're the world's largest team of data scientists and experts in machine learning and AI. We believe a mix of data, analytics, automation, and responsible AI can do almost anything — spark digital reinvention, widen the range of what humans can do, and breathe life into smart products and services.

In the Public Sector, we partner with government agencies, crown corporations, and public institutions to drive meaningful, citizen-centred transformation. We bring the full depth of Accenture's AI and data capabilities to solve complex challenges that matter at a societal scale.

You Are: A thought leader and practitioner at the intersection of AI strategy and data delivery — As a senior leader in the Data & AI practice, you will coach and mentor up-and-coming leaders, guide diverse multi-disciplinary teams, and help clients embed AI and data capabilities as a lasting part of their organisational culture — with a strong focus on responsible AI, data governance, and public trust.

Role Summary

As a Senior Leader
in Accenture’s Data &AI
practice, you will lead the strategy, design, and scaled delivery of AI & Data solutions for Utilities
industry and clients
. You will build reusable data/AI capabilities—covering ingestion, orchestration, governance, data products, analytics enablement, and model/AI lifecycle—so clients can accelerate time-to-value while meeting enterprise-grade requirements for security, privacy, quality, and responsible AI. The Utilities industry is at the center of the largest infrastructure transformation in a generation—the collision of decarbonization, unprecedented load growth from electrification and data centers, grid resilience against extreme weather events, affordability and regulatory pressure, and the shift to distributed, digitized, AI-enabled operations. You will own the Data & AI agenda for our Utilities portfolio across Canada, personally leading the most consequential CxO relationships, and set the pace for how the portfolio grows, delivers and shows up in the market.

Set direction for AI & Data Utilities: Own the target-state vision, architecture, and roadmap for data/AI utilities across complex enterprise landscapes (multiple systems, domains, and stakeholders).

Lead large-scale client engagements: Drive end-to-end delivery leadership across strategy, design, build, and transition-to-run, ensuring outcomes and adoption.

Operationalize reusable accelerators: Establish standards and scalable patterns (reference architectures, reusable pipelines, governance workflows, data product frameworks, and MLOps/LLMOps practices).

Shape the Utilities Data & AI agenda: own the industry point of view and go-to-market, including energy-transition advisory, rate case and regulatory environment, OT/IT convergence, grid-modernization and DERMS-enabling data platforms, wildfire and resilience analytics, customer-experience transformation and AI-enabled workforce and field operations. 12+ years of relevant experience in enterprise data platforms and/or AI/ML engineering, including architecture and operationalization.

Proven track record of building and growing an industry portfolio – origination, sales and expansion – with personally attributable multi-$MM record in annual originated sales and ownership of multi-$MM in managed revenue at portfolio scale, sustained across multiple years and through all least one full economic or industry cycle.

Recognized trusted advisor to C-suite and Board-level executives at large enterprise Utility industry clients, with the credibility and presence to lead the most challenging conversations on strategy, investment, and transformation outcomes in a rapidly changing Utilities landscape.

Strong background in enterprise data architecture and delivery for utility-style platforms (integration, orchestration, data products, governance, and data operations).

Strong experience in stakeholder and executive management and ability to translate technical strategy into business value.

Track record of building, leading & developing high-performance teams at scale and influencing without authority across client organizations and internal leadership.

Recognized eminence and thought leadership in Data & AI for Utilities – evidenced by such recurring keynote or mainstage presence at flagship industry forums (e.g. DistribuTECH, CERAWeek, Enlit, WEF Energy), published points of view carried by tier-one industry or business media in the last 24 months, and standing relationships with the leading Utilities in Canada as well as AI/Data analysts (Gartner, Forrester, Wood Mackenzie, S&P Global).

What is the opportunity?

The Senior Director-Head of CNB Wealth Business Architecture is a senior leadership role within City National Bank (RBC) Wealth Technology, reporting directly to the Head of CNB Wealth Technology.

The role is responsible for leading the CNB Wealth Business Architecture organization, with approximately 30 professionals, and driving the product strategy, roadmap, prioritization, and execution of technology capabilities that support City National Bank’s Wealth Management business.

The successful candidate will serve as a strategic partner to CNB Wealth business leadership, bringing deep Wealth Management industry expertise and a strong understanding of the products, platforms, workflows, operating models, and client experiences that underpin a modern wealth management organization.

In addition to the functional leadership responsibilities, the individual will serve as the Head of Toronto for CNB Wealth Technology, providing local leadership, employee engagement, talent development, and organizational oversight for the Toronto-based CNB Wealth Technology community.

What will you do?

Wealth Product Leadership

Lead the Wealth Business Architecture organization of approximately 30 professionals, establishing a high-performing, product-oriented culture focused on business outcomes and client value.
Define and execute the Wealth Product Development strategy in partnership with Wealth business leadership and the Head of Wealth Technology.
Own the product development lifecycle from ideation and prioritization through delivery, adoption, and continuous enhancement.
Translate Wealth business strategy and client needs into clear product strategies, roadmaps, priorities, and measurable outcomes.
Establish and maintain a disciplined product prioritization framework that balances strategic initiatives, business growth opportunities, client experience, regulatory requirements, technology modernization, and operational needs.
Ensure product roadmaps are aligned with the broader Wealth Technology strategy and enterprise technology architecture.
Partner closely with Engineering, Architecture, Data, Cybersecurity, Operations, and other technology functions to ensure successful delivery of product capabilities.
Drive transparency into product investment, priorities, dependencies, delivery progress, and business outcomes.
Establish appropriate product management practices, standards, governance, metrics, and operating rhythms across the organization.

Visa is a world leader in payments technology, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories, dedicated to uplifting everyone, everywhere by being the best way to pay and be paid.

At Visa, you'll have the opportunity to create impact at scale — tackling meaningful challenges, growing your skills and seeing your contributions impact lives around the world.

Join Visa and do work that matters – to you, to your community, and to the world. Progress starts with you.

The Consulting Director will be a key member of Visa Consulting and Analytics (VCA), a team within Visa Advisory Services that drives tangible, impactful and financial results for Visa’s network clients, including both financial services and merchants. Drawing on our expertise in strategy consulting, data analytics, brand management, marketing, operational and macroeconomics, VCA solves the most strategic problems for our clients.

Potential engagements could include market expansion, revenue uplift, segmentation, portfolio management diagnostics, authorization optimization strategies, assessments of digital product and marketing programs, development of new products with implementation roadmaps, and optimizing client customer servicing processes.

Proactively engage and manage advisory relationship with key clients and Visa client leadership in regular strategic & planning discussions

What's the opportunity?

We're looking for a product leader to own the roadmap for RBC's internal agentic AI platform end-to-end — from intake and prioritization through delivery and measurement. As Director, Product Strategy & Roadmap, you will decide what ships and when, ground those decisions in user value and adoption evidence, and own the product experience and analytics that make the platform usable and valuable at scale.

You will bring rigour to prioritization, fluency in agentic AI, and the credibility to partner with engineering on how the roadmap gets built — without owning the technical implementation.

Your responsibilities will include:

Roadmap ownership: Maintaining and communicating a rolling 12-month roadmap with clear, evidence-based prioritization rationale

User experience: Owning the end-to-end product experience across the platform — how users discover, adopt, build with, and get value from it — including the self-service builder, templates, and connector catalog as part of a coherent whole.
Product analytics: Building and maintaining adoption dashboards, usage telemetry, and value-realization measurement to drive decisions
Delivery partnership: Partnering with engineering on acceptance criteria, backlog, and delivery quality, staying engaged to protect the user outcome
Responsible AI in practice: Embedding the safety, governance, and transparency standards set by the AI Group's Safety and Responsible AI function into the roadmap and release gates
Market awareness: Conducting competitive and market analysis to inform platform direction

You're our ideal candidate if you:

Have 8+ years of product management experience, including 3+ in AI/ML products or enterprise platforms
Have a strong product-experience and design sensibility — able to shape how users discover, adopt, and succeed with a product, not only what features it has.
Have a deep working understanding of agentic AI: LLMs, tool-use, MCP connectors, RAG, and multi-agent orchestration
Have owned and delivered a product roadmap with measurable adoption outcomes
Are strongly analytical — able to define and track adoption metrics, build dashboards, and interpret telemetry
Have the technical fluency to partner with engineers on architecture decisions without writing code

Display creative thinking and consulting skills to deliver a continually improving service for the client

Experience with GSOC and intelligence tools, including threat monitoring, OSINT, and SOCMINT platforms

a leading global player in international healthcare and insurance solutions for internationally expatriate individuals and local high net worth individual in emerging countries.

It mainly operates as an insurance seller of health coverage products for corporates, individual expatriates, international students and travelers, and as a Third-Party Administrator for health insurance related claims.

The CFO will be relied upon to provide timely and meaningful monthly financial reporting, assist with the analysis of growth opportunities in foreign markets, prepare and monitor cash flow forecasts and provide insight into the ongoing strategic planning objectives for the organization.

Management of the adequate financial and accounting processes:
review and, if need be, recommendation for improvement, of the financial and accounting procedures and policies: revenue and expenses recognition, follow up and recognition of cash (insurer’s / own cash), balance sheet presentation;
ensure cash management is performed according to the Group rules and professional best practices;
check compliance with the accounting standards, and with local financial regulations;

Pluriannual financial business plans and yearly budget; recurring reforecast;

monthly, quarterly and yearly reporting sent to the MSH group’s management, to shareholders (including the Group reporting), and when need be to external auditors, in relation to all financial related information: budget, forecasts, management reporting (including headcount and litigation related provisions), financial accounts, cash management, impairment tests…;
ad hoc analysis of the business development, profitability profile and cash management outcome of the subsidiaries

Contribution to acquisitions and local development from the financial standpoint, within the frame of the acquisition policies and procedures of Group:
financial analysis of the target performance;
review of the business plan, analysis of value and financial support to the various steps of the negotiation;
supervision of financial due diligences;

Ensure all tax reports are delivered in due course and adequate form, and that all relevant taxes are acquitted
Optimize, within the frame of relevant regulation, tax incurred by the group companies;

Risk and compliance

Connection is everything. It drives us to innovate, explore, and stay close to what matters to us most. At Bell, we’re building a more connected future through world-class networks, AI-powered solutions, and digital experiences that elevate how people live, work, and play every day.

We believe in empowering people. That’s why we equip our teams with cutting-edge technology, AI tools, and a collaborative environment that supports creativity and growth. Want to be part of a diverse team where your work makes a real impact? If you’re inspired by innovation that advances how people connect and transforms what’s possible, you belong on #TeamBell.

At Bell, your skills and expertise will help set us apart as we continue to be the leading provider of digital connections and next generation services to businesses and governments.

Summary

Bell AI Fabric is building Canada's largest sovereign AI infrastructure platform. As Director, Strategy, you will work at the centre of its most important strategic, commercial, and operational priorities, helping shape decisions that will influence the future of AI infrastructure in Canada and ensuring those decisions translate into action and results.

This is a highly visible internal consulting and execution role with unusual breadth and access. Working directly with senior executives, Bell AI Fabric Board members, governments, customers, investors, and strategic partners, you will tackle complex questions with no obvious answer, bring clarity to competing perspectives, and help move the organization from discussion to decision to delivery.

Your work will span corporate strategy, partnerships, government engagement, commercial negotiations, major customer opportunities, and organizational execution. You will build the plans and governance required to deliver, step into critical moments where additional leadership or problem-solving is needed and see recommendations through to real-world outcomes.

This is a unique opportunity for a strategy or consulting professional who wants to help build something consequential, learn quickly across a wide range of issues, and have visible impact. You do not need to arrive knowing every part of the business; success will come from curiosity, sound judgment, strong execution, and a willingness to invest the effort required to figure things out.

Act as a trusted strategy partner and extension of the executive team, bringing independent judgment, anticipating what is required, and providing hands-on leadership on Bell AI Fabric's highest-priority opportunities and issues.
Lead structured problem-solving on complex questions related to growth, market positioning, commercial models, partnerships, major initiatives, and organizational scalability; distill complexity into clear choices, decisions, and actions.
Rapidly develop command of unfamiliar commercial, technical, operational, and stakeholder issues by identifying the critical facts, connecting perspectives, and isolating what matters most.

Evaluate and advance strategic partnerships, commercial opportunities, government initiatives, customer opportunities, and other priorities that support long-term growth.

A strong orientation toward quality and detail, with the ability to reconcile analyses, narratives, decisions, and deliverables across multiple workstreams.
Sound commercial judgment and negotiation capability, with the persistence to help close agreements, decisions, and outstanding projects.
Strong stakeholder management skills and the ability to govern, align, and mobilize senior stakeholders without formal authority.
High capacity and strong organization, with the ability to manage several urgent priorities, sustain pace, and improve the completeness and quality of the work.
Ability to operate with increasing independence, anticipate needs, step into unfamiliar issues, and invest the effort required to build understanding and deliver results.

Management consulting experience or equivalent training in structured problem-solving, analysis, executive communication, and high-quality delivery.
Strong research and synthesis capability, intellectual curiosity, and a demonstrated interest in learning and becoming credible on new topics.
Experience supporting partnerships, complex commercial negotiations, or major infrastructure and technology initiatives.

What's In It for You?

You won't inherit a playbook. You'll write it. You'll define the operating model, the culture, and the technical direction for a brand-new function, and shape a small, sharp team of 2 from day one. You'll report directly to the CTO and work closely with the Senior Leadership Team, as well as the Engineering, Product, Sales, and People teams. You'll tackle big questions like how to govern AI agents connected to company systems, and your answers will set policy at Klue. As Klue grows, so do the team and your scope. You have the power to shape what that looks like.

What You'll Do

Own security posture and incident readiness. Mature how Klue prevents, detects, and responds to security issues. Design the incident response process and governance, and make sure everyone knows their role before something goes wrong.
Run the compliance engine. Own the annual audit cycle against SOC 2 Type II, NIST CSF, and BSIMM, plus penetration testing, from evidence collection to a successful finish. Build audit methodology and documentation that make reviews faster and less painful for the whole company.
Be the security answer for go-to-market. Keep customer questionnaires, external assessments, and audits moving on time. Review and negotiate data protection agreements and security exhibits with customers and vendors so what we sign matches what we do.
Govern vendors, data, and privacy. Run full-spectrum vendor reviews, including sub-processor qualification. Own DLP, data retention, and the privacy framework for an international customer base, including data subject access requests.
Set the rules for AI and high-risk access. Own AI security governance: policies, risk acceptance, data handling, and permissioning for AI tools, agents, and integrations connected to company systems. Define and enforce access governance for high-risk systems, including admin access reviews, service accounts vs. individual credentials, and controls on sensitive logs and data.
Make security engineering's job easier. Set the security and compliance standard for Engineering's security work. Give the team the tooling, policy, and guidelines to build against, and translate their technical work into terms leadership and customers can act on.
Equip and enable every Kluebee. Own devices, access, and tooling across the full employee lifecycle. Manage the vendors behind our IT stack, set and hit reliability targets (SLOs) for corporate systems, and replace ad hoc fixes with repeatable processes that scale. Partner with People so onboarding and offboarding run smoothly. (Product infrastructure stays with Engineering.)

What Success Looks Like

One team, one roadmap. Within two quarters, Security, Compliance, and IT operate as one team with a shared roadmap and a regular operating rhythm.
Customers get fast, consistent answers. Questionnaires, audits, and sub-processor reviews are completed on time and in a repeatable way.
AI and access are governed, not improvised. High-risk systems and AI tools are covered by clear, documented policy, and admin access reviews are routine, not reactive.
Corporate systems are reliable. You define clear SLOs in your first quarter, and Klue meets or beats them.
We're ready when it counts. Incident response governance is documented and understood, and Engineering's security engineers have the tooling and guidelines to respond fast.
Day 1 just works. Every new Kluebee has working equipment and access on their first day, with no scrambling.
The budget is a set of clear choices. You actively manage the function's budget and make defensible tradeoffs between tooling, vendors, and headcount.
You're the default owner. The CTO and SLT turn to you for security, compliance, and IT. Engineering and GTM teams see you as the partner who makes their job easier, not another layer to work around.

What You Bring

Must Haves

You've run security and compliance at a company handling sensitive customer data. You're comfortable owning DLP, data retention, and privacy frameworks, and you can work through a security questionnaire or audit without panic.
You've led IT operations for a whole company, covering equipment, access, and tooling.
You know security frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIST) and global privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA) in depth.
You're comfortable with ambiguity and building without a playbook.
You communicate clearly with both technical peers and non-technical leaders, and can explain a risk to an engineer and to a CEO.
You've negotiated data protection agreements and security exhibits in vendor and customer contracts.
You understand AI security and governance: data retention commitments, access and permissioning for AI agents and integrations, and risk acceptance for AI tooling.
You've worked closely with product and engineering teams to turn security and compliance goals into reality.

Nice-to-Haves

You've owned a DevOps and/or security engineering function inside a larger engineering org.
You've brought previously siloed security, compliance, and IT teams together under one roof.
You know privacy and data residency frameworks for an international customer base.
You've managed distributed or hybrid teams.

The Associate Director, AI & Automation leads the implementation of artificial intelligence and process automation adoption for Thompson Rivers University. Reporting to the CIO and serving as a key advisor, this role supports TRU's AI and automation portfolio:
setting strategic direction and governance standards,
adoption review,
directing the Power Team initiative and future programs,
and building the team, partnerships, and institutional capability needed to scale responsible AI use across the university.

Some of the key accountabilities for this role are:

Strategic Leadership & Governance

Support TRU's institution-wide AI and automation strategy, setting direction, priorities, and success metrics in alignment with the university's strategic plan.
Adjudicating risk classification and review of proposed AI and automation use cases (e.g., under the Safe Start framework).
Serve as a key advisor to the CIO on AI strategy, opportunity, and risk; hold a standing voice in ITS leadership team.
Set institutional standards and policy guardrails for responsible AI and automation adoption.
Direct and mentor a growing team in the design, governance, and deployment of AI and automation solutions.
Maintain working command of MLOps principles (model versioning, monitoring, and deployment) to guide the team's technical practice.

Strategic Planning & Program Delivery

Develop and execute the multi-year roadmap for integrating AI and RPA into administrative and academic-support workflows, with Power Team as the flagship program.
Identify, prioritize, and business-case new automation and AI opportunities based on time, accuracy, consistency, and risk impact.
Set and track program-level goals (time saved, error reduction, adoption, satisfaction) and report progress against a defined roadmap, not just individual pilots.
Own budget planning and vendor/contract management for the AI and automation portfolio, including delegated authority for AI tool and automation procurement decisions.

Team Leadership & Resourcing

Build, structure, and grow the AI & Automation team, with accountability for hiring, performance management, and career development.
Define team structure and resourcing plans that scale with institutional demand, including a stated growth trajectory as the portfolio expands.

Training & Capability Building

Direct the design and delivery of training and enablement programs for administrative leaders and support staff on AI and automation tools.
Foster a culture of curiosity, experimentation, and responsible use across the institution.

Institutional & External Engagement

Represent TRU externally on AI and automation practice, including engagement with the BC/national peer community, sector consultations, and conference or panel participation.
Build and maintain relationships with administrative leaders, ITS teams, AI/automation vendors, and industry experts.
Contributes to the institutional narrative around AI and automation, building stakeholder trust and sustained momentum through regular communication of progress and outcomes.

Feedback, Metrics & Continuous Improvement

Establish a portfolio-level measurement framework and report efficiency gains, adoption rates, risk posture, and challenges to senior leadership on a regular cadence.
Collect and act on feedback from training sessions and pilot/program implementations to refine strategy, tools, and governance.
Hold the team accountable for outcomes, documenting both successes and lessons learned to inform the next phase of the roadmap

Required Skills, Experience and Knowledge

Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business Administration, or a related field required; Master's degree in a related field strongly preferred and weighted favourably.
At least five (5) years of leadership experience, ideally within a post-secondary or complex institutional setting, including experience building or scaling a team.
At least three (3) years of hands-on experience in software development, scripting, or automation engineering, with a strong foundation in coding best practices.
Demonstrated experience developing institutional policy, governance frameworks, or risk/adoption review processes — not solely technical delivery.
Experience managing vendor relationships, contracts, and budget for a technology program or portfolio.
Strong understanding of AI and RPA technologies and their institutional applications; prior experience building AI/ML platforms.
Familiarity with cloud AI/ML platforms such as AWS SageMaker, Azure Machine Learning, or equivalent.
Familiarity with organizational change management methodologies; experience leading change management and stakeholder engagement at an institutional level.
Excellent leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills, including experience representing an organization externally (peer institutions, sector bodies, conferences).
Ability to analyze data and feedback to drive continuous improvement across a program portfolio.

If the above position profile excites you and you would like to learn or know more about this great opportunity, then please contact Matt Norton, Associate Vice President Digital Strategies and Chief Information Officer, Information Technology Services at mnorton@tru.ca or call Matt at 250 852 6383 and please reference the position title.

jobs.title: Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, Trilogy (Remote) - $800,000/year USD
jobs.description:
Most finance executives inherit a system. You will redesign one, then decide where the capital goes.

Trilogy is looking for the executive who can turn a portfolio of businesses into a capital allocation system: continuously ranking where the next dollar should go, backing those decisions with rigorous models, and moving capital toward its highest-return uses. You will own the calls that matter: fund or kill a business line; invest or hold; acquire or walk away; refinance or pay down debt. Every recommendation must connect strategy to cash, liquidity, covenants, risk, and enterprise value.

Just as important, you will architect an AI-native finance function built to scale without decision bottlenecks. This does not mean sprinkling AI tools onto a traditional finance organization. You will redesign reporting, planning, controls, portfolio monitoring, and decision support around what AI and automation can now do. You won't need to personally build every workflow, but you must use AI deeply enough to know its edges: where it accelerates analysis, where it fails, and where expert judgment must take over. The result should be a smaller, more senior, higher-leverage finance organization rather than a growing pyramid of people and processes.

You will operate directly with Trilogy's CEO, board, lenders, and capital partners, with personal accountability for the financial truth behind major decisions. This is an $800K W-2 salaried role for someone who has already earned credibility at serious financial scale and now wants the mandate to compound enterprise value across an entire portfolio. If you want your impact measured by the quality of your capital decisions and the financial system you leave behind, apply.

What You Will Be Doing

Allocating capital across the portfolio: Run capital and portfolio reviews, rank competing uses of capital on risk-adjusted return, and make clear fund, hold, restructure, exit, debt-paydown, or acquisition recommendations.
Architecting an AI-native finance system: Redesign planning, reporting, consolidation, controls, portfolio monitoring, and financial workflows around AI, automation, and scalable systems rather than additional headcount.
Driving investments and transactions: Build and defend the financial case for strategic investments, M&A, financing, and refinancing, including integrated models, downside scenarios, capital structure, covenant implications, and execution plans.
Owning board and capital-partner communication: Give the CEO, board, lenders, and capital partners fast, quantified, defensible truth, with recommendations that make the decision and trade-offs explicit.
Building a high-leverage finance leadership team: Set the bar for a small group of exceptional finance leaders while creating systems that allow new ventures and greater complexity to be absorbed without linear organizational growth.

What You Won’t Be Doing

Running finance as a reporting factory. Closing the books and producing audit workpapers are the Controller's responsibilities. Your job is to turn financial information into better capital decisions.
Building a large finance organization to handle complexity. Scale should come from better systems, AI leverage, automation, and exceptional people, not layers of management.
Adding AI as a superficial productivity tool. You will architect workflows around its real capabilities and limitations, which requires substantial firsthand use.
Producing strategy decks without financial consequences. Major recommendations must carry the integrated model, downside case, capital implications, and execution guardrails behind them.
Managing the board through narrative. The numbers, assumptions, risks, and recommended action should be clear enough to withstand scrutiny.

Executive Vice President And Chief Financial Officer Key Responsibilities

You will define and own the multi-year AI product strategy and roadmap for the Solutions business unit, spanning agentic commerce, discovery, offer optimization and partner operations. You will turn that strategy into funded priorities, make trade-offs with executives, partners and engineering, and own outcomes including partner revenue, adoption, model quality and cost to serve. Six months: The team is staffed with builders and operating for speed, with clear ownership and rhythms with AI Product Operations and engineering; multiple AI products have gone from idea to live partner test in weeks.

10 or more years in product, including several years leading and developing product managers or applied AI teams, ideally in a B2B or platform business.
Hands-on experience designing and shipping ML, LLM or agent-based products that customers pay for, with a practical understanding of model drift, evaluation, hallucination, latency and cost trade-offs.
A track record of accelerating teams, hiring and developing builders, and moving products from idea to prototype to live partner test.
Strong commercial instincts: you connect product decisions to revenue, margin and partner outcomes, and collaborate effectively with engineering, data science, design and partner-facing teams.
Clear, direct communication with executives, partners and technical teams. Experience in travel, loyalty, e-commerce, marketplaces or pricing is an asset but not mandatory.

Travel is about the moments that make a journey feel personal. At Plusgrade, we build the technology that makes those moments possible, from upgrade offers and loyalty experiences to revenue tools used by 575+ airline, hospitality, cruise, rail, and financial services partners worldwide.

Job Description

The Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Data Center Development organization leads the planning, design, and delivery of the next generation of Oracle’s global data center portfolio. We are seeking a Senior Director of Data Center Development to provide strategic leadership and organizational oversight for the design of mission-critical infrastructure across OCI’s rapidly expanding global footprint.

This role is responsible for establishing and executing OCI’s data center design strategy across a portfolio of large-scale, highly complex developments. The Senior Director will lead a team of design management professionals and provide executive-level oversight of multidisciplinary design activities spanning architectural, structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, controls, and mission-critical infrastructure systems.

The position requires a combination of organizational leadership, technical depth, design governance, and portfolio management. The successful candidate will establish clear design requirements, drive consistency across projects and delivery partners, manage technical risk, and ensure that OCI’s facilities meet established requirements for performance, reliability, resiliency, scalability, constructability, and operational readiness.

The Senior Director will serve as a senior technical and organizational leader within OCI Data Center Development, partnering closely with Construction, Engineering, Operations, Network, Capacity Planning, Energy, Security, and other internal organizations. The role will also provide senior-level direction to colocation partners, architects, engineers, consultants, contractors, and other external stakeholders responsible for delivering OCI

Responsibilities

Responsibilities:

Lead the Data Center Design Management function for an assigned global or multi-region portfolio of hyperscale and mission-critical infrastructure projects.
Establish organizational priorities, expectations, governance processes, and performance standards for the design management team.
Lead, develop, and mentor design managers and design leadership personnel, establishing clear accountability for project execution, technical quality, and professional development.
Provide portfolio-level oversight of multidisciplinary data center design across architectural, structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, controls, life safety, and supporting infrastructure systems.
Establish and maintain design governance throughout the project lifecycle, from early planning and Basis of Design development through schematic design, design development, construction documentation, construction support, commissioning, and record documentation.
Ensure projects maintain alignment with OCI technical requirements, design standards, operational requirements, reliability objectives, and infrastructure strategies.
Provide senior technical leadership for high-density compute environments, including mechanical systems, liquid cooling, electrical infrastructure, controls, and other mission-critical systems supporting next-generation cloud and AI infrastructure.
Drive consistent implementation and continuous improvement of OCI global data center design standards, specifications, design criteria, and best practices.
Establish effective design review, technical approval, change management, and decision-making processes across the portfolio.
Identify systemic and project-specific design risks and ensure appropriate mitigation, escalation, and resolution before those risks impact construction, schedule, cost, reliability, or operations.
Lead resolution of complex multidisciplinary technical issues requiring coordination across internal organizations, design consultants, construction teams, operators, and external delivery partners.
Partner with Construction, Engineering, Operations, Network, Capacity Planning, Energy, Security, and other OCI organizations to ensure infrastructure requirements are coordinated and incorporated into project designs.
Provide senior-level oversight of architects, engineers, consultants, colocation providers, and other design partners responsible for delivering OCI infrastructure.
Establish expectations for consultant scope, performance, technical quality, schedule adherence, and design deliverables.
Ensure Basis of Design, SD, DD, permit, IFC, and record design packages meet OCI requirements and are appropriately reviewed and approved.
Drive standardization and repeatability while maintaining the flexibility necessary to address regional requirements, site conditions, utility constraints, code requirements, and evolving technology.
Evaluate proposed design changes and deviations to determine portfolio-level impacts to reliability, operations, schedule, cost, standards, and future scalability.
Develop and monitor design performance metrics, portfolio risks, technical issues, and organizational priorities, providing clear reporting and recommendations to executive leadership.
Support strategic planning for future data center capacity, emerging technologies, new infrastructure architectures, and evolving cloud and AI requirements.
Represent OCI Data Center Design Management in executive reviews, technical workshops, partner engagements, design reviews, and other internal and external forums.
Build a culture of technical rigor, accountability, collaboration, continuous improvement, and disciplined design governance across the organization.

Required Qualifications:

Professional licensure required as a Registered Architect (RA) or Professional Engineer (PE).
Accredited degree in Architecture, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Structural Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
12+ years of progressively responsible experience in data center, mission-critical, industrial, or large-scale infrastructure design and development.
Significant leadership experience managing design professionals, multidisciplinary technical teams, and external architecture and engineering organizations.
Demonstrated experience leading large-scale hyperscale, cloud, colocation, or mission-critical infrastructure programs.
Strong multidisciplinary understanding of data center architectural, structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, controls, life safety, and supporting infrastructure systems.
Demonstrated ability to establish and manage design governance, standards, technical requirements, and change control across multiple concurrent projects.
Experience managing complex project portfolios involving multiple sites, delivery partners, consultants, and internal stakeholders.
Strong understanding of data center mechanical and cooling infrastructure, with experience in high-density and liquid-cooled environments strongly preferred.
Strong understanding of data center electrical distribution, resiliency strategies, controls, commissioning, and operational requirements.
Demonstrated ability to identify, communicate, and resolve complex technical and organizational risks.
Experience working within accelerated design and construction programs where schedule, scalability, repeatability, and technical quality are critical.
Strong executive communication, organizational leadership, negotiation, and decision-making skills.
Ability to communicate complex technical issues clearly to both executive and technical audiences.
Working knowledge of applicable data center codes, standards, and industry guidance, including NFPA, ASHRAE, IBC, and other applicable international, national, and local requirements.

Preferred Qualifications:

15+ years of experience in mission-critical or large-scale infrastructure design and development.
Experience leading design organizations supporting hyperscale cloud or AI infrastructure.
Experience managing global or multi-region data center portfolios.
Experience developing and implementing enterprise-level data center design standards, specifications, and governance programs.
Experience with high-density compute environments, direct-to-chip liquid cooling, advanced thermal management, and next-generation data center infrastructure.
Experience with colocation and developer-led delivery models, including oversight of third-party design and construction partners.
Experience implementing formal design review, technical deviation, change management, and lessons-learned processes.
Working knowledge of BIM, digital design coordination, document management, and design collaboration platforms.
LEED AP, Uptime ATD, or other relevant mission-critical industry certifications.
Demonstrated experience developing high-performing technical teams and future organizational leaders.

jobs.title: Director, Global Strategy - Enterprise Planning
jobs.description:
Owning the design, governance, and continuous evolution of the enterprise planning system, ensuring strategic planning, annual operating planning, resource allocation, and performance reporting operate as an integrated enterprise process

 Leading the execution of the enterprise planning cycle, including Strategic Planning Kickoff, Long-Term Strategic Planning, and Quarterly Business Reviews, and partnering with Finance on Annual Operating Plan (AOP) and budget prioritization connected to business strategy

 Establishing and governing the enterprise planning cadence, ensuring cross-functional alignment, decision readiness, and the timely progression of key strategic milestones

 Building and maintaining the decision frameworks, governance structures, and planning standards that support enterprise-wide prioritization, accountability, and effective decision-making

 Partnering closely with Finance and business leaders to translate strategic priorities into actionable plans, resource allocation decisions, and measurable outcomes

 Leading the planning and coordination of Executive Committee and Board reviews, ensuring strategic issues are clearly framed, decisions are supported by relevant insights, and resulting actions are effectively tracked

 Managing the enterprise portfolio of strategic initiatives, tracking progress, interdependencies, risks, and outcomes while escalating issues requiring executive attention

 Developing scenarios, business cases, and trade-off analyses that enable leaders to evaluate opportunities, risks, investments, and resource allocation decisions

 Providing fact-based analysis, insights, and recommendations to support executive decision-making, prioritization, and enterprise performance discussions

 Establishing enterprise performance management frameworks, scorecards, KPIs, and reporting mechanisms that drive accountability, transparency, and execution against strategic objectives

 Driving alignment across executive leadership, functions, regions, Finance, and Amer Sports to establish a consistent enterprise planning and performance management operating model

 Maintaining visibility to key strategic and execution risks, ensuring mitigation plans are developed, monitored, and integrated into enterprise planning processes

 Developing executive-level communications, planning documents, and leadership briefings that translate complex business information into clear priorities, recommendations, and actions

 Serving as the steward of enterprise planning effectiveness, continuously evaluating planning processes, governance, and reporting mechanisms to improve decision quality, organizational alignment, and business outcomes

 Developing and maintaining the tools, templates, governance processes, and planning methodologies that strengthen enterprise planning capability and support execution against strategic and business plans
Evolving the enterprise planning system as the business scales—adding new planning horizons, integrating regional complexity, and improving the speed and quality of decisions

 Building repeatable frameworks and playbooks for planning processes that reduce dependency on heroic individual effort and increase organizational capability

 Partnering with Finance and regional teams to develop integrated financial and strategic planning models that connect long-range ambition to annual resource reality

 Developing the next generation of performance management tools—moving from tracking to accountability, and from reporting to action

 Supporting the Strategy team’s broader operating model evolution as new capability areas come online
You have a bachelor’s degree in business, strategy, or related field

 You have 10+ years of professional work experience in strategic planning, management consulting, project management, consumer products and/or retail

 You have a demonstrated track record as an outstanding problem solver and strategic You think in systems – you can see how the strategic planning connects to the budget planning, how the QBR connects to accountability, and how the strategic calendar creates or destroys leadership bandwidth

 You are a credible executive partner with the communication skills to work directly with a CDR and functional leaders, and to translate complexity into decisions

 You have significant experience partnering with Finance on resource allocation, budget prioritization, and performance tracking

 You bring sharp analytical capability and strong written communication, and you can build a rigorous framework and write a clear executive brief

 You have experience working across regional and global operating models, ideally with exposure to retail or consumer-facing businesses

 You are organized without being rigid, and you know when the plan needs to change and how to move the system accordingly

 You demonstrate high emotional intelligence, sound judgment, and the ability to influence without authority across senior stakeholders

 You hold yourself and others to a high standard for quality of thinking, clarity of communication, and follow-through
The salary range for this role is CAD$149,000 - CAD$195,000
