jobs.description:
Description And Requirements

The Director of Project Finance & M&A is responsible for leading financial analysis, structuring and financial due diligence for mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, and strategic investments in renewable energy assets and platforms across the United States and Canada.

Reporting to the Head of Finance & Insurance, this role plays a central role in evaluating transaction opportunities, structuring project financings, and supporting capital formation activities, including tax equity, tax credit transferability, and project debt.

The Director will work closely with the M&A, Business Development, Legal, Tax, and Asset Management teams, as well as external advisors and capital providers, to ensure robust financial evaluation and optimal financing structures for investments and operating assets.

The role requires strong expertise in renewable energy project finance, financial modeling, tax equity structures, transferability, and project-level debt financing.

To maximize collaboration and innovation, an essential function of this role is a regular onsite presence in an Enel office. 

The Instrument and Controls Specialist is responsible to support execute and provide configuration and maintenance services for the Process Control System and other automation systems at the Enel Green Power Facilities for Solar assets. Ensure facility controls automation and machinery function safely, efficiently, reliably and within budgetary limits, utilizing allocated resources, with the objective of meeting business goals for production while minimizing unscheduled equipment down time. Provide day-to-day maintenance activities and provide mentoring/coaching to less experienced employees.

What you will do Responsibilities, include, but not limited to:

M&A Financial Due Diligence and Transaction Support

Lead financial due diligence for acquisitions, divestitures, and joint venture transactions, including review of project financial models, assumptions, capital structures, and financing arrangements.

Evaluate project economics, financing structures, tax attributes, and key commercial contracts to identify financial risks and value drivers.

Coordinate with internal teams and external advisors on buy-side and sell-side transaction processes, including data room review, financial analysis, and diligence reporting.

Prepare investment committee materials, valuation analyses, and transaction recommendations for senior management.

Project Finance Structuring

Support the origination, negotiation, and closing of project financings including tax equity partnerships, transferability transactions, and term debt facilities.

Coordinate closely with lenders, tax equity investors, transferability buyers, and financial advisors during transaction execution.

Analyze and structure tax equity partnership transactions, including partnership flip structures and related financial modeling.

Conduct sensitivity analysis, valuation analysis, and financing optimization scenarios.

Ensure modeling assumptions are aligned with project contracts, tax structures, and financing agreements.

Provide financial input into investment committee materials and strategic decision processes.

Work closely with M&A, Development, Valuation, Legal, Tax, and Asset Management teams to support project execution and investment decision making.

What you will bring

Education

Master’s degree in Finance, Economics, Business Administration or related field

Experience

MBA, CFA or other professional designation preferred

Minimum 6–8 years of experience in project finance, investment banking, or renewable energy transactions

Direct experience with M&A financial due diligence and transaction execution

Demonstrated experience with tax equity structures, tax credit transferability transactions, and project debt financing

Experience In Renewable Energy Or Power Sector Required

Technical Skills

Advanced financial modeling and valuation skills

Strong understanding of project finance structures and capital markets

Experience reviewing and negotiating financing term sheets and transaction documentation

Professional Skills

Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities

Excellent written and verbal communication skills

Ability to present complex financial analysis to senior management

Strong negotiation and stakeholder management capabilities

Ability to manage multiple transaction processes simultaneously

Why join us?

Please see below for additional information on Enel North America rewards.

Enel North America offers its regular full-time employees affordable, quality healthcare for you and your family, life insurance and disability benefits to provide security, and retirement benefits to help you plan for your financial future. In addition, we offer an array of other benefits such as flexible spending accounts, tuition reimbursement and professional development allowance. 

Benefits are effective as of day one! 

Some additional perks to working with Enel North America include: 

401k with match fully vested as of day one. Enel-NA matches 100% of the first 4% that you contribute up to set IRS limits. 

Generous PTO that supports work/life balance including: 4 weeks annually of vacation as well as personal days, volunteer days, your birthday off, paid holidays, and sick time. Proration may apply during first year of employment. 

Paid leave programs 

The opportunity to grow and develop your career with the support and mentorship of senior leaders. 

The opportunity to work for one of the world’s most recognizable and respected brands in the energy industry that believes by working together we can create a new energy era in which the world can become more sustainable. 

An employee’s eligibility for these benefits shall be subject to the governing documents for such plans and programs and/or company policy. The benefits described above may be modified or eliminated with or without notice in accordance with the governing documents and applicable law.

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and the Selection Process

Enel North America is dedicated to providing equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender, national origin, citizenship, age, disability, sexual orientation, genetic information. We will not discriminate, in any employment decision, against any individual or group on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, gender, national origin, citizenship, age, disability, sexual orientation, genetic information, or veterans/national guard/military reserve status. This shall be done in compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local laws in every location in which Enel North America has facilities. Enel North America maintains a drug-free workplace and performs pre-employment substance abuse testing and background checks, where permitted by law. Accessibility – If you require accessibility assistance applying for open positions please contact EnelApplication@enel.com.

The selection process includes an initial introductory interview with the Recruiting team, followed by an interview with the relevant business line. If your profile matches the requirements of the role, we will contact you to share all the details of the next steps.

Enel North America is committed to providing a fair and transparent hiring process for all job seekers. We will never ask you to pay money or provide sensitive information, such as your social security number or bank account number, as part of the application process. We only hire through our official channels, which include our website and LinkedIn page. If you receive a job offer that did not come through one of those channels, it is likely a scam, and we suggest reporting it to the authorities.

We are looking for individuals who embody our values: trust, respect, innovation, proactivity, and flexibility.

Do you want to be a part of change? Apply now and join the Solar O&M team to help drive the energy transition with us!

Notice to Recruiters & Staffing Agencies

Enel North America has an internal talent acquisition department and designated career site for individuals looking to join our team. Enel North America will not accept unsolicited resumes from any external recruiters, staffing firms, search agencies or any fee-based referrals. Any unsolicited resumes sent to directly to Enel North America, in any capacity will be considered property of Enel North America. This policy is applicable to all Enel North America locations and will be the responsibility of third parties and vendors to understand this policy. Enel North America will not pay a fee for any placement resulting from the receipt of an unsolicited resume.

Who we are

Enel North America:

Enel North America is a proven renewables leader delivering clean, flexible and sustainable energy solutions.

As part of the Enel Group, we develop, build, own and operate renewable power plants and demand response solutions, with over 11 gigawatts (GW) of installed wind and solar capacity, over 1 GW of energy storage and nearly 5 GW of demand response in the US and Canada.

For nearly 25 years, we've reliably powered modern life and driven climate action with our people, partners and communities by putting sustainability at the center of everything we do. Enel is a top-five industry leader for clean power capacity in the US, demand response in North America and utility-scale battery storage in Texas.

We are a smart and passionate team working together to build the Enel North America that we want for the long-term – one that is founded on strong financial, social and environmental values. Being on our team means being part of lasting progress to create a thriving and more sustainable world for our climate and communities. It means valuing safety, trust, innovation, proactivity, flexibility and respect in all we do. Our vision is ambitious, and we'll get there together.

Enel Spa

Enel is a multinational power company and a leading integrated player in the global power and renewables markets, present in 27 countries worldwide.

At global level, it is the largest renewable player, the foremost electricity distribution network player by number of grid customers served and the biggest retail operator by customer base.

Enel generates electricity with approximately 93 GW of total capacity. Enel Green Power, the Group’s renewables arm, has a total capacity of approximately 68 GW and a generation mix that includes wind, solar, geothermal, and hydroelectric power, as well as energy storage facilities, installed in Europe, the Americas, Africa, Asia, and Oceania.

Enel Grids, the Group’s global business line dedicated to the management of the electricity distribution service worldwide, delivers electricity through a network of 1.9 million kilometers with more than 69 million end users connected to its distribution grids. Enel Commercial is the Group’s arm dedicated to customers around the world with the aim of effectively providing products and services based on their energy needs and encouraging them towards a more conscious and sustainable use of energy. It provides electricity, gas and integrated services to more than 29 million customers globally including households, enterprises, industries and public administrations. In addition, it offers flexibility services aggregating 10.2 GW and has over 34,000 owned public charging points for electric mobility.

Curious about us? Discover more at www.enel.com

jobs.title: Finance Director, Canada
jobs.description:
WHO ARE WE?

At Nexans our global vision is to electrify the future. For over a century, Nexans has played a crucial role in the electrification of the planet. With around 28,000 people in 42 countries, the Group is leading the charge to the new world of electrification: safer, sustainable, renewable, decarbonized and accessible to everyone Nexans recognizes the differences that make each employee valuable and unique.

WELCOMING YOU TO THE TEAM

Our story starts in 1911, manufacturing cables to support the distribution of power generated from Niagara Falls, Nexans has proudly contributed to Canada's growth. We have been involved in many of Canada's most ambitious projects; from dams, bridges, energy transmission and distribution to railroads and transportation. We are a vertically integrated manufacturer and our products are made at facilities located in Quebec, Ontario, and Saskatchewan.

As Finance Director, Canada, you will report directly to the VP Finance, North America. This role is being created as part of the North American transformation, establishing dedicated Canadian and US organizations under a new North American business group. The Finance Director will provide financial leadership for the Canadian business, partnering closely with the broader North American leadership team to drive financial performance and support the growth and development of the Canadian organization

GETTING TO KNOW THE POSITION

One of the strategic orientations that Nexans pursues consists in capturing growth and differentiating its offer by escalading the value chain from the production of cables towards the provision of innovative cable systems and services and solutions to better address the current and future needs of our partners and customers.

The Finance Director, Canada is responsible for driving the financial performance of the Canadian Business Unit in alignment with NAM objectives. The role oversees financial planning, budgeting, reporting, and controls, while ensuring compliance with Group policies and supporting sound business decisions. The Finance Director also leads and develops the Canadian finance team, partnering with the business to optimize financial performance and resources.

How You Make An Impact

Financial Strategy & Business Performance

Directs and oversees the financial activities of the Canadian organization, ensuring strong financial performance, sound governance, and alignment with Nexans Group and North American objectives.
Provides strategic financial leadership and insight to support business decisions, including investments, acquisitions, divestitures, capital allocation, pension matters, and other strategic initiatives.
Provides timely and accurate financial analysis, reporting, forecasts, and business indicators to support decision-making by Canadian and North American senior management, Nexans Corporate, and COMEX.
Acts as a strategic business partner to the leadership team and operational functions, providing financial expertise and challenging assumptions to support profitable and sustainable growth.
Monitors business and market trends, including relevant competitor and economic developments, and provides financial insights to support the organization's positioning and decision-making.
Provides financial advice and support in the negotiation and review of strategic commercial contracts and agreements, including contracts with significant financial, commodity, or foreign exchange exposure.

Planning, Budgeting & Forecasting

Leads the annual budgeting, forecasting, and financial planning processes, ensuring alignment with business objectives and Group requirements.
Continually improves the budgeting and forecasting process by strengthening financial discipline and developing the financial understanding of department and business leaders.
Oversees the monitoring of financial performance against budget, forecast, and business objectives, identifying risks, opportunities, and corrective actions.
Provides financial analysis and recommendations to support cost optimization and improve overall business performance.

Financial Reporting & Governance

Defines and oversees the monthly consolidated reporting process, including sales, P&L, MMR, and other key financial indicators for the Canadian organization and North American Business Group.
Ensures the timely and accurate preparation and consolidation of financial reports, management analysis, forecasts, and financial outlooks.
Ensures compliance with applicable accounting standards, Group policies, IFRS, and Canadian accounting and regulatory requirements.
Establishes, implements, and maintains appropriate financial policies, procedures, systems, and internal controls to safeguard company assets and ensure the integrity and reliability of financial information.
Represents Finance in internal and external audits and ensures timely follow-up and resolution of audit findings.

Cash, Treasury, Tax & Risk Management

Develops and implements strategies to optimize cash flow, working capital, liquidity, and overall financial performance.
Oversees treasury activities, banking relationships, credit policies, and other areas impacting the organization's cash position and financial resilience.
Ensures, in coordination with Nexans Corporate and relevant internal stakeholders, compliance with applicable Canadian tax requirements and monitors changes in legislation that may impact the business.
Identifies, assesses, and manages key financial and business risks, ensuring appropriate mitigation measures and controls are in place.
Provides financial guidance on matters involving foreign exchange, commodity exposure, financing, and other financial risks, as applicable.

Finance Transformation & Continuous Improvement

Leads initiatives to optimize financial processes, strengthen cost control, improve reporting efficiency, and increase the automation and digitalization of Finance activities.
Drives continuous improvement of Finance systems, processes, and controls to improve the overall efficiency, effectiveness, and quality of financial operations.
Ensures that Finance policies, procedures, and systems evolve in line with the organization's changing business needs and Group requirements.

Finance Leadership & Organizational Effectiveness

Leads and develops the Finance organization, ensuring appropriate capabilities, performance, succession, and professional development to support the organization's financial objectives.
Continuously assesses the effectiveness and organizational structure of the Finance function and implements improvements to enhance efficiency and business support.
Promotes a strong culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous improvement, compliance, and business partnership within the Finance organization.

North American & Group Collaboration

Supports and contributes to North American strategic initiatives and synergies, including cross-functional initiatives defined as NAM priorities.
Collaborates closely with Nexans Corporate, North American leadership, and other Finance leaders to ensure alignment of financial strategies, reporting, controls, and business priorities.
Provides financial support and analysis for major North American and Group initiatives, ensuring appropriate financial evaluation, risk assessment, and follow-up.
Ensures effective communication of financial performance, risks, opportunities, and recommendations to senior leadership and relevant stakeholders.

You will be expected to:

About Kinaxis

Are you looking to join an innovative, market-leading company where you can truly elevate your career? At Kinaxis we are serious about culture, we are serious about technology, we are serious about customers, and we are serious about not taking ourselves too seriously. If you are looking to be part of an incredible growth story, then we might just be the place for you!

In 1984, we started out as a team of three engineers. Today, we have grown to become a global organization with over 2000 employees around the world, 6 global office and a best-in-class HQ in Ottawa, Canada. As winners of several Top Employer awards globally, we are proud to work with our customers and employees towards solving some of the biggest challenges facing supply chains today.

Kinaxis is a global leader in modern supply chain orchestration, powering complex global supply chains, and supporting the people who manage them. Our powerful, AI infused platform provides full transparency and visibility across end-to-end supply chains, enabling our customers to make faster, better decisions. We are trusted by renowned global brands to provide the agility and predictability needed to navigate today’s volatility and disruption. With more than 40,000 users in over 100 countries, we are expanding our team as we continue to innovate and revolutionize how we support our customers.

Location

Ottawa and Toronto, CA - Hybrid

Other Canadian locations - Remote

About The Team

Our Financial Planning and Analysis (FP&A) team partners with leaders across the company to help drive business decisions. They work with stakeholders to highlight insights and analysis needed to make data-driven decisions that help fuel growth and operational excellence. The Director, Financial Planning & Analysis, is a trusted advisor and subject matter expert who brings a depth and breadth of knowledge and expertise in leading, directing, and developing the overall operations and delivery of revenue forecasting, consolidated forecasts and reporting, external metrics, and evolving financial planning strategies within Kinaxis.

This role is ideal for a forward-thinking finance leader who combines deep financial expertise with strong business acumen, operational excellence, and a passion for transforming finance through data, automation, and AI-enabled insights.

Partnering closely with the VP, Financial Planning & Analysis the Director, Financial Planning & Analysis is responsible for effective management and continuous improvement of budgeting and forecasting cycles and provides strategic financial consultation and support to the business.

Vacancy Status

This is an existing job vacancy

What you will do

Business Performance & FP&A Excellence

Build an integrated, enterprise-wide planning process across business units and regions to drive business objectives and long-term growth.
Develop key financial models and scenarios to evaluate strategic initiatives and investments, with a view to multi-year projections.
Lead scenario planning, sensitivity analysis, and financial modeling to support strategic decisions.
Manage and drive management reporting – analyze financial results, distill and synthesize issues and communicate key messages (including business risks) to the senior leadership team.
Support Board reporting, executive presentations, and investor reporting and communications.
Deliver actionable financial insights that influence investment priorities, resource allocation, pricing, and growth initiatives.
Demonstrated outstanding communication and executive presentation skills, with the ability to translate complex financial information into clear business insights.
Develop KPIs and performance dashboards that provide timely visibility into business health.
Foster strong partnerships across the organization including Product, Sales, Corporate Functions and other teams.

Finance Transformation & Technology

Modernize FP&A through automation, AI-enabled analytics, and scalable planning technologies.
Propose and implement continuous improvement of strategies, processes, systems, and policies to enhance the speed and effectiveness of forecasting and reporting.
Establish best-in-class planning processes, governance, and data quality.
Champion the use of modern planning platforms and business intelligence tools.

Leadership

Build, mentor, and develop a high-performing global FP&A organization.
Create a culture of accountability, curiosity, continuous improvement, and business partnership.
Lead organizational change and finance transformation initiatives across a global business, including exploring additional areas to implement AI initiatives.

What we are looking for

Post-secondary education in Finance, Accounting, Business, or a related field.
Professional accounting designation(CPA or legacy CA, CMA or CGA), CFA, or MBA.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, investment banking, private equity, or corporate finance, ideally with some experience in a high-tech, global, publicly traded organization.
Experience leading teams with direct and indirect reports.
Demonstrated financial acumen and expertise in data and financial modeling and scenario planning.
Advanced analytical, problem solving, and critical-thinking skills with the ability to coordinate input from multiple sources to develop impactful recommendations to achieve results for the business.
An articulate and professional communicator with the ability to provide clear, concise messaging to multiple audiences and present complex information across the organization.
Strong relationship-building and influencing skills and the ability to prioritize business requirements appropriately through a collaborative partnership approach.
Demonstrated ability to coordinate input from multiple complex sources, conduct environmental scanning, and sort through ambiguity to develop impactful recommendations for business decisions.
Deep and broad knowledge of financial analysis, forecasting, budgeting, and management reporting, including oversight of the annual financial planning process and related best practices.
Exceptional financial modelling skills with great attention to detail and the ability to distill complex issues into structured, actionable frameworks.
Highly proficient in Excel and PowerPoint, particularly for financial modeling, financial and data analysis, and presenting business cases or transaction summaries.
Ability to apply a structured problem-solving framework to ambiguous situations and drive decisions under tight timelines.
Significant experience developing business cases supported by financial analysis and modeling, with the ability to collaborate cross-functionally across the organization.

#Director

Our platform directly helps companies power the world’s supply chains. We see the results of what we do out in the world every day, when we see store shelves stocked, when medications are available for our loved ones, and so much more.

Companies across industries trust us to help them take control of their integrated business planning and digital supply chain. Some of our customers include Lockheed Martin, Unilever, P&G, ExxonMobil, Cisco and more.

ABOUT EMILY CARR UNIVERSITY OF ART + DESIGN

Situated on unceded, traditional and ancestral xʷməθkʷəy̓əm (Musqueam), Sḵwx̱wú7mesh Úxwumixw (Squamish), and səl̓ilw̓ətaʔɬ (Tsleil-Waututh) territories in Vancouver, Canada, Emily Carr University of Art + Design (ECU) is where creativity meets practice. Ranked among the world’s top 30 universities for art and design (QS 2024), ECU is recognized globally for its hands-on, practice-based teaching and learning environment that equips students to experiment, take risks and drive innovation.

Since 1925, ECU has championed bold ideas and emerging talent through a close-knit, studio-intensive setting that connects students with award-winning faculty, cutting-edge facilities, and real-world opportunities. Today, ECU serves more than 2,400 undergraduate and graduate students, along with thousands more through continuing studies, contributing to Canada’s cultural and creative sectors and shaping the future of art, media, design and research.

Having marked our centennial in 2025, ECU continues to ask what art and design can make possible.100 years in the making, we are shaping what comes next.

About The Role

Reporting to the Vice-President, Finance + Administration, the Director, Financial Services is responsible for leading the University in the ongoing process of continuous improvement in business and accounting practices. This position is responsible for the administration of financial policy, the overall management of accounting operations, financial report systems, and the monitoring of financial performance in accordance with University policy. The Director provides leadership and direction to the Finance Department and ensures the integrity of data in a complex integrated database (Colleague). A key function of the Director is to translate unstructured ideas into coherent presentations suitable for implementation according to the University’s needs.

Benefits Of Joining The Emily Carr Community

Enrollment in a comprehensive benefits package, including Dental Coverage, Extended Health, Disability Coverage and Life Insurance.
Membership in the College Pension Plan.
Competitive vacation and Professional Development benefits.

AS THE SUCCESSFUL APPLICANT, YOU SHOULD POSSESS

Professional designation in accounting from a recognized educational institution (CPA).
Minimum ten years of progressively responsible experience in financial and administrative management.
Expertise in budget planning, financial management and control, as well as administration of budget and financial resources.
Extensive experience with computer based accounting systems and large database.
Demonstrated knowledge in area of expertise, along with supervisory and leadership experience.
Expert communication, interpersonal and presentation skills with the ability to build relationships and cooperation on a University-wide level.
Ability to set and communicate high standards for group performance within the Financial Services department and to facilitate and motivate teamwork.
Strong analytical skills with the ability to apply sound judgement in problem solving and evaluate courses of action.
Ability to advise on and make complex financial decisions.
Strong computer skills with advanced proficiency in Word, Excel and PowerPoint.

Typical Duties

Develops, administers, and ensures compliance with guidelines, policies and procedures for effective financial management of the University’s resources leading to continuous improvement in business and accounting practices.
Reviews and prepares analyses of financial information and ensures the completion of both internal and external financial reports by communicated deadlines, including all provincial and federal reporting requirements.
Responds to requests for ad hoc information from the VP, Finance + Administration, the President + Vice-Chancellor, administrative management, and external agencies, and provides effective counsel and assistance.
Participates as required in short and long range strategic planning, collaborating with administrative management and producing coherent implementation plans from unstructured proposals.
Designs and maintains an internal control framework for the Financial Services area such that business loss is mitigated.
Manages cash flow requirements and invests surplus funds in line with established investment policy.
Responsible for the year-end audit processes and reviews preparation of annual working papers and financial statements for external auditors. Manages the preparation of analysis and supporting documents for review by the VP, Finance + Administration and the Ministry of Post-Secondary Education and Future Skills.
Directly supervises the management positions within Financial Services and ensures all responsibilities are carried out effectively. Maintains oversight of the Financial Services department staff including recruitment and selection, orientation, performance planning and review and ongoing training and development.
Collaborates with the Associate Vice-President, Human Resources in hiring, discipline, dismissal and grievance procedures and collective agreement administration relating to support staff. Produces labour costing for collective bargaining and participates directly in collective agreement negotiations.
Arranges for tenders of University banking services and external audits, establishing criteria to make decisions and providing reports and recommendations to the VP, Finance + Administration and the Board.
Responsible for the preparation of the annual budget. Responsible for ensuring the completion of weekly cheque runs, ensuring appropriate audit and authorization is performed before processing.

Manages the department budget and is responsible for expenditures and allocations within that budget.
Collaborates with the Executive Director, University Advancement + Events to maintain detailed financial records and provides advice on the management of endowed funds.
Acts for the VP, Finance + Administration in his/her absence.
Performs other related duties as required.

jobs.description:
Organization: Cambridge Memorial Hospital
Position: Director, Finance
Location: Cambridge, ON (on-site)
Salary: $155,000 - $185,000

THE ORGANIZATION
Cambridge Memorial Hospital (CMH) is more than a hospital: they are a cornerstone of a vibrant, rapidly growing community and an organization in transformation. Following a major redevelopment and expansion, CMH is redefining what exceptional community healthcare looks like, delivering high-quality, patient-centred care while building for the future. CMH is building healthier communities together . As a thriving acute care hospital serving the Waterloo Wellington Region and beyond, CMH provides comprehensive services including Emergency, Surgery, Medicine, Women’s and Children’s Health, Intensive Care, and Mental Health.

As healthcare continues to evolve, CMH is seeking an accomplished and forward-thinking Director, Finance to join our senior leadership team. This is a rare opportunity to influence strategy at an organization that combines the complexity of a large healthcare environment with the agility, collegiality, and impact of a community hospital.

As healthcare funding models evolve and system pressures increase, CMH is seeking a strategic and forward-thinking Director, Finance to play a critical leadership role in ensuring the organization’s long-term financial sustainability and operational excellence. This is a high-impact opportunity to serve as a trusted financial advisor to the Executive Team and Board Committees while leading a dedicated finance team in delivering robust financial stewardship in a complex healthcare environment

THE OPPORTUNITY
Reporting to the Vice President, Corporate Services & Chief Financial Officer the Director, Finance provides enterprise-wide leadership and oversight of the hospital’s financial operations, planning, reporting, treasury, and internal control environment.
Working at the intersection of finance, operations, and strategy, the Director will help guide the organization through evolving funding models, growth opportunities, capital investments, and system transformation initiatives.

The Director is responsible for advancing financial strategy, strengthening fiscal stewardship, optimizing funding opportunities, and ensuring regulatory compliance, while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement. As a key leader, the Director partners closely with clinical and operational leaders to align financial planning with organizational priorities. This role extends far beyond traditional financial oversight.

The Director is a trusted advisor and business partner who helps shape organizational strategy, supports critical decision-making, identifies opportunities for innovation and efficiency, and ensures CMH remains well-positioned to thrive in an increasingly complex healthcare environment.

As Director, Finance, you will drive strategic decision-making through:
Providing financial leadership and insight to the Executive Team, Directors' Council, and Board Committees, ensuring leaders have the information and analysis needed to make confident, informed decisions.
Leading long-range financial planning, capital planning, and sustainability strategies that support CMH's vision for growth and excellence.
Navigating evolving provincial funding models and healthcare priorities while identifying opportunities to optimize resources and strengthen organizational performance.
Developing and mentoring an engaged, talented finance team while fostering a culture of accountability, innovation, collaboration, and continuous learning.
Collaborating closely with clinical and operational leaders, the CMH Foundation, and community partners to support strategic initiatives, business cases, capital investments, and service enhancements.

IDEAL CANDIDATE
A senior leader with passion for healthcare and community impact.
Strong experience in hospitals with a minimum of 7–10 years of progressive financial experience navigating complexity and driving meaningful change.
Experience working within a publicly funded environment and familiarity with Ministry of Health reporting requirements.
Proven success leading budgeting, forecasting, audit, and financial reporting functions.
Experience presenting financial information to senior leadership and/or Board Committees.
The ability to think strategically with strong business and financial acumen while maintaining operational excellence.
Strong relationship-building and influencing skills and a collaborative leadership style that inspires confidence and trust and an ability to engage across disciplines.
Clear, confident communicator capable of translating complex financial information for diverse audiences.
Ability to lead effectively in a dynamic and evolving healthcare environment and a commitment to developing people and building high-performing teams.
Exceptional analytical and problem-solving skills.
Advanced knowledge of MIS guidelines, systems implementations, financial systems, financial modelling and advanced spreadsheet applications.
Familiarity with procurement practices and the Broader Public Sector Procurement Directive is an asset.
Bachelor’s degree in Commerce, Business, Finance, or related field.
Professional accounting designation (CPA or equivalent).

The Director, Finance role is a current existing vacancy. LHH Knightsbridge does not use artificial intelligence (AI) to screen, assess, or select applicants for a position.

At Cambridge Memorial Hospital (CMH), community matters to us. We acknowledge and are grateful for the opportunity to meet, work and offer healthcare on what is the traditional territories for the Anishinaabe, the Haudenosaunee and the Chinnonton.

We are committed to providing and fostering a respectful, caring, and inclusive workplace; one that generates belonging. We want a work culture where people are free to express their authentic selves and are able to bring their best daily. That includes a workplace that is free from violence, harassment and discrimination of any kind.

We welcome all applicants and encourage members of equity-deserving groups including Indigenous and LGBTQ2SIA+ communities regardless of race, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, lifestyle, age, educational background, national origin, religion, neurodiversity or physical ability. We promise to ask if needed, and to provide reasonable accommodation to you during the recruitment and selection process to ensure an equitable experience.

To support all of us in this journey, Cambridge Memorial Hospital is an employee partner with the Canadian Centre for Diversity & Inclusion (CCDI) and provides access to all CMH members to CCDI resources and education. We encourage you to reflect upon our inclusive commitment to you as we welcome and encourage you to explore a promising future career at CMH.

jobs.description:
We're transforming the grocery industry 

 At Instacart, we invite the world to share love through food because we believe everyone should have access to the food they love and more time to enjoy it together. Where others see a simple need for grocery delivery, we see exciting complexity and endless opportunity to serve the varied needs of our community. We work to deliver an essential service that customers rely on to get their groceries and household goods, while also offering safe and flexible earnings opportunities to Instacart Personal Shoppers. 

 Instacart has become a lifeline for millions of people, and we’re building the team to help push our shopping cart forward. If you’re ready to do the best work of your life, come join our table.

 Instacart is a Flex First team 

 There’s no one-size fits all approach to how we do our best work. Our employees have the flexibility to choose where they do their best work—whether it’s from home, an office, or your favorite coffee shop—while staying connected and building community through regular in-person events. Learn more about our flexible approach to where we work. 

 Overview 

 Instacart’s Enterprise AI team is building the next generation of intelligent solutions for retailers. We are seeking a Director of Enterprise AI Engineering and Machine Learning to lead the development of agentic AI products that help retailers solve complex business challenges and unlock new opportunities.

 In this role, you will work at the intersection of engineering, machine learning, data science, product, consulting, and forward-deployed engineering. You will partner directly with retailers and internal stakeholders to define ambitious opportunities, shape technical strategy, and deliver innovative solutions in a rapidly evolving, zero-to-one product environment.

 This is an opportunity to help establish a new area of innovation at Instacart while leading teams through the full product development lifecycle—from identifying customer needs and exploring emerging technologies to building, deploying, and scaling production-ready AI systems.

 About the Job 

 Lead the engineering and machine learning strategy for agentic AI solutions designed to address the needs of Instacart’s retail partners.

 Build, mentor, and inspire high-performing engineering and science teams, creating an environment that supports technical excellence, experimentation, and strong execution.

 Partner directly with retailers, product leaders, consultants, data scientists, machine learning engineers, and forward-deployed engineers to translate complex business problems into impactful AI products.

 Guide the development of systems that combine advanced machine learning, data, software engineering, and agentic capabilities, with an emphasis on reliability, scalability, usability, and measurable customer value.

 Establish direction in a zero-to-one product space, balancing long-term technical strategy with the need to move quickly, learn from early deployments, and adapt to changing customer and business requirements.

 Represent Enterprise AI across the organization, communicating tradeoffs, progress, risks, and opportunities to senior stakeholders and building alignment across technical and commercial teams.

 You will be joining a fast-paced environment where the technology, customer needs, and product direction will continue to evolve. Success will require comfort with ambiguity, a willingness to engage deeply in both strategy and execution, and the judgment to make thoughtful decisions while building new capabilities from the ground up.

  

 About You 

 Minimum Qualifications

 Demonstrated experience building and deploying agentic AI, generative AI, or machine learning products in production environments.

 Experience leading engineering, machine learning, data science, or applied science teams through product development and delivery.

 Experience partnering with product, business, customer-facing, and technical stakeholders to define requirements and deliver solutions to complex problems.

 Strong understanding of machine learning development practices, software engineering principles, data systems, and the operational considerations required to scale AI applications.

 Demonstrated ability to set technical direction, prioritize work, manage ambiguity, and deliver results in a fast-changing environment.

 Preferred Qualifications

 Deep technical expertise in agentic systems, large language models, machine learning platforms, or related areas of applied artificial intelligence.

 Experience delivering applied machine learning products at significant scale, including systems used by external customers or business partners.

 Experience leading cross-functional initiatives that span engineering, machine learning, data science, product, consulting, and customer-facing teams.

 Experience working directly with retailers, commerce platforms, or other enterprise customers to translate operational challenges into technology solutions.

 A track record of creating clarity and momentum in zero-to-one product environments while maintaining high standards for quality, responsible development, and customer impact.

Children’s Treatment Network (CTN) supports over 42,000 kids and youth with disabilities and other developmental needs. Funded by the Ministry of Children, Community and Social Services, CTN is an Ontario provincial government funded not\-for profit organization, that offers services through contracted partners in the education, health and community sectors. Through its innovative network model, CTN’s commitment to providing family\-centered care is anchored by an electronic client record that is shared across its partner organizations and provides the foundation for integrated plans of care and services.

Through Monks.Flow, its flagship AI ecosystem for marketing orchestration, Monks transforms marketing into a growth engine, collapsing timelines and connecting brands to culture in real time. jobs.title: Director, Enterprise AI Strategy & Transformation
jobs.description:
Job Purpose

Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, the Director, Enterprise AI Strategy & Transformation leads the development and execution of the organization’s enterprise AI strategy and transformation agenda to drive measurable business value, productivity, operational efficiency, innovation, and informed decision-making. The role serves as the organization’s AI subject matter expert and enterprise coordinating point, providing strategic guidance on AI opportunities, investments, governance, risk, technology, adoption, and value realization.

The Director partners with business and functional leaders to identify, prioritize, and implement AI and intelligent automation opportunities aligned with organizational objectives and financial goals. The role initially focuses on leveraging AI to enhance financial and operational performance, including forecasting, reporting, analysis, productivity, workflow efficiency, cost management, and decision-making, with successful capabilities and practices progressively expanded across other functions. The Director oversees the enterprise AI portfolio and lifecycle from opportunity assessment and business case development through solution selection, implementation, adoption, benefits realization, ongoing monitoring, and retirement.

Key Duties And Responsibilities

AI Strategy, Portfolio & Value Management

Develop and maintain the enterprise AI strategy, operating model, portfolio, and roadmap aligned with corporate objectives and financial goals.
Identify, evaluate, and prioritize AI opportunities based on strategic alignment, business value, cost, complexity, data readiness, risk, and organizational readiness.
Develop business cases, investment recommendations, and implementation roadmaps, including build, buy, configure, or partner options.
Establish performance measures, baseline metrics, and value-realization frameworks to track AI adoption, ROI, productivity, cost savings, revenue impact, and other business outcomes.
Provide executive leadership with visibility into AI investments, performance, realized benefits, opportunities, and risks.

AI Solution Development & Implementation

Lead the evaluation, design, development, and deployment of AI solutions across enterprise productivity, function-specific applications, intelligent automation, advanced AI, and emerging agentic capabilities.
Partner with business units and end users to identify opportunities, develop practical AI-enabled solutions, and improve processes and ways of working.
Oversee AI pilots, proofs of concept, and enterprise implementations through the full lifecycle—from opportunity identification and feasibility through deployment, adoption, benefits realization, monitoring, and retirement.
Coordinate with Cybersecurity, Human Resources and other stakeholders to ensure solutions are appropriately designed, implemented, adopted, and measured.
Assess solution performance and recommend whether initiatives should be scaled, enhanced, consolidated, paused, or retired based on business value, adoption, cost, and risk.

AI Governance, Risk & Responsible Adoption

Establish and maintain enterprise AI governance frameworks, policies, standards, controls, and risk-based processes to support responsible AI adoption.
Ensure AI initiatives are appropriately assessed for cybersecurity, privacy, data, intellectual property, legal, ethical, third-party, model, and business continuity risks.
Maintain an enterprise inventory of approved AI technologies, platforms, models, agents, and material use cases, with appropriate review, approval, testing, human oversight, monitoring, and escalation requirements.
Ensure data quality, classification, access, security, information governance, and regulatory requirements are addressed before AI solutions are deployed.
Monitor the evolving AI landscape, regulatory expectations, and associated risks, and update governance practices as required.

Enterprise AI Adoption & Change Management

Lead enterprise AI literacy, adoption, and change-management initiatives across executives, leaders, employees, technical teams, and advanced AI users.
Develop and deliver role- and function-specific training, guidance, and resources to promote effective and responsible use of AI.
Serve as the enterprise resource for AI strategy, best practices, use-case guidance, and adoption support.
Measure AI utilization, adoption, training effectiveness, employee feedback, and business outcomes to continuously improve AI enablement.
Coordinate internal subject matter experts, technology teams, business stakeholders, and external partners to support successful AI adoption

Vendor, Technology & Partner Management

Evaluate AI technologies, vendors, consultants, platforms, and implementation partners against business requirements, value, security, architecture, scalability, risk, and total cost of ownership.
Manage AI technology and vendor relationships to ensure service quality, effective implementation, and value realization.
Maintain oversight of the enterprise AI technology portfolio to identify duplicate capabilities, unnecessary licensing, overlapping solutions, and opportunities for consolidation.
Monitor emerging AI technologies—including generative AI, large language models, predictive AI, intelligent automation, computer vision, and agentic AI—and assess their practical business applicability and potential value.

Qualifications, Skills, And Educational Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field; Master’s degree preferred.
Minimum seven (7) years of progressive experience in AI, data analytics, digital transformation, automation, technology, or related fields, including significant experience leading enterprise AI or generative AI adoption.
Proven experience leading complex, enterprise-wide AI or business transformation initiatives from strategy and business case development through implementation, adoption, scaling, and measurable value realization.
Strong business and financial acumen, including experience with budgeting, forecasting, reporting, business case development, technology investment evaluation, performance measurement, and ROI.
Strong knowledge of AI technologies, including generative AI, machine learning, predictive analytics, intelligent automation, large language models, AI agents, and emerging AI capabilities, with an understanding of data, cybersecurity, privacy, and AI governance.
Strong strategic thinking, analytical, communication, stakeholder management, project management, and change management skills, with the ability to translate complex technology into practical business solutions and influence cross-functional decisions.
Strong technical and business judgment to evaluate AI solutions, vendors, risks, data and technology dependencies, and investment decisions. Professional certifications in AI, analytics, project management, responsible AI, or AI governance are considered an asset.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS AND WORKING CONDITIONS

Standard office setting - hybrid arrangement (4 days in-office)
Fast paced office environment
Travel expectations between facilities in Mississauga and North York

Job Description 

 WHAT IS THE OPPORTUNITY?
 The Enterprise Chief Controls Office (ECCO) is a centralized first line of defense group (1LOD) with the goal of embedding a culture of risk ownership and operational excellence by elevating the control environment and driving consistency and quality of risk practices to minimize loss and regulatory sanction, drive cost efficiencies, and accelerate execution to enable growth. The Operational Resilience and Business Continuity Management (BCM) team provide leadership in designing and implementing strategic vision, long-term operational model, roadmap and program governance across our platforms in the 1LOD. Working in partnership with platform and business unit Operational Resilience, BCM and Incident Management teams, this central team drives an enterprise-wide strategy to strengthen first line capabilities by driving consistent risk and control practices, embedding resilience into the way we lead, operate and respond to disruption while enabling critical business outcomes. The team is integral in evolving the operating model, governance, and relationship to other resilience risk areas, serving as a single first-line voice to unify, standardize and elevate Resilience capabilities in alignment with ECCO's mandate to embed risk ownership and operational excellence across the organization

 The Enterprise Chief Controls Office & Strategic Execution team (ECCO & SE) is seeking a visionary Director of Resilience CoE Strategy & Transformation to architect RBC's transformational initiative uplift Business Continuity Management and Operational Resilience capabilities across the enterprise. In this role, you will work closely with senior leadership to support the development and execution of RBC's multi-year operational resilience and BCM strategic program while driving enterprise-wide maturity progression across BCM and Operational Resilience capabilities. You will establish strategic milestones, embed industry best practices, and lead the consolidation of fragmented capabilities into a cohesive, best-in-class function. Collaborating across business platforms and functions to align strategic priorities, you will research emerging resilience trends and drive stakeholder engagement to transform resilience from a compliance mandate into a strategic competitive advantage. This is a career-defining opportunity to build a world-class function from the ground up, shape RBC's long-term resilience strategy, and position the organization as an industry benchmark for organizational preparedness and decisive response to operational disruptions.

 WHAT WILL YOU DO?
 Support development and execution of the multi-year operational resilience and BCM strategic program roadmap across enterprise platforms

 We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. jobs.title: Director of Data
jobs.description:
**Purpose in Every Position**


Pebl puts a world of talent at your fingertips. With our AI\-powered Global Work Platform, companies can hire, pay, and manage employees in 185\+ countries—removing risk, red tape, and guesswork from global growth. Backed by more than a decade of compliance leadership and local expertise, Pebl helps businesses move fast, stay compliant, and scale with confidence. With Pebl, companies everywhere can hire great talent anywhere.

**Where Your Work Moves the Needle.**


At Pebl, every team member drives our success. Joining us means more than filling a role—you’re accountable for results and impact. Our values guide how we operate, execute, and collaborate across borders. By putting them into action, you’ll help us scale faster, compete harder, and lead the future of global work.

**What Makes You a Great Fit**


We are seeking a highly technical, deeply analytical, and aggressively innovative Director of Data to lead our data strategy, infrastructure, and AI integration. You will not just be managing a team; you will be the chief storyteller for our data and the evangelist for our "AI Everywhere" initiative.


Based out of our Palo Alto office, you will sit at the intersection of R\&D and our core business functions—specifically Marketing, Sales, Operations, Finance, and Legal—ensuring that Pebl’s vast repository of global employment and compliance data is secure, accessible, and actionable.

***In\-office collaboration is required at our Toronto office Monday through Wednesday.***

**How You'll Make An Impact:**

**1\. Architect the Future (Technical \& Hands\-On Data Engineering)**

* Own the vision and execution of Pebl’s modern data infrastructure.
* Serve as the ultimate technical authority on data engineering, ensuring highly scalable, performant, and reliable data pipelines.
* Champion strict data security, privacy, and governance protocols to protect our global payroll, HR, and compliance data.

**2\. Drive Actionable Business Insights (Analytical Powerhouse)**

* Transform complex datasets into clear, actionable strategies across all departments.
* Partner with Marketing and Sales to optimize our growth funnel, CAC, and conversion rates.
* Collaborate with Operations, Finance, and Legal to improve billing accuracy, payroll speed, and compliance tracking.

**3\. Champion "AI Everywhere" (AI Native Operations)**

* Lead the charge to make Pebl a truly AI\-native company.
* Bring AI capabilities to our R\&D offerings, such as enhancing our compliance assistant, Alfie.
* Engage directly with Marketing, Sales, Operations, Finance, and Legal to embed AI into their daily workflows, driving massive internal efficiency.

**4\. Bridge the Gap (Communication \& Storytelling)**

* Act as the ultimate translator between deep technical R\&D work and overarching business objectives.
* Master the art of data storytelling to present complex insights to the executive team and the board in a compelling way.

**5\. Build and Foster the Team (Leadership)**

* **Lead the Charge:** Be a hands\-on, execution\-oriented leader who ensures delivery of strong business results.
* **Be the NBA Coach:** Recruit top\-tier talent and assemble a high\-performing team of data engineers, analysts, and AI specialists.
* **Be the Gardener:** Foster a culture of continuous learning and psychological safety to cultivate a data\-driven mindset across the entire company.

**Let's Connect If You Have:**

* **Extensive Technical Background:** 15\+ years of experience in data engineering, data science, or analytics, with at least 5 years in a senior leadership role.
* **Modern Stack Mastery:** Deep, hands\-on expertise orchestrating our specific modern data infrastructure stack: **Snowflake, Fivetran, Atlan, Looker, and Monte Carlo**.
* **AI/ML Track Record:** Proven experience deploying LLMs, machine learning models, and AI tools for both production products and internal operational workflows.
* **Cross\-Functional Business Acumen:** Demonstrated ability to collaborate with Marketing, Sales, Operations, Finance, and Legal to tie data initiatives directly to top\-line growth and bottom\-line efficiency.
* **Exceptional Communication:** A track record of weaving data into compelling business narratives for non\-technical stakeholders.
* **Work Style:** Ability to work from our Palo Alto office Monday through Wednesday to collaborate directly with the executive and R\&D teams.

**Our Commitment to You**


At Pebl, we’re committed to supporting our team with comprehensive rewards and benefits designed to meet diverse needs across roles and locations. Our core offerings include:

* **Flexible Time Off** – Take the time you need to recharge.
* **Parental Leave** – Support for growing families.
* **Health and Dental Insurance** – Where applicable, to cover you and your loved ones.
* **Retirement Savings \+ Employee Incentive Plan** – Plan for the future while sharing our success.


Please visit our career page for more information.

**Pebl is an Equal Opportunity Employer.**


We power global teams and believe diverse perspectives drive innovation and impact. Employment decisions at Pebl are based on qualifications, merit, and business needs. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, or gender identity), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable law. We’re committed to fostering an inclusive culture where every teammate can thrive and do the best work of their career—anywhere in the world.

Organization: Securian Canada

Position Title: Head of Total Rewards & Talent Intelligence

Reports to: Chief Human Experience Officer

Location: Toronto (hybrid)

THE COMPANY

Securian Canada is a technology-enabled insurance organization with more than 70 years of experience serving Canadians through financial institutions, associations, affinity organizations, and other strategic distribution partners. As an independent subsidiary of Securian Financial Group, the company combines deep local market expertise with the resources and scale of a leading North American insurance organization. Focused on helping Canadians build greater financial security, Securian Canada offers a range of life, creditor, and specialty insurance solutions designed to meet evolving consumer needs. The organization has established a strong reputation for customer-focused innovation, leveraging technology, data, and digital capabilities to enhance both product offerings and client experiences.

In recent years, Securian Canada has experienced significant growth and transformation through strategic investments, business expansion, and acquisition activity, further strengthening its market position. Despite its increased scale and sophistication, the organization continues to foster a culture characterized by agility, collaboration, inclusion, and an entrepreneurial approach to innovation and continuous improvement.

THE ROLE

Reporting to the Chief Human Experience Officer, the Head of Total Rewards & Talent Intelligence is a critical leadership role responsible for shaping and executing a holistic total rewards and talent analytics strategy.

This role integrates deep functional leadership in compensation and rewards with the forward-looking use of data and insights to inform talent and business decisions. The mandate spans strategy, design, governance, and execution, while serving as a trusted advisor to senior leadership and the Board on compensation matters.
The Head of Total Rewards & Talent Intelligence leads a team and plays a central role in ensuring that reward strategies, talent insights, and workforce decisions are scalable, financially sustainable, and aligned with business priorities.

This is a build-and-shape role, requiring a leader who can operate both strategically and hands-on, establishing frameworks, elevating capabilities, and delivering impact to the business in a high-growth environment.

KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES

Total Rewards Strategy & Design

Lead the design and evolution of an integrated total rewards strategy aligned with business objectives, culture, and growth ambitions
Oversee all aspects of compensation, including base, incentive, and other variable programs

Evaluate market competitiveness and effectiveness of programs, recommending adjustments as needed

Executive Compensation & Governance

Prepare materials and provide insights for Board and Committee reporting, including compensation analysis and recommendations
Ensure strong governance, internal controls, and compliance with applicable standards

People Analytics & Workforce Insights

Develop insights related to workforce trends, capability gaps, performance, engagement, and retention
Translate data into clear, actionable recommendations for senior leadership
Advance the use of systems, analytics, and dashboards across the organization

Enterprise Partnership & Advisory

Partner across HR and the business to align rewards, talent priorities, and enterprise goals

M&A and Strategic Initiatives

Lead Total Rewards and People Analytics support for M&A due diligence and post acquisition integration
Provide guidance on compensation harmonization, workforce alignment, and organizational implications
Support broader strategic initiatives, including growth, restructuring, and expansion efforts

Operational Excellence & Risk Management

Ensure accuracy and integrity of critical processes including compensation cycles and executive reporting
Drive operational efficiency, process improvement, and automation based on modern AI tools
Identify and mitigate financial, compliance, and operational risks

Team Leadership

Lead and develop a small, high-impact team across Total Rewards and People Analytics
Build a strong consultative capability within the team
Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement

CANDIDATE PROFILE

Experience & Expertise

Deep expertise in total rewards, including compensation design and executive compensation
Experience in growth-oriented, evolving, or transformation environments
Strong capability in data and talent analytics
Exposure to M&A, integration, or large-scale organizational change initiatives

Enterprise mindset with the ability to align people strategies with business priorities

jobs.title: Associate Director of Finance
jobs.description:
This is an exciting opportunity to shape the future of one of McMaster's most dynamic and entrepreneurial portfolios. As the Associate Director, Finance, Ancillary Operations
, you will provide strategic financial leadership across five diverse and revenue-generating businesses, including Housing & Conference Services, Hospitality Services, The Campus Store, Media Production Services, and Parking Services
, overseeing a portfolio of approximately $112 million in annual operations
. In this newly created role, you will play a pivotal part in designing and leading a shared-services finance model, driving operational excellence, strengthening financial sustainability, and influencing key business decisions that enhance the experience of students, employees, and campus visitors. Working closely with senior leaders across the University, you will have a unique opportunity to build something new, modernize financial practices, and help position McMaster's ancillary enterprises for long-term success and growth.

Job Description

Job Summary:

The Associate Director, Finance – Ancillary Operations provides strategic and operational leadership for the full range of financial activities across the Ancillary Operations portfolio, including Housing and Conference Services Hospitality Services, Campus Store, Parking Services, Media Production Services, and other assigned operations. The role is accountable for integrating financial planning and analysis, accounting and financial operations, financial reporting, controls, revenue and pricing analysis, and business performance management to support the financial sustainability and effective operation of the portfolio.

The Associate Director provides strategic financial advice to support business planning, investment, resource allocation, revenue generation, pricing, and operational decision-making. The role provides oversight of portfolio financial activities and establishes effective financial management practices, controls, and evaluate and improve processes across diverse operations.

Through a functional reporting relationship to the Controller, the Associate Director ensures Ancillary Operations financial activities are aligned with institutional accounting requirements, financial policies, controls, systems, and reporting standards, while representing the financial and business requirements of Ancillary Operations within the broader University finance function.

Accountabilities:

1. Financial & Business Leadership

Provide financial leadership across the Ancillary Operations portfolio, integrating financial priorities and activities across diverse revenue-generating operations.
Lead the development and execution of annual budgets, forecasts, multi-year financial plans, and longer-term financial strategies aligned with portfolio and institutional objectives.
Serve as the senior financial advisor to the Executive Director and Ancillary leadership team on financial sustainability, resource allocation, investment, and financial performance.
Establish financial priorities and plans for the portfolio and provide direction on how financial objectives and targets will be achieved.

2. Financial Planning, Revenue & Business Performance

Provide leadership and financial advice related to revenue generation, revenue diversification, pricing strategies, capital and deferred maintenance planning and strategies, cost-recovery models, margins, and financial sustainability.
Partner with business leaders to evaluate and shape new services, business opportunities, service delivery models, building and space refresh planning, and revenue-generating initiatives.
Establish approaches for assessing profitability, margins, return on investment, break-even points, and other measures of financial and business performance.
Monitor market, demand, volume, revenue, cost, and other business drivers and assess their implications for portfolio financial performance in collaboration with campus business partners.
Identify significant financial risks and opportunities and lead the development of strategies to improve business and financial outcomes.

3. Accounting, Financial Operations & Reporting

Provide oversight of accounting, financial reporting, and transactional financial activities across Ancillary Operations, ensuring accurate, timely, efficient, and appropriately controlled financial operations.
Ensure appropriate oversight of revenue and expenditure transactions, accounts receivable and payable activities, internal and external billings, reconciliations, journal entries, and other portfolio financial processes.
Ensure appropriate accounting treatment, internal controls, documentation, approvals, reconciliations, and financial controls are consistently applied across operations.
Oversee portfolio financial reporting, including financial results, forecasts, variance analysis, revenue, expenses, margins, and other key financial measures.
Establish clear roles, responsibilities, service expectations, internal controls and processes for financial activities undertaken within Ancillary Operations.
Resolve complex accounting and financial management issues in collaboration with the Controller and other areas of central Finance.
Lead opportunities to standardize, streamline, and automate financial processes while maintaining appropriate financial controls and service levels.
Lead and manage all internal and external financial audit processes; including the year-end process in collaboration with central Finance.

4. Financial Governance, Controls & Stewardship

Establish and maintain effective financial management practices, processes, and controls across the Ancillary Operations portfolio.
Ensure portfolio financial activities comply with University policies, accounting requirements, financial controls, and applicable regulatory requirements.
Interpret institutional financial requirements and determine appropriate approaches for implementation across the portfolio.
Assess the effectiveness of portfolio financial controls and lead corrective action in response to identified risks, deficiencies, or compliance issues.
Support internal and external audit activities and ensure appropriate resolution of findings related to portfolio financial operations.
Promote and advance financial accountability, stewardship, and consistent application of financial practices across Ancillary Operations.
Recommend improvements to financial policies, practices, and controls based on changing business requirements and identified risks.

5. Partnership & Institutional Alignment

Serve as the primary financial partner to the Executive Director, Ancillary Operations and provide financial leadership to the broader Ancillary leadership team.
Translate complex financial, operational, and business information into clear insights and recommendations for senior decision-makers.
Present financial performance, forecasts, business cases, risks, opportunities, and recommendations to senior leadership and other decision-making forums.
Build effective relationships with the Controller, central Finance functions to ensure alignment between portfolio and institutional financial requirements.
Represent Ancillary Operations in institutional financial planning, budgeting, reporting, accounting, and financial process discussions.
Ensure portfolio financial plans, accounting practices, reporting, systems, and controls align with institutional frameworks and standards.
Contribute to University-wide financial initiatives and provide input into institutional practices and processes based on the needs and complexity of revenue-generating operations.

6. People Leadership

Lead, develop, and provide direction to financial professionals supporting the Ancillary Services portfolio.

Delegate operational financial activities appropriately to enable effective oversight of the broader finance function and focus on portfolio-level priorities and longer-term planning.

Mission Statement

The Salvation Army exists to share the love of Jesus Christ, meet human needs and be a transforming influence in the communities of our world.

Job Description

Position Summary

The Director of Finance manages one of the regional financial accounting and advisory services groups of The Salvation Army for Canada and Bermuda and has responsibility for relationship management and for providing financial and strategic advice to the various mission partner leadership teams within the related region. The Director of Finance conducts financial reviews as required, monitors overall financial health for various operating units in Canada and Bermuda and through a collaborative approach with the appropriate divisional or territorial leadership teams, develops action plans to address concerns when needed. The Director of Finance recommends and administers policies and procedures pertaining to such matters and is responsible for ensuring the integrity of the accounting records in accordance with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles.

Key Accountabilities

Lead the delivery of financial accounting and advisory services across multiple operating entities, ensuring sound financial management, compliance, and alignment with organizational objectives.
Develop, implement, and maintain accounting policies, procedures, financial controls, and chart of accounts standards to support accuracy, consistency, and regulatory compliance.
Monitor and assess the financial health, performance, and long-term sustainability of operating units, identifying risks and recommending corrective actions to strengthen financial outcomes.
Conduct financial reviews, analyze key performance indicators, and collaborate with leadership to develop and implement action plans that address financial and operational concerns.
Partner with mission leaders and stakeholders to provide strategic financial advice, interpret policies, and support informed decision-making on operational and organizational priorities.
Lead the budgeting, forecasting, and financial planning processes, including annual operating and capital budgets, long-term forecasts, variance analysis, and performance monitoring.
Oversee financial reporting, account reconciliations, and month-end and year-end processes to ensure the accuracy, completeness, and integrity of financial information.
Manage internal and external audit activities, regulatory filings, charitable and tax returns, and financial statement preparation to meet all compliance and reporting requirements.
Support cash flow management, capital projects, government funding initiatives, and stakeholder reporting by providing financial analysis, forecasts, budgets, and funding-related guidance.
Supervise, mentor, and develop finance staff while fostering strong stakeholder relationships, building financial management capacity, and promoting continuous improvement across finance operations.

Completion of an undergraduate degree in Accounting or a related discipline.

Extensive knowledge of accounting principles, financial management practices, and financial reporting requirements, including regulatory compliance and audit processes.
Experience developing solutions to complex business and financial challenges, managing large-scale initiatives, and exercising sound judgment with a high degree of independence.
Strong understanding of integrated business systems, automated workflows, and accounting technologies, including cloud-based and web-enabled applications.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and financial analysis tools, with the ability to interpret, analyze, and present complex financial information.
Excellent written and verbal communication, stakeholder engagement, and customer service skills, with the ability to convey complex information clearly and effectively.
