jobs.description:
The Opportunity

The Pharmacy Examining Board of Canada (PEBC), a national not-for-profit certification and assessment body for the pharmacy profession, is seeking an Interim Vice-President, Psychometrics and Data Analytics.

This is a highly strategic executive mandate. PEBC is looking for a strong, proven leader who can redefine its psychometric and data strategies and provide senior leadership across psychometrics, enterprise data strategy, analytics, governance and business intelligence.

Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer and serving on the Senior Management Team, the Interim Vice-President holds overall accountability for psychometrics and related data analysis, and leads PEBC’s enterprise data strategy, data analytics and business intelligence, data governance, and reporting. The role ensures the validity, reliability, fairness and defensibility of high-stakes national certification examinations, and positions data as a strategic asset informing decision-making across the organization.

Combining strategic leadership with deep technical authority, the Interim Vice-President advances psychometric and analytic practice through established and emerging methodologies, research and evidence-informed decision-making.

Key Responsibilities

Oversee the psychometric quality of all assessments, validity, reliability, fairness and defensibility, through test design and administration support, standard setting, equating, scaling, scoring and results reporting.
Ensure consistent application of psychometric methodologies across assessments, in line with professional standards and best practices.
Direct statistical and forensic analyses of examination outcomes, candidate performance and testing incidents (including remote proctoring) to support fair, evidence-based decisions.
Lead the initial development and implementation of an enterprise data governance framework, data quality, integrity, security, privacy, retention, definitions and stewardship, alongside metadata management, a data catalogue, and master and reference data management.
Govern analytical and AI/machine-learning models used in or affecting assessments, including model validation, bias and fairness testing, performance monitoring, drift detection and documentation.
Own the reporting, dashboard and data-visualization environment, including self-serve business intelligence for senior leadership, the Board and stakeholders, underpinned by a governed single source of truth and semantic layer.
Champion a data strategy that treats assessment and operational data as a strategic asset, and advance analytics from descriptive and diagnostic reporting toward predictive and prescriptive capability.
Steward the multi-year data strategy and analytics roadmap aligned to the strategic plan, in collaboration with technology leadership, which owns the underlying data platform and engineering.
Chair the data governance operating model, with named data owners and stewards in each function, reporting through the Senior Management Team to the CEO.
Advise on psychometric and standard-setting decisions with high-stakes or policy-level impact, and on statistical and forensic findings related to testing irregularities.
Partner closely with executive peers in Assessments, Technology and Operations, and present psychometric results, validity evidence and recommendations to the Board's examinations committee.
Lead all HR matters for the Psychometrics and Data Analytics department, including recruitment, training, retention and performance management, along with annual business priorities, projects and budget.

Qualifications

PhD required, ideally in psychometrics or educational measurement, or in a closely related quantitative discipline such as statistics.
Significant progressive senior leadership and management experience, including leading technical teams or functions.
Substantial experience as a psychometrician in educational or psychological testing (typically eight or more years), including high-stakes assessment.
Strong expertise in psychometric methodologies, including standard setting, equating and scaling.
Experience leading or overseeing enterprise data strategy, data governance, data analytics and business intelligence/reporting.
Proven ability to design, conduct, interpret and present psychometric analyses and studies in high-stakes assessment contexts.
Strong data analysis and scientific-computing skills, and familiarity with business-intelligence and data-visualization tools.
Experience leveraging data science, machine learning or emerging AI tools to support measurement and analytics.
Assets: exposure to predictive/prescriptive analytics and AI/ML model governance; professional certification and licensure experience; proficiency in French.

The Ideal Candidate

You are a strong, seasoned leader with a track record of setting direction, someone who has redefined strategy for a technical function, not just managed one. You bring high professional standards and a strong commitment to assessment quality, fairness and defensibility, with sound analytical judgment on complex, high-impact psychometric and data issues. You balance strategic leadership with technical rigour, hands-on where needed and treat data integrity, security and privacy as paramount. You are a credible, confident and collaborative communicator, able to translate complex psychometric and data concepts for non-technical audiences, inspire and develop a technical team, and operate independently in a high-stakes assessment environment.

Working Conditions

This is a fully remote position open to candidates located in Canada or the United States. Occasional travel may be required.

How to Apply

This is an interim executive engagement; the anticipated term will be confirmed with shortlisted candidates.

To express interest, please submit a cover letter and résumé to Vanessa at Peak Performance HR at vanessa@peakperformancehr.com. Please reference “Interim VP, Psychometrics and Data Analytics” in the subject line.

All inquiries and applications will be treated in confidence.

This role is a replacement, and AI will not be used during the recruitment process.

Position Overview

Genome Atlantic
brings businesses, governments, and researchers together to focus expertise and investment on Atlantic Canada’s priorities. We help partners turn insights from DNA into practical solutions that improve health, increase productivity, and drive business growth and job creation. The team at Genome Atlantic is connected by a collaborative way of working and a shared commitment to making an impact across Atlantic Canada. 

We are looking for an experienced finance leader who, working as part of a skilled team, appreciates seeing the impact of what they do.

As our Director, Finance & Administration
, you will be the senior financial leader in the organization and a trusted partner to our President & CEO. This is both a leadership role and a hands-on one. You will provide financial insight and advice, while also being directly involved in the accounting, reporting, budgeting, audit, funding and administrative work that keeps the organization aligned with its commitments and vision.

One day you may be preparing financial information for the Board or advising the CEO on an important decision. The next, you may be collaborating on a project with other Genome Center Finance leads , reconciling financial information, working through a funding claim, coordinating an audit requirement, reviewing a contract or solving an operational issue.

For the right person, that combination of collaborative leadership, variety and hands-on involvement is part of what makes the opportunity interesting.

If you are a CPA who enjoys meaningful work, fostering strong relationships and being part of an experienced team where people know and support one another, we would love to hear from you!

The Opportunity

Reporting to the President & CEO, the Director, Finance & Administration
is responsible for the financial stewardship of Genome Atlantic and the effective administration of across important internal business functions, including:

• accounting, financial management and reporting
• budgeting, forecasting and financial analysis
• funder and project financial management
• external audit and financial controls
• Board and Finance & Audit Committee reporting
• contracts and agreements
• payroll and benefits administration
• selected HR and policy administration
• technology and vendor coordination
• organizational systems and administration

This position has one direct report, the Senior Coordinator, Projects and Finance, and is responsible for providing direction, support and appropriate oversight. The role also works closely with the President & CEO, colleagues, Board members, funders, auditors, project partners and external advisors and contractors.

This role combines strategic financial leadership with hands-on involvement in the day-to-day work. You will contribute directly to Genome Atlantic’s financial and administrative operations, provide trusted advice to the CEO and Board, and help ensure the systems and processes that support the organization are reliable, well managed and effective.

Areas of Responsibility

Financial Leadership & Stewardship

Oversee and work directly within Genome Atlantic’s financial management systems, accounting records, controls and policies; lead budgeting; monitor financial performance; prepare quarterly and annual financial reporting; coordinate the annual audit; and provide financial analysis and advice to support decision-making.

Funding & Project Financial Management

Prepare and oversee financial claims and reporting for funding partners, support project budgeting and financial administration, monitor project financial performance and maintain strong relationships with funders, institutional partners and other Genome Centres.

Board & Governance Support

Prepare and present financial information to the Finance & Audit Committee and Board of Directors and support the President & CEO with the financial and administrative aspects of governance.

Contracts, People & Administration

Work directly with contracts, agreements, payroll and benefits administration, employee documentation, policies, technology and other organizational processes, while coordinating with external professional partners as needed.

Team & Organizational Support

Work collaboratively with an experienced team, share knowledge, strengthen processes and contribute beyond a narrow functional boundary when needed. You will provide direction and support while also valuing the expertise and organizational knowledge of the people around you.

Experience and Qualifications

We are looking for someone who combines strong technical finance expertise with practical business judgement and an approachable, collaborative working style. This includes:

A CPA designation in good standing
A minimum of five years of progressively responsible accounting and financial management experience, including senior-level responsibility for a finance function.
Broad experience across the full financial cycle, including accounting operations, budgeting and forecasting, financial reporting, cash management, financial controls, year-end activities and external audit.
Experience preparing and presenting financial information to senior leaders, Boards and/or Finance and Audit Committees, with the ability to translate financial information into clear, practical advice that supports good decisions.
Experience managing externally funded programs, projects or contribution agreements, including budgets, financial claims, reporting and reconciliation.
Experience building effective relationships with funders, government agencies, institutional partners, auditors and other professional advisors.
Experience supporting, supervising or developing others, with a collaborative approach that respects the knowledge and expertise colleagues bring.
A high level of attention to detail and accuracy, with the discipline to ensure financial information, reporting, records and follow-through are complete, reliable and well managed, while still keeping sight of the bigger picture. 
Experience working effectively with external service providers and professional partners, including accounting and IT support.
Experience with payroll, benefits and confidential employee and compensation information.
Clear communication skills and the ability to build trusted working relationships through responsiveness, dependability and follow-through.
Comfort taking ownership, working independently and knowing when to seek input or involve others.
Comfort moving between strategic advice and hands-on execution, sometimes within the same day.
A practical mindset and an interest in strengthening systems, simplifying processes and helping the organization work effectively.
Flexibility, good humour and a willingness to contribute where needed as part of a small, collaborative team.
Experience with not-for-profit accounting and governance is not required but would be highly valued.
Experience in contract administration, policy or HR administration, research, innovation, academic, government-funded or project-based environments would be an asset.
Strong Microsoft Excel and Microsoft 365 skills are important; experience with QuickBooks would be an asset.

Work Environment

This is a full-time hybrid position based in Halifax, Nova Scotia
.

Genome Atlantic’s current hybrid model includes working in the Halifax office on Tuesday
, Wednesday
and Thursday
, with flexibility to work remotely on Monday and Friday.

Periodic travel within Atlantic Canada and elsewhere in Canada may be required. The role also includes predictable periods of increased activity associated with quarter-end and year-end reporting, audits, funding requirements, Board meetings and project milestones.

Physical Requirements

Ability to sit at a desk or workstation for extended periods of time while performing computer-based work.
Ability to communicate effectively in English with team members, stakeholders, and clients through verbal and written communication.
Ability to travel to other Genome Canada/Genome Centre offices, partner sites, and out-of-province conferences as needed.

Eruditus and its sister company Emeritus provide Small Private Online Courses (SPOCs) to students all over the world. EMERITUS enables working professionals who cannot enroll in full-time courses to access a top-tier, affordable education that will give them the skills needed to be the business leaders of tomorrow. The Emeritus and Eruditus global team include 1,000+ employees located in the US, Dubai, Mexico, India, China, and Singapore.

Information about the Program Leader role:

Emeritus is seeking a Program Leader
for the Kellogg Executive Education Program AI-First Marketing Strategy: Executing Intelligent Systems for Growth Live Online Program .
The Program Leader is a subject matter expert that serves as the front-line academic support for learners in the course, supporting the delivery of a high-impact, 8-weeks online program. The Program Leader will be working closely with the Emeritus Academic Delivery Team. Candidates must have industry experience and demonstrated knowledge of the course subject area. They will guide learners through complex topics like AI-driven strategies, frameworks, and challenges in real-world contexts.
This is a great role for someone who wants work flexibility and the chance to diversify their resume with consultancy and teaching experience. This is an independent contractor position in a remote setting.

Responsibilities of the Program Leader role:

Facilitate weekly live sessions and moderate required discussion boards
Moderate and guide learner engagement during faculty live sessions
Support learners in synthesizing live session content delivered by the faculty
Assist with capstone assignment challenges
Grade specific assignments while aligning with the suggested rubric
Collaborate with instructional designers to improve engagement and comprehension
Monitor learner progress and provide support or escalation as needed

Qualifications for the Program Leader role:

Bachelor’s degree in marketing, business, communications or a related field plus MBA from a top university.
10+ years of progressive marketing leadership experience including ownership of brand, growth demand generation and digital strategy.
Proven experience integrating AI technologies into marketing operations, campaign execution, analytics and customer engagement.
Deep understanding of modern AI -driven marketing tools and platforms, including generative AI, predictive analytics, marketing automation, CRM systems and personalization engines.
Demonstrated ability to build and scale AI-first marketing workflows that improve efficiency, campaign performance and customer acquisition.
Proven experience leading multi-channel campaigns across paid media, content marketing, SEO, email, social media and lifecycle marketing.
Strong understanding of prompt engineering, AI assisted content generation, workflow automation, and responsible AI usage in marketing.
Proven experience managing transformation projects from initiation to closure.
Experience providing guidance and recommendations to management to ensure marketing strategy or innovation plans align with company goals.
Experience supporting executive or mid-career professionals
in continuing education is highly preferred.
Excellent communication, facilitation, and interpersonal skills with an ability to listen effectively, respond appropriately, and maintain a mutual comfort level while working with a diverse population.
Ability to translate content into actionable insights.
Empathetic and learner-centered approach.
Comfortable in an online environment, navigating LMS platforms (Canvas), Zoom, Slack, or similar environments.
Strong organizational and time-management skills to manage weekly cycles of engagement and support.

Program Description and Context:

The AI
‑ First Marketing Strategy: Executing Intelligent Systems for Growth
program from Kellogg Executive Education is an eight-week online experience that prepares leaders to navigate a pivotal shift: AI is redefining how organizations grow and compete. Many organizations continue to operate between experimentation and execution, using AI tools in isolation rather than integrating them into a connected system. As generative AI (gen AI) expands marketers’ ability to create, personalize and act at scale, participants will learn to build marketing systems that operate continuously, adapt in real time and drive measurable growth. This program will enable participants to architect this shift through the Intelligent Marketing Operating System (I-MOS) framework, developed by Professor Mohanbir Sawhney, a globally recognized authority in AI, marketing and business innovation. I-MOS defines what to do and shows how to apply AI across your marketing system. By learning to apply AI across connected workflows and align intelligence, decisioning, execution and governance, participants will build the capability to design high-performing marketing systems that continuously evolve.
Duration: 8-weeks (estimated learner commitment: 4–5 hours/week).
Structure: Blend of asynchronous Canvas activities and live Zoom sessions.
Target Audience: Mid- to senior-level professionals and leaders seeking to integrate AI in their marketing strategy.

 Advance analytical capabilities related to emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence and data-driven investment insights, and assess their implications for portfolios, markets and investment processes.
 Lead innovation in cross-asset correlation, tail-risk analysis, scenario design and forward-looking portfolio assessment methodologies.

 Leadership & Influence

Founded by former National Security Agency (NSA) cyber operations experts who applied their learnings to bring national security-grade technology solutions to commercial customers around the world, Blackpoint Cyber is in hyper-growth mode, fueled by a recent $190m series C round.

At Blackpoint Cyber, we value high-quality execution, ownership, and strong morals. Our principles are never tested, and we are proud to always do right by our customers. Blackpoint Cyber is seeking a strategic and visionary Director of Platform Engineering to lead the development and execution of its Unified Security Posture data platform, which powers the company’s data-centric cybersecurity solutions. This leader will serve as the single-threaded owner for the roadmap and operations of the cloud-based platform, including vendor integrations, developer and data tooling, identity, authentication, tenant management, and other core services.

This role will drive vision and execution across multiple engineering teams, working cross-functionally with internal stakeholders, product leaders, and site reliability engineering partners. The Director of Platform Engineering will translate business and technical needs into clear strategies, oversee roadmap execution and service quality, and build a high-performing organization through strong hiring, mentorship, and technical leadership. As a highly visible leader, this person will also help establish company-wide operational excellence practices for instrumentation, incident response, root cause analysis, and remediation.

Key Responsibilities

Define and drive the platform roadmap aligned with product and business goals.
Partner across the Product organization and SRE team to ensure platform security, reliability, and scalability.
Lead the development of the data pipeline, integrating with Blackpoint’s endpoint agent and vendor data, including storage, tiered access, and query capabilities.
Deliver platform services and public APIs supporting core functions such as tenant management, identity, and role-based access control.
Lead platform tooling and APIs that accelerate AI/ML and business intelligence initiatives.
Oversee developer productivity tooling, including CI/CD systems.
Define the long-term vision for the data platform by implementing best practices in data architecture, modeling, and governance, while staying current on emerging technologies and trends.
Build strong relationships with internal stakeholders and partners.
Foster excellence in platform reliability, scalability, security, and software quality.
Hire, develop, and grow a high-caliber team of platform and data engineers, scaling the team and organizational structure as needed.
Drive the adoption of AI across the development lifecycle (AI DLC) to increase engineering productivity, accelerate delivery, improve software quality, and enable teams to build and deliver high-quality products more efficiently

Qualifications

15+ years of experience in software development, preferably in cybersecurity, including at least 5 years of people management experience leading multiple teams.
Proven experience leading a Platform Engineering function at the Director level.
5+ years of experience working with large-scale AWS cloud solutions and technologies such as Postgres, Elastic, Redis, streaming data platforms, and ETL processes.
Hands-on experience architecting and building complex data platforms and service integrations.
Deep knowledge of CI/CD, production deployment at scale, and data pipeline orchestration.
Demonstrated ability to drive high-impact initiatives and long-term strategic goals.
Strong leadership, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
B.S. or M.S. in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Why Join Blackpoint Cyber

If you are passionate about cybersecurity and have a proven track record of leading and managing software engineering teams, we encourage you to apply for this exciting opportunity. Blackpoint Cyber offers competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, and a dynamic work environment where you can make a real impact in the field of cybersecurity.

Blackpoint Cyber welcomes and encourages applications from qualified individuals of all races, colors, religions, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, marital status, or any other legally protected status. Our client is a family-owned, international food and beverage organization with restaurant operations spanning multiple countries, including Canada. The company operates a growing portfolio of globally recognized quick-service restaurant brands.

With a strong track record of growth and an entrepreneurial culture, the organization continues to invest in its people, operations and finance infrastructure to support its expanding business across multiple entities, brands, jurisdictions and currencies.

About the Opportunity

Our client is seeking a Vice President, Finance to join its senior leadership team and play a critical role in strengthening and evolving the finance function across Canada and the UK.
Reporting to the CFO, this is a broad, highly visible leadership role that combines strategic finance leadership with hands-on ownership of core financial processes. The successful candidate will oversee financial and management reporting, FP&A and commercial finance, treasury and banking relationships, and provide financial leadership on M&A and other strategic initiatives.
The role is well suited to a finance leader who can operate comfortably at both the VP and Controller level - someone who can provide strategic insight and decision support to senior leadership while maintaining a strong grasp of the underlying financial detail and reporting infrastructure.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Reporting

Take ultimate ownership of the financial and management reporting function across Canada and the UK.
Review and ensure the accuracy, integrity and timeliness of financial reporting prior to presentation to the CFO.
Oversee the preparation and review of monthly, quarterly and annual financial reporting.
Partner with internal and external stakeholders, including auditors and advisors, on financial reporting matters.
Ensure appropriate reporting processes, controls and accounting policies are in place across the organization.
Provide financial insight and analysis to support senior leadership decision-making.

FP&A & Commercial Finance

Lead the annual planning, budgeting and forecasting processes across the business.
Develop and maintain the company's business plan and financial models.
Establish reporting and performance measurement frameworks that connect financial results to business decisions.
Partner with operational and commercial leaders to evaluate performance, identify trends and develop actionable recommendations.
Track performance against budget, forecast and strategic objectives, providing meaningful variance analysis and recommendations.
Support decision modelling and scenario analysis for major business initiatives.
Work closely with the UK finance team, leveraging its established commercial finance and FP&A capabilities while strengthening the Canadian function.

Cash Management & Treasury

Take ownership of cash management and treasury activities across Canada and the UK.
Develop strong relationships with banking partners and financial institutions.
Oversee liquidity, cash flow forecasting and working capital management across two countries and two currencies.
Develop improved visibility and controls around cash movements between Canada and the UK.
Provide senior leadership with clear insight into liquidity, funding requirements and cash flow.

M&A & Strategic Projects

Provide financial leadership and support throughout M&A and other strategic transactions.
Act as a key finance point of contact during transaction execution and subsequent integration.
Partner with the CFO and external advisors on financial analysis, due diligence and transaction-related activities.
Serve as the bridge between transaction execution and the operational transition of acquired businesses.
Lead or participate in other strategic finance initiatives and projects as the business evolves.

Finance Transformation & Systems

Serve as the finance project owner for the company's transition to IFRS 16 lease accounting.
Act as the primary finance point of contact for auditors, consultants and other external advisors throughout the implementation.
Lead the financial requirements and stakeholder coordination associated with the project rather than performing the underlying transactional work.
Support the organization's evolution from its current Sage ERP environment toward Sage Intacct.
Bring experience with ERP implementations, finance transformation and process optimization to help build a more scalable finance infrastructure.

The Ideal Candidate

The successful candidate will be a commercially minded finance leader who combines strong technical accounting and controllership fundamentals with sophisticated FP&A and business partnering capabilities.

12+ years of progressive finance experience, with experience operating at a senior finance leadership level.
Experience leading financial reporting and controllership functions in a complex, multi-entity organization.
Strong FP&A, budgeting, forecasting and financial modelling capabilities.
Experience managing cash flow, treasury functions and banking relationships.
Experience working across multiple entities, currencies and/or jurisdictions.

Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to work effectively with executives, operational leaders, auditors, consultants and banking partners.
A hands-on, entrepreneurial approach and the ability to move seamlessly between strategic thinking and detailed execution.
A CPA or equivalent professional accounting designation is preferred.

Reporting directly to the VP of Finance, the Director, Finance, will play a critical role in strengthening the Company’s core accounting operations, close processes, and financial controls. This role is heavily focused on improving the quality, timeliness, and reliability of financial reporting through process development, simplification, and automation.

The Director, Finance will oversee monthly, quarterly and annual close activities for the consolidated Sym‑Tech entities, ensure strong balance sheet discipline through robust reconciliations and detailed financial reviews, and provide technical accounting guidance across the organization. While the role includes elements of financial analysis and planning, the primary emphasis is on accounting fundamentals, execution excellence, and building scalable, repeatable processes.

The role provides technical accounting guidance throughout the organization to ensure the consistency of accounting practices and principles throughout the operational business.

The successful candidate will be hands‑on, detail‑oriented, and capable of leading teams through change while operating effectively in a growing, complex environment. This position has two direct reports, and overall responsibility for Financial Reporting, OEM Accounting, and select FP&A activities.

Position Functions:

Core Accounting, Close, and Controls

On time, accurate and complete financial reporting for the Company. Analyze and prepare dashboards on balance sheets, income statements, financial position forecasts and capital expenditure reporting.
Manage month‑end, quarter‑end, and year‑end close processes, including journal entries, reconciliations, ad-hoc analyses and financial reporting.
Ensure accurate accounting for bordereaux, premium flows, claims funds, and insurer settlements.
Oversee cash management, trust accounts, and insurer reconciliation processes.
Own and continuously improve the monthly and annual close processes, including developing standardized timelines, checklists, and accountability across the team.
Lead efforts to simplify, automate, and streamline close‑related activities to improve efficiency, accuracy, and cycle time.
Ensure strong balance sheet integrity through timely, well‑documented account reconciliations and resolution of open items.
Perform detailed reviews of monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements, with a strong focus on accuracy, completeness, and underlying drivers.
Strengthen core accounting fundamentals, including journal entry discipline, reconciliations, documentation standards, and internal controls.

Financial Reporting & Technical Accounting

Provide timely, insightful financial analysis on divisional and business unit performance, including revenue, margin, expense, and cash drivers.
Champion data-driven culture within the finance team and broader organization.
Oversee all divisional financial reporting, ensuring accuracy, timeliness, and alignment with local requirements and US GAAP.
Support the VP, Finance on technical accounting matters, including documentation and assessments for management and external auditors.
Serve as a subject matter expert on accounting standards and their application, including supporting M&A due diligence and integration activities.
Act as the primary liaison with OEM partners for quarterly, interim, and year‑end financial reporting requirements.

Process Improvement & Team Leadership

Develop and implement clear processes, policies, and procedures to support consistent execution across the finance organization.
Lead, coach, and develop the finance team, driving ownership, accountability, and discipline around key deliverables.
Partner with Corporate Finance to ensure alignment on close processes, reporting standards, and reconciliation expectations.

Select Planning & Analysis Support

Provide targeted financial analysis to support management decision‑making, including variance analysis and trend identification.
Support budgeting and forecasting activities as needed, with an emphasis on ensuring inputs are grounded in accurate accounting data.

Audit, Compliance & Governance

Manage relationships with external auditors and oversee audit execution to ensure timely resolution of findings.
Enhance the accuracy and integrity of the Company’s reported financial results.
Ensure compliance with Amynta and Sym‑Tech policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements.

Minimum Qualifications & Competencies:
University degree in Business/Accounting, with professional accounting designation (CPA).
5+ years of progressive management experience with knowledge of all aspects of corporate accounting and financial management.
Strong technical accounting skills (i.e. U.S. GAAP) and strong internal controls and procedures.
Strong preference for candidates who have worked in an entrepreneurial, high growth environment in a privately held business.
Demonstrated ability to "roll up the sleeves" and work with the team in a hands-on capacity.
Advanced computer skills (Word, Excel ,and PowerPoint) and knowledge of ERP accounting systems.

Ability to hold a strong right hand to general management, with sound judgment on when to appropriately escalate issues and concerns.
Ability to lead a team, driving ownership, accountability, and discipline around key accounting and reporting processes.
Expert in project planning, with a proven ability to organize, prioritize, and manage responsibilities to consistently meet deadlines in environments with overlapping and potentially competing priorities.
Attention to detail and a high degree of accuracy.
Excellent communication and organizational skills with the ability to quickly build credibility, rapport and relationships at multiple levels of the organization
A team player and consensus builder.

jobs.title: Director, Finance
jobs.description:
About the Organization

Our client is a family-owned, international food and beverage organization with restaurant operations spanning multiple countries, including Canada. The company operates a growing portfolio of globally recognized quick-service restaurant brands.

With a strong track record of growth and an entrepreneurial culture, the organization continues to invest in its people, operations and finance infrastructure to support its expanding business across multiple entities, brands, jurisdictions and currencies.

About the Opportunity

Our client is seeking a Director, Finance to join its Canadian finance leadership team and play a key role in strengthening the organization's financial reporting and controllership capabilities.

Reporting to the VP, Finance and CFO, this role will have primary responsibility for entity-level and brand-level financial reporting across the Canadian business, with a particular focus on the organization's largest brand portfolio. The Director will also oversee Canadian cash forecasting and provide financial insight and support to senior leadership.

This is a predominantly controllership-focused leadership position, ideally suited to a strong accounting and finance professional who combines technical depth with commercial awareness and the ability to operate in a growing, multi-entity organization.

While the immediate mandate is focused on Canada and core controllership responsibilities, there is meaningful opportunity for the successful candidate to expand their scope over time into group-level FP&A, commercial finance, M&A and broader strategic finance responsibilities.

Key Responsibilities:

Financial Reporting & Controllership

Take ownership of financial reporting across all Canadian legal entities.
Oversee the preparation, review and delivery of accurate and timely monthly, quarterly and annual financial statements.
Ensure appropriate accounting policies, controls and reporting processes are maintained across the Canadian organization.
Review financial results and investigate significant variances, trends and anomalies.
Ensure the integrity and consistency of financial data across entities and reporting periods.
Partner with the VP, Finance and CFO to ensure Canadian reporting meets group requirements.
Coordinate with external auditors, advisors and other stakeholders as required.
Support the ongoing enhancement of financial controls, processes and reporting infrastructure.
Identify opportunities to improve the efficiency, accuracy and scalability of the Canadian finance function.

Brand-Level Reporting

Own financial reporting and analysis across the Canadian brand portfolios.
Develop and maintain brand-level reporting that provides leadership with clear visibility into financial and operating performance.
Analyze brand performance against budget, forecast and prior periods.
Provide meaningful variance analysis and identify key drivers of financial performance.
Partner with operational and brand leadership to translate financial results into actionable business insights.
Ensure consistency between entity-level accounting and brand-level management reporting.

Cash Flow & Treasury

Own cash flow forecasting across the Canadian entities.
Develop and maintain short- and medium-term cash flow forecasts.
Monitor cash requirements, working capital and liquidity across the Canadian business.
Partner with the VP, Finance and CFO on broader treasury and cash management activities.
Provide visibility into upcoming funding requirements and significant cash movements.
Support relationships with banking partners and other financial institutions as required.

FP&A & Commercial Finance

Support the annual budgeting, forecasting and planning processes.
Provide financial analysis and decision support to Canadian leadership.
Partner with operational stakeholders to understand business performance and financial drivers.
Support scenario modelling and analysis for key business initiatives.
Contribute to the development of management reporting and performance metrics.

The precise scope of FP&A and commercial finance responsibilities will evolve as the finance organization continues to develop.

Strategic & Group Finance

Support the VP, Finance and CFO on broader finance initiatives and special projects.
Provide financial analysis and support for strategic initiatives, including potential M&A activity where appropriate.
Participate in finance transformation, systems implementation and process improvement initiatives.
Contribute to initiatives designed to create greater consistency between Canadian and broader group finance processes.
Develop the capability to take on broader group-level responsibilities as the organization and the individual's experience evolve.

The Ideal Candidate

The successful candidate will be a strong controllership and financial reporting leader who is comfortable operating in a dynamic, entrepreneurial environment.

You will likely bring:

8–12+ years of progressive accounting and finance experience, including significant controllership or financial reporting responsibility.
Strong technical accounting and financial reporting capabilities.
Experience overseeing multiple legal entities and/or business units.
Experience producing entity-level and management-level financial reporting.
Strong understanding of budgeting, forecasting and financial analysis.
Experience with cash flow forecasting and working capital management.
Strong analytical skills and the ability to identify the underlying drivers of financial performance.
Experience working with external auditors and other professional advisors.
Experience in a multi-entity, multi-location or complex operating environment.
ERP experience; exposure to Sage or Sage Intacct would be an asset.
Experience with finance transformation or ERP implementation would be considered an asset.
CPA designation or equivalent professional accounting qualification is preferred.
Strong communication skills and the ability to build relationships with senior stakeholders and operational leaders.
A hands-on approach and willingness to operate at both the detailed and strategic levels.
Restaurant or food & beverage industry experience is not required. Experience within a complex, multi-entity organization is more important.

What Makes This Opportunity Unique

This role provides the opportunity to join a growing organization and take meaningful ownership of the Canadian finance and reporting function across multiple entities and brands.

The immediate mandate is strongly rooted in controllership, financial reporting, brand performance and cash forecasting, providing the successful candidate with a broad understanding of the Canadian business.

At the same time, the role has significant room to evolve. As the finance organization grows, there is an opportunity for the Director to expand into FP&A, commercial finance, M&A and broader group-level responsibilities, creating a strong path toward future senior finance leadership opportunities.

jobs.title: Vice President, Finance
jobs.description:
The Vice President, Finance, Americas
is responsible for providing strategic financial leadership and oversight across the Americas region. This role partners with executive and business leaders to drive financial performance, support growth initiatives, ensure compliance with financial and regulatory requirements, and deliver accurate financial planning, reporting, and analysis. The VP Finance leads regional finance functions, including accounting, budgeting, forecasting, tax, treasury, internal controls, and financial operations, while fostering a high-performing team and supporting the achievement of organizational objectives.

Reports to the Chief Financial Officer.

Responsibilities

1. Financial Reporting & Accounting

Oversee accounting operations for the Americas region, including general ledger, month-end/quarter-end closing, and consolidation.
Own inventory accounting for the Memphis distribution center — valuation methodology, standard costing, cycle counts, and obsolescence/reserve policy.
Ensure COGS accuracy and margin analysis tied to distribution operations.
Ensure accuracy of financial statements prepared in accordance with local GAAP in each jurisdiction (US, Canada, and LatAm countries).
Prepare and submit financial reports in compliance with IFRS and Group accounting standards, ensuring quality and compliance.
Coordinate with external auditors for annual audits, implement improvement plans, and maintain effective communication with internal and external audit teams.
Work closely with the HQ finance team to ensure consistency in reporting formats, policies, and processes.

2. Compliance

Maintain and enhance internal control and accounting procedures to align with Group policies and US/Canadian/LatAm regulations.
Ensure customs and bonded warehouse compliance — duty deferral, in-bond transfers, and CBP requirements — for the Memphis distribution center, partnering with trade compliance and logistics teams.
Ensure compliance with local direct and indirect tax regulations, including corporate income tax, VAT/GST, and multi-state US sales/use tax nexus; complete filings accurately and on time.
Regularly review the reasonableness of intercompany transfer pricing across US, Canada, and LatAm entities, and assess associated risks.

3. Treasury & Financial Planning

Manage cash-flow, working capital, and banking relationships across the Americas to ensure liquidity and efficient funding.
Support financing activities and treasury optimization.
Provide budgeting, forecasting, and financial analysis to support operational decision-making across HQ, sales & marketing offices, and the distribution center.

4. System & Process Enhancement

Drive ERP system integration and automation to improve reporting efficiency, data accuracy, and close timelines.
Identify process improvement opportunities across order-to-cash and purchase-to-pay to enhance timeliness and reliability of financial information.

Qualifications and Experience

Bachelor's degree or above in Accounting, Finance, or related field; CPA/ACA/ACCA qualification preferred.
Minimum 15 years of accounting or finance experience, including at least 6 years in a managerial or Controller role.
Solid knowledge of IFRS, US/Canadian tax regulations, compliance, and internal controls.
Experience with distribution or logistics operations, including inventory accounting and customs/bonded warehouse environments, strongly preferred.
Hands-on SAP experience, particularly ERP implementation or migration, is a strong plus.
Previous experience in multinational or listed companies is a strong plus.
Proven leadership experience building and managing multi-country/multi-entity finance teams.
Strong written and verbal English communication skills for global stakeholder management. Chinese is a plus for Group-level communication.

Competencies (Skills & Behaviors)

Strong AI awareness with hands-on experience implementing AI tools or automation workflows within a finance environment.
Experience supporting regional or global finance functions.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Familiar with transfer pricing and cross-border tax principles.
Comfortable operating at senior leadership/executive committee level, with strong stakeholder management and influencing skills.
Familiar with inventory and sales/purchase management.

Leadership & Strategic Influence

Partner with Americas business, sales, and marketing leadership to provide financial insights, operational performance analysis, and cost control recommendations.
Build, lead, and develop a high-performing finance team across Montreal HQ, sales & marketing offices, and the Memphis distribution center; drive talent development and succession planning.
Act as a strategic finance partner to the Americas leadership team, contributing to regional business strategy, investment decisions, and capital allocation.
Report to the Group CFO on financial performance, risks, and strategic priorities, representing Americas Finance in Group-level executive discussions.

jobs.title: Associate Director, Regulatory Affairs (Regulatory Intelligence)
jobs.description:
Telix Pharmaceuticals is a dynamic, fast-growing radiopharmaceutical company with offices in Australia (HQ), Belgium, Japan, Switzerland, and the United States. Our mission is to deliver on the promise of precision medicine through targeted radiation. At our core, we exist to create products that seek to improve the quality of life for people living with cancer and rare diseases.
You will be supporting the international roll-out of our approved prostate cancer imaging agent and helping us to advance our portfolio of late clinical-stage products that address significant unmet need in oncology and rare diseases.

See Yourself at Telix

The Associate Director, Regulatory Affairs (Regulatory Intelligence), will be responsible for monitoring, analyzing, and interpreting global regulatory developments to ensure the company’s compliance and strategic positioning in the pharmaceutical market. This role involves collecting and disseminating regulatory information, providing insights to internal stakeholders, and supporting the development of regulatory strategies. Supports the Senior Director, Regulatory Affairs (Labeling/Ad-Promo), in efforts to influence the regulatory environment.

Key Accountabilities

Proactively monitors and assesses global regulatory environments for emerging changes in laws, regulations, and guidance impacting drug and device development.
Tracks and evaluates updates from key regulatory authorities (e.g., FDA, EMA), industry associations, and external intelligence sources.
Maintains and continuously enhances regulatory intelligence databases and tools to ensure accurate, timely, and efficient dissemination of information.
Analyzes regulatory developments, including guidance documents, policies, and regulations, to determine potential impact on internal processes, development programs, and regulatory strategies. Anticipates and tracks regulatory changes over time, delivering timely, accurate, and actionable updates to impacted stakeholders across the organization.
Partners with Quality to ensure appropriate change control processes are initiated and tracked through implementation when regulatory changes impact internal procedures.
Translates complex regulatory information into clear, actionable insights for cross-functional stakeholders.
Develops and delivers regulatory intelligence communications, including newsletters, alerts, trackers, and periodic reports.
Responds to internal inquiries by providing tailored regulatory intelligence summaries and detailed analyses to support decision-making.
Leads and facilitates regulatory intelligence meetings to include review and discussion of ad hoc query requests, regulatory background package requests, health authority guidance, Federal Register notices, public commenting opportunities, newsletter content, training sessions, and knowledge-sharing forums.
Coordinates cross-functional discussions to evaluate the impact of new or revised regulatory requirements. Collaborates closely with key functions, including Quality, Pharmacovigilance, Clinical, CMC, and Regulatory Affairs, to ensure alignment and effective implementation.

Contributes to cross-functional initiatives and organizational projects by providing regulatory intelligence expertise and strategic insight.

Proficient in using regulatory intelligence tools and databases.

Strategic thinking & regulatory innovation: Capable of strategic thinking and proposing innovative solutions involving regulatory issues, while being a team player who invites response and discussion
Performance & accountability: Comfortable in a fast-paced, results-driven, and highly accountable work environment

jobs.title: Chief Technology Officer
jobs.description:
POSITION OVERVIEW

Reporting directly to the CEO, the CTO will lead the company’s technology strategy, engineering organization, product development, and adoption of engineering automation and applied AI. The role combines executive technology leadership with strong hands-on engineering judgement across software, embedded systems, electronics and hardware/software integration. The CTO will establish the company’s technical architecture and roadmap, maintain a sustainable engineering foundation and technology capability, lead complex international programs, and support demanding customers and manufacturing activities.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Define and maintain the company’s technology architecture, product roadmap and engineering priorities with the CEO; lead technology-selection decisions, establish technical standards, prepare engineering resource and budget plans, and manage approved resources within delegated authority.
Lead and develop the existing engineering organization, including recruitment as required, technical ownership, people development, performance management and resource allocation; maintain a scalable technical foundation and organizational capability to support current products and future growth.
Lead complex software, electronics and embedded-product programs across distributed and cross-functional teams, covering product definition, feasibility, architecture, development, integration, validation, release, manufacturing support and lifecycle maintenance.
Provide technical leadership for embedded and hardware/software co-development, including STM32 and comparable MCUs, FPGA-based systems, ARM/SoC platforms, board-level design and integration, component and peripheral selection, low-level software, device drivers/HAL, system bring-up, debugging and production issue resolution.
Lead sustained technical engagement with Mandarin-speaking customers, manufacturing operations and engineering partners, including requirements analysis, design reviews, tailored solution development, factory and system integration, project coordination, technical escalation and major issue resolution.
Lead engineering automation and applied-AI initiatives that improve development efficiency, quality and product value, including evaluation and integration of modern AI/agent technologies with appropriate validation, security, reliability controls and human oversight.
Establish project-management, development-process, quality-control and technical-risk practices appropriate for complex commercial products; monitor delivery commitments and report progress, significant risks, resource requirements and technology investment needs to the CEO.
Participate in international customer, partner, factory and project-site activities as required, including technical assessment, integration, project delivery and support.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

A master’s degree in Electrical or Electronic Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Automation, Artificial Intelligence, or a closely related engineering or technical discipline.
At least 15 years of technology and product-development experience in software, embedded systems, semiconductors, intelligent systems, industrial technology, automotive electronics, mobile platforms or related fields, including substantial responsibility in large-scale, cross-functional and internationally distributed R&D environments.
At least 6 years of technology-management experience with responsibility for multidisciplinary engineering teams. Demonstrated experience building or substantially scaling an engineering organization and establishing effective technical ownership, people-development, accountability and resource-management mechanisms.
A sustained record of leading large and technically complex programs across countries, time zones and engineering disciplines, with responsibility for architecture, delivery, quality and technical risk.
Strong embedded and systems-engineering background, including Linux, processor/SoC/MCU platforms, hardware/software integration, low-level interfaces, device drivers/HAL and system debugging; ability to lead architecture reviews and make sound trade-offs across performance, reliability, cost and maintainability.
Experience delivering and supporting demanding international customer programs, translating complex requirements into practical and customized technical solutions, and leading major technical issue resolution; strong understanding of mature project-management, development-process, quality-control and release practices.
Practical experience applying modern AI-assisted development and/or agent technologies to real engineering or product-development workflows, including integration, validation, effectiveness assessment and appropriate human oversight.
Advanced professional English sufficient to independently lead international technical and business meetings, architecture and solution discussions, customer coordination and professional documentation; approximately CEFR C1 level or equivalent.
Professional working proficiency in Mandarin sufficient to independently conduct technical requirements discussions, design reviews, project coordination, factory/system integration, technical escalation and complex issue resolution with Mandarin-speaking customers, manufacturing operations and engineering partners.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

Interdisciplinary expertise combining electrical/electronic engineering with intelligent systems, automation, computing or AI.
Broad hands-on embedded/software experience involving ARM platforms, STM32 or comparable MCUs, FPGA-based systems, board/peripheral integration, JTAG/SWD, TRACE32 or comparable professional embedded-debug environments, together with experience integrating and maintaining open-source or third-party software in commercial products.
Experience in automotive electronics, mobile computing, semiconductor platforms, industrial/manufacturing systems or marine-related technologies; multimedia, audio/video, DSP or graphics expertise is an advantage.
Advanced AI engineering experience involving coding agents, engineering toolchain/workflow integration, reliability and security controls, performance optimization and organization-wide adoption.
Engineering-management experience in a large international technology company, with exposure to mature global project-management, quality-control and customer-delivery practices.

jobs.title: VP Senior Applied AI Full-Stack Engineer
jobs.description:
We are seeking a senior technical leader specializing in building high-performance, interactive data visualization platforms and enterprise reporting engines. This is an expert-level role focused on creating advanced, web-based analytical applications that combine rich, interactive frontends with highly optimized, data-intensive backends and distributed query engines. A mandatory and critical secondary focus of this role is the design and creation of custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools. You will build the bridge between LLMs/AI agents and our enterprise data layers, including Starburst, enabling AI to autonomously and securely query, analyze, and report on massive datasets.

Core Responsibilities

You will own the end-to-end design and delivery of sophisticated FinTech tools used directly by investment bankers, front-office traders, and financial analysts. This requires translating complex financial workflows into intuitive, high-fidelity web interfaces. Your primary focus will be on architecting and building highly interactive, web-based analytical dashboards using Angular and React, allowing users to slice, dice, and explore massive datasets in real-time.

A key function is leveraging Starburst (Trino) to query massive, distributed datasets with sub-second latency. You will design and implement robust backend microservices (Java/Spring Boot) optimized for low-latency data retrieval, heavy aggregation, and streaming large datasets to the frontend. Furthermore, you will be responsible for designing and optimizing scalable ETL processes to manage huge volumes of financial data.

A mandatory responsibility is to design, build, and maintain custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and tools. This enables AI agents and LLMs to securely interface with internal databases, APIs, and reporting engines. You will also architect enterprise-grade document generation engines using the Aspose suite to programmatically create high-fidelity financial reports from complex templates.

As a hands-on player/coach, you will deliver complex data visualizations and reporting engines while mentoring junior engineers. This includes critically reviewing and taking ownership of all AI-generated code (Java, Angular, React, SQL) to ensure structural integrity, security compliance, and production readiness, while applying a deep functional understanding of Corporate and Investment Banking (CIB) to all projects.

Key Qualifications

Required Skills & Experience:

Systems Fundamentals: Strong foundation in systems analysis, design patterns, data analysis, and the full software development lifecycle (SDLC), including unit testing and CI/CD practices.
Backend Development: Extensive hands-on experience with Java and Spring Boot for building scalable, low-latency microservices and reactive data streaming APIs.
Frontend & Visualization: Strong, hands-on experience with Angular 19+, React, TypeScript, HTML5, and Web Sockets for building interactive, data-intensive dashboards.
Data Federation & Querying: Hands-on experience with Starburst (Trino) for querying massive, distributed datasets across federated enterprise data sources.
Databases & Data Modeling: Deep experience with relational databases (Oracle, SQL Server) and NoSQL (MongoDB), including physical/logical database design, data modeling, and performance tuning.
ETL & Data Processing: Proven experience designing high-throughput ETL pipelines and optimizing data flows for real-time reporting.
Enterprise Reporting: Experience building document generation engines using the Aspose suite (Aspose.Words, Aspose.Cells, Aspose.PDF).
MCP Tool Creation: Demonstrated ability to design and build custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers to securely connect LLMs and AI agents to enterprise data.
AI-Assisted Engineering: Hands-on proficiency with AI coding tools (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot) and the ability to write structured prompts and engineer high-quality context (schemas, API specs) for AI agents.
Collaboration Tools: Strong experience with GitHub for source control and Jira for project management.

Preferred Skills & Experience:

8+ years of relevant experience
Experience designing and implementing agentic AI workflows and integrating AI agents directly into CI/CD pipelines.
A strong understanding of event-driven systems and real-time message streaming platforms like Apache Kafka or RabbitMQ.

Domain

Functional understanding of Banking — able to articulate why their work matters, not just how it is built.

What Sets This Role Apart

This is not a conventional engineering role. You are expected to operate as a force multiplier — directing AI agents across multiple workstreams, validating output for production safety, and coaching others to do the same. The measure of success is not lines of code written, but outcomes delivered, quality maintained, and the team's collective capability raised.

jobs.description:
Position Description

Artificial Intelligence is reshaping every industry, transforming how organizations operate, innovate, and create value. But organizations aren't looking for more technology. They're looking for trusted advisors who can help them modernize operations, transform how work gets done, and realize measurable business outcomes.

At CGI, we're building on decades of consulting excellence, proven AI capabilities, and global innovation to help clients navigate this transformation. We're looking for a business consulting leader who can help expand that capability while influencing how we continue to bring AI enabled business transformation to market.

As Canada's largest IT and business consulting services firm, and a global leader with more than 400 offices worldwide, CGI combines the entrepreneurial spirit of a local business with the strength, scale, and expertise of a global organization. We call our employees Partners for a reason: 90% are shareholders who take ownership of our success. Here, you'll have the autonomy to influence strategy, the resources to make an impact, and the opportunity to help shape the future of consulting.

Your Role: Lead Transformation. Shape Strategy. Enable Growth.

As a Director Consulting, Business Transformation & AI, you'll serve as a senior business transformation consultant and trusted advisor, helping organizations understand how AI can create practical, measurable business value and realize sustainable value from their AI investments.

Working alongside CGI's Directors of Consulting Services, you'll bring deep expertise in business transformation and AI to strengthen client relationships, shape strategic opportunities, and guide organizations through complex transformation initiatives. Rather than owning client accounts, you'll complement our account leaders by helping clients develop transformation strategies, modernize business processes, and accelerate responsible AI adoption.

You'll also help shape the continued evolution of CGI's Business Transformation & AI consulting capabilities across the Atlantic Business Unit. Building on CGI's established consulting practice, global AI expertise, and proven client success, you'll have the opportunity to influence our strategy, evolve consulting offerings, strengthen our market presence, and help define how we continue delivering AI enabled transformation for our clients.

You'll collaborate closely with CGI's technical AI specialists, architects, and delivery teams, serving as the bridge between client business objectives and successful implementation.

If you're passionate about business transformation, executive advisory services, emerging technologies, and helping organizations prepare for what's next, we'd love to hear from you.

Your future duties and responsibilities

Client Leadership & Strategic Advisory

Serve as a trusted advisor to client stakeholders, business leaders, technology leaders, and executives on business transformation, AI adoption, and digital modernization.
Lead executive workshops that help organizations define transformation priorities, AI strategies, investment roadmaps, and measurable business outcomes.
Advise clients on operating model redesign, organizational change, Responsible AI, governance, and workforce transformation.
Build trusted relationships with key client stakeholders, decision makers, and influencers, strengthening CGI's position as a trusted transformation partner.

Opportunity Shaping & Business Development

Provide business transformation and AI expertise that strengthens client relationships and shapes strategic opportunities.
Support executive presentations, discovery workshops, proposals, business cases, and transformation roadmaps.
Collaborate across CGI consulting, engineering, cloud, cybersecurity, data, and account and delivery teams to recommend and shape integrated client solutions.
Bring innovative thinking, market insight, and consulting expertise to strategic pursuits and client engagements.

Practice Leadership & Thought Leadership

Help shape and evolve CGI's Business Transformation & AI consulting capabilities across the Atlantic Business Unit.
Contribute to consulting methodologies, reusable assets, market offerings, executive workshops, and leading practices.
Mentor consultants and help build AI fluency across CGI's consulting Partner community.
Represent CGI through conferences, executive forums, industry events, and thought leadership initiatives while staying current on emerging business and technology trends.

Solution Leadership

Translate client business challenges into practical transformation opportunities enabled by AI and digital technologies.
Connect clients with the right CGI capabilities, technical specialists, delivery teams, and alliance partner solutions.
Help ensure consulting engagements deliver measurable business outcomes and long term client value.

Required Qualifications To Be Successful In This Role

12+ years of experience in management consulting, business transformation, digital transformation, technology consulting, or advisory services.
Demonstrated success advising organizations on complex business transformation initiatives and translating emerging technologies into measurable business outcomes.
Strong understanding of Artificial Intelligence, Generative AI, Data & Analytics, Digital Transformation, and the evolving technology landscape.
Demonstrated executive presence with the ability to influence senior client stakeholders, facilitate strategic discussions, and build trusted relationships.
Experience supporting business development through executive advisory, opportunity shaping, proposals, workshops, and strategic consulting engagements.
Comfortable collaborating with technical AI specialists and delivery teams without needing to be the primary solution developer.
Exceptional communication, facilitation, presentation, and relationship building skills.
Degree in Business, Engineering, Computer Science, Data Science, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Familiarity with Responsible AI, AI governance, enterprise transformation, and organizational change management.

Asset Qualifications

MBA or graduate degree in Business, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Organizational Change, or a related discipline.
Certifications in AI, Cloud, Business Architecture, Digital Transformation, Change Management, or related disciplines.
Experience working with public sector, healthcare, credit unions, financial services, utilities, or other regulated industries.
Bilingualism (English/French) is considered an asset.
Willingness to travel within Canada and internationally as required (travel estimated at 25% and primarily within Atlantic Canda).

CGI is providing a reasonable estimate of the pay range for this role. The determination of this range includes factors such as skill set level, geographic market, experience and training, and licenses and certifications. Compensation decisions depend on the facts and circumstances of each case. A reasonable estimate of the current range is $100,000–$190,000. This role is an existing vacancy.

Together, as owners, let’s turn meaningful insights into action.

Life at CGI is rooted in ownership, teamwork, respect and belonging. Here, you’ll reach your full potential because…

You are invited to be an owner from day 1 as we work together to bring our Dream to life. That’s why we call ourselves CGI Partners rather than employees. We benefit from our collective success and actively shape our company’s strategy and direction.

Your work creates value. You’ll develop innovative solutions and build relationships with teammates and clients while accessing global capabilities to scale your ideas, embrace new opportunities, and benefit from expansive industry and technology expertise.

With that growth is a vision to be the most innovative healthcare provider in community rehabilitation, workplace health and wellness, and medical assessment services. Lifemark was acquired by Loblaw Companies on May 10, 2022.

Role Overview:

Lifemark Health Group is hiring a Director, Technology Delivery and Enablement to lead our Application Development Team and advance the modernization of our enterprise application landscape. Reporting to the VP, Engineering and Security Services, you will oversee the development, implementation, modernization, and ongoing reliability of critical business applications supporting Lifemark’s national operations.

In this hands-on technology leadership role, you will lead teams of developers, DevOps engineers, and QA specialists to deliver secure, scalable, and resilient solutions while evolving our engineering practices and technology platforms. You will champion modern approaches including cloud-native architecture, DevSecOps, platform engineering, intelligent automation, and AI-assisted software development, while improving application observability, engineering productivity, and delivery effectiveness.

Working closely with business and technology leaders, you will help shape Lifemark’s application modernization and technology strategy, including the responsible adoption of generative AI and emerging technologies, reduction of technical debt, modernization of legacy platforms, and continued evolution of our Azure ecosystem. You will also collaborate across departments, security and infrastructure teams, architecture, data and analytics, and external technology partners to ensure technology investments deliver measurable business value.

About You:

You are an experienced technology leader with a strong background in software and application development and a track record of leading high-performing technical teams. You combine hands-on technical depth with strong people leadership, delivery discipline, and the ability to translate business needs into secure, scalable technology solutions.

You are comfortable managing multiple concurrent initiatives, guiding application architecture and development practices, building strong cross-functional and vendor relationships, and continuously improving release management, DevOps, monitoring, quality, and reliability. You communicate clearly, develop talent, and stay current with emerging technologies and industry best practices.
